title: Why Global Baby Care Products Market is demanding globally with
summary: The global baby care products market is experiencing significant demand, driven by increasing parental awareness of child safety, rising disposable incomes, and the growth of the working women population. Key players like Procter & Gamble, Kimberly Clark, and Johnson & Johnson are leading this market, which is projected to grow to over $110 billion by 2025 with a CAGR of 6%. North America currently holds the largest share due to high expenditure and progressive technology, though high costs and a lack of regulatory guidelines pose challenges to market growth.

title: Michel Khalaf to Lead MetLife
summary: Michel Khalaf has been named to lead MetLife. The article reports on this leadership change at MetLife, effective January 8, 2019.

title: Inspire Medical Systems scores win with Blue Cross Blue Shield Association
summary: Inspire Medical Systems received a positive assessment from the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association’s Evidence Street for its obstructive sleep apnea therapy. This assessment is expected to facilitate broader insurance coverage for Inspire therapy among BCBS companies. The report highlights the therapy's effectiveness for specific patient criteria, validating its clinical evidence.

title: UnitedHealth Group to Launch Electronic Health Records Platform in 2019; Will It Guide Physicians to Preferred Clinical Laboratory Providers?
summary: UnitedHealth Group plans to launch an electronic health records (EHR) platform by the end of 2019, leveraging its existing Rally mobile wellness platform and targeting 50 million members and one million providers. The new Individual Health Record (IHR) aims to complement existing EHRs by connecting data from multiple sources, potentially positioning UnitedHealth as a central point in healthcare and influencing physician choices for clinical laboratories. This move highlights the increasing importance for clinical laboratories to develop informatics strategies that deliver actionable intelligence to stakeholders.

title: Walmart and CVS Split Over Pricing
summary: Walmart and CVS Health's partnership has ended due to a dispute over prescription drug pricing, leading CVS pharmacies to no longer include Walmart pharmacies in their network for most consumers. CVS stock fell 1.5 percent following the announcement, with CVS citing Walmart's requested rates as leading to higher costs for their clients and consumers. Despite the split, CVS stated its retail pharmacy network remains robust, with over 63,000 other pharmacies providing ample access for its members.

title: JPMorgan spinoff Kadena puts blockchain on AWS—and on the table for small and medium-sized businesses
summary: Kadena, a JPMorgan spinoff, is making blockchain technology accessible to small and medium-sized businesses by moving its development platform to Amazon Web Services (AWS), aiming to reduce development costs. This move allows companies, including those in healthcare, to experiment with and implement rudimentary blockchain solutions with ease. The company hopes to democratize blockchain access, moving beyond the current landscape where adoption has been primarily by larger firms due to high development costs.

title: P&G buys purpose-driven feminine care marketer This Is L.
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has acquired This Is L., a purpose-driven feminine care products maker known for its L. brand made with organic cotton. The acquisition aligns with P&G's strategy to center its business around purpose and tap into the disruptor market for organic materials in feminine care. This move complements P&G's existing feminine care portfolio and reflects a broader CPG trend of acquiring startup brands.

title: Providence St. Joseph snaps up blockchain-powered RCM platform Lumedic
summary: Providence St. Joseph Health has acquired Lumedic, a blockchain-enabled revenue cycle management platform, for an undisclosed sum. This acquisition positions Providence St. Joseph as the first integrated provider-payer system with a scalable blockchain tool for RCM, aiming to increase efficiencies and reduce costs. The deal involves creating a new company with Lumedic's assets and team, retaining the Lumedic brand, and seeking partnerships with other health-related entities.

title: CVS Health Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year Results and Provides 2019 Full Year Guidance
summary: CVS Health announced its fourth quarter and full-year 2018 results, highlighted by the $70 billion acquisition of Aetna and strong financial performance. The company provided 2019 guidance, anticipating a transitional year focused on integrating Aetna and addressing market challenges to position for future growth. Full-year 2018 revenues increased by 5.3% to $194.6 billion, with GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations at $(0.57) due to significant goodwill impairment charges related to the Long-Term Care business.

title: Trump rebate rule will hike premiums for seniors, CVS Health CEO says
summary: CVS Health's CEO, Larry Merlo, warned that a Trump administration proposal to eliminate drug rebates would increase Medicare premiums for seniors, potentially making up to 70% of beneficiaries worse off. While top pharmaceutical companies support the rule, pharmacy benefit managers like CVS Health argue it would impede efforts to lower treatment costs. The Department of Health and Human Services, however, maintains the rule would bring transparency and lower out-of-pocket spending, projecting much smaller premium increases.

title: The Top 15 U.S. Pharmacies of 2018: M&A Reshapes the Market
summary: This article identifies the top 15 U.S. pharmacies by prescription dispensing revenues for 2018, highlighting how mergers and acquisitions have reshaped the market. The analysis reveals that the largest pharmacies, including CVS Health, Walgreens Boots Alliance, and the combined Cigna/Express Scripts, control a significant portion of dispensing revenues. It also notes the growing role of specialty pharmacies operated by PBMs, accounting for a large share of their revenues.

title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Diagnostic Gets Medicare Coverage
summary: Veracyte Inc. has secured Medicare coverage for its Envisia Genomic Classifier, a diagnostic tool for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), effective April 1, 2019. This approval from the Palmetto GBA MolDx program makes the diagnostic available to 55 million Medicare patients, addressing a critical need for accurate and timely IPF diagnosis given high rates of misdiagnosis in the US. The Envisia classifier is Veracyte’s third genomic test to achieve Medicare-covered status, aiming to improve patient outcomes by accelerating appropriate treatment.

title: As telemedicine grows, a ‘digital front door’ lowers health-care costs
summary: Telemedicine is transforming healthcare delivery, offering a more affordable way to provide primary care through virtual examinations and partnerships between health systems and telemedicine providers. Companies like Teladoc are at the forefront, demonstrating significant cost savings for patients and attracting investor interest due to their growth and expansion beyond standard care into behavioral health services. The global telemedicine market, currently around $1 billion, is projected to grow substantially to $113.1 billion by 2025, indicating vast potential for expansion.

title: Your U.S. Equity Fund Is More Global Than You Think
summary: This article examines how U.S. equity funds are more globally exposed than commonly perceived by analyzing revenue streams by region. Morningstar's new proprietary data reveals that many popular U.S. index-tracking ETFs have significant revenue exposure outside the United States, particularly in emerging Asian markets and the eurozone. The analysis highlights that relying on a company's headquarters or stock listing alone provides a flawed picture of a fund's true geographic allocation.

title: The Future of Virtual Healthcare With Teladoc
summary: Teladoc, founded in 2002, is the largest provider of telehealth services in the US, with over 3 million members. The company reported $418 million in revenue for 2018, an 80% increase from the previous year, under the leadership of CEO Jason Gorevic. Teladoc offers 24/7 access to affordable, high-quality medical care through videoconferencing or telephone consultations, boasting a 97% patient satisfaction rate.

title: Humana To Expand Senior Care Clinic Network To New Markets
summary: Humana is expanding its senior-focused primary care network to new markets, including Charleston, S.C., Houston, and Memphis, Tenn., building on the success of its value-based care approach. The insurer aims to improve health outcomes and control costs for its 3.9 million Medicare Advantage enrollees by growing its network of owned, joint venture, and alliance clinics. This expansion, including partnerships like the one with Walgreens, is designed to reduce hospital admissions and provide integrated care for seniors.

title: Has Employment Become the Goal of the U.S. Healthcare System?
summary: The U.S. healthcare system spends more than any other nation but yields poor results. One major unintended consequence of its complexity is its reliance on the industry for jobs, making it the largest and fastest-growing employment sector. The article suggests shifting spending towards social services to improve both health outcomes and employment.

title: UnitedHealthcare’s Investments in Affordable Housing to Help People Achieve Better Health Surpass $400 Million
summary: UnitedHealthcare has invested over $400 million in affordable housing initiatives to address social determinants of health, creating more than 4,500 new homes across 80 communities in 18 states. These investments support developments with on-site services, aiming to improve health outcomes and reduce healthcare costs for underserved populations including seniors, veterans, and individuals experiencing homelessness. The company's efforts include significant investments in projects like PATH Metro Villas in Los Angeles and Capital Studios in Austin, Texas.

title: AI at the Top Healthcare Companies in the World - Current Initiatives
summary: This article explores the current AI initiatives of three major healthcare companies: McKesson, UnitedHealth Group, and Cardinal Health. It highlights their focus on white-collar automation, business intelligence, and predictive analytics rather than traditional R&D. The article details specific partnerships, acquisitions, and platforms each company uses to leverage AI for operations, claims management, and value-based care.

title: Optum Is a Major Differentiator for UnitedHealth Group
summary: Optum, UnitedHealth Group's health services business, significantly contributed to the company's fiscal 2018 performance with substantial revenue and earnings growth. The company is leveraging OptumRx, OptumInsight, and OptumHealth to improve patient outcomes, reduce healthcare costs, and enhance profitability through data analytics and an evidence-based care delivery network. Key segments like OptumInsight, OptumHealth, and OptumRx all reported strong year-over-year revenue increases, demonstrating Optum's vital role in UnitedHealth Group's strategy and financial success.

title: After Bernie’s Tweet, UnitedHealth’s CEO Describes ‘Wholesale Disruption’ Of Medicare For All
summary: UnitedHealth Group CEO David Wichmann expressed concerns about "wholesale disruption" to the American healthcare system from certain "Medicare for All" proposals, following Senator Bernie Sanders' tweet criticizing UnitedHealthcare. Wichmann advocated for universal coverage through existing public and private platforms, highlighting the growth of UnitedHealth's Medicare Advantage plans and the company's strong Q1 2019 financial results. He argued that proposals eliminating private insurers would jeopardize patient-doctor relationships, destabilize the health system, and increase costs without improving access.

title: Sell in May, and Go Away? Maybe At Least Rotate? or Hedge…
summary: This article discusses the "Sell in May and go away" adage for traders, exploring alternatives like rotating into less affected sectors or using inverse/leveraged inverse ETFs. It highlights potential opportunities in healthcare and technology stocks, citing specific companies and Direxion ETFs. The piece emphasizes that traders have choices to navigate seasonal market trends, whether by shifting focus or hedging against potential downturns.

title: Health-care stocks keep getting hammered — Wall Street says this is why
summary: Health-care stocks continue to face significant pressure, as Wall Street attributes the downturn to the evolving political landscape, including growing calls for lower drug prices and "Medicare for All." This political uncertainty is particularly impacting the sector, with notable health companies seeing substantial losses in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. An analyst noted that volatility in health-care stocks often increases during election cycles, suggesting a cyclical pattern to the current market behavior.

title: Anthem and UnitedHealth Group among top competitors to acquire Magellan Health
summary: Anthem and UnitedHealth Group are among the leading contenders to acquire Magellan Health, with the bidding process advancing to the second round. Analysts suggest Magellan's diverse assets, including Managed Medicaid and behavioral health benefits, would complement the acquirers' existing portfolios, especially in light of Anthem's development of IngenioRx and UnitedHealth's search for specialty Rx and regional players. The potential acquisition comes amidst pressure from activist investors for Magellan Health to sell itself to boost value after a significant drop in its stock price.

title: UnitedHealth CEO's pay passed $18 million in 2018; Optum chief got $21 million in his first year
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. CEO David Wichmann's pay exceeded $18 million in 2018. The Optum chief, who was not named in the provided text, received $21 million in his first year. This news comes as Wichmann recently voiced opposition to a single-payer healthcare system.

title: UnitedHealth CEO's pay was $21.5 million in 2018
summary: UnitedHealth Group CEO David Wichmann's total compensation for 2018 was $21.5 million, a significant decrease from his 2017 compensation when he cashed in stock options. This pay package included a salary of $1.3 million and was 316 times the median employee pay. The article also notes that former CEO Stephen Hemsley's 2018 pay was $65.6 million, largely due to exercised stock options and vested awards from prior years.

title: Pfizer, McKesson, Others Join MediLedger’s Blockchain Project Working Group
summary: Pfizer, McKesson, AmerisourceBergen, and Premier have joined the MediLedger Project Contracting and Chargebacks working group to leverage blockchain technology for improved supply chain efficiency. This initiative aims to streamline the complex chargeback process and enhance data integrity for the pharmaceutical industry. The MediLedger network is also establishing a decentralized blockchain for saleable return drug verification, with goals to go live by Q2 2019.

title: UnitedHealth's David Wichmann buys record $4.6 million worth of UNH stock
summary: David Wichmann, CEO of UnitedHealth Group Inc., recently bought 20,000 shares of UnitedHealth stock for approximately $4.6 million. This purchase, made on May 3, represents a significant insider transaction. The article highlights other related news concerning UnitedHealth and its CEO, including previous salary information and company outlooks.

title: Shaving Start-Up Harry’s Will Be Sold to Owner of Schick for $1.37 Billion (Published 2019)
summary: Harry's, a shaving start-up, is being acquired by Edgewell Personal Care, the owner of Schick and Wilkinson razor brands, for approximately $1.37 billion in stock and cash. This deal highlights a trend of established companies purchasing younger, internet-born competitors, similar to Unilever's acquisition of Dollar Shave Club. Post-acquisition, Harry's founders, Andy Katz-Mayfield and Jeff Raider, will manage Edgewell's U.S. operations, aiming to strengthen their position as a distant second to Procter & Gamble's Gillette in the men's shaving market.

title: Shaving upstart Harry's is selling for $1.37 billion to the company that owns Schick razors
summary: Edgewell Personal Care, owner of Schick and Wilkinson razor brands, announced its plan to acquire U.S.-based shaving startup Harry's for $1.37 billion in a cash-and-stock deal. This acquisition aims to expand Edgewell's presence in the rapidly growing U.S. grooming market, with Harry's founders Andy Katz-Mayfield and Jeff Raider joining Edgewell's executive team. The deal makes Harry's the latest shaving startup bought by a larger rival, highlighting the increasing focus on the men's grooming industry.

title: 2019 Women in Business Awards: Mary Welsh, UnitedHealth Group Inc.
summary: Mary Welsh of UnitedHealth Group Inc. is recognized with a 2019 Women in Business Award for her role as chief security officer. She leads the largest organization worldwide with a female chief security officer and brings 20 years of public and private sector security experience to transform the role of women in the security industry.

title: Does an echocardiogram cost $210 or $1,830? UnitedHealth calls out price variation.
summary: UnitedHealth Group's analysis of 12.5 million diagnostic tests in 2017 revealed significant price variations for common procedures like echocardiograms, ranging from $210 to $1,830. The report suggests that tackling this variation could save $18.5 billion, as current price differences are not tied to improved patient outcomes or provider quality, but rather market power. This finding echoes similar concerns raised by other insurers, such as Anthem, regarding the cost disparities in outpatient imaging.

title: Quest Diagnostics says 12 million patients may have had their personal information exposed
summary: Quest Diagnostics announced that the personal information of 11.9 million customers may have been compromised. This breach occurred through AMCA, a billing vendor, which had an "unauthorized user" gain access to its system. The exposed data included Social Security numbers and medical information but not test results, and Quest has suspended its use of AMCA while an investigation is underway.

title: LabCorp: 7.7 Million Consumers Hit in Collections Firm Breach
summary: Medical testing giant LabCorp disclosed that personal and financial data on approximately 7.7 million consumers were exposed due to a breach at its third-party billing collections firm, American Medical Collection Agency (AMCA). This follows a similar disclosure by Quest Diagnostics, whose 11.9 million patients were also affected by the same breach, highlighting a widespread security issue with the collections firm. The exposed data for LabCorp consumers could include names, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, date of service, provider, balance information, and potentially credit card or bank account details.

title: Dividend Stock Analysis of UnitedHealth Group (UNH)
summary: This article provides a dividend stock analysis of UnitedHealth Group (UNH), highlighting its consistent dividend growth over 10 years and recent 20% dividend increase. The author discusses the company's strong earnings growth, integrated business model, and potential resilience against political risks, making it an attractively valued stock for dividend growth investors.

title: Kellogg’s, General Mills Are Investing in Their Small Competitors
summary: Large food companies like Kellogg's and General Mills are increasingly investing in smaller, disruptive "challenger brands" through corporate venture capital arms. This strategy allows them to regain market share lost to agile startups that cater to changing consumer tastes and leverage digital marketing and lean operations. These investments provide challenger brands with capital, industry knowledge, and supply chain expertise, while helping established companies spur innovation.

title: How Tandem Diabetes Care found its way back from near-bankruptcy
summary: Tandem Diabetes Care has made a significant turnaround from near-bankruptcy in 2017 thanks to technological advancements, strategic financing, and competitor exits from the market. The company's t:slim X2 Insulin Pump and upcoming Control-IQ algorithm are driving growth, despite challenges like UnitedHealthcare's exclusive deal with Medtronic. Tandem aims to increase insulin pump market penetration by offering easy-to-use devices and is working to re-engage with major payers.

title: UnitedHealth Group Wins FTC Approval Of DaVita Deal On Divestiture Conditions
summary: UnitedHealth Group received FTC approval for its $4 billion acquisition of DaVita Medical Group, but with conditions requiring the divestiture of a health plan network in Las Vegas to Intermountain Healthcare. The deal, which faced a long regulatory process due to monopoly concerns in the Las Vegas area, integrates DaVita Medical Group's practices into UnitedHealth's OptumCare. This acquisition is part of a broader trend of health insurers incorporating healthcare providers to offer coordinated care and lower costs.

title: UnitedHealth Agrees to Buy Payments Firm Equian for $3.2 Billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group has agreed to acquire health-care payments firm Equian for approximately $3.2 billion. Equian, currently owned by private-equity firm New Mountain Capital, specializes in payment-processing services for health-care companies and insurers, focusing on reducing overpayments. It is anticipated that Equian will be integrated into UnitedHealth's Optum health-services arm.

title: UnitedHealthcare agrees to $3.2B deal to acquire payments firm Equian
summary: UnitedHealth Group plans to acquire healthcare payments firm Equian LLC for approximately $3.2 billion. This acquisition is expected to bolster Optum’s health services, especially given Equian's expertise in payment integrity and claims data management. The deal follows other significant acquisitions by UnitedHealth, including DaVita Medical Group, as the company continues to expand its healthcare services portfolio.

title: UnitedHealth scoops up health tech startup PatientsLikeMe
summary: UnitedHealth Group has acquired PatientsLikeMe, an online network for individuals with chronic conditions. This acquisition follows the Trump administration's earlier nixed deal for PatientsLikeMe with a Chinese-investor-owned company. PatientsLikeMe will continue to operate independently within UnitedHealth Group's research and development arm, ensuring patient privacy.

title: Omada Health Raises $73 Million to Accelerate Program Expansion
summary: Omada Health announced a $73 million funding round led by Wellington Management Company LLP to expand its digital care program, which includes support for chronic diseases, anxiety, and depression. The company's integrated approach, combining human coaching and technology, aims to provide personalized interventions and achieve sustainable health outcomes for its participants. This funding will help Omada deepen collaborations with health plans, employers, and health systems to further develop its personalized health programs.

title: UnitedHealth Group Shuffles Senior Leadership
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced significant leadership changes at its two major divisions, with Dirk McMahon becoming CEO of UnitedHealthcare and Daniel Schumacher taking over McMahon's previous role as president and COO of Optum. These changes come as part of a strategic reshuffle amid strong company performance, including a 12 percent jump in annual revenue in 2018.

title: UnitedHealthcare Gets New CEO, as Division Execs Dance a Do-Si-Do
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced leadership changes following the retirement of UnitedHealthcare CEO Steve Nelson. Dirk C. McMahon will succeed Nelson as UnitedHealthcare CEO, while Daniel J. Schumacher will take over McMahon's previous role as Optum's president and COO. These changes affect C-suite posts for both the UnitedHealthcare and Optum divisions.

title: UnitedHealth Group Shuffling C-Suite Executives
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced C-suite executive changes following the unexpected retirement of Steve Nelson, the top executive at UnitedHealthcare. Dirk McMahon will replace Nelson, while Daniel Schumacher will take over McMahon's role as president and chief operating officer of Optum. These leadership changes are effective immediately and come amidst political scrutiny from figures like Bernie Sanders regarding private insurers' roles in healthcare.

title: Alpern accepted more pharma payments than any U.S. medical school dean in 2018
summary: Yale School of Medicine Dean Robert Alpern received $648,183 from pharmaceutical companies Abbott Laboratories and AbbVie, Inc. in 2018, making him the highest-paid medical school dean by pharmaceutical payments in the U.S. that year. He defended these payments as similar to those received by other deans serving on corporate boards, though data indicates his receipts were significantly higher than his peers and the average U.S. physician. The article also highlights a past instance where Alpern failed to disclose a conflict of interest related to his industry ties in a published study.

title: UnitedHealth backs Inspire Medical’s sleep apnea implant
summary: UnitedHealthcare announced it will provide coverage for Inspire Medical Systems' obstructive sleep apnea therapy starting August 1. This decision follows similar coverage commitments from Aetna and several BlueCross BlueShield plans, broadening access to Inspire's hypoglossal nerve neurostimulation system. The expanded coverage boosts Inspire's total covered members to 125 million and contributed to a more than 4% rise in the company's stock.

title: The Big Three Generic Drug Mega-Buyers Drove Double-Digit Deflation in 2018. Stability ahead? (rerun)
summary: This article analyzes how the three largest generic drug purchasing organizations drove double-digit deflation in generic drug prices in 2018. It profiles these "mega-buyers" – Red Oak Sourcing, Walgreens Boots Alliance with AmerisourceBergen, and Econdisc Contracting Solutions/Innovative Product Alignment – detailing their market impact and recent strategic moves. The author predicts a stabilization, and possible rise, in oral generic prices over the next 12 to 18 months due to manufacturers exiting highly competitive categories.

title: Kroger Health and Myriad Genetics Launch Pilot Program to Improve the Treatment of Depression
summary: Kroger Health and Myriad Genetics have partnered to launch a pilot program aimed at improving the treatment of depression for Kroger Prescription Plan members. The program will utilize Myriad Genetics' GeneSight® pharmacogenomic test in nearly 500 Kroger pharmacies across five states. This genetic test helps clinicians personalize treatment plans by analyzing how a patient's genomics may affect psychiatric drugs, with the goal of improving outcomes, productivity, and lowering healthcare costs.

title: UnitedHealth Group's political and financial heft just keeps growing
summary: UnitedHealth Group's stock fell despite raising profit projections, though its substantial financial power in the U.S. health care system remains. The company, which is more than just an insurer, continues to expand its reach into various health care services and actively lobbies to influence policy in its favor. Its growing influence means any health reforms must contend with its significant market presence and political efforts.

title: Digital Health Care Startup Livongo Joins the List of Health-Tech Companies to IPOs This Year
summary: Digital health company Livongo is set to go public, pricing its shares at $28 apiece and raising $355 million, valuing the company at $2.5 billion. This IPO is part of a new wave of digital health companies entering public markets after a three-year drought, including other firms like Health Catalyst and Phreesia. Livongo, which provides technology to manage chronic conditions like diabetes, saw its revenue more than double in 2018, though its net losses also widened.

title: Procter & Gamble shares jump on earnings beat, optimistic 2020 outlook despite Gillette write-down
summary: Procter & Gamble reported stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings and revenue, leading to a jump in share price, despite an $8 billion write-down of its Gillette brand. The company offered an optimistic forecast for fiscal 2020, projecting revenue growth of 3% to 4% and adjusted EPS growth of 4% to 9%. This performance was driven by strong organic sales growth, particularly in health care and fabric/home care segments, and strategic price increases.

title: $23.5M settlement reached in suit over acquisition of Louisville's Passport Health Plan
summary: A $23.5 million settlement was approved in November 2022 in a class-action lawsuit filed against Evolent Health regarding its acquisition of Louisville's Passport Health Plan. The lawsuit, filed by Saxena White P.A., alleged that Evolent Health and its executives made false and misleading statements to investors about the acquisition of the financially struggling Passport. The settlement applies to individuals and entities who purchased or acquired Evolent Health stock between January 10, 2018, and May 28, 2019.

title: DaVita Medical names new NM regional president
summary: Jack Towsley has been appointed as the new president of DaVita Medical Group’s New Mexico region. This announcement follows DaVita Inc.'s prior sale of its subsidiary DaVita Medical Group to Collaborative Care Holdings LLC, a subsidiary of UnitedHealth Group Inc., for $4.34 billion.

title: Cigna mulling sale of group benefits insurance business: report
summary: Cigna is reportedly considering selling its group benefits insurance business, including disability, life, and accidental death and dismemberment plans, which are valued at $6 billion. This potential divestiture aligns with Cigna's strategy to intensify its focus on healthcare, following its acquisition of pharmacy benefit manager Express Scripts. The move reflects a broader trend of vertical consolidation among major healthcare players.

title: Cigna Health Services Business Pioneers an Innovative Solution to Affordably Bring Life-Changing Therapies to Patients
summary: Cigna's health services business is launching Embarc Benefit Protection℠, an innovative solution designed to make breakthrough, potentially life-changing therapies more affordable and accessible for patients. This new offering combines the expertise of Express Scripts, eviCore, Accredo, and CuraScript SD to protect consumers from out-of-pocket costs and shield organizations from high-priced medicine shocks. The program aims to address the rapidly increasing cost of gene therapies, with an intention to include treatments like Luxturna™ and Zolgensma®.

title: Phreesia partnering with North Carolina DHHS on social determinants of health screening
summary: Phreesia is collaborating with the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services on a $650 million Healthy Opportunities pilot project to screen patients for social determinants of health. This partnership allows North Carolina healthcare providers to use Phreesia's platform to identify patients with unmet social needs, aligning with Phreesia's mission to help manage healthcare costs and improve outcomes. The announcement was made during Phreesia's second-quarter earnings call, which reported significant revenue growth following its public debut, though adjusted EBITDA was lower than the prior year due to increased operating expenses.

title: UnitedHealth Group acquires 'payment integrity' firm
summary: UnitedHealth Group has acquired Equian, an Indiana-based "payment integrity" firm, reportedly for $3.2 billion. Equian helps insurance companies recover inaccurate payments and ensures efficient use of healthcare dollars. This acquisition aligns with Optum's strategy to provide end-to-end payment integrity solutions.

title: Medicare Advantage open enrollment starts this week. Here are the health plans' star ratings for 2020
summary: Medicare Advantage open enrollment for 2020 begins with beneficiaries expected to enroll in plans with higher star ratings and lower premiums. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reported that 81% of beneficiaries with drug coverage will be in a plan with four stars or more, and premiums have decreased by about 14%. Kaiser Permanente leads the star ratings with an average of 4.6 stars, while other major insurers like UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, and Anthem also performed well.

title: U.S. Stock ETFs Jump on Promising Start to Earnings Season
summary: U.S. stock ETFs surged due to a strong start to the third-quarter earnings season, driven by upbeat results from companies like UnitedHealth Group, Johnson & Johnson, and JPMorgan Chase. Despite this optimism, Wall Street analysts maintain a pessimistic outlook for overall S&P 500 earnings, forecasting a significant drop. Meanwhile, global markets remain cautious due to ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions.

title: David Dalvey
summary: David Dalvey, managing general partner at Brightstone Venture Capital, is recognized for his significant board service to Celcuity Inc. He played a crucial role in the biotech firm's growth, including its 2017 IPO. Dalvey's investment philosophy prioritizes people and the importance of solving significant problems, drawing on his extensive experience as an investor and board member for numerous successful startups.

title: UnitedHealth Raises Profit View as Revenue from Pharmacy Benefits Grows
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. raised its 2019 earnings forecast for the third time this year, driven by strong revenue growth in its pharmacy benefits unit and core health insurance business. The company also surpassed Wall Street profit estimates, with its shares rising in premarket trading. This positive outlook comes despite increased scrutiny on healthcare costs ahead of the 2020 U.S. presidential elections.

title: UnitedHealthcare plan faces Medicare sanction
summary: UnitedHealthcare is facing enrollment restrictions in 2020 for one of its Medicare Advantage health plan contracts due to not meeting the required 85% Medical Loss Ratio (MLR) for three consecutive years. The company attributed this non-compliance, in part, to a reduction in tax liability from federal legislation and states that current enrollees will maintain coverage and benefits. UnitedHealthcare anticipates resuming enrollment in 2021 after achieving the MLR threshold in 2019.

title: DNA Tests For Psychiatric Drugs Are Controversial But Some Insurers Are Covering Them
summary: Genetic tests aiming to match patients with psychiatric medications are gaining insurance coverage despite controversy over their efficacy. UnitedHealthcare began covering these tests, and other insurers are expected to follow, fueling a market where companies like Myriad Genetics are seeing significant sales. While some advocate for their use as an additional tool, many researchers and even the FDA express skepticism due to weak evidence and the potential for inappropriate treatment decisions.

title: ‘We’re Not As Healthy As We Should Be.’ Fitbit CEO James Park Discusses New AFib Detection Partnership With Bristol-Myers Squibb-Pfizer
summary: Fitbit CEO James Park announced a new partnership with Bristol-Myers Squibb-Pfizer Alliance to detect symptoms of atrial fibrillation (AFib) at the TIME 100 Health Summit. Park emphasized Fitbit's transformation into a "behavior-change company" to address serious health conditions and rising healthcare costs, contrasting their approach with competitors by focusing on education instead of just alerts. Fitbit is also in talks with the FDA for approval of its AFib detection software and highlights the profound impact of data from wearables on public health and cost savings.

title: Who is UnitedHealthcare?
summary: This article by Texas Dentists for Medicaid Reform (TDMR) introduces UnitedHealthcare, which is set to be awarded the third DMO contract for Texas Medicaid. It provides background on UnitedHealth Group, detailing its size, presence in Medicaid/Medicare programs across 30 states, and involvement in Texas. The article also highlights some controversies surrounding the company and presents a Harris County CHIP report card as an indicator for dentists.

title: New York Regulator Probes UnitedHealth Algorithm for Racial Bias
summary: New York's Department of Financial Services is investigating a UnitedHealth Group Inc. algorithm for potential racial bias. A study suggested the algorithm prioritized care for healthier white patients over sicker black patients. The regulator has asked UnitedHealth to demonstrate the algorithm is not discriminatory or cease its use.

title: Regulators probe racial bias with UnitedHealth algorithm
summary: New York regulators are investigating UnitedHealth Group over an algorithm researchers say exhibits racial bias, leading to poorer care for black patients. The "Impact Pro" algorithm, which helps hospitals assess patient health risks and manage care, is criticized for underestimating the health needs of black patients because it predicts healthcare costs rather than illness, and black patients historically have had less access to care. Regulators are calling on UnitedHealth to either demonstrate the algorithm is not discriminatory or cease its use.

title: UnitedHealth, an insurance giant, just scooped up patient monitoring start-up Vivify Health
summary: Optum, a division of UnitedHealth Group, has acquired Vivify Health, a patient-monitoring start-up specializing in remote patient monitoring. The acquisition allows UnitedHealth to expand its footprint in the growing market for remote health tools, which aims to reduce costly emergency room visits by intervening earlier. The terms of the deal were not disclosed, but Vivify Health had previously raised over $20 million in funding.

title: Teladoc revenues, visits rise on heels of UnitedHealth contract
summary: Teladoc Health reported a significant rise in third-quarter revenue and visits, partly driven by a contract with UnitedHealthcare. Despite the revenue growth, the company experienced a net loss for the quarter. Analysts remain optimistic about Teladoc's future due to its diversified platform, new service launches, and increased flexibility for telehealth benefits in Medicare Advantage plans.

title: Optum Acquires Remote Patient Monitoring Company Vivify Health
summary: Optum, a division of UnitedHealth Group, has acquired Vivify Health, a remote patient monitoring company based in Plano, TX. Vivify Health provides a cloud-based, device-agnostic platform for holistic remote care management, serving large health systems and organizations. The terms of the acquisition were not disclosed, and Vivify Health had previously raised $23.4M in funding.

title: Health Insurance Market Competition Landscape and Demands Till 2025: ICICI Lombard, Aviva, AXA, Zurich Insurance Group Ltd., International Medical Group, UnitedHealth Group Inc., Bupa, Blue Cross, Liberty International Insurance, AIG, MetLife & More
summary: This article analyzes the global health insurance market, projecting significant growth from 2018 to 2025 due to strategies like new product launches and expansions by major players. It highlights key market drivers such as increasing surgical procedures and a rising geriatric population, along with restraints like high costs. The report also identifies major market segments, types of coverage, providers, plans, and key geographic regions and companies involved.

title: Optum CEO Andrew Witty named UnitedHealth Group president
summary: Sir Andrew Witty, currently the CEO of Optum, has been appointed president of UnitedHealth Group Inc. He will continue to serve in his role as Optum CEO. The announcement was made by the company on a Monday morning.

title: Why Anthem Stock Climbed 12.1% in October
summary: Anthem's stock rose 12.1% in October due to better-than-expected earnings and guidance, influenced by strong reports from rival UnitedHealth and its own positive third-quarter results. The company reported increased sales, EPS, membership growth, and higher premiums, along with positive guidance for full-year EPS, which helped alleviate investor concerns about "Medicare for all" plans.

title: UnitedHealth Group names Optum CEO as president
summary: UnitedHealth Group has appointed Andrew Witty, CEO of its Optum division, as president of the parent company. Witty will continue his role at Optum while overseeing enterprise business strategy, a move aimed at accelerating innovation and growth for the company's health system development. David Wichmann remains the chief executive of UnitedHealth Group.

title: UnitedHealth's move to new $35M De Pere office would retain jobs, create new opportunity in Howard
summary: UnitedHealth Group is planning a $35 million move to a new office building in De Pere, which aims to provide a more modern and right-sized workspace for its Brown County workforce of over 1,000 employees. The move is supported by approximately $4 million in city assistance from De Pere, including land purchase rebates, property tax rebates, and road improvements. This relocation will also create a new commercial opportunity for UnitedHealth's existing five-story headquarters building in Howard.

title: Market rotation persists, Russell 2000 tags 52-week high
summary: U.S. stocks are higher early Monday, driven by trade-related optimism and marking the beginning of a holiday-shortened week. The S&P 500 reached a new record high, while the Russell 2000 Index achieved a 52-week high, indicating rotational price action in the market. Financials are approaching a 12-year peak.

title: Alexa can remind you to take your medication
summary: Amazon's Alexa has launched new features allowing select customers to set medication reminders and request prescription refills through voice commands, in partnership with Omnicell and Giant Eagle Pharmacy. This initiative aims to simplify medication management at home while prioritizing user privacy and security through voice profiles and personal passcodes. Amazon plans to expand these features to more pharmacies in the future, highlighting the ongoing innovation in voice technology for healthcare.

title: UnitedHealth Group: 2020 Revenues To Eclipse $260B
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced that its 2020 revenues are projected to surpass $260 billion, an increase of about 9% from the previous year. The company, through its UnitedHealthcare and Optum units, is expanding its health insurance and medical care provider businesses. This outlook reinforces its position as a key industry bellwether, with rivals also actively expanding their healthcare provision.

title: UnitedHealth & AXA remain world’s largest insurers by NPW
summary: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated and AXA maintained their positions as the world's largest insurers by net premiums written (NPW) in 2018. While several Japanese insurers dropped out of the top 25, companies like Ping An Insurance, Kaiser Foundation Group of Health Plans, Liberty Mutual, MetLife, and Healthcare Services Corp saw significant movement or new entry into the list. The article also highlights the ranking by non-banking assets, where AXA overtook Allianz.

title: UnitedHealth projects major revenue boost in 2020 on the back of continued Optum growth
summary: UnitedHealth Group projects significant revenue growth in 2020, estimating between $260 billion and $262 billion, driven largely by its Optum division. Optum, which provides pharmacy benefit management and care services, is expected to continue its double-digit growth and contribute over half of the company's after-tax operating earnings. UnitedHealth also aims to improve its Medicare Advantage business, particularly by leveraging OptumCare's presence.

title: David Tepper Trims UnitedHealth, Exits Intelsat
summary: David Tepper, head of Appaloosa Management, made several adjustments to his firm's portfolio during the third quarter of 2019. Notable moves include significantly trimming holdings in UnitedHealth Group and Humana, and completely exiting positions in Intelsat and Centene Corp. Tepper also reduced stakes in SPDR S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production ETF, Mr. Cooper Group, and Clearway Energy.

title: Anthem Data Breach, Ross Class Action Settlements Paying Out
summary: Top Class Actions viewers are reportedly receiving payments from two class action settlements: an Anthem data breach settlement and a Ross "compare at" pricing settlement. The Anthem settlement, valued at $115 million, addresses a 2015 data breach that compromised the personal information of 79 million individuals, with Class Members receiving checks for out-of-pocket losses. The Ross settlement, for $4.85 million, compensates customers who were allegedly misled by deceptive "compare at" pricing, with gift cards being distributed.

title: UnitedHealth Group touts Optum effect on its corporate growth
summary: UnitedHealth Group is projecting significant revenue growth for the coming year, largely driven by its Optum division for health care services, including pharmacies and clinics. While the core health insurance business faces some challenges like stagnant enrollment and weak performance in certain markets, Optum's strong growth is expected to contribute over 50% of the company's earnings in 2020. The company revealed financial forecasts for 2019 and 2020, projecting revenue of $242 billion for 2019 and $260 billion to $262 billion for 2020, with corresponding adjusted net earnings per share.

title: UnitedHealth's Witty describes Optum's ambitions for 'seamless' consumer health experience
summary: Optum, a division of UnitedHealth, aims to create a "seamless" healthcare experience for consumers at the local level by leveraging its vast care services and technology infrastructure. The company is building a digital platform to connect directly with patients and providers, rolling out this experience city by city. Optum expects to be a major driver of UnitedHealth's growth, contributing significantly to its operating earnings.

title: UnitedHealth Group to acquire specialty pharmacy Diplomat in $300M deal
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced its acquisition of Diplomat, a specialty pharmacy and infusion services provider, for $300 million or $4 per share. Diplomat will be integrated into OptumRx, Optum’s pharmacy services division. This acquisition aims to improve health outcomes and lower care costs, expanding OptumRx's innovative specialty pharmacy and infusion solutions.

title: Progressive: Report on Political Spending Related to Company Values and Policies
summary: Shareholders are requesting The Progressive Corporation issue a public report detailing risks and costs associated with state policies affecting reproductive rights, and strategies to mitigate these risks. This request stems from concerns about the impact of such policies on employee hiring, retention, productivity, and the company's brand, especially given Progressive's stated commitment to diversity and inclusion. The resolution, filed by As You Sow, recommends the report evaluate impacts on employees and brand risks, and include public policy advocacy and human resource strategies.

title: UnitedHealth Group paying $300 million for specialty pharmacy
summary: UnitedHealth Group's Optum unit is acquiring Diplomat Pharmacy, a Michigan-based specialty pharmacy business, for approximately $300 million plus assumed debt. The deal, valued at about $540 million including debt, is set to expand OptumRx's services, particularly in specialty pharmacy and infusion. Analysts noted that while Diplomat struggled with its PBM business, the acquisition is seen as a strategic and financial positive for UnitedHealth Group.

title: Omada Health Selected for Express Scripts Industry-First Digital Health Formulary
summary: Omada Health announced that its digital care programs for Diabetes Prevention, Type 2 Diabetes, and Hypertension will be included on the Express Scripts Digital Health Formulary starting in early 2020. This inclusion, which followed a rigorous four-stage selection process, will make Omada's personalized, human-led care experiences available to Express Scripts clients, including employers and group health plans. Omada expects this partnership to provide tens of millions of individuals across the country with access to their chronic disease programs, reinforcing the shift towards digital care in healthcare.

title: Cigna Will Sell Non-Medical Insurance Unit To New York Life For $6.3 Billion
summary: Cigna announced it would sell its group life and disability insurance unit to New York Life Insurance for $6.3 billion to better focus on its healthcare businesses. The proceeds from the sale will be used to increase Cigna's share repurchase authority by $3 billion and pay down debt from its acquisition of Express Scripts. New York Life sees the acquisition as an opportunity to add millions of new policyholders.

title: Will you be covered?
summary: Cigna insurance customers, including Seacoast educators and University System of New Hampshire employees, may lose in-network coverage at Portsmouth Regional Hospital and HCA Healthcare services starting February 1st due to an ongoing dispute over rates. Both parties express hope for a resolution, but unions are concerned about the potential impact on their members, highlighting cases like a high-risk pregnancy patient unsure if she can deliver at her hospital.

title: FedEx Earns No. 14 Spot on the FORTUNE World’s Most Admired Companies List
summary: FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) has been named the No. 14 most admired company in the world by FORTUNE magazine, marking its 20th consecutive year on the list. The company tied with American Express and Netflix and was the only company in the Delivery category to rank in the Top 20. This recognition highlights FedEx's strong financial performance and corporate reputation, attributed to its 490,000 team members globally.

title: The World Congress 8th Annual Patient Congress
summary: The 8th Annual World Congress Patient Congress, scheduled for April 6-7, 2020, in Philadelphia, focuses on improving patient access and health outcomes. The event features multiple tracks, including Patient Adherence and Engagement, Patient Advocacy, and a Copay Summit, with speakers from prominent healthcare organizations. Drug Channels readers can receive a discount by registering with a special promo code by March 31, 2020.

title: Encompass Health’s 2020 M&A Strategy Leans Towards Hospice
summary: Encompass Health (NYSE: EHC) plans to focus its 2020 M&A strategy on larger acquisitions in the home health and hospice space, with a particular emphasis on hospice due to disruptions in home health caused by the Patient Driven Groupings Model (PDGM). The company anticipates targeting private equity-backed firms despite high industry multiples, aiming to invest $50 million to $100 million in growth opportunities. This strategy follows a successful 2019 acquisition of Alacare Home Health & Hospice, which significantly boosted its hospice admissions and segment growth.

title: UnitedHealth is making more money from things that have nothing to do with health insurance
summary: UnitedHealth Group, primarily known as a health insurance carrier, is increasingly generating profit from its Optum subsidiaries, which focus on services outside traditional health insurance. In Q4 2019, Optum's profit surpassed UnitedHealthcare's, largely driven by OptumRx and other healthcare services like physician practices and urgent care clinics. This shift indicates UnitedHealth's strategy to become a broader healthcare provider beyond just insurance.

title: Publicly traded health insurers' revenue nears $1 trillion mark
summary: Publicly traded health insurers are approaching a significant financial milestone, with their total revenue nearing $1 trillion. This figure highlights the substantial economic scale and growth within the health insurance sector.

title: Subi Sethi Joins Clearwater as Chief Client Officer
summary: Clearwater Analytics announced that Subi Sethi has joined the company as Chief Client Officer, responsible for leading the firm’s global operations team. Sethi brings extensive experience in driving operational transformation and will oversee Global Delivery, Data, Reconciliation, Client Services, and Strategic Account Management teams. Her focus will include uniting and creating efficiencies across Clearwater's international offices to strengthen global servicing capabilities.

title: Checkup for $30, Teeth Cleaning $25: Walmart Gets Into Health Care
summary: Walmart is entering the healthcare market by offering low-cost medical services such as $30 checkups and $25 teeth cleanings in its new Walmart Health centers. This initiative aims to capture a share of the $3.6 trillion health spending by leveraging its large customer base and providing accessible care, even for those without insurance. The retail giant's move positions it as a competitor to existing healthcare providers like CVS and Amazon in communities nationwide.

title: American Express, Dow Inc. share losses contribute to Dow's nearly 850-point fall
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average is experiencing a significant decline, largely due to losses in American Express and Dow Inc. shares. American Express shares are down 5.6% and Dow Inc. shares are down 5.4%, contributing substantially to the index's nearly 850-point intraday fall. Other companies like Visa, UnitedHealth, and United Technologies are also adding to the market downturn.

title: Why Apple and Johnson & Johnson's new heart study is a big deal for digital health
summary: Apple and Johnson & Johnson are partnering on a large-scale study to determine if the Apple Watch can detect atrial fibrillation in seniors, making it one of the largest randomized digital health trials ever. The study involves a unique collaboration between a tech company, a pharma giant, and a retailer (Best Buy), aiming to provide subsidized Apple Watches to 150,000 participants and address cardiologists' concerns about broad-based screening by focusing on a high-risk demographic. If successful, the initiative could lead to private Medicare plans covering Apple Watches and advance the concept of "aging in place" through digital health solutions.

title: Needy Patients ‘Caught In The Middle’ As Insurance Titan Drops Doctors
summary: UnitedHealthcare is dropping hundreds of doctors from its New Jersey Medicaid network, forcing thousands of low-income patients to find new physicians. Doctors allege that UnitedHealthcare is attempting to steer patients toward Riverside Medical Group, which is owned by its sister company, Optum, both subsidiaries of UnitedHealth Group. This move highlights concerns about "vertical consolidation" in healthcare and its impact on patient-doctor relationships and healthcare costs.

title: Change Healthcare Inc. Announces the Completion of Split-Off of McKesson’s Ownership Interest
summary: Change Healthcare Inc. announced the successful completion of McKesson Corporation's disposition of its ownership interest in Change Healthcare. This transaction involved an exchange offer where McKesson stockholders received Change Healthcare shares, making Change Healthcare an independent market leader. The company's CEO, Neil de Crescenzo, highlighted their established platform, innovation engine, and strong customer relationships position for future growth.

title: Opinion: As Bernie Sanders is essentially finished, health-care stocks are screaming buys
summary: This opinion piece argues that healthcare stocks have become "screaming buys" due to Bernie Sanders's diminishing chances of winning the presidency, which removes the threat of "Medicare for All." Despite concerns about the U.S. healthcare system's preparedness for COVID-19 and a recent drop in healthcare stock prices, investors are advised to consider these stocks given the changed political landscape. The article suggests that Joe Biden's looming victory eliminates a major political risk for the sector.

title: Furloughed vs Laid Off: Advantages, Disadvantages, and Differences
summary: This article explains the differences between furloughs and layoffs, their implications for employees and employers, especially concerning pay, benefits, and unemployment eligibility during economic downturns like the COVID-19 pandemic. It details how each affects hourly versus salaried staff, PTO, and healthcare continuation, including ACA and COBRA considerations. The piece also outlines the critical rule that furloughed employees cannot perform any work during their time off.

title: UnitedHealth Group Accelerates Nearly $2 Billion in Payments and Support to Health Care Providers to Help with COVID-19 Financial Challenges
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced it is accelerating nearly $2 billion in payments and financial support to health care providers in the U.S. to help address the financial pressures caused by the COVID-19 emergency. This initiative includes accelerating claim payments and providing up to $125 million in small business loans to clinical operators. The move aims to allow care providers to focus on delivering essential care during the pandemic.

title: Lawsuits accuse United, Cigna of underpaying for behavioral health claims
summary: Four class-action lawsuits have been filed against United Behavioral Health and Cigna Behavioral Health, accusing them of underpaying providers for mental health services. The lawsuits allege that the insurers used a third-party vendor, Viant, to negotiate dramatically reduced reimbursements, leading to significant balance bills for patients and breach of contract for providers. Patients and providers are seeking justice in federal courts, claiming that regulators have ignored their complaints about these unethical practices.

title: Draganfly Selected to Develop “Pandemic Drone”
summary: Draganfly has been selected to develop a "pandemic drone" in response to the COVID-19 crisis, designed to detect infectious and respiratory conditions in groups of people. Working with Vital Intelligence Inc. and the University of South Australia, the drone will utilize various sensors and AI to monitor heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, sneezing, coughing, and fever, while also measuring social distancing. The initial deployment is planned for U.S. "hot zones" like New York, with potential future applications in public safety and workplace monitoring.

title: HCA profit down 45% amid COVID-19 volume depression
summary: HCA Healthcare reported a nearly 45% drop in first-quarter 2020 profit to $581 million, missing Wall Street expectations, due to significantly lower patient volumes caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The company withdrew its 2020 guidance and adjusted its capital allocation strategy, including suspending share repurchases and dividends, while also developing a reboot and recovery plan. Despite the financial headwinds, HCA has avoided layoffs by redeploying staff and implementing a special pandemic pay program, with senior leadership taking pay cuts.

title: $350,000 on Hand Sanitizer: How Werner is Responding to the COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: Werner Enterprises has spent over $350,000 on hand sanitizer and implemented comprehensive measures to protect its drivers and employees during the COVID-19 pandemic. CEO Derek Leathers emphasizes compassion and data-driven decisions, drawing on the company's existing pandemic plan and emergency response experience. Werner has adapted to significant disruptions in supply chains, with executives taking salary reductions while supporting drivers with pay if impacted by the virus.

title: CEO Pay Watch: UnitedHealth's David Wichmann made more than $52 million last year
summary: UnitedHealth Group CEO David Wichmann earned over $52 million in 2019, while former CEO Stephen Hemsley also made over $50 million, primarily from exercised stock options and vested restricted stock. Their compensation was largely due to long-term equity awards granted in previous years. Despite the COVID-19 economic downturn, UnitedHealth executives have not taken salary cuts, and the company has raised pay for some employees and implemented COVID-19 related benefits.

title: Report: Optum in talks to buy virtual therapy provider for $470 million
summary: Optum, a unit of UnitedHealth Group Inc., is reportedly in discussions to acquire AbleTo, a New York-based virtual mental health services provider. The potential deal is valued at approximately $470 million. This acquisition would expand Optum's presence in the virtual therapy market.

title: Molina To Buy Magellan Medicaid And Medicare Plans For $820 Million
summary: Molina Healthcare announced its agreement to acquire Magellan Complete Care from Magellan Health for $820 million. This acquisition will expand Molina's Medicaid and Medicare government health benefits into new markets across six states, including Arizona, Massachusetts, and Virginia. The deal is expected to increase Molina's member base to over 3.6 million in 18 states and project pro-forma revenues exceeding $20 billion in 2020.

title: MiMedx Provides Update on Payment Protection Program Loan
summary: MiMedx Group, Inc. announced its decision to repay in full the Payment Protection Program (PPP) Loan received through the federal relief effort. The company previously utilized these funds to maintain full employment amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, which had negatively impacted its sales due to restricted access and canceled surgeries. MiMedx had also implemented cost-containment measures, including temporary salary reductions, to avoid layoffs.

title: Senior-Housing Communities Face Higher Vacancy Rates Amid Coronavirus
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic and the "aging-at-home movement" are leading to higher vacancy rates in senior-housing communities. Increased use of telemedicine is also contributing to seniors delaying or choosing not to move into such facilities, exacerbating a pre-pandemic supply glut. Senior-housing companies like Ventas Inc., Welltower Inc., and Healthpeak Properties Inc. have reported declines in occupancy and revenue, with stock values falling significantly.

title: Kimberly Salmon to lead Hanover Insurance Group Foundation
summary: Kimberly Salmon has been appointed as the assistant vice president of community relations at The Hanover Insurance Group, where she will lead the Hanover Insurance Group Foundation and community relations functions. Previously, Salmon served as the director of community relations and engagement at Fallon Health. In her new role, she will also be responsible for employee engagement and volunteerism.

title: UnitedHealth, Microsoft build app to guard their offices from Covid-19 (and maybe yours, too)
summary: UnitedHealth and Microsoft have partnered to develop an app called ProtectWell aimed at screening employees for COVID-19 symptoms or exposure. The app utilizes UnitedHealth's clinical and data analytics capabilities along with Microsoft's AI-powered healthcare bot. It is designed to help companies reopen their offices safely during the pandemic.

title: Hershey Company pledges to end deforestation as part of its supply chain
summary: The Hershey Company has committed to ending deforestation in its global cocoa supply chain by stopping new deforestation and promoting agroforestry. This initiative involves not sourcing cocoa from areas with recent deforestation and implementing tree planting programs. Hershey will work with organizations like the World Cocoa Foundation and plans to release a comprehensive forestry plan by the end of 2018 to achieve its goals.

title: Omada Health acquires remote physical therapy company
summary: Omada Health has acquired Physera Health, a remote physical therapy company, for a reported $30 million, adding musculoskeletal care to its existing digital health platforms for diabetes, hypertension, and behavioral health. This acquisition, fueled by $57 million in new funding, expands Omada's integrated care offerings to address the increased demand for online healthcare during the Covid-19 pandemic. Both companies target employers and individuals, with Physera aiming to reduce unnecessary imaging and surgery costs for its clients.

title: Optum scoops up post-acute care company NaviHealth
summary: UnitedHealth Group's Optum has acquired NaviHealth, a company specializing in post-acute care management services. While terms were not disclosed by Optum, sources indicate the deal is valued at approximately $2.5 billion. NaviHealth will operate as a standalone entity aligned with OptumHealth, retaining its current leadership.

title: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) Dividend Stock Analysis
summary: This article provides a dividend stock analysis of UnitedHealth Group (UNH), highlighting its consistent dividend growth over 11 years and its recent 15.70% dividend increase. It discusses UNH's business model, risk factors including potential healthcare model disruption, and its financial performance with strong EPS growth and share repurchase programs. The author also notes UNH's attractive valuation based on forward earnings and dividend yield.

title: UnitedHealth Group Increases Housing Investments To $500M To Address Social Determinants
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced an increase in its investments in affordable housing to $500 million to tackle social determinants of health. This move highlights insurers' growing focus on reducing healthcare costs and improving outcomes beyond traditional medical treatments by addressing issues like housing insecurity. The investment includes $100 million for the Health & Housing Fund, aiming to create over 1,000 new homes and provide on-site health-related services for residents.

title: UnitedHealth Group Invests Another $100M in Affordable Housing
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced an additional $100 million investment in affordable housing, increasing its total commitment to $500 million since 2011. This new investment will fund projects across the U.S. through a partnership with Health & Housing Fund, SAHF, and NAHT, aiming to improve health outcomes through quality housing. The company has previously helped fund 80 affordable housing projects, providing 4,500 homes in 18 states.

title: Aetna’s Denial of ConforMIS Implants Results in Suit
summary: ConforMIS, Inc. and a patient have sued Aetna, Inc. and Aetna Life Insurance Company for wrongfully denying claims for customized total knee implants. They allege Aetna changed its policy in 2018 to categorize these implants as "experimental and investigational" despite FDA clearance and prior coverage. Plaintiffs cite approval from other organizations and Aetna's own prior approval to support their claim that the ConforMIS System is neither experimental nor investigational.

title: Hospices Contend with COVID Relief Funding Questions
summary: Many hospice providers received unsolicited federal relief funding through the CARES Act, leading to uncertainty regarding legal rules and restrictions for its use. Organizations are questioning whether to accept the funds and how to properly allocate them to COVID-19 related expenses as federal guidance remains unclear. Larger hospice companies are debating returning funds to avoid potential risks, while others segregate the money pending further clarification.

title: UnitedHealth Group Invests $100 Million More in Affordable Housing
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced an additional $100 million investment in affordable housing, reaffirming its commitment to addressing the social determinants of health. This investment aims to increase access to safe and stable housing, which is a critical factor influencing overall health outcomes. The initiative expands on the company's existing efforts to support community health and well-being through strategic investments.

title: Tim Herbert
summary: This article profiles Tim Herbert, President/CEO of Inspire Medical Systems Inc. It highlights his leadership since Inspire's spin-off from Medtronic in 2007, the company's IPO in 2018 (NYSE: INSP), and its growth in revenue, despite a net loss in 2018. A significant development mentioned is UnitedHealthcare's decision to cover Inspire's therapy.

title: New Research From Fidelity and Business Group on Health Finds 95% of Employers Now Include Emotional and Mental Health Programs in Well-Being Platforms
summary: New research from Fidelity Investments and Business Group on Health indicates that 95% of employers now incorporate emotional and mental health programs into their corporate well-being platforms, a trend accelerated by the global pandemic. The 11th annual Health and Well-Being Survey also found that the average budget for well-being programs increased by 36% to $4.9 million in 2020, with continued emphasis on work/life balance and financial incentives. These findings, though partially collected before the pandemic, highlight the growing importance of mental health support in the workplace.

title: Hormel opens health center for team members
summary: Hormel Foods Corporation is opening a health center in Austin, Minn., in partnership with Premise Health, to provide high-quality, affordable healthcare to its team members and their families. The center will offer services like primary care, physical therapy, and lab services, building on Hormel's existing relationship with the Mayo Clinic for specialist referrals. This initiative aims to serve approximately 4,700 eligible individuals, reflecting Hormel's commitment to employee well-being.

title: Helping patients where they are: An interview with the president of CVS Caremark
summary: Alan Lotvin, president of CVS Caremark, discusses the impact of COVID-19 on the US healthcare system and strategies for improvement, including a shift to in-home care models. He highlights CVS Caremark's adaptation during the pandemic, the need for flexible healthcare capacity, and addresses healthcare disparities. Lotvin expresses hope for a rapid vaccine development and resolution of access inequalities.

title: UnitedHealthcare adds coverage of Tandem insulin pumps
summary: UnitedHealthcare has expanded its coverage to include insulin pumps from Tandem Diabetes for members across various plans, leading to a 12% stock increase for Tandem. This decision marks a shift from UnitedHealthcare's previous preferred provider agreement with Medtronic, providing greater patient choice for diabetes technology, although Tandem's pumps may still require pre-authorization while Medtronic's do not. The move addresses calls from the diabetes community for broader access to different devices and is seen as a significant win for patient autonomy.

title: The Top 15 U.S. Pharmacies of 2019: Specialty Drugs Drive the Industry’s Evolution (rerun)
summary: This article analyzes the top 15 U.S. pharmacies in 2019, revealing that specialty drugs and vertical integration significantly influenced market share. Prescription dispensing revenues reached a record $446 billion, with the top seven pharmacies accounting for about 70%. The report highlights the growing role of mail and specialty pharmacies operated by PBMs, which derived over half of their gross profits from these activities.

title: Walmart jumps into health insurance market, including Medicare
summary: Walmart is entering the health insurance market, including Medicare policies, confirmed by job postings for Medicare sales managers and insurance agents. This move follows the retailer's expansion in healthcare, including its Care Clinics and the recent acquisition of the medication management tech platform CareZone. Analysts suggest Walmart's extensive reach and competitive pricing on basic healthcare services could significantly impact the market and increase competition, especially for Medicare plans.

title: Diageo announces creation of paper-based bottle for Johnnie Walker
summary: Diageo announced the creation of a 100 percent plastic-free, paper-based spirits bottle made from sustainably sourced wood, set to debut with Johnnie Walker in early 2021. This initiative is part of a new partnership with Pilot Lite to launch Pulpex Ltd., a sustainable packaging technology company. Pulpex Ltd. has also formed a consortium with companies like Unilever and PepsiCo, aiming to launch branded paper bottles in 2021 that are fully recyclable and meet food-safe standards.

title: Aparna Abburi To Lead Growth Of Cigna Medicare Advantage Business
summary: Aparna Abburi has been appointed president of Cigna's Medicare Advantage (MA) business, tasked with spearheading aggressive growth in key markets and through product diversity. Her extensive industry experience, including her previous role as president of Medicare business at Health Care Services Corporation, is expected to accelerate Cigna's expansion goals for its MA business. Cigna aims for 10 percent to 15 percent annual customer growth in its MA segment, building on its largest expansion to date last year.

title: GoHealth nabs blockbuster IPO raising $914M
summary: GoHealth, a Medicare-focused health insurance marketplace, successfully completed its initial public offering, raising $914 million and seeing its shares jump 23% on its first day of trading. This makes it the largest healthcare IPO of 2020 so far, with the company planning to use the new funds to hire more licensed insurance agents and expand its services. Co-founder Brandon Cruz expressed both relief and stress, noting the company's 20-year history and mission to improve access to healthcare.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Bill Ackman, Ray Dalio, Chris Rokos, Kyle Bass, Guess?, Inc. (GES), UnitedHealth Group Inc (UNH), and More
summary: This article covers various hedge fund and insider trading news including Bill Ackman's $4 billion blank-check IPO, Chris Rokos calling staff back to the office, Kyle Bass's bullish outlook on Bitcoin, gold, and silver, and details about a trade secrets battle involving Ray Dalio's Bridgewater. It also discusses academic vindication for Wall Street's hedge fund obsession and the surge in hedge fund assets in Q2 2020.

title: Three Accomplished Women Join Santa Clara’s Board of Trustees - July 2020 - News & Events
summary: Santa Clara University announced the addition of three accomplished women leaders to its Board of Trustees: Kathleen Duncan, Molly Joseph '96, and Gisel Ruiz '92. These new trustees bring diverse experience from non-profits, healthcare, and retail, enriching the university's strategic guidance during a crucial time. Their appointments are expected to significantly benefit the 169-year-old Jesuit institution as it navigates current challenges and strives to uphold its mission.

title: Employers Rank Cigna Highest, UnitedHealthcare Lowest for Driving Health Care Quality in A New Survey of Employee Benefits Executives
summary: A new survey by The Leapfrog Group found that employers ranked Cigna highest and UnitedHealthcare lowest for driving health care quality. Overall, employers gave health plans a "C" for effectiveness, indicating a general dissatisfaction with their efforts to improve quality and reduce costs. The survey highlights a call for health plans to be more responsive to employer demands for improvements in health care quality and cost-effectiveness.

title: Unilever expects income tax dept questions on Horlicks deal tax math from GlaxoSmithKline Plc
summary: Unilever anticipates questions from India's tax department regarding the tax-deductible amount following its acquisition of Horlicks from GlaxoSmithKline Plc. The company expects approximately ₹11,200 crore (₹1.3 billion) of goodwill to be tax-deductible, believing it has a strong legal basis for this claim despite expected challenges. This acquisition, which also involved HUL separately acquiring the Horlicks brand for ₹3,045 crore to save on royalty costs, concluded in April of the current year.

title: Humana Buys $100 Million Stake In Doctor House Call Company, Heal
summary: Humana is investing $100 million in Heal, an in-home primary care company that specializes in doctor house calls and telemedicine. This partnership aims to expand value-based primary care services to seniors in Humana's Medicare Advantage plans across new markets. The investment reinforces Humana's strategy to focus on home-based care as a key growth driver, particularly within its Medicare Advantage business.

title: Major U.S. Health Insurers Report Big Profits, Benefiting From the Pandemic (Published 2020)
summary: Major U.S. health insurers like Anthem, UnitedHealth, and Humana reported significantly higher second-quarter profits in 2020, in some cases doubling their earnings from the previous year. This surge in profits is attributed to a reduction in medical claims due to the postponement of elective surgeries and fewer doctor visits during the pandemic. Regulations under the Affordable Care Act may require some of these earnings to be returned to consumers as rebates, and the Trump administration has urged insurers to consider speeding up these refunds or reducing premiums.

title: The guidebook for resilient animal agriculture
summary: The Environmental Defense Fund (EDF) has released a "Guidebook for Resilient Animal Agriculture" to help companies in the animal agriculture sector address the impacts of climate change and the global pandemic. The guidebook offers a roadmap for building resilient and sustainable supply chains. It provides step-by-step guidance for setting sustainability goals, implementing solutions, and measuring progress.

title: Smarter Health Care Deductibles Are a Win-Win for Employers and Employees
summary: This article argues that employers can save money on health benefits without burdening employees by implementing "smarter deductibles." It suggests focusing on chronic conditions by adopting value-based insurance design (VBID) to reduce or eliminate patient cost-sharing for high-value services, and also reducing low-value care. The piece highlights that strategies like those used by Eli Lilly, combining high-deductible health plans with VBID concepts, have led to slower healthcare cost increases.

title: Humira Maker to Settle California Lawsuit for $24 Million
summary: AbbVie Inc., the maker of Humira, has agreed to pay $24 million to settle a California lawsuit alleging it violated an insurance fraud law. The lawsuit, filed in 2018, claimed AbbVie offered unlawful perks to doctors and used nurses as "ambassadors" to persuade them to prescribe Humira without proper disclosure. As part of the settlement, AbbVie will reform its marketing practices, though it continues to deny wrongdoing.

title: Prices on Georgia’s insurance exchange shaping up to stay fairly stable
summary: Prices on Georgia's health insurance exchange for 2021 are projected to remain fairly stable, with moderate increases and some premium cuts, in contrast to previous years' spikes. All six current insurers are returning, and the average premium increase is 6.53 percent, which is lower than expected given the COVID-19 pandemic.
