Insurers have seen increased profits during the pandemic as many people postponed medical procedures, although job losses due to COVID-19 may lead more Georgians to seek coverage through the exchange or face being uninsured.

title: Humana sues Trump administration over ACA cost-sharing reduction payments
summary: Humana has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration to recover nearly $2 million in Affordable Care Act (ACA) cost-sharing reduction payments that were eliminated in late 2017. The insurer claims it suffered significant financial losses because it was legally required to provide cost-sharing reductions to eligible insureds despite not receiving the promised government reimbursements. This action follows the position of other insurers who also sued to recover these payments, which Humana argues caused instability in insurance markets.

title: EY and Procter & Gamble team up on supply chain offering
summary: EY and Procter & Gamble (P&G) have broadened their alliance to offer supply chain expertise, combining their strengths to help businesses navigate challenges, particularly those exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic. This collaboration will address various supply chain processes, including strategy, planning, and distribution, leveraging advanced tools and joint teams. P&G, recognized for its leading supply chain operations, aims to share its successful methodologies with clients through EY to enhance responsiveness, productivity, and cost savings.

title: Inspire Medical Systems, Inc. Announces Two Additional Coverage Policies from Blue Cross Blue Shield Healthcare Plans
summary: Inspire Medical Systems, Inc. announced that two more Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS) plans, Florida Blue and BCBS Minnesota, will now cover its Inspire therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. This addition brings the total number of BCBS plans covering Inspire therapy to 31, and the total number of commercial coverage policies to 58, representing over 190 million lives. The company also noted that Inspire therapy has Medicare coverage nationwide, increasing access for patients and physicians.

title: Why it’s taken Quest so long to clear its COVID-19 testing backlog
summary: Quest Diagnostics experienced significant delays in COVID-19 test turnaround times during July, lagging behind its rival LabCorp. The article attributes these delays to several factors, including Quest's substantial presence in early COVID-19 hotspots like Florida, its large number of hospital clients requiring priority testing, and supply chain constraints for testing platforms and reagents. While Quest has since improved its turnaround times through increased capacity and sample pooling, its credibility was temporarily questioned by a CNN report regarding discrepancies in reported wait times.

title: Ransomware Attack Impacts Medical Debt Collections Firm R1 RCM
summary: Medical debt collections firm R1 RCM systems were taken down due to a ransomware attack, impacting sensitive patient data. This incident is part of a larger trend of cyberattacks on healthcare organizations, including email hacks and data breaches affecting COVID-19 patient information. The article highlights other security incidents and the rising threat of ransomware that posts stolen data online.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s CDO On The Key Success Factors For Chief Data Officers
summary: Fawad Butt, Chief Data Officer of UnitedHealth Group & Optum, discusses the evolving role of the CDO, emphasizing the shift from "data janitors" to delivery-focused leaders responsible for products and platforms. He outlines key success factors for CDOs, including establishing a clear data strategy tied to business objectives, developing a robust data organization with lifecycle management, and effectively balancing centralized and federated data approaches. Butt also identifies common pitfalls such as poor change management, lack of leadership support, and low data literacy within organizations.

title: North Texas Group Offers Virtual Training To Help Prevent Suicide
summary: A North Texas group, the Jordan Elizabeth Harris Foundation, is providing virtual training to equip people with the skills to intervene in a suicide crisis. The training, based on the QPR (question, persuade, refer) method, is free and available to adults and children aged 10 and older. This initiative comes as more Americans report thoughts of self-harm amid ongoing social distancing measures.

title: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock saw a modest gain of 0.92% on a strong trading day, closing at $311.67. This performance outpaced the broader market, with both the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average posting increases. The company's stock, however, remained below its 52-week high, and its performance relative to competitors like Anthem Inc., Humana Inc., and Centene Corp. was mixed.

title: Activist sets sights on another health-care company with break-up potential
summary: Activist investor Engaged Capital has targeted Evolent Health Inc. (EVH), acquiring a 9.99% stake with the aim of unlocking intrinsic value. Engaged Capital intends to push Evolent Health to divest its underperforming True Health segment and focus on its profitable services business. This strategy could lead to a sale of the entire company, with Engaged Capital prepared to nominate directors if constructive engagement fails.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Maven nabs former WeWork exec; Geisinger Health Plan hires ex-Humana leader
summary: This "Chutes & Ladders" column details recent executive hires and appointments across the healthcare industry. Key moves include Maven hiring former WeWork executive Michael Kopelman as CFO and Sonia Millsom as CCO, Geisinger Health Plan appointing ex-Humana leader Mark McCullough as CFO and COO, and Cerner naming William Mintz as Chief Strategy Officer. The article also touches on appointments at Anthem Inc. and Centene Corp.

title: Apple stock drop makes history with $179B loss
summary: Apple experienced the largest single-day market cap drop for a U.S. listed company, losing over $179.92 billion (8%) in value on Thursday. This significant decline followed a period where Apple had recently become the first U.S. company to reach a $2 trillion valuation. Despite the drop, its market cap remains at the $2 trillion level, and analysts largely maintain a "strong buy" rating as the company prepares to release a 5G iPhone.

title: World-Champion Gymnast Aly Raisman Partners with Sanvello to Advance Mental Health Solutions
summary: World-champion gymnast Aly Raisman has partnered with Sanvello, a digital mental health care provider and a UnitedHealth Group company, to advance mental health solutions. This partnership coincides with Sanvello's launch of new mental health coaching services and an expanded therapy offering. Raisman, an active user of Sanvello, will help promote mental health care and contribute to developing new services, leveraging her personal experience.

title: An Exclusive Interview with Renowned Health Coach Stephon Clinkscales
summary: This article features an interview with health coach Stephon Clinkscales, who discusses his approach to physical and mental well-being. He emphasizes the importance of discipline and hard work in achieving fitness goals, and how physical health positively impacts mental health and self-confidence. Clinkscales also addresses the challenges men face today regarding mental health and masculinity, stressing that valuing oneself physically leads to valuing others.

title: Walmart pharmacy ready to give flu shots
summary: Walmart has launched a new digital scheduler for customers to book flu vaccine appointments at its 4,700 pharmacies and is offering free flu shots to its 1.5 million employees. The retail giant is implementing several initiatives, including in-store flu shot events and online scheduling to make vaccination accessible and efficient while adhering to COVID-19 safety protocols. These efforts are part of Walmart's broader focus on community healthcare and supporting associates during the pandemic.

title: 2020 Twin Cities CIO of the Year Orbie Awards Finalist: François Charette, Optum
summary: François Charette, CIO of OptumRx and Optum, has been recognized as a finalist for the 2020 Twin Cities CIO of the Year Orbie Awards. With over 20 years of technology experience, this acknowledgment highlights his significant contributions to the field. The article also provides links to related news concerning UnitedHealth Group and Optum.

title: Aetna ships Caring for You kits to millions of Medicare members
summary: Aetna, a CVS Health company, is sending "Caring for You" kits containing self-care items like thermometers, hand sanitizer, and face masks to millions of its Medicare Advantage members. These kits aim to support members during the COVID-19 pandemic and flu season, particularly those most vulnerable and at home. This initiative builds on Aetna's broader efforts to assist Medicare members during the public health emergency, which also includes waiving cost shares for certain medical visits.

title: Cigna rebrands health services division, including Express Scripts, as Evernorth
summary: Cigna is rebranding its health services segment, including Express Scripts, as Evernorth, to position its offerings as a comprehensive solution for third parties such as other payers, employers, and government businesses. This move is part of Cigna's strategy to diversify revenue streams by making its health services a one-stop shop. The Evernorth brand will encompass products like Accredo, Evicore, and new programs such as Healthy Ways to Work and FamilyPath, with 90% of its business already coming from external clients.

title: Myomo lands Medicare coverage
summary: Myomo announced it received authorization to be a Medicare provider through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, allowing it to bill Medicare directly for its MyoPro orthosis in 39 states plus Washington, D.C. The company is working on coverage for the remaining 11 states and views this as a crucial step towards broader reimbursement, following last year's receipt of HCPCS codes from CMS. MyoPro is an upper-limb orthosis designed to restore function to weakened or paralyzed arms, using a patient's own EMG signals.

title: ETA Spotlight // Monica Weaver, MBA ’07
summary: Monica Weaver, an MBA ’07 graduate, discusses her journey to acquire and operate TGI Direct, a company specializing in direct mail communications for highly regulated industries. She shares insights into her search process, including pivoting from an investor-funded search fund to a self-funded acquisition, and the initial weeks of operating her new business. Weaver also advises aspiring entrepreneurs to focus on building strong relationships with bankers and brokers over an expensive proprietary search.

title: UnitedHealth in Talks to Buy Pharmacy Startup DivvyDose
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. is reportedly in advanced discussions to acquire DivvyDose, an online pharmacy startup, for approximately $300 million. This potential acquisition highlights the ongoing consolidation and competition in the online pharmacy sector, following Amazon's purchase of PillPack in 2018.

title: PROCEPT BioRobotics Announces Medicare and Commercial Reimbursement Coverage for Aquablation Therapy for Enlarged Prostate
summary: PROCEPT BioRobotics announced that National Government Services (NGS) is the first Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) to establish a final coverage policy for Aquablation therapy for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), effective November 1, 2020. This coverage, along with positive positions from Anthem and Humana earlier in 2020, significantly expands access to Aquablation therapy for Medicare and commercially insured patients across the United States. Aquablation therapy offers a safe and effective transurethral procedure for enlarged prostates with reproducible results and low rates of complications.

title: Airlines bank on leisure travelers as business trips dry up in coronavirus pandemic
summary: Airlines are contending with the drastic decline in business travel due to the coronavirus pandemic by shifting their focus to leisure travelers. They are offering fare sales, adding routes to vacation destinations, and permanently eliminating change fees for most domestic tickets to attract passengers. Despite these efforts, passenger volumes remain significantly lower than pre-pandemic levels, and the industry faces uncertainty during the slower fall season.

title: Molina To Buy Affinity Health Plan For $380 Million In Medicaid Deal
summary: Molina Healthcare has announced a definitive agreement to acquire substantially all assets of Affinity Health Plan for $380 million in cash. This acquisition will expand Molina's Medicaid government health benefits business deeper into New York, adding over 280,000 subscribers and $1.3 billion in annual premium revenue. This is Molina's latest acquisition this year, following an $820 million deal to buy Magellan Complete Care, as the company continues to activate its growth strategy in government-subsidized health plans.

title: UnitedHealth has acquired DivvyDose, a competitor to Amazon's PillPack
summary: UnitedHealth Group has acquired DivvyDose, a start-up that competes with Amazon's PillPack by delivering pre-sorted medications to patients, especially those with chronic conditions. The deal was reportedly valued at just over $300 million. This acquisition reflects a larger trend of retailers and health plans investing in online pharmacy services to broaden their customer base and footprint in the pharmacy market.

title: UnitedHealth Group buys DivvyDose to compete with Amazon's PillPack: report
summary: UnitedHealth Group has acquired DivvyDose, an online pharmacy startup, for over $300 million to enter the online pharmacy market and compete with Amazon's PillPack. DivvyDose specializes in delivering pre-sorted medications to patients with multiple chronic conditions. This acquisition highlights a growing trend of health plans and retailers investing in digital pharmacy solutions to serve the increasing number of consumers managing chronic illnesses.

title: Gilead Sciences Settles Medicare Kickbacks Claims with DOJ for $97M
summary: Gilead Sciences has agreed to pay $97 million to settle allegations from the U.S. Department of Justice that the company violated the False Claims Act by receiving Medicare kickbacks. The settlement addresses claims that Gilead used a 501(c)(3) foundation, Caring Voice Coalition (CVC), to unlawfully cover co-pays for its pulmonary arterial hypertension drug, Letairis. This action allegedly induced patients to purchase the drug and undermined Medicare's co-pay structure, which is designed to guard against inflated drug prices.

title: Big fight over drug pricing heads to the Supreme Court
summary: The Supreme Court is set to hear a case regarding state authority to regulate drug pricing, specifically concerning pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs). The case, Rutledge v Pharmaceutical Care Management Association, pits 47 state attorneys general against major corporations like CVS Health, Cigna, and UnitedHealth. The outcome will determine whether federal law (ERISA) preempts state regulation of PBMs, with both sides warning of higher drug costs if the other prevails.

title: Walmart insurance expands to all 50 states
summary: Walmart has expanded its licensed insurance agency, Walmart Insurance Services, to all 50 states, now equipped to sell Medicare insurance plans. The company aims to simplify the enrollment process and help customers find plans that best fit their needs, representing multiple carriers such as Humana, UnitedHealthcare, and Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield. This expansion aligns with Walmart's mission of helping people save money and live better by being a trusted partner in their healthcare journey.

title: Cigna becomes third major payer to restrict MRIs, CT scans at hospitals
summary: Cigna has joined two other major payers in restricting the use of MRIs and CT scans at hospitals. The move aims to reduce healthcare costs by encouraging outpatient imaging. This makes Cigna the third prominent insurer to implement such a policy.

title: Walmart announces plan to sell insurance
summary: Walmart is entering the health insurance market through its new brokerage, Walmart Insurance Services. The company will offer Medicare insurance plans, including Part D, Medicare Advantage, and Medicare Supplement plans, from various major health insurance carriers. This move aligns with Walmart's mission to help customers save money and improve their lives by providing accessible and trusted healthcare options.

title: Customer Wins Power Bike After Ordering 1kg Milo Refill from Jumia
summary: A Lagos-based forex trader, Mr. Emeka Oscar Chukwumanjo, won a Suzuki Power Bike in a Jumia-Nestle raffle draw after purchasing a 1kg Milo Refill. Mr. Chukwumanjo, a frequent Jumia customer, expressed his surprise and delight at winning such a significant prize. The Head of Marketing at Jumia Nigeria, Ms. Olajumoke Bolu-Kujero, highlighted that this prize is one of many benefits customers receive when shopping on Jumia, emphasizing their partnerships with brands like Nestle to offer affordable products and incentives.

title: Accenture Launches Vaccine Management Solution to Support COVID-19 Immunization Programs
summary: Accenture has launched a comprehensive vaccine management solution to help governments and healthcare organizations rapidly plan and execute COVID-19 vaccination programs. The solution expands on Accenture’s contact tracing capabilities and includes modular components for vaccine management and tracking, supply management, community education, contact management, analytics, and organizational support. Built in part on the Salesforce platform, this initiative aims to address the varied needs for developing and running mass immunization efforts worldwide.

title: M Health Fairview, CentraCare leaving Humana Medicare Advantage network
summary: M Health Fairview and CentraCare are exiting the Humana Medicare Advantage network, a move that could affect over 10,000 Minnesotans. Those impacted may face higher out-of-pocket costs unless they switch insurers. This decision follows M Health Fairview's previous announcement of job cuts and a hospital closure.

title: 3 Healthcare Industry Themes Accelerated by COVID-19
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly accelerated three key themes within the healthcare industry: diversified healthcare delivery, digital innovation, and the biopharmaceutical revolution. The article, by Carlyle's Global Healthcare team, highlights the increasing demand for efficient and adaptable provider organizations, the accelerated adoption of digital health solutions like telemedicine, and the expedited research and development in biopharmaceuticals for vaccines and treatments. It emphasizes how these trends are reshaping global healthcare systems and investment strategies.

title: Hospital Chain to Return $6 Billion in Pandemic Aid Ahead of Schedule
summary: HCA Healthcare, one of the largest hospital chains in the U.S., announced it will return $1.6 billion in federal pandemic relief and repay $4.4 billion in loans, totaling $6 billion. This decision signifies the $1 trillion hospital sector's recovery from pandemic-induced disruptions that led to suspended surgeries and revenue plunges. The company's move serves as an indicator of the industry's rebound ahead of schedule.

title: Froedtert Health discloses some patient information may have been stolen in data breach at contractor
summary: Froedtert Health announced that some patient information, including names, addresses, and dates of visits, may have been compromised in a data breach at its contractor, Blackbaud Inc. The breach affected 3,074 patients, though Social Security numbers or financial data were not stolen. Blackbaud, a fundraising services provider, stated it stopped a ransomware attack and paid to ensure the stolen data was destroyed.

title: Preferred Pharmacy Networks Dominate in 2021 Medicare Part D Plans: The Scoop on Cigna, CVS Health, Humana, WellCare, and More
summary: An analysis of 2021 Medicare Part D plans reveals the continued dominance of preferred cost sharing pharmacy networks, with 98% of regional prescription drug plans (PDPs) utilizing this model. This represents a significant increase since 2011, when only 7% of PDPs had preferred networks. Major companies like Cigna, CVS Health, Humana, and WellCare are exclusively offering plans with preferred networks, with none providing an open network for 2021.

title: CNA staffing, turnover will be a top focus, federal official vows
summary: A federal official pledged that staffing and turnover among certified nursing assistants (CNAs) in long-term care facilities will be a top priority for the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). This commitment comes as research highlights high CNA turnover rates (129% annually) and their critical role in direct resident care, despite often receiving low pay and limited benefits. Experts are calling for significant changes, including a minimum wage standard of $20/hour for CNAs, to address these systemic issues.

title: Bind lands $105M funding round to fuel expansion into fully insured health plan market
summary: Bind, a health benefits company, secured a $105 million Series B funding round to expand its "on-demand" health plans into the fully insured market. Founded by entrepreneur Tony Miller, who previously sold two companies to UnitedHealth Group, Bind aims to disrupt the health insurance industry by offering plans with no deductibles or coinsurance and transparent pricing. The company plans to use the capital to accelerate growth and operate in over 30 states by the end of 2021.

title: Anthony Welters Joins Gilead Sciences’ Board of Directors
summary: Anthony Welters has been appointed to the Board of Directors of Gilead Sciences, Inc. Welters brings extensive experience from his career, including his role as Senior Adviser to the Office of the CEO of UnitedHealth Group and founding AmeriChoice. His appointment is expected to provide valuable perspective to Gilead's board in its mission to deliver transformational medicines.

title: Minnesota’s biggest companies open their wallets to political candidates, and risk
summary: Minnesota's largest corporations contribute significantly to political campaigns, often through third-party groups, which can link them to controversial issues and negative advertising. This practice poses a reputation risk, as money trails can lead to unexpected associations that conflict with a company's public values. While some companies are adopting policies to increase transparency or restrict certain donations, the reliance on dark money and indirect giving remains prevalent.

title: Business Icons’ Wisdom Echoes in This Firm’s Investments
summary: This article highlights how private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) distinguishes itself through its operational focus, inherited from its founders and advisors like Jack Welch. CD&R offers more than just capital, providing operational expertise to improve businesses, as demonstrated by examples like naviHealth and UK retailer B&M. The firm frequently engages in partnership transactions, allowing sellers to retain significant ownership, and specializes in sectors like healthcare, consumer, tech services/software, and industrials.

title: Suddenly Unemployed? Healthcare Options You Should Consider
summary: This article explores various healthcare options available to individuals who suddenly become unemployed, especially in light of economic shifts like those caused by COVID-19. It details alternatives to employer-sponsored health insurance, including COBRA, Marketplace coverage under the Affordable Care Act, coverage through a parent's plan, Medicaid, Medicare, and short-term plans. The piece advises careful consideration of eligibility, cost, provider networks, and health status when selecting a healthcare option.

title: Over 80% of Health Execs Have Artificial Intelligence Plans in Place
summary: A survey by Optum reveals that 83% of healthcare organizations have an AI strategy in place, with an additional 15% planning to develop one. Healthcare executives are increasingly recognizing the tangible benefits of AI, such as cost savings, improved patient outcomes, and business process automation, particularly accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite growing adoption, challenges like lack of data transparency and concerns about the human role in decision-making still exist, emphasizing the need for explainable AI interfaces and integrated human judgment.

title: UnitedHealth names new chief legal officer as Marianne Short announces retirement
summary: UnitedHealth Group has appointed Matthew Friedrich as its new chief legal officer, effective January 11. Friedrich will succeed Marianne Short, who is set to retire from her position as General Counsel in January. He joins UnitedHealth from Cognizant Technology Solutions Corp., where he also served as general counsel.

title: Medical Innovation and Experts | TELUS Health Care Centres
summary: TELUS Health Care Centres offer a wide range of corporate healthcare programs, individual preventive healthcare, and occupational health services across Canada. They emphasize innovation, personalized care, and prevention-focused approaches, supported by a network of medical professionals and digital health expertise. The services include virtual care, physical care centres, and mobile units, aiming to improve employee health, engagement, and individual well-being.

title: GSK Consumer Healthcare mulls local production of new dental care brand in India
summary: GSK Consumer Healthcare is considering local manufacturing in India for its newly launched Polident denture care brand, with plans to make India an export hub for neighboring markets. The company aims to partner with third-party manufacturers initially, building on its existing oral care sales network and targeting urban denture wearers. This move follows GSK's divestment of its health food drinks portfolio to Unilever, reaffirming its commitment to OTC and oral health brands in India.

title: UnitedHealth Group: 2021 Revenues To Eclipse $277 Billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced a 2021 revenue projection of $277 billion to $280 billion, representing an 8% growth, alongside updated 2020 projections of $257 billion. The company's strategy focuses on expanding its health insurance and Optum medical care provider units, emphasizing value-based care models and increased use of technology like digital coaching and telehealth. Sir Andrew Witty also returned to the company as president of UnitedHealth and CEO of Optum, following a leave of absence to aid vaccine development.

title: Optum CEO Andrew Witty returns to UnitedHealth after Covid-19 vaccine work at WHO
summary: Sir Andrew Witty, the CEO of Optum and president of UnitedHealth Group, has returned to the company after co-leading Covid-19 vaccine development efforts at the World Health Organization. Witty had taken a leave of absence earlier in the year for this global health initiative. He resumes his leadership roles within UnitedHealth Group.

title: Aetna will cover noninvasive prenatal testing for all pregnancies
summary: Aetna has announced that it will expand coverage for noninvasive prenatal testing to include all pregnancies. This change in policy comes as a significant update for expectant parents, making this testing more accessible. The article was published by Modern Healthcare.

title: Company of the Year: Teladoc
summary: Teladoc was named Company of the Year for 2020 due to its unprecedented capitalization on the COVID-19 pandemic's tailwinds in the telehealth sector. The company expanded significantly through M&A, including an $18.5 billion acquisition of Livongo, despite initial investor wariness and increasing competition. Teladoc's strategic positioning as a single access point for virtual care led to substantial growth, with volumes tripling year-over-year in Q3 2020.

title: UnitedHealthcare Introduces Enhancements for Wearable Device Well-being Program, Including Access to Apple Fitness+ at No Additional Cost
summary: UnitedHealthcare has enhanced its Motion wearable device well-being program, offering eligible members at least six months of Apple Fitness+ at no additional cost starting in 2021. The program also introduces new ways to earn financial rewards for various physical activities beyond walking, including cycling and elliptical use, with the goal of making activity goals more accessible. These enhancements aim to provide digital resources and financial incentives to help members improve their health and well-being.

title: US medical industry urged to reassess paid events amid doctor kickback concerns
summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has issued a rare "fraud alert," urging the medical industry to re-evaluate paid events for doctors due to concerns over kickbacks. This alert comes after federal investigations revealed that such payments often induce the prescribing of specific drugs or devices, sometimes for off-label uses. The move signals increased scrutiny on industry-funded speaker programs and serves as a warning to both companies and physicians about violating anti-kickback statutes.

title: Hope is here: COVID-19 vaccine arrives at HCA Healthcare facilities
summary: HCA Healthcare facilities began receiving and administering the COVID-19 vaccine to frontline workers in mid-December 2020, marking a significant turning point in the pandemic. Key personnel across various locations, including South Carolina, Virginia, and Tennessee, were among the first to receive the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine, expressing hope and gratitude for the scientific achievement. The article also provides a Q&A section addressing common concerns about vaccine types, safety, development speed, and distribution plans.

title: Tenet inks deal to sell urgent care business as it doubles down on surgery centers
summary: Tenet has agreed to sell its urgent care division, CareSpot and MedPost, to FastMed, as part of its strategy to concentrate on its ambulatory surgery center business. This divestiture will allow Tenet to "sharpen its focus" on its outpatient surgical business, United Surgical Partners, especially after a recent $1.1 billion deal to acquire up to 45 new surgery centers. The move also highlights Tenet's strategy to divest from non-core areas and compete in the growing musculoskeletal outpatient surgery market, facing increasing competition in the urgent care sector from companies like CVS Health and Walgreens.

title: Centene, Optum Ventures back $18M investment in Diameter Health to spur health data interoperability
summary: Major insurer Centene, along with Optum Ventures and other existing investors, has backed an $18 million Series B funding round for Diameter Health to advance healthcare data interoperability. This investment highlights the growing market value insurers place on data sharing and analytics, especially as the industry moves towards greater collaboration and digitization. Diameter Health's technology, which normalizes and integrates clinical data, will be crucial in assisting healthcare organizations and health plans in improving patient care and achieving cost efficiencies.

title: iShares Global Healthcare ETF IXJ
summary: The iShares Global Healthcare ETF (IXJ) tracks the performance of healthcare companies worldwide. Established in 2001, it mirrors the S&P Global 1200 Healthcare Sector Index and invests at least 80% of its assets in stocks comprising this index. As of April 2022, IXJ had $3.49 billion in net assets across 116 holdings, including major players like UnitedHealth Group, Johnson & Johnson, and Pfizer.

title: RAM spends $100m on three regional hospital investments
summary: Real Asset Management (RAM) has invested $100 million in three regional hospital properties: Dubbo Private, Mayo Private, and North West Private. These assets, acquired from Vital Healthcare Property Trust, will be part of an essential services real estate trust that RAM plans to float in mid-2021. The portfolio, focusing on long-term sustainable income yield in high-growth corridors, now brings RAM's total holdings to approximately $500 million, including 13 retail centers and six healthcare investments.

title: Diameter Health gains $18M in new funding
summary: Diameter Health, a health data optimization and interoperability company, secured $18 million in Series B funding led by Centene Corp., bringing its total funding to $30 million. The company plans to invest the new capital in product development, specifically expanding its Fusion integration solution and adding AI/machine learning capabilities. This funding comes as increased efforts to advance interoperability and curb information blocking are accelerating in the U.S.

title: After decades as a hospital operator, Tenet shifts its focus to surgery centers
summary: Tenet Health is shifting its primary focus from hospital operations to ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) following a significant acquisition that will make its ASC footprint nearly five times larger than its hospital portfolio. This strategic move is anticipated to boost ambulatory earnings to nearly half of the company's overall earnings next year, reflecting a broader industry trend of shifting procedures away from hospitals due to regulatory changes, reimbursement models, and patient preferences. The company is actively divesting from less competitive hospital markets and urgent care businesses to concentrate on high-growth areas like musculoskeletal procedures within ASCs.

title: The technology solutions post-acute care providers picked up in 2020
summary: In 2020, Medline signed 800 customer contracts for its Post-Acute Solutions program, a 30% increase from the previous year, to help post-acute care providers with technology-based quality and workforce management. The demand for real-time data tools grew significantly as providers sought solutions to improve clinical performance, staff engagement, and operational health amidst the challenges of the pandemic. Medline partnered with companies like OnShift, Real Time Medical Systems, and HealthStream to offer these crucial tools.

title: The Truth About Weight Watchers
summary: WW (formerly Weight Watchers) has rebranded to focus on holistic wellness beyond just weight loss, incorporating mental health and sleep in their programs. The article delves into the company's history, its science-backed point system for food, and the various advantages of its membership, including virtual meetings and coaching. It also highlights how WW caters to diverse dietary needs and integrates with modern meal kit services.

title: Closely watched healthcare play by Amazon, JPMorgan and Berkshire Hathaway to shutter
summary: Haven, the ambitious healthcare venture created by Amazon, JPMorgan Chase, and Berkshire Hathaway, is set to shut down by the end of February. The company, which aimed to tackle healthcare complexity and costs, had garnered significant attention but also saw executive departures and few public achievements. Many of its 60 employees are expected to be absorbed by the founding companies, which will continue their individual healthcare initiatives.

title: What Centene Gets for Its $2.2 Billion Magellan Acquisition
summary: Centene Corp. announced its definitive agreement to acquire Magellan Health Inc. for $2.2 billion, including debt, paying a 15% premium per share. This acquisition aims to expand Centene's whole health capabilities, establish a leading behavioral health platform, and add millions of new enrollees to its government-sponsored health care plans. The deal is expected to address the critical need for better integrated physical and mental health care, especially given the rise in behavioral health issues exacerbated by the pandemic.

title: Haven, the Amazon-Berkshire-JPMorgan venture to disrupt health care, is disbanding after 3 years
summary: Haven, the joint venture formed by Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase to revolutionize healthcare, is disbanding after three years. Many of its 57 employees are expected to be placed within the founding companies, which will continue to pursue individual healthcare initiatives and collaborate informally. The closure highlights the significant challenges of disrupting the complex U.S. healthcare system.

title: Amazon, Berkshire and JPMorgan Will End Joint Health Care Venture (Published 2021)
summary: The joint venture Haven, formed by Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase to innovate health care delivery for their employees, is disbanding at the end of February, three years after its inception. The initiative, which aimed to disrupt the health care industry by leveraging the scale of three large employers, faced logistical hurdles in developing solutions applicable to all three companies. This quiet dissolution marks the end of a high-profile collaboration that once sent shock waves through the health insurance sector.

title: World’s Largest Insurers 2020: AM Best Ranks UnitedHealth, Allianz on Top
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. maintained its top position in AM Best's ranking of the world's largest insurance companies by net premiums written for the sixth consecutive year in 2019. Allianz SE and Prudential Financial, Inc. surpassed AXA S.A. in the non-banking assets ranking. The report, published in BestWeek, details shifts in the top global insurers for both net premiums written and non-banking assets.

title: P&G, Billie Cancel Deal After FTC Suit
summary: Procter & Gamble's planned acquisition of women’s shaving brand Billie has been called off after the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) filed a suit to block the deal, citing concerns over competition. Both companies agreed not to pursue a prolonged legal challenge. This follows a similar FTC intervention that led to the cancellation of Edgewell Personal Care's acquisition of Harry's.

title: Kaiser Permanente ranked No. 1 in consumer satisfaction, Insure.com finds
summary: A recent Insure.com survey found that Kaiser Permanente ranked first in consumer satisfaction among commercial health insurers for 2021. The survey highlighted that competitive pricing and strong customer service were key differentiators for top-performing plans, with UnitedHealthcare showing significant improvement and Centene ranking last among the 15 major U.S. insurers. Despite ongoing industry challenges, the majority of customers expressed satisfaction and intent to renew their policies.

title: UnitedHealth, Ping An, AXA top list of world’s largest insurers by premiums
summary: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated maintained its position as the world's largest insurance company by net premium written (NPW) in 2019, followed by China's Ping An Insurance and French insurer AXA. The article details the top ten insurers by NPW and highlights significant movers in terms of year-on-year growth and declines. It also ranks insurers by net non-banking assets, with Allianz SE taking the top spot in 2019.

title: UnitedHealth to pay nearly $8B for technology company Change
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced it will acquire healthcare technology company Change Healthcare for nearly $8 billion in cash. The acquisition will integrate Change Healthcare into UnitedHealth's OptumInsight segment, enhancing its capabilities in data analytics and revenue cycle management. This move is expected to bolster Optum's already high profit margins within UnitedHealth's diverse business portfolio.

title: UnitedHealth to Purchase Change Healthcare for $8 Billion
summary: UnitedHealth (UNH) has agreed to acquire Change Healthcare (CHNG) in a deal valued at approximately $13 billion, including debt. The acquisition price of $25.75 per share represents a 41% premium over Change Healthcare’s closing price and expands UnitedHealth’s Optum technology business. The transaction values the health technology company at about $8 billion in equity.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s Optum, Change Healthcare to combine in $13.5B deal
summary: UnitedHealth Group's subsidiary Optum announced it will acquire healthcare technology company Change Healthcare for $13.5 billion in an all-cash deal. This acquisition aims to enhance OptumInsight's offerings with Change Healthcare's data analytics, research, and revenue cycle management capabilities, simplifying healthcare services and processes. The transaction includes $25.75 per share and close to $5 billion in Change Healthcare's debt, with the deal expected to close in the second half of the year pending approvals.

title: OptumInsight and Change Healthcare Combine to Advance a More Modern, Information and Technology-Enabled Health Care Platform
summary: Optum, a part of UnitedHealth Group, and Change Healthcare have agreed to combine, aiming to advance a more modern, information, and technology-enabled health care platform. This merger will integrate Change Healthcare's technologies with OptumInsight's software, data analytics, and services to streamline clinical, administrative, and payment processes, ultimately improving health outcomes and lowering costs. The acquisition values Change Healthcare's common stock at $25.75 per share in cash and is expected to be accretive to UnitedHealth Group's earnings per share in 2022.

title: Anche la famiglia miliardaria Stevanato investe in PatchAi, startup healthcare di un under 30
summary: PatchAi, an Italian digital health startup, has successfully closed a €1.7 million funding round, with the billionaire Stevanato family's investment vehicle, Sfem Italia, leading one of the tranches. This funding will enable PatchAi to expand its business into new therapeutic areas and scale internationally. The startup, which uses an AI-powered empathetic virtual assistant to improve patient engagement and clinical research, has already seen significant success with adherence rates up to 95% and partnerships with leading pharma companies like Novartis and Roche.

title: Get High Dividend Exposure with the HDEF ETF
summary: The article discusses the Xtrackers MSCI EAFE High Dividend Yield Equity ETF (HDEF) as an option for investors seeking high dividend exposure with international diversification. HDEF offers exposure to developed markets outside the U.S., focusing on high-dividend stocks while hedging against currency risk. This strategy aims to provide stable dividend payments, exemplified by its top holding, Unilever PLC.

title: The Asset Approach to Healthcare Business Valuation
summary: This article discusses the asset approach to healthcare business valuation, particularly relevant in an industry undergoing consolidation. It highlights how federal laws like the Anti-Kickback Statute and Stark Law necessitate fair market value valuations in ongoing referral relationships, making the asset approach a compliant valuation method. The method focuses on adjusting assets and liabilities to fair market value, including fixed assets and the assembled workforce, to determine a compensable fair market value of the business without accounting for referral value.

title: General Mills halts donations to Republicans who voted to block Biden win
summary: General Mills has announced it will halt political donations to Republican members of Congress who voted against the certification of Joe Biden's election win. This decision affects 147 Republicans, including Minnesota representatives Jim Hagedorn and Michelle Fischbach. Several other Minnesota companies, such as Best Buy, 3M, Target, UnitedHealth Group, Cargill, and Thrivent, are also suspending or reviewing their political contributions following the Capitol insurrection.

title: Encompass Health Building MA Momentum, Still Exploring ‘Strategic Alternatives’ for Home Health Business
summary: Encompass Health (NYSE: EHC) is continuing to explore "strategic alternatives" for its home health and hospice segment, which may include a sale, merger, spin-off, or IPO. Despite a dip in home health admissions and revenues in Q4 2020, the company expects volumes to increase in the latter half of 2021 and is focusing on expanding Medicare Advantage partnerships and deploying new quality-reporting tools. Encompass Health also plans to manage rising nursing compensation costs through operational efficiencies and technology.

title: Anthem's Medicare Advantage membership up 18% in 2020
summary: Anthem reported a significant 18% increase in its Medicare Advantage membership in 2020, reaching 1.4 million members, with projections for continued double-digit growth in 2021. Despite this growth, the insurer's fourth-quarter profits for 2020 fell short of Wall Street expectations, dropping 41% compared to the previous year, though full-year revenue saw a substantial increase. The company attributed its strong overall performance in 2020 to the diversity of its portfolio and its commitment to customers amidst the challenges of the pandemic.

title: Genomind Alleges Negligent Misrepresentation, ERISA Violation Against UnitedHealth Group
summary: Genomind Inc. has filed a complaint against UnitedHealth Group, alleging negligent misrepresentation and violations of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). Genomind claims that UnitedHealth Group misrepresented coverage for its Professional PGx Express product, a genetic testing service for psychiatric medications. The lawsuit argues that after Genomind overhauled its test to meet United's requirements, the insurer still withheld payments and misled the company about the reasons for non-payment.

title: Informing Hospital Growth and Revenue Goals for ISI
summary: Atrium helped Intuitive Surgical, Inc. (ISI) enhance its relationship with hospitals by leveraging CRM Analytics and Salesforce Sales Cloud. This solution allows ISI's clinical sales teams to create data-driven value statements for hospital executives, directly connecting the da Vinci Surgical System's impact to hospital growth and revenue goals. The initiative transformed Business Alignment Meetings (BAMs) into customer-outcome-focused discussions, leading to tailored business cases for hospitals.

title: UnitedHealth to pay nearly $8B for technology company Change
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced it will acquire healthcare technology company Change Healthcare for nearly $8 billion in cash. This acquisition aims to bolster UnitedHealth's OptumInsight segment, enhancing its data analytics and revenue cycle management capabilities. The deal is expected to close in the second half of the year, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals, and positively impacted both companies' stock prices.

title: U.S. Bancorp hires wealth management executive from JPMorgan Chase
summary: U.S. Bancorp has hired Scott Ford from JPMorgan Chase to lead the affluent unit of its wealth management group. Ford will oversee a team of 1,400 employees, serving clients with at least $100,000 in investments or $250,000 to $3 million in total balances. This strategic hire follows the departure of Mike Ott and aligns with U.S. Bancorp's broader efforts to expand its wealth management services, including a recent acquisition from MUFG Union Bank to boost its West Coast presence.

title: How Do We Report ICHRA Coverage on Forms 1094-C and 1095-C?
summary: This article explains how applicable large employers (ALEs) should report Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement (ICHRA) coverage on Forms 1094-C and 1095-C. It details that ICHRA offers count towards the 95% threshold for avoiding an employer shared responsibility penalty and outlines specific information required on Form 1095-C, including age, terms of offer, ZIP code, and the employee's required contribution. The article also mentions the reporting obligations for MEC and crucial deadlines for furnishing and filing these forms.

title: UnitedHealth Group appoints new CEO
summary: UnitedHealth Group has appointed Sir Andrew Witty as its new chief executive officer, succeeding David Wichmann who is retiring after three years. Witty previously led UnitedHealth Group's Optum unit and served as an envoy for the WHO's COVID-19 efforts, bringing extensive healthcare experience to the role. He will lead a chief executive office team including CFO John Rex and newly appointed President and COO Dirk McMahon.

title: UnitedHealth Group CEO Wichmann to retire, Optum chief Witty named successor
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced that CEO David Wichmann will retire, with Optum chief Andrew Witty named as his successor. Witty will take on the CEO role immediately and join the company's board, while Wichmann will assist with the transition through March. Additionally, Dirk McMahon, CEO of UnitedHealthcare, will become the company's president and chief operating officer.

title: UnitedHealth names former Glaxo CEO Witty to lead company
summary: UnitedHealth Group has announced the promotion of Sir Andrew Witty, former CEO of GlaxoSmithKline, to become the health insurance provider's next CEO, effective immediately. Witty was pictured in 2010 when he previously served as a leader for GlaxoSmithKline. This move signifies a major leadership change for the healthcare giant.

title: UnitedHealth names former Glaxo CEO Witty to lead company
summary: UnitedHealth Group has named former GlaxoSmithKline leader Sir Andrew Witty as its new CEO, effective immediately. Current CEO David Wichmann will retire after more than three years in the role. Witty previously served as president of UnitedHealth’s Optum segment and then president of the parent company, following his tenure running GlaxoSmithKline.

title: UnitedHealth Names Witty CEO as Wichmann Retires Abruptly
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. has appointed Andrew Witty, the former CEO of GlaxoSmithKline Plc, to succeed Dave Wichmann as CEO. Witty, who has led UnitedHealth's Optum division since 2018, will begin his new role immediately, while Wichmann will remain for a transition period through March. Wichmann served as CEO for fewer than four years.

title: UnitedHealth Group names new CEO, COO
summary: UnitedHealth Group has announced the appointment of a new Chief Executive Officer and Chief Operating Officer. The article provides details on these leadership changes within the company. This move is significant for the healthcare giant's future direction.

title: UnitedHealth Names Andrew Witty as CEO as David Wichmann Retires - WSJ
summary: Andrew Witty has been named CEO of UnitedHealth Group, succeeding David Wichmann, whose retirement was an abrupt surprise to executives and investors. Witty, formerly the CEO of GlaxoSmithKline and head of UnitedHealth's Optum unit, recently returned from a leave to assist the World Health Organization with Covid-19 efforts. Wichmann, who became CEO in September 2017, will transition out of his role through March.

title: UnitedHealth Group CEO David Wichmann steps down; Andrew Witty named successor
summary: UnitedHealth Group has announced that Andrew Witty will succeed David Wichmann as CEO. Wichmann is retiring after leading the insurance and health care giant since 2017. Witty previously served as CEO of Optum and had been on leave to work with the World Health Organization on COVID-19 vaccine efforts.

title: Who is UnitedHealth's new CEO Andrew Witty?
summary: This article announces Sir Andrew Witty as the new CEO of UnitedHealth Group. Witty was previously hired in 2018 to lead UnitedHealth Group's Optum division, which handles the majority of UnitedHealth's non-health insurance business. The article also provides links to related news concerning Witty's career progression and involvement with COVID-19 vaccine development.

title: Private Equity Health Care Acquisitions – January 2021
summary: This article by the Private Equity Stakeholder Project (PESP) tracks private equity-backed healthcare acquisitions in January 2021, highlighting the growing investor interest and associated risks. It details acquisitions by firms like Levine Leichtman Capital Partners and Audax Group, noting past legal issues faced by some of their portfolio companies, including alleged billing fraud. The report provides a comprehensive list of add-on acquisitions and new PE investments/buyouts from the specified month.

title: UnitedHealth’s Exiting CEO to Get Salary, Bonus for 2 Years
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. will compensate outgoing CEO Dave Wichmann with two years' salary and bonus following his unexpected retirement, as disclosed in a securities filing. Wichmann, who led the company for less than four years, has been succeeded by former pharmaceutical executive Andrew Witty, effective immediately. The compensation package is equivalent to what he would have received as severance.

title: Centene Corp to slash 3,000 jobs
summary: Major US health insurer Centene Corporation announced plans to eliminate 3,000 jobs and 1,500 open positions, primarily due to "significant overlap" from recent acquisitions. Despite the job cuts, Centene reported strong financial results for 2020, with total revenues of $28.3 billion in Q4 and $111.1 billion for the full year, driven by acquisitions and growth in government-sponsored programs. CEO Michael Neidorff emphasized the company's focus on continued growth through expansion and technological advancement.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s Wichmann Realized Over $156 Million as CEO
summary: David S. Wichmann, former CEO of UnitedHealth Group, realized over $156 million in total compensation during his tenure from September 2017 to February 2021. He retired on February 2, 2021, and was succeeded by Sir Andrew P. Witty, whose annual target compensation package details are provided. Wichmann's retirement marks him as the 10th CEO from the Equilar 500 to announce their resignation in 2021.

title: Interim HealthCare Inc. Continues Strong Momentum with Latest Acquisition; Representing One of Three Bold Strategic Moves for Parent Company, Caring Brands International
summary: Caring Brands International (CBI), parent company to Interim HealthCare, announced three significant home healthcare franchise acquisitions, including Interim HealthCare of San Diego, Bluebird Care in Ireland, and Just Better Care in Australia. These strategic moves aim to strengthen CBI's global presence and meet the increasing demand for home healthcare services, especially exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The acquisitions allow for expanded support and growth in key markets, providing comprehensive care to more individuals.

title: UnitedHealth's Wichmann to earn 2 years salary, bonuses post-retirement
summary: David Wichmann, the outgoing CEO of UnitedHealth Group, will receive two years' salary and bonuses upon his full exit from the company next month. This compensation is classified as retirement by the company due to his long tenure and successful leadership. Wichmann's base salary in 2019 was $1.4 million, with total compensation reaching $18.9 million that year.

title: The great GP surgery takeover: US giant seizes four practices in Camden
summary: A US health insurance company, Centene Corporation, has taken control of four GP surgeries in Camden, impacting 370,000 patients across London. This move, achieved through a subsidiary taking over existing provider AT Medics, has been criticized by NHS campaigners as a secretive step toward privatization, raising concerns about profit-driven healthcare and the long-term dismantling of the NHS public service model. Despite national efforts to scale back NHS outsourcing, the private sector has secured significant contracts over the years.

title: UnitedHealth Group PESTLE Analysis
summary: This article provides a detailed PESTLE analysis of UnitedHealth Group, examining the political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental factors that influence its business operations. It highlights how the company navigates government policies, economic shifts, societal trends, technological advancements, legal regulations, and environmental considerations to shape its strategies and maintain resilience. The analysis underscores the importance of understanding these external factors for UnitedHealth Group's performance in a dynamic global healthcare landscape.

title: 9 Companies In The Healthcare Industry, Net Worth Ranked
summary: This article ranks nine leading healthcare companies based on their net worth, highlighting their significant contributions to the global economy, especially during the pandemic. Companies like Johnson and Johnson, CVS Health Corp, and UnitedHealth Group Inc. are featured for their substantial revenues, market capitalization, and diverse services ranging from pharmaceuticals and health insurance to medical device manufacturing and managed care. The piece emphasizes the industry's crucial role in developing life-saving drugs and shaping the economy.

title: Class Action Alleges Surgical Care Affiliates, Other Entities Operated ‘No-Poach’ Agreement Conspiracy
summary: A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Surgical Care Affiliates (SCA) and related entities, including UnitedHealth Group and Tenet Healthcare, alleging violations of the Sherman and Clayton Acts. The complaint claims that these companies engaged in "no-poach" agreements to suppress senior-level employee compensation by agreeing not to solicit or hire each other's employees without consent. This lawsuit follows a Department of Justice criminal indictment against SCA for similar labor market collusion.

title: UnitedHealth’s New CEO Sees Better Blending of Key Units Ahead
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc.'s new CEO, Andrew Witty, believes there is significant room for growth by enhancing coordination between the company's various healthcare units. He plans to boost technology services, potentially expand internationally, and better integrate the UnitedHealthcare and Optum divisions to unlock "untapped potential."

title: Physician Offices an Engine for Hospice Referral Growth
summary: Physician offices are identified as a significant opportunity for hospice referral growth in 2021, with 41% of hospice leaders surveyed indicating this. This growth area is driven by changing demographics, evolving payment models, and shifts in patient accessibility during COVID-19, which saw fewer referrals from facility-based settings. Educating physicians on the value of hospice care and engaging with managed-care companies are key strategies for hospices to capitalize on this trend and overcome misconceptions about hospice care.

title: How Does Cigna Long Term Disability Work?
summary: This article explains how Cigna long-term disability insurance works, detailing its purpose to cover a portion of income for policyholders unable to work due to injury or illness. It outlines the benefits, the claims process, eligibility requirements including a list of potentially covered conditions, and highlights challenges faced by claimants, especially in light of the COVID-19 pandemic. The article also advises on legal options if a claim is denied.

title: Minnesota businesses join mass COVID-19 vaccination campaign
summary: Minnesota's largest employers are actively encouraging COVID-19 vaccination among their workers, offering incentives like paid time off and transportation assistance, and providing educational resources to combat vaccine hesitancy. This widespread corporate involvement is seen as crucial for overcoming the pandemic, especially given the challenges posed by misinformation and an unprecedented vaccine rollout. Businesses like UnitedHealth Group, Target, General Mills, and Best Buy are participating in this effort, which is being supported by organizations like the Business Roundtable to build public confidence in vaccines.

title: UnitedHealthcare Hearing Launches Virtual Option to Help Plan Participants Remotely Access Hearing Health Care and Treatment
summary: UnitedHealthcare Hearing has introduced Right2You, a new virtual care option designed to expand access to custom-programmed hearing aids for individuals nationwide and eligible UnitedHealthcare members. This program helps reduce the need for in-person appointments for hearing aid fittings and adjustments, potentially saving consumers 50% to 80% on costs. The initiative aims to improve hearing health care delivery, particularly important given the decline in in-person appointments due to COVID-19 and the growing prevalence of hearing loss.

title: Cleveland Clinic Collaborates with Lilly, Anthem to Add New Heart Surgery Option for Lilly Health Plan Members
summary: Cleveland Clinic, in collaboration with Eli Lilly and Company and Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, is offering a new heart surgery option for eligible Lilly health plan members. This program provides access to complex cardiac surgery at the Cleveland Clinic Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute, which has been ranked as the best in the nation for cardiovascular care. The initiative aims to provide high-quality healthcare while managing costs through bundled pricing and covering travel and accommodation expenses for eligible participants.

title: Humana CFO to depart
summary: Humana's CFO, Brian Kane, is stepping down after seven years to pursue other opportunities. Susan Diamond, president of Humana's home business, will serve as interim CFO while the company searches for a permanent replacement. During his tenure, Kane managed significant industry consolidation and oversaw considerable expansion in Humana's hospice and home healthcare business.

title: Learning healthcare: bringing 20 years of patient safety progress to COVID-19 at HCA Healthcare
summary: HCA Healthcare has leveraged two decades of patient safety advancements, guided by Dr. Jonathan Perlin, to enhance care during the COVID-19 pandemic, resulting in a 28% improvement in survival rates for COVID-19 patients. The article details the evolution of patient safety initiatives since 1999 reports like "To Err Is Human" and highlights HCA Healthcare's contributions in maternal safety, infection prevention, and sepsis detection through tools like SPOT and the NATE platform. It also emphasizes the importance of health equity as a foundational aspect of patient safety.

title: DOJ investigating UnitedHealth Group's $13 billion Change Healthcare acquisition
summary: The Department of Justice is investigating UnitedHealth Group's $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare. The article was published on March 26, 2021, and highlights concerns related to potential anticompetitive practices following the merger.

title: Doctors Accuse UnitedHealthcare of Stifling Competition (Published 2021)
summary: UnitedHealthcare is being sued in two states by U.S. Anesthesia Partners, a large group of anesthesiologists, who accuse the insurer of stifling competition by forcing them out of its network and coercing hospitals and surgeons to stop referrals. The lawsuits, filed in Colorado and Texas, claim United engaged in "unlawful tactics and pressure campaigns," including offering surgeons contracts that pay more if they steer patients away from U.S. Anesthesia Partners. UnitedHealthcare refutes these claims, stating the lawsuits are an attempt to pressure them into higher rate demands and accusing private-equity-backed physician groups of demanding double or triple the median rates for services.

title: 10 innovative examples of telehealth in action
summary: This article showcases ten innovative examples of how telehealth is being utilized to transform healthcare delivery, spurred by the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights how virtual care can improve convenience for patients and staff, extend access to care, and address various medical needs from remote screening and digital check-ins to tele-ICUs, wearable biosensors, and teledentistry. The examples demonstrate a broader shift towards integrating virtual solutions into the future of healthcare.

title: State of Hawaii Selects UnitedHealthcare to Serve its Medicaid Beneficiaries
summary: The state of Hawaii has selected UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Hawaii to administer its QUEST Integration Medicaid program statewide, effective July 1, 2021. This five-and-a-half-year contract covers various programs including TANF, CHIP, ABD, and LTSS, aiming to improve the overall health and well-being of Hawaii’s Medicaid beneficiaries through patient-centered care. UnitedHealthcare, which already serves around 114,000 people in Hawaii, will expand its reach to a portion of the more than 400,000 adults and children eligible for the state’s Medicaid program.

title: Anesthesiology Group Squeezed 'Like a Boa Constrictor' Sues Insurer
summary: U.S. Anesthesia Partners (USAP) is suing UnitedHealthcare (UHC) in Texas and Colorado, alleging anti-competitive practices aimed at forcing USAP doctors out of network and undermining their business relationships. USAP claims UHC's actions, including bribing surgeons and penalizing facilities, are intended to boost UHC's profits and those of its affiliates like Optum, while UHC counters that USAP demands egregiously high rates. The insurer argues paying USAP at median rates would save employers significant amounts, whereas USAP asserts UHC's practices risk patient access to quality care and can increase overall healthcare costs.

title: UnitedHealthcare names veteran exec as new CEO
summary: UnitedHealth Group has appointed Brian Thompson as the new CEO of UnitedHealthcare, the nation's largest insurer. Thompson, who previously led UnitedHealthcare's government business, will focus on driving continued growth across the company. This leadership change follows Dirk McMahon's move to president and COO of UnitedHealth Group, and Andrew Witty's succession as UHG CEO after David Wichmann's retirement.

title: UnitedHealth CEO makes first changes to leadership team
summary: UnitedHealth Group CEO Andrew Witty announced his first major leadership changes, appointing Brian Thompson as the new CEO of UnitedHealthcare, the nation's largest health insurer. Thompson previously led UnitedHealthcare's Medicare business, which saw significant growth in Medicare Advantage plans. The changes also include new leadership roles within Optum, including Dan Schumacher as Chief Strategy and Growth Officer and Heather Cianfrocco as CEO of OptumRx.

title: Brian Thompson Named CEO of UnitedHealthcare
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. has appointed Brian Thompson as the new CEO of UnitedHealthcare, its insurance unit. UnitedHealthcare is the company's largest business. The announcement was made on Wednesday, April 7, 2021.

title: How Tractor Supply Company is helping vaccinate rural America against COVID-19 | Opinion
summary: Tractor Supply Company is actively supporting COVID-19 vaccination efforts in rural America through its "Rolling Up Our Sleeves" initiative. The company is educating its 42,000 team members and their communities about vaccination, offering a $50 payment and time off for team members who get vaccinated, and facilitating onsite vaccination clinics. Tractor Supply has also implemented various safety measures since the pandemic began, including retaining an infectious disease expert, encouraging sick employees to stay home with pay, and providing PPE and care packages.

title: Brian Thompson Named Chief Executive Officer of UnitedHealthcare Unit
summary: Brian Thompson has been appointed as the Chief Executive Officer of UnitedHealthcare, the health benefits business of UnitedHealth Group. Thompson previously led UnitedHealthcare's government programs, including Medicare & Retirement and Community & State businesses. In his new role, he will focus on driving growth across all segments and ensuring access to affordable, high-quality healthcare.

title: Six companies will split $20B in managed-care work under biggest contract in Ohio history
summary: Ohio has unveiled the six companies selected for a historic $20 billion Medicaid managed care contract, aimed at transforming the state's healthcare system for over 3 million low-income or disabled residents. This restructuring includes changes to the problematic pharmacy benefit manager system and care for children with behavioral health challenges. The state anticipates potential legal challenges from companies that weren't awarded contracts, similar to past re-bidding processes.

title: The ARKG ETF: Genomic Focus with a Twist
summary: The ARK Genomic Revolution Multi-Sector Fund (ARKG) is an actively managed ETF that focuses on genomics but also invests in other healthcare growth areas like telemedicine, as exemplified by its exposure to Teledoc. The fund seeks long-term capital growth by investing in companies that merge healthcare with technology to advance genomic sequencing and improve healthcare, agriculture, and pharmaceuticals. Despite a recent decline in Livongo app downloads, analysts project strong revenue for the Teladoc subsidiary, highlighting the growth potential in virtual health services.

title: MMIT Payer Portrait: UnitedHealthcare
summary: UnitedHealthcare (UHC) is the largest health insurer in the U.S., significantly expanding its presence across various markets, including Medicare Advantage. Its pharmacy benefits are managed by OptumRx, which has driven industry-wide integration through acquisitions like Diplomat Specialty Pharmacy and DivvyDose. UHC's planned acquisition of Change Healthcare faces regulatory scrutiny due to antitrust concerns raised by the American Hospital Association.

title: UnitedHealth Group vs. Clover: Which Health Insurance Stock is a Better Buy? By StockNews
summary: This article compares UnitedHealth Group (UNH) and Clover Health Investments (CLOV), two diversified healthcare companies. It highlights that both companies are well-positioned for revenue growth due to extended enrollment periods and expanding Medicare options. The piece aims to determine which of these health insurance stocks is a better investment.

title: Economic impact of coverage expansion for NIPT
summary: A study involving Harvard Pilgrim Health Care and Illumina Inc. found that expanding coverage for noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT) through a performance-based, risk-sharing agreement significantly increased NIPT use and decreased conventional prenatal screening methods, with only a negligible increase in per member per month (PMPM) cost. The findings support the idea that NIPT offers higher accuracy benefits, leading to fewer false positives and invasive diagnostic tests, and its cost is expected to decline over time. This collaborative approach between payers and industry provides greater access to advanced technology and builds public evidence for its effectiveness.

title: Cohere Health scores $36M for platform aimed at streamlining care
summary: Cohere Health has raised $36 million in Series B funding, led by Polaris Partners, for its care-collaboration platform. The platform aims to streamline the prior authorization process, improve communication between providers and health plans, and facilitate evidence-based care plans. The funds will be used to expand its digital health plan solutions, which automate preauthorization.

title: With $27 Million In Funding, A Tiny Fintech Takes Aim At Cigna, Aetna And UnitedHealthcare
summary: Level, a New York-based fintech startup founded by Paul Aaron, has secured $27 million in Series A funding to disrupt the health insurance industry. The company aims to make insurance benefits more efficient and affordable for employees, initially focusing on dental and vision plans. Level differentiates itself by offering quick claim processing, a user-friendly app, and a unique self-funded model that allows businesses to get refunds for unused benefits, positioning itself as a challenger to established giants like Cigna, Aetna, and UnitedHealthcare.

title: Humana Inc. Overcharged Medicare Nearly $200 Million, Federal Audit Finds : Shots - Health News
summary: A federal audit by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' Office of Inspector General found that Humana Inc. improperly collected nearly $200 million from Medicare in 2015 by overstating patient illnesses. Humana disputes the findings but could face a record penalty if the recommendation to repay is finalized. The audit highlights broader issues with Medicare Advantage plans overbilling taxpayers, and the OIG plans more such audits using extrapolation methods.

title: How Much Do Natera Test Results Cost With Insurance?
summary: Consumers are reporting that Natera test results can cost significantly more than initial quotes, with some bills being thousands of dollars higher than expected. Despite Natera's claims of affordable out-of-pocket costs and widespread insurance acceptance, many patients face denied claims and exorbitant charges, leading to calls for potential class-action lawsuits. The issue is partly attributed to "unbundling" services, where Natera codes single tests as multiple components to inflate costs.

title: CVS Health Quietly Made Massive Donation to Dark-Money Group Fighting Access to Care
summary: CVS Health made a $5 million donation to the Partnership for America’s Health Care Future (PAHCF), a dark-money group lobbying against proposals like Medicare for All and the public option. This donation is the largest known contribution to PAHCF, which actively campaigns to discourage health care reforms aimed at controlling costs and expanding access. Despite the donation, CVS Health is not listed as a coalition member of the group, which also receives funding from other major healthcare players and spends heavily on political influence.

title: Cigna to launch new small group health plan in CT
summary: Cigna announced it is launching a new health plan in Connecticut targeted at small businesses with 50 or fewer workers, years after leaving the market. The Bloomfield-based insurer partnered with New York-based Oscar to offer the "Cigna + Oscar" plan, which received regulatory approval and will begin sales on July 1. This launch comes amidst a debate in the state legislature over a proposed public health plan that has drawn criticism from the insurance industry, including Cigna.

title: Minnesota IPO Mania? Agiliti, SkyWater Technology Go Public
summary: Two Minnesota companies, Agiliti Inc. and SkyWater Technology Inc., recently went public, signaling significant IPO activity in the state. Agiliti, a medical equipment management company, raised $368.4 million with its IPO, planning to use the capital for acquisitions and debt reduction. Chipmaker SkyWater Technology raised $112.1 million and intends to use the proceeds for working capital, growth, and potential strategic investments.

title: UnitedHealth Group's David Wichmann paid nearly $18M in his last year as CEO
summary: David Wichmann, former CEO of UnitedHealth Group Inc., received $17.87 million in compensation during his final year in the role. This compensation results in a CEO-tomedian-employee-pay ratio of 321 to 1, given the median employee earned $55,696 in fiscal 2020.

title: UnitedHealth former CEO David Wichmann earned $42.1M in his last year
summary: David Wichmann, former CEO of UnitedHealth Group, earned $42.1 million in compensation in his final year, primarily from long-term equity awards, a decrease from his $52.1 million compensation the prior year. His successor, Andrew Witty, received $17.4 million in compensation, including a $550,000 bonus for his performance before taking an unpaid leave to work with the WHO on COVID-19 vaccine development. UnitedHealth Group reported a 6% increase in revenue to $257 billion and a 12% increase in earnings per share to $16.03 in 2020, with its stock achieving a 21% total return.

title: Welltower Sees 'Even Further Upside' from Genesis Exit as the Nursing Home Giant Restructures
summary: Welltower (NYSE: WELL) announced an even greater return than previously expected from its exit of the troubled Genesis HealthCare relationship, with CEO Shankh Mitra touting a 9% unlevered return after Genesis repays its outstanding debt. The complex deal involved selling 51 Genesis-operated nursing homes, transitioning facilities to regional operators, and transferring PowerBack rehabilitation facilities to Welltower's joint venture with ProMedica. While anticipating some near-term earnings dilution, Welltower expects significant value creation for shareholders through the deployment of $745 million in proceeds.

title: Nestlé to Buy The Bountiful Company Core Brands for $5.75 Billion
summary: Nestlé has agreed to acquire the core brands of The Bountiful Company from KKR for $5.75 billion, including brands like Nature’s Bounty, Solgar, Osteo Bi-Flex, and Puritan’s Pride. This acquisition aims to strengthen Nestlé Health Science's position as a leader in the nutrition and supplements market, capitalizing on the increasing consumer focus on health and wellness. The deal is expected to close in the second half of the year, further expanding Nestlé's presence in the growing global dietary supplements market.

title: How insurers are working to bridge racial gaps in maternal care
summary: This article discusses how insurers are working to address racial disparities in maternal care. It highlights efforts by the insurance industry to improve health outcomes and reduce the gap in care for mothers from different racial backgrounds. The focus is on the strategies and initiatives deployed by insurers to tackle this critical issue.

title: Fighting MS through innovation
summary: This article discusses the critical need for innovation in treating multiple sclerosis (MS), particularly concerning timely diagnosis, early treatment, and the development of new therapies. It highlights the significant economic and social burden of MS on patients, families, and society, using a French study that calculated a cost of EUR 2.8 billion annually. The piece emphasizes that investing in innovative treatments and technologies, such as the MS Copilot® app, can improve patient outcomes and significantly reduce the burden of the disease.

title: Unilever, Coca-Cola and Colgate-Palmolive join AB InBev’s sustainability accelerator
summary: Unilever, Coca-Cola, and Colgate-Palmolive have joined AB InBev's 100+ Accelerator to fund and pilot sustainable supply chain innovations. This collaboration aims to scale existing projects and broaden the accelerator's reach through financial backing and real-world testing of technologies in their own supply chains. The initiative seeks to supercharge the adoption of sustainable solutions for a more sustainable future.

title: Top 4 Factors Driving Revenue Cycle Management Growth, 2021
summary: This article discusses the top four factors driving the growth of Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) solutions in the healthcare industry. These factors include the increasing burden of claims, a rapid shift towards automated operational procedures, the outsourcing of supplementary operational services, and a growing focus on patient satisfaction among healthcare professionals. The article highlights how RCM solutions are crucial for financial stability in healthcare and projects the global RCM market size to reach USD 258.1 billion by 2027.

title: Mental Wellness Wednesday with UnitedHealthcare: Depression and the pandemic - ABC11 Raleigh-Durham
