summary: This article features Dr. Alton L. Williams from UnitedHealthcare discussing depression during Mental Wellness Awareness Month. Dr. Williams outlines signs of depression and offers coping strategies like engaging in new hobbies or reaching out to loved ones. He advises seeking professional help from primary care or mental health practitioners if symptoms are noticed.

title: UnitedHealthcare To Offer New Post-Discharge Support for Retirees with Employer Group Medicare Advantage Plans
summary: UnitedHealthcare announced a new offering called UnitedHealthcare Healthy at Home, designed to support retirees transitioning home after hospital or skilled nursing facility discharge. This program, specifically for Group Retiree Medicare Advantage plans, provides meal delivery, transportation, and in-home personal care to improve recovery and reduce readmissions. UnitedHealthcare aims to enhance retirees' health and healthcare experience with this holistic approach, available to employers starting January 1, 2022.

title: Pfizer and Organon Provide a Glimpse of Biosimilars Strategy
summary: Pfizer reported a 45% increase in first-quarter 2021 revenues, with biosimilar sales up 79%, driven by several recent launches. The company reiterated its commitment to combating rebates and working with legislators to ensure patient savings. Organon, Merck's planned biosimilars and women's health products spinoff, revealed its strategy to launch several biosimilars, including Hadlima in the U.S. in 2023, and aims to introduce 1 to 2 new biosimilars annually through partnerships.

title: Tencent-backed Waterdrop slumps in NYSE debut
summary: Tencent-backed online insurance technology firm Waterdrop Inc. saw its shares tumble 14.5% in its NYSE debut, opening at $10.25 after being priced at $12 in its IPO which raised $360 million. The company's CEO, Shen Peng, stated that Waterdrop would prioritize user growth over short-term profit and aims to become China's version of UnitedHealth Group in a decade, focusing on its online insurance business before expanding into healthcare. This debut was a test for investor appetite in Chinese fintech amidst regulatory crackdowns, but Waterdrop emphasized proactive communication with regulators.

title: Tencent-backed Waterdrop tumbles in NYSE debut
summary: Chinese insurance technology company Waterdrop Inc experienced a rocky debut on the New York Stock Exchange, with its shares opening below their offer price and closing down over 19 percent. Despite the initial tumble, the Tencent-backed company views its IPO as a new beginning, raising $360 million to expand its healthcare service and insurance business in China. Waterdrop's CEO aims to serve people in lower-tier cities and the tech-savvy young generation, aspiring to become a "China's version of UnitedHealth Group" by collaborating with various partners to provide affordable healthcare.

title: Waterdrop Makes NYSE Debut, Aims to become China’s UnitedHealth Group in 10 Years
summary: Chinese online insurance technology company Waterdrop Inc. debuted on the NYSE, aiming to raise $360 million in its IPO and expand its user base in China's lower-tier cities. The company seeks to become China's equivalent of UnitedHealth Group within a decade, despite reporting a widening net loss in 2020. Waterdrop plans to focus on user growth and expand into healthcare businesses to diversify income, prioritizing domestic market expansion before international endeavors.

title: ServiceNow Enhances Vaccine Administration Management, Unveils New Product for the Future of Healthcare
summary: ServiceNow announced updates to its Vaccine Administration Management solution and introduced a new Healthcare and Life Sciences Service Management product, aimed at streamlining vaccine distribution and improving patient experiences. The company's technology is being utilized by organizations globally, including North Rhine-Westphalia in Germany, to efficiently schedule and administer millions of vaccinations. The new Healthcare and Life Sciences Service Management product extends these capabilities to a broader range of healthcare scenarios, leveraging workflows to improve front, middle, and back-office operations and enhance patient engagement.

title: Why UnitedHealth sees combined powers of its health plan, Optum as a competitive advantage
summary: UnitedHealth Group is strategically focusing on finding synergies between its health plan, UnitedHealthcare, and Optum to enhance performance and achieve a competitive advantage. CEO Andrew Witty highlighted the significant "untapped potential" in Optum's diverse business lines, including its role as a PBM, data firm, and healthcare provider. The company aims to leverage these combined strengths, particularly in value-based care and technology, to innovate and improve patient experiences.

title: After Millions in Settlements, H.I.G. Capital Faces Multiple Health Care Fraud Suits
summary: Private equity firm H.I.G. Capital is facing multiple health care fraud lawsuits and has been involved in multimillion-dollar settlements for alleged fraudulent billing practices by its portfolio companies. Two specific instances highlighted are a $4 million settlement involving South Bay Mental Health Center for Medicaid fraud and a $41 million settlement by Surgery Partners for Medicare fraud. These cases raise concerns about H.I.G.'s oversight and involvement in its healthcare investments.

title: In Honor of International Nurses Day: Four Master of Nursing Students Shine in the Spotlight
summary: This article celebrates International Nurses Day by highlighting the stories of four master of nursing students from partner universities: Simmons University, Georgetown University, and USC. It features Mary Kathleen Haber, who sought deeper connections as a nurse practitioner; Isabel and Annabelle Vives, a mother-daughter duo pursuing nurse practitioner roles; and James Byass-Rascoe, who transitioned from the Navy to nursing. The piece emphasizes the critical role of nurses, especially during the global pandemic, and showcases their dedication, expertise, and compassion.

title: Chipotle Launches New Virtual Mental Wellness Platform For Employees
summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill announced a new virtual mental wellness platform called Strive, in partnership with Aduro, to support its employees. This platform offers 1:1 coaching, personalized well-being goals, and incentives for Restaurant Managers, Field Leaders, and Restaurant Support Center employees. The initiative also ties into Mental Health Action Day with a push notification to Chipotle Rewards members, reinforcing the company's commitment to employee well-being alongside existing benefits and financial wellness programs.

title: Vistria Group, Large Hospice Companies Invest in Muse Healthcare, Medalogix
summary: The Vistria Group, along with home health and hospice providers LHC Group, Amedisys, and Encompass Health, has invested in and recapitalized post-acute data analytics companies Muse Healthcare and Medalogix. Following the investment, the two companies will merge under the Medalogix brand, aiming to develop machine learning solutions to identify patients needing home health, hospice, or palliative care earlier and assist in care coordination. This initiative seeks to improve patient outcomes by ensuring care is provided in the home and addressing the issue of short hospice lengths of stay.

title: Alignment Healthcare's “Care Anywhere” Program Sets Industry Standards for Care of Chronically Ill Seniors, Achieving Double Industry Average Member Satisfaction
summary: Alignment Healthcare's "Care Anywhere" program has achieved an unparalleled Net Promoter Score of 76 among its members, nearly doubling the industry average for satisfaction in caring for chronically ill seniors. The program utilizes a high-tech, high-touch approach with its AVA™ platform and dedicated care teams to coordinate personalized care, optimize clinical outcomes, and reduce healthcare costs. This model has prevented avoidable utilization of the healthcare system, leading to significant reductions in hospitalization, emergency room visits, and skilled nursing facility admissions for at-risk members.

title: Two More Minnesota Companies Added to Fortune 500 List
summary: Minnesota saw an increase in its representation on the 2021 Fortune 500 list, with 18 companies making the cut, up from 16 the previous year. Two new Minnesota-based companies, Fastenal and Patterson Cos. Inc., were added to the list, while UnitedHealth Group maintained its top 10 position. The article details the rankings and revenues of all 18 Minnesota companies included in the Fortune 500.

title: UnitedHealth Group names new chief diversity, equity and inclusion officer
summary: UnitedHealth Group has appointed Joy Fitzgerald as its new chief diversity, equity, and inclusion officer. This move highlights the company's focus on DEI initiatives.

title: UnitedHealth Group names new chief diversity, equity and inclusion officer
summary: UnitedHealth Group has appointed Joy Fitzgerald as its new Chief Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Officer. Fitzgerald previously held the chief diversity & inclusion officer role at Eli Lilly and Co. Her appointment signifies UnitedHealth Group's continued focus on diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives.

title: Health Catalyst: An agile approach to healthcare data
summary: Health Catalyst provides an agile approach to healthcare data through its Adaptive Data Architecture, helping healthcare organizations improve clinical, financial, and operational outcomes. The company offers a solution comprising a Data Operating System, Analytics Applications, and Services Expertise, enabling measurable value within months, as demonstrated by its partnership with Northwell Health. During the pandemic, their integrated data platform helped clients respond to challenges in various phases: Prepare, Prevent, Recover, and Plan.

title: CMI Media Group and Compas Announce Executive Elevations
summary: CMI Media Group and Compas have announced significant executive elevations to support their next phase of growth. Stan Woodland, founder and CEO, will transition to Executive Chairman, while Dr. Susan Dorfman will become CEO & President of CMI Media Group, and Jim Woodland will take on the role of CEO of Compas. These changes, effective July 1, 2021, are driven by immense growth and market opportunities for both agencies.

title: 5 goals in UnitedHealth Group's sustainability report
summary: UnitedHealth Group released its sustainability report outlining five key goals. The article was published on June 16, 2021. It was authored by Mari Devereaux.

title: UnitedHealth outlines return-to-office plan, will lift office capacity July 6
summary: UnitedHealth Group has announced its return-to-office plans, stating that capacity limits at its U.S. offices will be lifted starting July 6. This decision marks a significant step in the company's post-pandemic operational adjustments.

title: Target eyes new era of sustainability with ‘Target Forward’
summary: Target has launched "Target Forward," a new comprehensive sustainability strategy aiming to positively impact people and the planet. This plan focuses on creating sustainable brands, eliminating waste, and advancing equity for employees and communities over the next two decades. Key commitments include achieving net-zero emissions and zero waste-to-landfill by 2040, and boosting Black employee representation by 20% by 2023.

title: Biogen and Eisai Update for the Alzheimer’s Disease Community
summary: Biogen and Eisai Inc. issued an update for the Alzheimer's disease community following the accelerated FDA approval of ADUHELM™ (aducanumab-avwa) on June 7, 2021. The companies detailed their plans for completing confirmatory trials, clarified the appropriate patient population for ADUHELM, and addressed pricing, patient access, and health equity considerations. They also provided important safety information regarding the treatment, including potential side effects like Amyloid Related Imaging Abnormalities (ARIA).

title: The Top 15 U.S. Pharmacies of 2020: Market Shares and Revenues at the Biggest Companies (rerun)
summary: This article rereleases popular posts, specifically focusing on the top 15 U.S. pharmacies of 2020. The updated article discusses market shares and revenues, noting that U.S. prescription dispensing revenues reached a record $465 billion in 2020. It highlights the increasing market concentration due to vertical integration and the growing role of specialty pharmacies, which accounted for over 38% of prescription revenues.

title: 10 Stats That Demonstrate the Impact of Employer-Sponsored Health Plans
summary: A Cigna report titled "The Heart of a Healthy Workforce: Employer-Sponsored Health Plans are Key to Economic Prosperity" highlights the significant impact of employer-sponsored health plans on employee well-being, business productivity, and economic prosperity. The article provides ten statistics demonstrating this impact, including improved employee engagement and retention, reduced healthcare costs for employers, and substantial socioeconomic value to the U.S.

title: 7 Tips for Coping with Scan Anxiety
summary: This article provides seven tips for cancer survivors to cope with "scanxiety," the anxiety experienced before or after medical scans like X-rays, CT scans, or MRIs. It highlights that such anxiety is normal and offers strategies like distraction, sharing experiences, meditation, exercise, self-care, understanding result delivery, and acknowledging feelings to manage stress and fear. The advice aims to help patients stay calm and confident throughout their survivorship journey.

title: Walmart teams with Novo Nordisk to launch private brand analog insulin
summary: Walmart is collaborating with Novo Nordisk to introduce its first private label analog insulin, ReliOn Novolog, which will be sold exclusively in Walmart and Sam's Club pharmacies. This initiative aims to provide insulin at a significantly lower price point, saving consumers between 58% and 75% compared to other insulin products. The move expands Walmart's ReliOn diabetes portfolio and follows other efforts by the retailer to increase access to affordable healthcare and medications for its customers.

title: Obesity Drug's Promise Now Hinges On Insurance Coverage
summary: Wegovy, a new obesity drug, has shown significant weight loss results in clinical trials, tripling the average weight loss compared to other drugs. Despite its effectiveness and good safety profile, its high cost of $1,000 to $1,500 per month raises concerns about insurance coverage, which is crucial for patient access. Many private insurers do not cover obesity drugs, and Medicare specifically excludes them, creating a major barrier for the millions who could benefit from this long-term treatment.

title: UnitedHealth's limits on out-of-network care seen as surprise billing ban reaction
summary: UnitedHealth is reportedly limiting out-of-network care, a move seen as a reaction to the surprise billing ban. This policy change could have significant implications for healthcare providers and patients regarding access to and coverage for medical services. The specifics of how these limits will be implemented and their broader impact on the healthcare landscape are key concerns.

title: UnitedHealthcare Introduces the Use of Predictive Analytics to Expand its Capabilities to Address Social Determinants of Health
summary: UnitedHealthcare has introduced predictive analytics to identify individuals in employer-sponsored benefit plans who may need support for social determinants of health, such as access to nutritious food or affordable housing. This new capability builds on existing initiatives for Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries and aims to improve well-being, lower costs, and enhance engagement in clinical intervention programs. Call center advocates connect individuals to low- or no-cost community resources based on identified needs, leveraging data from UnitedHealthcare members and broader market analyses.

title: HCA AND THE FUTURE OF HEALTHCARE
summary: This article discusses HCA Healthcare's partnership with Google Cloud for digital transformation, its controversial past involving fraud and an insider trading scandal, and its subsequent comeback through strategic acquisitions and a return to public markets. It analyzes HCA's financial performance, growth strategies, and future prospects, especially concerning expanding into new healthcare markets like senior living and outpatient care. The author evaluates whether HCA stock is a good buy, considering its aggressive expansion, debt management, and potential long-term growth despite short-term revenue concerns.

title: Changemakers: Susan Diamond, CFO, Humana
summary: Susan Diamond, CFO of Humana, discusses the company's strategy to disrupt the traditional home health model by integrating payer and provider services, focusing on value-based care. She highlights Humana's efforts to create a full continuum of home-based care capabilities, including investments in Kindred at Home, and the importance of interoperability and real-time information access in health care. Diamond also reflects on past career experiences and Humana's role in advancing higher-acuity care in the home, particularly accelerated by the pandemic.

title: How The Pandemic Triggered The Obesity Surge In America
summary: A new study reveals a significant increase in childhood obesity during the pandemic, with rates rising from 13.7% to 15.4% among children aged 2-17. This surge mirrors weight gain observed in adults and disproportionately affected younger, poorer, Hispanic, and African-American populations. The article highlights that this trend exacerbates a long-standing issue of rising obesity rates in America, noting that such early-life obesity can lead to increasingly severe health problems and a diminished quality of life for future generations.

title: Maker of computerized cardiac models HeartFlow to go public via $2.4B SPAC merger
summary: HeartFlow, a company specializing in computerized heart models for coronary diseases, announced plans to go public through a $2.4 billion SPAC merger with Longview Acquisition Corp. II. The deal is expected to provide $400 million in cash for growth and product development. HeartFlow's FDA-cleared FFRCT Analysis tool uses CT scan data to create personalized 3D heart models, aiding in diagnosing and treating coronary artery disease.

title: Profits swell when insurers are also your doctors
summary: UnitedHealth Group is significantly increasing its profits by acquiring and owning a larger part of the healthcare system, specifically medical providers. This strategy allows the company to retain more of the premiums it collects, as demonstrated by the substantial rise in "intercompany eliminations." This approach circumvents federal caps on insurance profits by shifting revenue to the provider side, a model now being mimicked by other insurers.

title: Gelesis, a Consumer-Focused Biotherapeutics Company and the Maker of Plenity®, to Become a Publicly Traded Company via Merger with Capstar Special Purpose Acquisition Corp.
summary: Gelesis, a biotherapeutics company known for its weight management product Plenity®, announced its merger with Capstar Special Purpose Acquisition Corp. The transaction values the combined company at an implied market value of approximately $1.3 billion and an enterprise value of $1.0 billion, aiming to fund the full commercial launch of Plenity and expand manufacturing. The combined company's securities are expected to trade on the NYSE under the symbol "GLS."

title: Consumer Spotlight: Cosmetics, Men’s Grooming and a Shift to Personal Care
summary: The men's cosmetics industry is experiencing substantial growth, driven by changing consumer preferences of millennials and Gen Z, a push towards gender-neutral products, and the influence of K-pop culture. The market is expected to reach $183 billion by 2027, with legacy brands acquiring niche companies and an increasing demand for sustainable and personalized skincare. This indicates a secular shift in purchasing habits, creating significant opportunities in the consumer beauty space.

title: Column: Our top private health insurer is rolling in cash. And it's reducing coverage
summary: David Lazarus critiques UnitedHealthcare, the largest private health insurer, for reducing coverage despite significant profits. The company initially delayed a policy to deny emergency care coverage and is proceeding with limits on out-of-network treatment, particularly for residential and rehabilitation facilities. Lazarus argues that these moves highlight the profit-driven nature of the U.S. healthcare system and calls for a single-payer system to prioritize patient well-being over corporate profits.

title: UnitedHealthcare to Provide Millions of Members with Year-Long Access to the Peloton App
summary: UnitedHealthcare and Peloton are partnering to offer millions of UnitedHealthcare members year-long access to the Peloton App or a four-month waiver for an All-Access Membership at no additional cost, starting September 1. This collaboration aims to make fitness and wellness more accessible, building on the increased demand for at-home exercise sparked by the COVID-19 pandemic. The program supports both new and existing Peloton members by integrating exercise into daily routines through a variety of live and on-demand classes.

title: Anthem, Humana drop $140M to launch a next-generation pharmacy benefit management platform
summary: Anthem and Humana have invested $138.3 million to launch DomaniRx, a new pharmacy benefit management (PBM) platform, in partnership with SS&C. This joint venture aims to disrupt the PBM market by offering enhanced data analytics, end-to-end transparency on drug costs, and a cloud-based claims adjudication platform. The initiative seeks to address issues within the PBM landscape, where a few major players dominate, and to make prescription drug pricing more transparent and efficient for payers and patients.

title: Anthem, Humana join hedge fund administrator to launch technology for PBMs
summary: Anthem and Humana have formed a joint venture called DomaniRx with hedge fund administrator SS&C Technologies Holdings to develop a cloud-native claims adjudication platform for pharmacy benefit managers. SS&C Technologies will hold the majority stake, while Anthem and Humana will each hold a minority interest, investing approximately $925 million collectively. The platform aims to disrupt the industry with open-source technology, providing insights from millions of claims transactions and enabling customization for clients like Humana, its first customer.

title: UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Aetna all unveil new policies restricting biologics use
summary: UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, and Aetna have all introduced new policies that restrict the use of biologics. This development could significantly impact patients relying on these advanced medications and the healthcare providers prescribing them. The article highlights how these major insurers are tightening control over biologic drug access.

title: ¿Cuáles son las empresas españolas con más ingresos en 2020?
summary: The article discusses the "Fortune Global 500" list for 2021, highlighting Spanish companies with the highest revenues in 2020. Banco Santander, Telefónica, and ACS lead among Spanish firms but have fallen in global rankings due to the pandemic's impact. Inditex and Naturgy Energy notably dropped off the list, while Walmart topped global rankings for the eighth consecutive year.

title: Extra Bullish on Healthcare? Consider Leverage, the CURE ETF
summary: This article suggests considering the Direxion Daily Healthcare Bull 3X ETF (CURE) for investors who are extra bullish on the healthcare sector due to ongoing dynamic trading opportunities despite market volatility. CURE seeks 300% daily performance of the Health Care Select Sector Index and has shown a 56% gain in 2021, driven in part by strong Q2 earnings from holdings like United Health. The article emphasizes that CURE is intended for seasoned investors due to the inherent risks of leveraged ETFs.

title: Omada Health Announces Steve Cook as New Chief Financial Officer Amid Significant Company Growth
summary: Omada Health has appointed Steve Cook as its new Chief Financial Officer. Cook, formerly of One Medical and Salesforce, brings significant financial planning experience as Omada Health continues to expand its digital care programs, workforce, and member enrollments. The company is focusing on employee growth, a remote-first policy, record enrollments, and engagement amidst its significant growth period.

title: CVS hedges on 2022 earnings growth target as COVID-19 uncertainty persists
summary: CVS Health Corp is hedging on its 2022 double-digit earnings growth target due to persistent uncertainty caused by COVID-19 vaccination and testing demand, as well as medical costs. The company revised its 2021 COVID-19 vaccine administration estimates downward but raised its 2021 adjusted earnings forecast after exceeding second-quarter profit estimates. These challenges, along with a planned minimum wage hike, could impact its future growth.

title: AHA continues to voice concerns over proposed UnitedHealth Group acquisition of Change Healthcare
summary: The American Hospital Association (AHA) has again expressed serious concerns to the Department of Justice’s Antitrust Division regarding UnitedHealth Group’s proposed acquisition of Change Healthcare. The AHA argues that any potential remedy is unlikely to resolve the anticompetitive impacts of the deal. They believe the merger would distort patient care and claims processing, detrimentally affecting consumers and healthcare providers.

title: Drug Overdose Deaths Reached New High in 2020, Says CDC
summary: Drug overdose deaths in the U.S. reached an all-time high of over 93,000 in 2020, a nearly 30% increase from the previous year, according to a CDC report. The majority of these deaths were attributed to opioids, particularly synthetic opioids like fentanyl, and the COVID-19 pandemic is cited as a significant contributing factor due to increased stress, limited access to treatment, and isolation. Family physicians are urged to be vigilant in screening patients for behavioral health and substance abuse issues and to offer medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder.

title: Amid COVID, 2.5 mln people sign up for U.S. health insurance -White House
summary: The White House announced that 2.5 million people have enrolled in health insurance through Affordable Care Act marketplaces during a special enrollment period extended due to COVID-19. This initiative, part of President Biden's efforts, aims to make healthcare more affordable and accessible, especially for those who lost employer-related insurance during the pandemic. The American Rescue Plan further reduced premiums, saving families an average of $40 per person per month.

title: Teladoc backs national virtual primary care plan for self-funded companies
summary: Aetna has announced new nationwide virtual primary care plans for self-funded employers, built around Teladoc's physician care team model. These plans will integrate virtual visits with continuous relationships with virtual care physicians, access to other virtual services, and in-person care options through Aetna's network and CVS Health services. The initiative aims to cater to the growing demand for telehealth solutions, while also offering options for physical appointments when needed.

title: UnitedHealth settles charges it denied mental health, substance abuse coverage
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. has agreed to pay approximately $15.7 million to settle federal and New York state charges that it illegally denied coverage for mental health and substance abuse treatment. The company was accused of imposing more restrictive limits and using algorithms that hindered treatment for these conditions compared to physical health issues. UnitedHealth has stated it no longer uses the challenged practices and is committed to providing care consistent with federal and state rules.

title: Centene back in good graces of Ohio Medicaid after $88M settlement
summary: Ohio Medicaid has included Buckeye Health Plan, a Centene subsidiary, in its $20 billion managed-care contract, despite earlier deferral due to a lawsuit. This decision follows an $88.3 million settlement between Centene and Ohio concerning allegations of Medicaid fraud. While Centene does not admit fault, the settlement and inclusion provide Ohioans with more choices for health plans within the Medicaid program.

title: UnitedHealth Group loses in overpayments case
summary: A U.S. Court of Appeals reversed a 2018 district court decision, ruling against UnitedHealth Group in an overpayments case. The court rejected UnitedHealth's claims that a CMS rule requiring Medicare Advantage plans to report and return identified overpayments within 60 days resulted in underpayments, stating that the Medicare statute's text, structure, or logic does not apply actuarial equivalence to the overpayment-refund obligation. Separately, UnitedHealth Group and its affiliates also agreed to pay over $13 million to resolve litigation regarding federal and state mental health parity laws.

title: UnitedHealthcare acquires Golden Valley-based health plan PreferredOne
summary: UnitedHealthcare has acquired Golden Valley-based health insurer PreferredOne, expanding its presence in the Minnesota health insurance market. The acquisition allows UnitedHealthcare to deepen relationships with employers and gain geographic expertise, particularly in the self-funded and fully-insured plan segments. This move strengthens UnitedHealthcare's competitive position in its home state, while Fairview Health Services, PreferredOne's former owner, focuses on healthcare provision.

title: UnitedHealth acquires insurer PreferredOne from Fairview Health, expanding reach in Minnesota
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. is expanding its presence in the Minnesota insurance market by acquiring PreferredOne from Fairview Health. While UnitedHealth is the nation's largest health insurer, this deal represents a significant move to strengthen its position within its home state. The article also mentions a previous acquisition by UnitedHealth Group Inc. of Empresas Banmedica for $2.8 billion in December 2017.

title: Winnebago Industries moving corporate HQ from Iowa to Eden Prairie
summary: Winnebago Industries is relocating its corporate headquarters from Forest City, Iowa, to Eden Prairie, Minnesota, effective December 1. The company, which manufactures motor homes, trailers, and boats under brands like Winnebago and Grand Design, has maintained executive offices in Eden Prairie since 2016. While moving its headquarters, Winnebago will continue to operate its manufacturing hub and retain 2,100 employees in northern Iowa, with plans for growth there.

title: West Elects Molly Joseph to the Board
summary: West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. (NYSE: WST) has announced the election of Molly Joseph to its Board of Directors, bringing the total number of directors to 11. Joseph, former CEO of UnitedHealthcare Global, brings extensive experience in leading medical delivery and health insurance systems to West's board. Her expertise is expected to be a valuable asset to the company's mission in injectable drug administration.

title: Joy Fitzgerald, UnitedHealth Group’s Chief Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Officer, Shares Her Passion for a Brighter Future
summary: Joy Fitzgerald, UnitedHealth Group’s Chief Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Officer, emphasizes the importance of women owning their power and advocating for gender equality in the workplace. She discusses the need to dismantle old habits that make women feel they need to over-prove themselves and highlights her commitment to creating change for future generations.

title: The Interconnected Nature of Profitability and Sustainability
summary: This article argues that long-term business success is inextricably linked to sustainability, questioning whether an unsustainable company can thrive in the long run. It emphasizes that businesses must broaden their time frame for success, redefine it beyond mere profit maximization to include shared value, and adopt comprehensive measurement tools that account for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) impacts. The piece suggests a paradigm shift from profit maximization to value optimization, highlighting examples like SAP's cost avoidance through climate action and Unilever's Sustainable Living Plan.

title: Smoked Fish Market to See Huge Growth by 2026 | High Liner Foods, ConAgra, Unilever, General Mills
summary: A new research publication by Advance Market Analytics predicts significant growth for the global smoked fish market by 2026. This growth is attributed to increasing consumer demand for healthy, protein-based, and ready-to-eat food options, alongside innovations in smoking technologies. Key players in the market include Kraft Heinz, High Liner Foods, ConAgra, Unilever, and General Mills, among others.

title: Column: Delta Air Lines' raising insurance rates for unvaccinated makes sense — and it's a scary idea
summary: Delta Air Lines is imposing a $200 monthly surcharge on unvaccinated employees' health insurance, citing the financial burden of COVID-19 hospitalizations. While acknowledging the "cold logic" that those likely to get sick should pay more, the author raises concerns about this "slippery slope" leading to higher rates for individuals with other health conditions or lifestyle choices deemed "unhealthy." The column ultimately argues that while Delta's intent to encourage vaccination is understandable, penalizing employees based on health risks, even those tied to personal choices, is a concerning and potentially inhumane public policy.

title: EQT Exeter Acquires 8 Delaware County Buildings for $48.5 Million
summary: EQT Exeter has acquired eight buildings in the Naamans Creek Business Center in Boothwyn, Delaware County, for $48.5 million. The properties, totaling 265,757 square feet, were 100 percent leased to 16 tenants, including Pentec Health and UnitedHealth Group, at the time of the acquisition. SSH Real Estate sold the buildings to EQT Exeter, having previously purchased them in multiple transactions for a total of $28 million, indicating a significant increase in industrial property values over time.

title: UnitedHealth Group To Expand Obamacare To Seven New States In 2022
summary: UnitedHealth Group is set to expand its health insurance products into seven new states for individual and family coverage in 2022, building on the increased enrollment seen during the Biden administration's special enrollment period. The UnitedHealthcare unit, which had previously scaled back its presence in Obamacare exchanges, is now re-entering and growing in markets like Alabama, Florida, and Texas. This expansion reflects a more stable market and a need for coverage options, contrasting with the Trump administration's efforts to curtail Obamacare.

title: NC patients sue insurance company over claims of thousands of dollars in surprise bills
summary: Six Charlotte-area patients and Providence Anesthesiology Associates filed a class-action lawsuit against UnitedHealth Group after the insurer dropped Providence from its network, leading to unexpected and large medical bills for patients. UnitedHealth Group disputes the claims, stating that Providence is the entity responsible for "exorbitant charges" and that it will defend itself against the lawsuit. The dispute stems from UnitedHealth's alleged offer of a 60% decrease in reimbursement rates to Providence, which had been in-network for 27 years.

title: United Health Foundation Donates $1 Million to Support Residents of Louisiana Affected by Hurricane Ida
summary: The United Health Foundation has donated $1 million to assist Louisiana residents in recovering from Hurricane Ida. The funds will be distributed among four community-based organizations to provide immediate assistance and support long-term rebuilding efforts. Additionally, UnitedHealth Group is offering support to its members and employees, including access to care, early prescription refills, and a free emotional support helpline.

title: Humana/Anthem PBM Venture Could Attract More Blues Plans
summary: Humana Inc. and Anthem, Inc. have partnered with SS&C Technologies Holdings, Inc. to form DomaniRx, a new joint venture aimed at creating a cloud-based PBM claims adjudication platform. This initiative, valued at $925 million, seeks to provide a "best-in-class" platform, with Humana as its first customer, and is expected to attract Blues plans and Medicare Advantage plans due to its potential for innovation, efficiency, and market competition against the "big three" PBMs. Industry experts suggest it could also facilitate greater integration of pharmacy benefits with overall care management.

title: 3 Healthcare Stocks Cathie Wood Loves Right Now
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest has recently increased its positions in three healthcare stocks: Pfizer, Signify Health, and Teladoc Health. The article explains Wood's rationale for investing in these companies, citing Pfizer's dividend and vaccine success, Signify Health's profitable niche in value-based care, and Teladoc Health's comprehensive digital health services despite competition.

title: How to find the right OB-GYN for you
summary: Choosing the right OB-GYN and hospital is a crucial decision for expecting parents. This article emphasizes that the best choice is subjective, depending on individual healthcare needs, values, and goals. It advises first selecting a hospital based on factors like location, amenities, medical infrastructure, and care philosophy, then finding an OB-GYN affiliated with that facility who aligns with personal preferences and specific health needs.

title: Centene Will Group Medicare Offerings Under Wellcare Brand
summary: Centene is consolidating all its Medicare offerings under the Wellcare brand to streamline member experience and improve engagement. This move follows Centene's acquisition of Wellcare in 2020 for $17.3 billion and aims to better align with the company's strategy as its Medicare footprint grows. The article also touches on Centene's other acquisitions, like that of Magellan Health, and similar acquisition trends among other major payers such as Humana and UnitedHealth Group.

title: Humana says pandemic is slowing routine care again
summary: Humana reports a recent increase in COVID-19 hospitalizations among its Medicare Advantage members, coinciding with a decline in non-COVID inpatient and outpatient care. This trend, similar to last year, suggests that the pandemic is once again causing delays in routine medical care, which could impact Humana's financial performance.

title: U of M Looks to Tackle Medical Device Cybersecurity
summary: The University of Minnesota is launching a new center dedicated to medical device cybersecurity, funded by five major healthcare companies including Boston Scientific and Medtronic. This initiative aims to address increasing cybersecurity threats to cloud-based medical devices and will focus on research, technology development, education, and training. The center will be led by veterinary medicine professor Katey Pelican and will host roundtables, a hackathon, and develop a short course and internship program.

title: Feds penalize UnitedHealthcare plans for underspending premiums on medical care for seniors
summary: The federal government has sanctioned three UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plans for failing to spend a minimum of 85% of premium revenue on medical care for seniors for three consecutive years. These sanctions prevent the Minnetonka-based insurer from enrolling new subscribers in these plans until 2023, though existing members will not be affected. UnitedHealthcare attributes the underspending to patients deferring care during the COVID-19 pandemic, stating that they typically meet or exceed the required medical loss ratio.

title: Digital Surgery Leader Caresyntax Extends Series C to Total Raise of $130 Million; BlackRock Funds and ProAssurance Join to Accelerate Growth
summary: Caresyntax, a leader in digital surgery, announced a $30 million extension to its Series C funding round, bringing the total raise to $130 million. BlackRock Funds and ProAssurance joined as investors, aiming to accelerate the company's growth and platform development. The funding will support new data solutions for value-based care providers and expand Caresyntax's risk management model in the United States.

title: Delta’s Extra $200 Insurance Fee Shows Vaccine Dilemma for Employers (Published 2021)
summary: Delta Air Lines has implemented a policy requiring unvaccinated employees to pay an additional $200 per month for health insurance, starting November 1. This move, which comes after one vaccine received full federal approval, represents a distinct approach compared to companies mandating vaccines. Delta states this is to increase vaccination rates and noted that recent COVID-19 hospitalizations among its employees were all unvaccinated, costing the company approximately $50,000 per stay.

title: Cigna Foundation Expands Commitment to Help Thousands of Students, Educators, and Families Access Healthy Food, Mental Health Support
summary: The Cigna Foundation is expanding its commitment to support students, educators, and families by addressing food insecurity and mental health challenges. They are allocating $2.2 million from their Healthier Kids For Our Future® program to 16 schools with low-income student populations. These funds will support programs designed to eliminate food insecurity, encourage mindfulness, teach resiliency, and reduce loneliness and depression among students, in partnership with local nonprofits.

title: CVS to hire 25,000 pharmacy, retail workers
summary: CVS Health Corp. announced a plan to hire 25,000 clinical and retail workers to meet the growing demand for COVID-19 vaccinations and testing, as well as an anticipated increase in flu cases. Most of the positions are for licensed pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, and nurses at CVS Pharmacy locations, with additional roles in retail stores. This hiring drive comes amidst a tight labor market and follows CVS's earlier announcement to raise its minimum hourly wage to $15 by July 2022.

title: Johnson & Johnson says additional dose boosts Covid vaccine efficacy
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced that a global study revealed its Covid-19 vaccine is more effective as a two-dose regimen, showing 75% efficacy against moderate to severe cases globally and 94% in the U.S., with 100% effectiveness against severe disease. The company also stated that the efficacy of its single-shot vaccine does not wane and that a booster dose further enhances protection, submitting this data to the FDA and other regulators. These findings could support broader booster availability and increase the vaccine's usage.

title: Should You Buy Merck Stock At $72?
summary: The article analyzes Merck (NYSE: MRK) stock, concluding that it is undervalued at its current price of around $72. Despite underperforming the S&P 500, the company has seen significant revenue and net income growth, driven largely by its oncology drug Keytruda. The authors project a potential price of $91, suggesting the stock is a buying opportunity for long-term gains.

title: At U.S. Bank under Cecere, doing a giant deal takes 'discipline'
summary: U.S. Bank CEO Andrew Cecere greenlit the company's largest deal in two decades: the $8 billion acquisition of MUFG Union Bank. Cecere emphasized a disciplined approach to mergers and acquisitions, stressing the importance of meaningful opportunities and aligning with U.S. Bank's growth strategy, particularly in the faster-growing West Coast market. The acquisition is expected to increase U.S. Bank's size by 20% and includes plans to integrate MUFG Union Bank's customer activity onto U.S. Bank's systems, despite initial IT risk management concerns.

title: 2021 CIO of the Year ORBIE Awards: Jorge Populo focuses on innovation in role at UnitedHealthcare
summary: Jorge Populo of UnitedHealthcare is recognized as a Super Global Finalist in the 2021 Twin Cities CIO of the Year ORBIE Awards. These awards celebrate chief information officers for their excellence in technology leadership. Populo is specifically highlighted for his focus on innovation within his role at UnitedHealthcare.

title: UCF moves in cancer center tenants, plans future expansions to Lake Nona campus
summary: UCF has opened its Lake Nona Cancer Center, which is now home to various cancer research and treatment tenants. The university has plans for future expansions to its Lake Nona campus, following the recent opening of a hospital nearby.

title: The Watchdog — With Andrew Mais
summary: Andrew Mais, Connecticut's Insurance Commissioner, navigated the insurance industry through the COVID-19 pandemic and addressed issues like premium refunds and business interruption policies. He also spearheaded initiatives tackling racial discrimination within the insurance sector, including co-chairing the NAIC's Special Committee on Race and Insurance. Mais, who is set to become NAIC president in 2024, has focused on balancing industry needs with consumer protection, encouraging innovation, and promoting diversity and inclusion.

title: Discrimination Suit Filed Against UnitedHealth Group by Former Employee
summary: A former employee, Sharnett Bush, has filed a discrimination lawsuit against UnitedHealth Group Incorporated and Optum Services, Inc. alleging race and disability discrimination. Bush claims a hostile work environment, retaliation after taking disability leave for stress and migraines, and wrongful termination after developing further health issues despite requesting accommodations. The lawsuit seeks various financial damages and is represented by Hogie & Campbell.

title: Sun Life Boosts U.S. Business With DentaQuest Buy
summary: Canadian insurer Sun Life has agreed to acquire DentaQuest for $2.48 billion, aiming to expand its presence in the U.S. publicly-funded dental benefits market. This acquisition will double Sun Life's U.S. employee benefits business by revenue and position it as a leader in government dental benefits, adding an estimated US$100 million in underlying profit in its first year. DentaQuest, currently owned by the nonprofit CareQuest Institute for Oral Health and private equity firm Centerbridge, services over 33 million members and is projected to have $2.7 billion in revenue for 2021.

title: Startup PBMs' ties to legacy competitors spark transparency questions
summary: The article "Startup PBMs' ties to legacy competitors spark transparency questions" by Nona Tepper, published on October 5, 2021, discusses concerns about the relationships between new Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) and established PBM companies. This connection raises questions regarding transparency within the PBM industry.

title: The hospital of the future: Contactless payments, happy patients
summary: This article discusses the growing demand for contactless payments in healthcare, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights how hospitals can evolve their payment systems to meet consumer preferences, emphasizing a phased approach and cross-functional team collaboration. The piece also notes the evolving strategic role of hospital CFOs in driving these technological changes to improve patient experience and operational efficiency.

title: UnitedHealth Group to require COVID-19 vaccine for many U.S. employees
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced a COVID-19 vaccine mandate for many of its U.S. employees, effective by November 30, with exemptions for medical or religious reasons. This move by the nation's largest health insurer aligns with a growing trend in the healthcare sector and possibly federal contractor requirements. Other healthcare organizations like Allina Health System and Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation have also implemented mandates, with varying compliance rates.

title: Teladoc takes its primary care service nationwide with Aetna slated to roll out in early 2022
summary: Teladoc is expanding its Primary360 virtual primary care service nationwide to commercial health plans, employers, and other payers, with Aetna launching in early 2022. The service aims to increase access to primary care, detect chronic diseases early, and provide a unified healthcare experience. Initial results show the program is helping members with diagnoses and utilizing other Teladoc services, highlighting the growing market for tech-enabled primary care.

title: Dexcom taps Garmin for first real-time API integration
summary: Dexcom has announced its first real-time API integration partner, Garmin, following FDA clearance to allow third parties to access its continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data. This partnership will enable users to view their blood glucose levels and trends directly on Garmin wearables and cycling computers, offering a crucial tool for managing blood sugar during physical activity. Dexcom is also working on its next-generation CGM, the G7, and has previously identified Livongo, Welldoc, and UnitedHealthcare's Level2 as other partners utilizing its real-time connectivity solutions.

title: UnitedHealth Group's latest profit soars past $4 billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported a third-quarter profit exceeding $4 billion, prompting the company to raise its financial guidance for the year. The Minnetonka-based health care giant's strong performance was driven by its Optum division, despite ongoing challenges from COVID-19 costs and staffing shortages across the healthcare industry.

title: Intelerad Acquires Ambra Health to Become a Global Industry Leader in Cloud PACS and Enterprise Imaging
summary: Intelerad Medical Systems has acquired Ambra Health, combining two KLAS Research category leaders to create a superior cloud solution for diagnostic imaging. This acquisition significantly expands Intelerad's capabilities, adding Ambra's robust cloud VNA and image exchange functionality, and allows the combined company to enhance distributed radiology, collaborative care, and life science research. The move underscores the growing trend of hospitals and health systems adopting cloud-based imaging solutions to improve accessibility and patient outcomes.

title: Report says UnitedHealth Group was top recipient of questionable Medicare payments
summary: A federal agency disclosed that UnitedHealth Group was the top recipient of questionable Medicare risk-adjustment payments in 2017, receiving $3.7 billion. These payments were based on billing practices using patient chart reviews and health risk assessments, which investigators are concerned might be improperly inflating payments. UnitedHealth Group defended its practices, while the OIG raised questions about payment integrity and recommended CMS investigate the appropriateness of these payments.

title: Alzheimer’s Drug Is Bonanza for Biogen, Most Likely at Taxpayer Expense (Published 2021)
summary: Biogen's new Alzheimer's drug, Aduhelm, which was approved despite scientific objections and scant evidence of efficacy, is projected to be a major financial success for the company. The drug is priced at $56,000 annually per patient, with additional monitoring costs, and its significant expenses are expected to be largely covered by Medicare, potentially increasing insurance premiums and out-of-pocket costs for families.

title: UnitedHealth lawsuit claims TeamHealth upcoded claims for $100M in fraud
summary: UnitedHealthcare has filed a lawsuit against physician staffing firm TeamHealth, alleging the company upcoded for services to the tune of $100 million. TeamHealth's CEO claims the lawsuit is a distraction from a separate suit filed by TeamHealth against UnitedHealthcare over underpayments, alleging UnitedHealth profits by downcoding claims. This forms part of an ongoing dispute between the two companies, including previous lawsuits over payment withholding and out-of-network reimbursements.

title: Precision payments startup Anomaly gets $17M to reduce wasteful spending
summary: Anomaly, a healthcare startup, has secured $17 million in Series A and seed funding to combat wasteful spending in the healthcare payments system. The company leverages artificial intelligence and machine learning to identify and prevent overpayments and billing errors, aiming to reduce friction between payers and providers. Anomaly's technology helps curb the estimated $300 billion annually lost to payment errors, improving precision in healthcare financial transactions.

title: UnitedHealthcare to become first for-profit HMO in Minnesota's Medicaid program
summary: UnitedHealthcare will become the first for-profit HMO in Minnesota's Medicaid program, a significant change stemming from a 2017 law allowing for-profit competition. This contract award enables the Minnetonka-based company to expand its business in its home state, offering beneficiaries in the seven-county metro area another health plan option. The move ends a nearly 40-year tradition of exclusively nonprofit health insurers in the state's managed care Medicaid market, sparking discussions about the implications of private sector involvement in public health services.

title: For Veterans, Mental Health Is the Next Battlefront
summary: This article examines the significant mental health challenges faced by veterans and active-duty military members, highlighting issues like PTSD, depression, and traumatic brain injury, which are often exacerbated by deployments and the transition to civilian life. It emphasizes the persistent stigma surrounding mental health in the military culture and the challenges veterans face in accessing adequate treatment despite the availability of resources. The article also provides advice for loved ones on how to support veterans and advocates for expanded access to mental health services, especially in underserved areas.

title: The Oncology Institute of Hope and Innovation Exceeded Quality Standards and Saved Medicare More Than $1M in 2020
summary: The Oncology Institute of Hope and Innovation (TOI) saved Medicare over $1 million in 2020 through the Oncology Care Model (OCM) program, equating to more than $3,000 per patient episode. This achievement builds on nearly $5 million saved since the program's inception, while also maintaining above-average performance in OCM's Quality Measures. TOI attributes this success to its value-based oncology care model, which includes coordinated care, 24/7 symptom management, and a wide range of in-house services and clinical trials across 50 community-based practice locations.

title: Healthcare’s AI Future - In Conversation with Andrew Ng and Fei-Fei Li
summary: This article summarizes a fireside chat between AI experts Andrew Ng and Fei-Fei Li concerning the future of AI in healthcare. It covers four key takeaways: barriers to AI adoption, significant unsolved healthcare problems beyond diagnostics, the importance of empathy and collaboration between technical and non-technical professionals, and strategies for avoiding the perpetuation of bias in AI systems. The experts emphasize the need for human-centered AI that addresses operational issues and incorporates ethical considerations from the outset.

title: Judge tosses lawsuit against AARP over 'Medigap' insurance plans
summary: A federal judge has dismissed a class action lawsuit against AARP, which accused the elder advocacy group of charging an undisclosed commission for AARP-branded supplemental health insurance plans. The judge ruled that the plaintiffs failed to demonstrate actual injury, as they did not claim their plans would have been cheaper without the "royalty" payments AARP received from UnitedHealth. AARP receives 4.95% of Medigap policy payments from UnitedHealth, categorized as a "royalty" for using its intellectual property.

title: Use UnitedHealth Group 'Poor Person’s' Covered Call To Reduce Volatility
summary: This article suggests using a "poor person's covered call" strategy, a diagonal debit spread using LEAPS options, to manage volatility and reduce risk when investing in UnitedHealth Group (UNH) stock. The strategy involves buying a long-term, deep-in-the-money LEAPS call and selling a shorter-term, slightly out-of-the-money call option. While UNH has shown robust performance, this options strategy offers a way to leverage potential returns at a lower cost and limit risk compared to outright stock ownership.

title: UnitedHealth Group Supports Removing Race From Key Kidney Care Diagnostic Equation
summary: UnitedHealth Group is endorsing the elimination of race from a crucial kidney-function diagnostic equation, aligning with new recommendations from the National Kidney Foundation and the American Society of Nephrology. This move is part of UnitedHealth Group's broader effort to advance health equity and remove unintended biases in healthcare. The organization's "Addressing Clinical Bias Working Group" is actively reviewing clinical algorithms to address potential biases and reduce health disparities.

title: CVS Health sees 2022 profit meeting Street estimates as COVID-19 costs subside
summary: CVS Health announced that its 2022 adjusted profit target is expected to meet Wall Street estimates, anticipating stabilization in its health insurance unit's medical costs after a surge due to COVID-19. The company also raised its 2021 profit forecast. Despite higher medical costs in its Aetna insurance businesses, increased pharmacy sales from COVID-19 vaccines and tests helped offset these impacts.

title: 加拿大ETF：未来10年可以让你致富的3只超级科技ETF
summary: The article discusses three Canadian technology-focused ETFs that are poised for significant growth in the next decade. These include iShares Global Healthcare ETF for the rapidly expanding medical technology sector, Evolve Cyber Security ETF to capitalize on increasing cybersecurity investments, and Horizons Robotics and Automation ETF for the burgeoning robotics and AI industries. The ETFs offer investors diversified exposure to high-growth tech sectors without the need for individual stock picking.

title: CVS sometimes forces people to use its pharmacies. Now the Supreme Court will weigh in
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court is set to hear a case involving CVS Health and other major corporations that allegedly "patient steer" individuals to their own mail-order pharmacies for expensive "specialty drugs." Patients, particularly those with complex conditions like cancer and HIV/AIDS, argue that this practice, facilitated by Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs), leads to inferior care and discriminates against the disabled. CVS maintains that these policies are not intentionally discriminatory and help control costs, stressing that appellate courts have issued differing opinions on the matter.

title: Should You Invest in the Fidelity MSCI Health Care Index ETF (FHLC)?
summary: The article analyzes the Fidelity MSCI Health Care Index ETF (FHLC), a passively managed ETF offering broad exposure to the Healthcare - Broad sector. Launched in 2013, FHLC has over $2.96 billion in assets, an expense ratio of 0.08%, and a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold). The fund's top holdings include Johnson & Johnson, UnitedHealth Group, and Thermo Fisher Scientific, and it has shown strong performance with a 17.68% gain YTD as of November 2021.

title: DoubleVerify acquires OpenSlate to strengthen CTV, social video targeting
summary: DoubleVerify has acquired OpenSlate, a contextual targeting platform for CTV and social video, in a cash and stock transaction valued at $150 million. This acquisition aims to provide marketers with an end-to-end solution for optimizing their advertising efforts by combining OpenSlate's pre-campaign tools with DoubleVerify's post-flight measurement suite. The deal highlights the growing demand for alternatives to third-party cookies and strengthens DoubleVerify's position in the rapidly expanding social video and CTV markets.

title: Former Anthem VP Named President of Aspire, CareMore
summary: Catherine Campbell, former VP of strategy at Anthem, Inc., has been appointed president of CareMore and Aspire. Anthem, the parent company of Aspire and CareMore, will leverage Campbell's expertise in government programs and consumer-centric strategies. CareMore and Aspire focus on providing care to vulnerable and medically complex patient populations, with Aspire being the nation's largest non-hospice palliative care company.

title: CVS Will Close 900 Stores Over Next 3 Years, Convert to New Store Formats
summary: CVS Health plans to close approximately 900 retail stores, about a tenth of its total, over the next three years, with 300 closures annually. This move is part of the company's strategy to adapt to changing customer needs and convert to new store formats, including HealthHUB locations focused on primary care and chronic condition management. The company expects to take an impairment charge of $1 billion to $1.2 billion in the fourth quarter for the closures.

title: UnitedHealth Group taps Wilson as new chief medical officer
summary: UnitedHealth Group has appointed Margaret-Mary Wilson, M.D., as its new chief medical officer, effective December 5. Wilson, formerly executive vice president and associate chief medical officer, will lead clinical innovations with a focus on health equity, succeeding Richard Migliori, M.D. This appointment comes as UnitedHealth Group aims to address 600 million gaps in care by 2025 and enhance preventive care and cost-efficient services.

title: The case for "unbundling" self-funded health benefit programs
summary: This article discusses the benefits of "unbundling" self-funded health benefit programs for employers. By separating plan administration and medical stop-loss insurance, employers can gain better insights into claims data, choose specialized vendors, and potentially achieve significant cost savings. The article highlights that while self-funded plans aim to mitigate costs, many fail to optimize them when using bundled arrangements with large insurance carriers.

title: UnitedHealth Group names Dr. Margaret-Mary Wilson new chief medical officer
summary: Dr. Margaret-Mary Wilson, a high-ranking executive at UnitedHealth Group Inc., is set to become the company's chief medical officer beginning next month. The Minneapolis / St. Paul Business Journal reported the appointment, highlighting her existing role within the insurance giant.

title: UnitedHealth CEO sees lower COVID-19 costs ahead, keeps eye on Omicron
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. CEO Andrew Witty stated that the company expects the impact of COVID-19 on 2022 earnings to be half of that in 2021, primarily affecting its insurance business, and projected 2022 earnings of $21.10 to $21.60 per share. However, he noted it's too early to determine if the new Omicron variant will alter this outlook, emphasizing the need for scientific community assessment.

title: Nigerian-born Margaret-Mary Wilson is UnitedHealth Group’s next chief medical officer
summary: Dr. Margaret-Mary Wilson, a Nigerian-born top executive at UnitedHealth Group, has been appointed as the company's next chief medical officer, effective December 5, 2021. She will succeed Dr. Richard Migliori and lead the clinical innovations for America's largest health insurer. Wilson's extensive background includes roles in internal and geriatric medicine, patient safety, and global healthcare systems management.

title: UnitedHealth Group projects more than $300 billion in revenue next year
summary: UnitedHealth Group forecasts revenue exceeding $300 billion in 2022, projecting 10-11% growth to between $317 billion and $320 billion. This growth is expected across both its UnitedHealthcare insurance arm and its Optum health services division, with Medicare Advantage and OptumHealth identified as key drivers. The company also anticipates significant growth in adjusted earnings per share and overall profit for the coming year.

title: CVS Health, Microsoft Partner To Bring ‘Digital First’ Care To Customers
summary: CVS Health and Microsoft Corp. announced a five-year partnership to personalize care for CVS's over 100 million customers, utilizing Microsoft's technology and cloud services. The collaboration aims to accelerate CVS's digital transformation, deliver customized health recommendations, improve medication adherence, and enhance operational efficiency for front-line workers. Financial terms were not disclosed, but the initiative focuses on leveraging data and technology to improve customer experience and care delivery.

title: UnitedHealth CEO Andrew Witty promises more collaboration between Optum, insurance units
summary: Andrew Witty, CEO of UnitedHealth Group, is emphasizing increased collaboration between the company's two primary divisions: the insurance provider and the health-services business Optum. This initiative aims to foster greater synergy between the nation's largest insurer and its health care delivery/technology components.

title: Cigna’s Chief Digital Officer: The Future of Health Care is Digital-First
summary: Cigna's Chief Digital Officer, Katya Andresen, discusses how the pandemic accelerated digital transformation in healthcare, leading to increased virtual care adoption. She emphasizes a "digital-first and customer-first" mindset to enhance healthcare experiences, utilizing data for more coordinated, proactive, and personalized care, ultimately driving affordability and better outcomes.

title: Cigna, NEA lead $750 million financing deal for Bright Health
summary: Bright Health has secured $750 million in financing, led by Cigna and New Enterprise Associates (NEA). The health insurance startup projects over 50% growth next year, with anticipated revenues exceeding $6.3 billion. This significant funding will support its continued expansion and operations.

title: Bright Health banks $750M investment from Cigna Ventures, New Enterprise Associates
summary: Insurtech startup Bright Health has secured a $750 million investment from Cigna Ventures and its largest shareholder, New Enterprise Associates. The funds will be used to support Bright Health's growth and enhance its alignment model. Cigna will also lend its payer expertise, and the investment, which allows for conversion to common stock at $4.55 per share, is expected to close in January.

title: TeamHealth wins $60 mln in underpayment suit against UnitedHealthcare
summary: A Nevada state court jury ordered UnitedHealthcare Inc. to pay physician outsourcing company TeamHealth Inc. $60 million in punitive damages for underpaying for emergency care, in addition to $2.65 million in compensatory damages previously awarded. TeamHealth accused UnitedHealthcare of drastically underpaying for services, while UnitedHealthcare plans to appeal, alleging TeamHealth demands egregious rates. The healthcare dispute involves allegations of improper billing practices from both sides.

title: Insurtech Bright Health raises $750M from Cigna, NEA
summary: Insurtech company Bright Health secured a $750 million investment from Cigna Ventures and New Enterprise Associates, following a challenging third quarter but reaffirming strong revenue guidance for 2021 and 2022. The funding, expected to close in January, will support continued growth and involves the sale of convertible perpetual preferred stock. This partnership aims to expand access to affordable, personalized healthcare through Bright Health Group's alignment model.

title: Healthcare Triangle (HCTI) Acquires DevCool, an Electronic
summary: Healthcare Triangle (HCTI) announced the acquisition of DevCool, an EHR-focused healthcare IT and managed services company, a move expected to add approximately $20 million in revenues. This acquisition aims to strengthen HCTI's leadership in healthcare IT by improving patient care, reducing IT costs, and accelerating EHR deployments, especially for cloud hosting. The combined entity plans to leverage cloud technologies to enhance clinical, operational, and financial performance for healthcare providers and integrate DevCool’s client base with HCTI’s SaaS platforms.

title: Thorne HealthTech Announces Multi-Year Partnership with Professional Cycling Team, Human Powered Health
summary: Thorne HealthTech has announced a multi-year partnership with the professional cycling team, Human Powered Health. As the Official Personalized Health Solutions Partner, Thorne HealthTech will provide health testing and nutritional supplements to the team's elite athletes to enhance their performance. This collaboration highlights Thorne's commitment to personalized, scientific wellness solutions for athletes.

title: Virta Health Reveals Triple-Digit Growth With Health Plans Amid Industry Shift Towards Diabetes Reversal
summary: Virta Health has announced significant growth, working with over 20 national and regional health plans, marking a 133% year-over-year increase with insurer customers. This expansion comes as nearly half of its insurer partners, including Humana and Providence Health Plan, now offer Virta's diabetes reversal treatment to their self-funded employer groups, reaching over 5 million covered lives. The company attributes this growth to an industry-wide shift towards diabetes reversal and its clinically proven treatment, which has shown to save payers $425 per patient per month.

title: 'We do exist': Some Americans suffer life-changing COVID vaccine injuries
summary: This article details the experiences of several Americans who claim to have suffered severe, life-altering injuries after receiving COVID-19 vaccines. Individuals like Brianne Dressen, Shaun Barcavage, Cody Flint, Joel Wallskog, and Suzanna Newell describe a range of debilitating symptoms, from neurological issues and chronic pain to loss of career, and express frustration with public health agencies for what they perceive as a lack of acknowledgment and support for vaccine-injured individuals. Despite their experiences, many of them state they are not anti-vaccine but advocate for greater transparency and treatment for those who experience adverse reactions.

title: CDC narrows use of J&J vaccine due to concerns about rare blood clots
summary: The CDC has narrowed the recommended use of the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine due to concerns about a rare blood-clotting disorder called thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS). A panel of experts advised preferring Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech vaccines, although the J&J vaccine will remain available for those who prefer it. The rare blood clots are more prevalent in women aged 30 to 49, with about 15% of TTS cases being fatal.

title: Prudential Financial To Freeze Some Retiree Medical Benefits In 2022
summary: Prudential Financial plans to freeze contributions to retiree medical savings accounts (RMSA) in summer 2022 and will also limit the timeframe for retirees to use accrued funds to 20 years, rather than a lifetime. This move, similar to changes made by Vanguard, has drawn criticism from former employees who feel betrayed by the company's shift away from its long-standing benefits. Experts note this is part of a broader trend among large employers to reduce healthcare liability by shifting costs to retirees, despite the company's focus on retirement planning.

title: How's Senator Joe Manchin Tied to the EpiPen Scandal?
summary: Senator Joe Manchin's daughter, Heather Bresch, was the former CEO of Mylan, the company behind EpiPen. Bresch is criticized for overseeing a significant price increase of EpiPen and for her role in market monopolization through an agreement with Pfizer, which led to a class-action lawsuit. Manchin's wife and Mylan's campaign contributions to Manchin also draw scrutiny regarding their connections to the EpiPen controversy.

title: Cortrophin Gel Now Available in US at AllianceRx Walgreens Prime
summary: Cortrophin Gel, an injectable medication for acute flares in multiple sclerosis (MS) and other autoimmune diseases, is now available in the U.S. through AllianceRx Walgreens Prime. Relaunched by ANI Pharmaceuticals after previously falling out of use, the gel works similarly to corticosteroids to reduce inflammation during flare-ups. It is also approved for conditions beyond MS, including rheumatoid arthritis and nephrotic syndrome.

title: How the payer space changed in 2021, from virtual-first plans to digital mental health
summary: The payer space saw significant changes in 2021, driven by the acceleration of virtual care due to COVID-19. Key developments included the launch of virtual-first health plans by major insurers like UnitedHealthcare and Cigna, several insurtech companies going public, and a substantial increase in funding and adoption within the digital mental health sector. These shifts reflect a broader trend towards leveraging technology to improve access and affordability in healthcare.

title: Insperity and UnitedHealthcare Extend Relationship through 2026
summary: Insperity (NYSE: NSP) and UnitedHealthcare (NYSE: UNH) have extended their 20-year relationship for medical and dental coverage. This agreement continues medical coverage through 2026 and dental coverage through 2024, aiming to provide premium healthcare benefits to Insperity's worksite employees, increase plan participation, support national expansion, and achieve administrative cost savings.

title: Insperity and UnitedHealthcare Extend Relationship Through 2026
summary: Insperity, Inc. announced the extension of its 20-year relationship with UnitedHealthcare for medical and dental coverage. This agreement continues medical coverage through 2026 and dental coverage through 2024, aiming to provide premium healthcare benefits and achieve administrative cost savings. The partnership underscores both companies' efforts to manage rising healthcare costs.

title: Symplr to buy Midas analytics solutions suite from Conduent in $340M all-cash deal
summary: Symplr, a cloud-based data management solutions provider, is acquiring Conduent’s Midas Suite of Solutions in a $340 million all-cash deal. This acquisition will enhance Symplr's healthcare operations and GRC software portfolio with integrated quality outcomes and machine learning-based advanced analytics. The Midas suite, which generated $72 million in revenue in 2020, includes patient safety, quality, and advanced analytics solutions used by 2,200 healthcare facilities.

title: The top 20 companies on a hiring spree for remote workers this year
summary: FlexJobs released its annual report identifying the top 100 companies hiring for remote positions in 2022, with a particular focus on the top 20. The report highlights a significant increase in remote job listings and the continued demand for flexible work arrangements, driven by job seekers' preferences during the "Great Resignation." Companies like HubSpot, Mayo Clinic, and Stitch Fix are new to the list, while others like Anthem and Dell Technologies are consistent top employers for remote roles.

title: JPM 2022: Morgan Health, Kaiser Permanente partner on health equity
summary: Morgan Health and Kaiser Permanente are partnering to focus on health equity for JPMorgan Chase's California employees, beginning this month. They plan to jointly collect and report health equity metrics and introduce performance guarantees tied to health equity for JPMorgan employees starting in 2023. Morgan Health also aims to expand into new markets and integrate digital capabilities through its investment in Vera Whole Health, which is merging with Castlight Health.

title: Brazil's Rede D'or and Bueno family bid for UnitedHealth's Amil - report
summary: Brazilian hospital chain Rede D'or and the Bueno family are reportedly competing to acquire healthcare plan operator Amil, currently controlled by UnitedHealth Group. Amil, originally founded by the Bueno family, was sold to UnitedHealth Group in 2010 but has faced recent losses in its individual plans portfolio. Rede D'or's shares saw a 1.5% increase in afternoon trading following the news.

title: Entrepreneurs accuse UnitedHealth of not paying them for $1B business
summary: Two former high-level executives from UnitedHealth Group Inc. are suing the company, alleging they have not been adequately compensated for a business line they helped establish, which is now valued at over $1.5 billion. UnitedHealth Group denies these accusations.

title: Optum again a big revenue driver for UnitedHealth in 2021
summary: Optum continued to be a significant revenue contributor for UnitedHealth in 2021. The article highlights UnitedHealth Group's fourth-quarter net income of $4.07 billion, or $4.26, as reported on Wednesday. This illustrates the ongoing financial strength of the largest U.S. health insurer.

title: UnitedHealth Group Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Financial Results
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported robust financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2021, with revenues reaching $287.6 billion and double-digit growth across both Optum and UnitedHealthcare. The company also affirmed its 2022 growth and performance objectives, including projected revenues of $317 billion to $320 billion and adjusted net earnings of $21.10 to $21.60 per share. These results reflect accelerating innovation and expanding capabilities within the enterprise.

title: UnitedHealthcare partners with Walmart on free at-home COVID tests
summary: UnitedHealthcare is partnering with Walmart and other retailers to provide free at-home COVID-19 tests to over 26 million commercial insurance subscribers, a benefit mandated by the Biden administration. The insurer anticipates that reduced healthcare utilization due to the omicron variant surge may offset the cost of this testing program. This announcement coincided with UnitedHealth Group reporting strong fourth-quarter earnings, exceeding analyst expectations with profit surging 84% to over $4 billion.

title: Telemedicine and Ulcerative Colitis: An HCP Perspective
summary: Dr. Marla Dubinsky, a gastroenterologist, discusses the role of telemedicine in managing ulcerative colitis (UC) during the COVID-19 pandemic. She highlights how virtual appointments allow for continuous disease management, address patient concerns about COVID-19, and facilitate connections with various healthcare team members beyond gastroenterologists. Dr. Dubinsky also touches on overcoming technological challenges and ensuring patients continue to receive necessary care and medications.

title: Video Quick Take: UnitedHealth Group’s Madhu Palkar on Leveraging Technology to Simplify and Transform Health Care
summary: Madhu Palkar, Chief Strategy Officer at UHC Global, discusses how UnitedHealth Group is using technology to simplify and transform health care. She emphasizes that technology helps create an integrated, transparent, and easy-to-navigate experience for consumers, benefiting various stakeholders by reducing complexity and improving outcomes. Palkar also explains how digital solutions help manage health costs by integrating services, streamlining processes, and leveraging data analytics to improve access and tailor offerings for diverse global communities.
