title: Why California Medical Staffs Should Review Their Bylaws
summary: A recent court case, Bichai v. Davita, Inc., emphasizes that California medical staff bylaws cannot impose a stricter burden of proof for judicial review hearings than what is mandated by state law. The case involved a physician whose application for membership and privileges was denied, and a subsequent hearing where the medical staff's bylaws-prescribed burden of proof was found to be inconsistent with California Business and Professions Code § 809.3(b). The court ruled the initial hearing unfair, highlighting the importance for medical staffs to review and align their bylaws with statutory requirements to ensure fair peer review processes.

title: DaVita, Kent Thiry lose bid to dismiss criminal antitrust charges
summary: A federal judge has denied DaVita, Inc., and its former CEO Kent Thiry's motion to dismiss criminal antitrust charges. The charges allege that DaVita entered into illegal non-solicitation agreements with competitors, which the judge ruled falls under existing prohibitions on horizontal market allocation under the Sherman Antitrust Act. DaVita faces potential fines of up to $100 million per count, and Thiry could face up to 10 years in prison and a $1 million fine per offense.

title: Charles Berg Joins Cigna as President of U.S. Government Business & Senior Advisor
summary: Charles "Chuck" Berg has joined Cigna Corporation as President of U.S. Government Business and Senior Advisor. In this role, he will be responsible for expanding Cigna’s Medicare Advantage and Individual & Family Plan businesses and will report directly to CEO David Cordani. Berg brings extensive experience from previous leadership positions at DaVita Medical Group, WellCare Health Plans, and Oxford Health Plans.

title: Target’s Kamau Witherspoon to become Shipt CEO
summary: Kamau Witherspoon, Target's senior vice president of operations, has been appointed as the new CEO of Shipt, succeeding Kelly Caruso. He will officially take over on March 1, with Caruso transitioning to an advisory role until April 1. Witherspoon's extensive background in operations at Target, UnitedHealth Group, and Yum! Brands is expected to drive Shipt's continued growth in same-day delivery services.

title: Alphabet Stock Split: A Win for Retail Investors … And the Dow?
summary: Alphabet's 20-for-1 stock split aims to make its shares more accessible to retail investors and potentially opens the door for its inclusion in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. While fundamentally inconsequential, the split could provide a tailwind for GOOGL stock. Its impact on the Dow would also be significant, altering sector weighting and index composition considerations.

title: Anthem relies on flexible partner-not-build strategy in shift to value
summary: Anthem is pursuing a "partner-not-build" strategy for its transition to value-based care, differentiating itself from competitors like UnitedHealth and Humana which favor acquisitions. This capital-efficient approach involves partnering with clinical platforms and aggregators to bring physicians into alternative payment models, allowing Anthem flexibility and avoiding the operational burdens of ownership. The insurer believes this method is more sustainable and supports faster scaling of coverage while enabling reinvestment in other key areas.

title: CVS Health reports strong fourth quarter and full-year 2021 results, confirms 2022 full-year EPS guidance
summary: CVS Health announced strong financial results for the fourth quarter and full-year 2021, driven by growth across all segments, including significant contributions from COVID-19 testing and vaccinations. The company confirmed its 2022 full-year EPS guidance while revising its cash flow from operations guidance. Additionally, CVS Health outlined strategic omnichannel health initiatives, including retail store optimization and a dividend increase.

title: UnitedHealth was 2021's most profitable payer. Here's a look at what its competitors earned
summary: UnitedHealth Group was the most profitable payer in 2021, earning $17.3 billion, more than double its closest competitor, CVS Health, which had $7.9 billion in profit. While UnitedHealth led in profit, CVS Health generated the highest revenue for the year. All six major national payers were profitable in 2021, though Humana posted a Q4 loss and Centene landed in sixth place for the year in profitability.

title: MetLife Inc. stock falls Wednesday, underperforms market
summary: MetLife Inc. (MET) stock fell 0.06% on Wednesday, closing at $71.53, while the broader market saw mixed trading with the S&P 500 rising and the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling. The stock underperformed against competitors like Prudential PLC ADR, Assurant Inc., and UnitedHealth Group Inc. MetLife Inc. closed just $1.02 below its 52-week high reached on February 11th.

title: Zynex: Letter Indicates UnitedHealthcare Is Terminating Contract - An Undisclosed Loss Accounting For 50%+ EBITDA
summary: Strong evidence suggests UnitedHealthcare is terminating its contract with Zynex effective February 15th, an event not disclosed to investors. This would mean Zynex loses its largest payor and only national commercial network, potentially impacting 50-100% of its EBITDA. The termination is likely due to billing abuses and could lead to UHC pursuing Zynex for overpayments, posing significant downside for the stock.

title: Vertical integration secures PBMs as ‘arsonists and firefighters’ of drug prices
summary: The article discusses how the vertical integration of the three largest pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) with insurance carriers has significantly contributed to rising prescription drug costs in the U.S. Experts argue that PBMs, originally meant to manage drug benefits, now profit from both sides of the supply chain through opaque practices like spread pricing and reclassifying rebates as fees. Advocates are pushing for increased transparency and regulatory oversight at both federal and state levels to curb PBM influence and control drug prices, with some success observed in state-level legislative efforts.

title: Omada Health Closes $192 Million Series E Financing to Bring Virtual-First Care to Millions
summary: Omada Health has successfully closed a $192 million Series E funding round, led by Fidelity Management & Research Company, to expand its virtual-first chronic care services. This strategic financing will accelerate the company's growth, allowing for increased hiring, technological advancements, and deeper investment in its Insights Lab to address chronic conditions more effectively. The company has seen record growth, now serving over 1,700 customers and 550,000 members, and aims to further its mission of improving health outcomes for millions across the U.S.

title: U.S. sues to block UnitedHealth's $8 bln deal for Change Healthcare
summary: The U.S. Justice Department has sued to block UnitedHealth Group's $8 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare, arguing the deal would give UnitedHealth access to competitors' data and increase healthcare costs. Both companies provide software for processing healthcare claims, and the Justice Department claims the merger would give them at least 75% of that market. UnitedHealth stated it would vigorously defend its position, calling the Justice Department's stance "deeply flawed" and based on speculative theories.

title: Feds sue Minnesota-based UnitedHealth over company acquisition
summary: Federal regulators are suing to block UnitedHealth Group’s proposed $8 billion acquisition of technology company Change Healthcare. The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) argues that the deal would harm competition in health insurance markets and for technology used by insurers to process claims. UnitedHealth Group, which operates the largest health insurer in the United States, plans to vigorously defend the acquisition.

title: Justice Department sues to block UnitedHealth's bid for Change Healthcare
summary: The U.S. Justice Department has filed a lawsuit to prevent UnitedHealth Group from acquiring Change Healthcare in a $7.84 billion all-cash deal. The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, argues that the merger would harm competition. UnitedHealth Group has announced its intention to fight the lawsuit, calling the Justice Department's position "deeply flawed."

title: UnitedHealth unit settles Mass. drug overcharge case for $5.8 mln
summary: OptumRx, a pharmacy benefit manager unit of UnitedHealth Group Inc, has agreed to a $5.8 million settlement with the Massachusetts attorney general. The settlement resolves allegations that OptumRx overcharged for drugs covered by workers' compensation insurance in the state. As part of the agreement, OptumRx will pay the sum and implement new procedures to prevent future overcharging.

title: UnitedHealth Group Will ‘Vigorously’ Defend Against Federal Lawsuit to Block Acquisition
summary: UnitedHealth Group is facing a federal civil lawsuit filed by the Department of Justice, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison, and New York Attorney General Letitia James to block its proposed $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare. The lawsuit alleges the acquisition would harm competition in commercial health insurance markets and critical health care claims technologies, giving UnitedHealth an unfair advantage and access to rivals' sensitive information. UnitedHealth Group disputes these allegations, stating the merger would increase efficiency and lower costs, and has vowed to vigorously defend against the lawsuit.

title: Attorney General Ellison sues to block UnitedHealth Group proposed acquisition of Change Healthcare
summary: Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison has filed an antitrust lawsuit, joining the U.S. Department of Justice and the State of New York, to block UnitedHealth Group's proposed acquisition of Change Healthcare. The lawsuit alleges that the merger would significantly increase healthcare costs and decrease competition, leading to a near monopoly in certain healthcare technology markets. Ellison argues that the acquisition would give UnitedHealth Group too much market power and access to sensitive data, harming consumers, providers, and other insurers.

title: Best Fertility Insurance: IVF Coverage & More
summary: This article reviews the best fertility insurance providers, including UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Aetna, Wellcare, and Progyny, detailing what each offers in terms of IVF coverage and other fertility treatments. It explains what fertility insurance is, what it should cover (doctor's visits, diagnostics, treatments), and who should consider purchasing it. The piece also highlights how coverage varies by state and insurer, providing guidance on choosing a suitable plan.

title: The vast majority of Centene and Humana's $209 billion in revenues came from taxpayers.
summary: The article highlights that most of Humana and Centene's substantial 2021 revenues, totaling $209 billion, originated from taxpayers, despite only a small fraction of their 44 million enrollees being private-paying customers. It details how both companies have shifted focus towards government-funded programs like Medicaid and Medicare Advantage, with minimal growth in their commercial health plan sectors. The author, a former Humana employee, criticizes this trend, noting rising premiums and deductibles for commercially insured individuals.

title: ‘Keep Kent Thiry happy’: Prosecutors air statements of alleged DaVita conspiracy in court
summary: Prosecutors in a federal court case against DaVita, Inc. and its former CEO, Kent Thiry, revealed statements from co-conspirators regarding an alleged illegal scheme to restrict employee movement between companies. The Justice Department accuses them of implementing non-solicitation agreements that suppressed competition. A jury trial is scheduled, and the court is preparing for the extensive evidence and arguments related to the alleged antitrust violations.

title: WPP's Mark Read on why Coca-Cola, Google and Unilever are pivotal to the network's future
summary: Mark Read, CEO of WPP, discussed the company's strong 2021 performance, driven by growth in digital marketing, media, e-commerce, data, and technology. He highlighted the importance of strategic partnerships with major clients like Coca-Cola, Google, and Unilever for future growth and client-agency collaboration. Read also addressed WPP's response to the situation in Ukraine, its hiring plans, and adjustments to workplace strategy.

title: Multiplan’s ‘Independent’ Prices Can Be Set by Insurers, Sources Allege; Evidence in Nevada Jury Trial Corroborates Allegation
summary: A Capitol Forum investigation alleges that Multiplan's "independent" prices for out-of-network healthcare services can effectively be set by large health insurers such as UnitedHealth, Aetna, and Cigna. Evidence from a Nevada jury trial, which awarded $60 million in punitive damages to emergency room physician groups against UnitedHealthcare, corroborated these allegations, showing insurers manipulate Multiplan's algorithmic pricing through "meet or beat" target pricing and overrides. This practice, initially intended to reduce costs for insurers, can lead to increased out-of-pocket expenses for patients through balance billing and raises significant legal and regulatory risks for Multiplan and its clients, echoing past industry scandals involving price manipulation.

title: The Health Care Trend That Might Make Us Sicker
summary: The article discusses the ethical implications of health insurance companies investing in healthcare startups. It highlights potential conflicts of interest, where insurers might direct patients towards services offered by companies they have a financial stake in, potentially impacting the quality of care and exacerbating power imbalances in the healthcare system. The authors propose that regulations similar to those for physicians, such as the Stark Law and the Sunshine Act, should be extended to health insurance companies and health systems to ensure transparency and prevent self-enrichment.

title: Humana adds Cerner’s Feinberg to board amid activist pressure
summary: Humana has appointed David Feinberg, CEO of Cerner, to its board of directors following an agreement with activist investor group Starboard Value LP to refresh the board. This move is part of the health insurer's cost-cutting plan and efforts to reinvest in its Medicare Advantage business, where it recently faced lower-than-expected enrollment. Feinberg brings expertise in leveraging healthcare and patient data from his previous roles at Google and Cerner, aiming to improve clinical care and customer experience while reducing costs for Humana.

title: S&P 500 헬스케어 섹터에 투자하는 ETF - XLV ETF 소개
summary: 이 기사는 S&P 500 헬스케어 섹터에 투자하는 대표적인 ETF인 XLV(Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund)를 소개합니다. XLV는 낮은 변동성과 꾸준한 배당 성장을 특징으로 하며, 주요 제약 및 헬스케어 서비스 기업들을 포함하고 있습니다. 현재의 금리 인상기 시장 환경에서 헬스케어 섹터 투자의 이점을 강조하며, 포트폴리오의 안정성을 높이는 데 XLV가 좋은 선택이 될 수 있음을 제안합니다.

title: Encompass Health's home health unit attracts acquisition interest-sources
summary: Private equity firms, including Advent International, and companies like Aveanna Healthcare Holdings Inc., are reportedly interested in acquiring Encompass Health Corp's home health and hospice business, Enhabit. Encompass had previously announced plans to spin off Enhabit in the first half of 2022 and later stated openness to a sale or merger. The potential sale of Enhabit could be valued at up to $3 billion, with a shortage of nurses and regulatory hurdles influencing consolidation in the U.S. home care sector.

title: New $450M Investment in Cigna Ventures to Drive Health Care Transformation, Innovation, and Growth
summary: Cigna announced an additional $450 million investment in Cigna Ventures, its corporate venture fund, to accelerate health care transformation, innovation, and growth. This funding will support health tech startups focused on making health care more affordable, simple, and predictable. Cigna Ventures will concentrate investments on insights and analytics, digital health and experience, and care delivery and enablement, building on previous successful partnerships like the acquisition of MDLIVE.

title: Multiplan: Company’s Information Sharing, Meetings Practices Could Raise Antitrust Concerns, Experts Say
summary: Multiplan, a company assisting health insurers in underpaying healthcare provider bills, faces potential antitrust scrutiny due to practices revealed in recent litigation. Experts highlight concerns over Multiplan sharing sensitive information with UnitedHealth Group about competitors' rate caps and hosting annual meetings where executives from rival insurance companies discussed their successes using Multiplan's services. These actions could constitute anticompetitive information sharing and a "hub-and-spoke" conspiracy, potentially leading to antitrust liability, especially if they resulted in reduced payments to providers.

title: The Top 15 U.S. Pharmacies of 2021: Market Shares and Revenues at the Biggest Companies
summary: This article identifies the top 15 U.S. pharmacies of 2021 based on prescription dispensing revenues, which totaled $501 billion. It highlights that the top seven companies accounted for over 70% of these revenues and discusses how upcoming business changes and specialty medication trends are reshaping the pharmacy landscape. The report also touches on the significant revenue generated by pharmacies from administering COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Our Ultimate Stock-Pickers' Top 10 Buys and Sells
summary: This article identifies the top 10 high-conviction buys and sells among Morningstar's Ultimate Stock-Pickers for the fourth quarter of 2021, based on an aggregate analysis of their holdings. It highlights key companies like Microsoft and 3M as top buys and Marsh & McLennan as a prominent sell, detailing the Morningstar analysts' fair value estimates, economic moats, and investment theses for these firms. The report assists investors by providing insights into attractive investment ideas and valuation considerations.

title: Regulators put UnitedHealth-Change Healthcare Merger on Life Support
summary: The Department of Justice has filed a lawsuit to block UnitedHealth Group's $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare, Inc., disagreeing with the companies' claim that the merger would benefit consumers through streamlined healthcare processes and reduced costs. The DOJ argues that the deal would allow UnitedHealth to gain unfair access to competitors' sensitive information and control healthcare technology innovations, highlighting a shift in antitrust enforcement under the Biden administration.

title: Lawmakers Seek Investigation of Opioid Settlement Deductions
summary: Lawmakers are calling for an investigation into whether four opioid companies (Cardinal Health, McKesson Corporation, AmerisourceBergen, and Johnson & Johnson) are improperly claiming billions of dollars in tax deductions for their $26 billion opioid settlement payments. The letter to the Treasury Secretary and Attorney General highlights concerns that these deductions would shift the financial burden to taxpayers and underscores that tax code amendments in 2017 prohibit deductions for settlements related to law violations. It also questions Cardinal Health's use of a CARES Act provision for prior year tax benefits.

title: Blue Cross Blue Shield Owner Anthem Seeks to Rebrand to Elevance Health
summary: Anthem Inc., owner of several Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, plans to rebrand as Elevance Health Inc. to reflect a broader business focus beyond traditional health insurance. The company has diversified into areas like behavioral health, home-based care, and data analytics, seeking to achieve a premium valuation similar to UnitedHealth Group. While the new name aims to resonate with Wall Street and employees, branding experts suggest it might be difficult to connect with consumers who will still encounter the Anthem brand through their health coverage.

title: Anthem (ANTM) to be Renamed as Elevance Health for Rebranding
summary: Anthem, Inc. (ANTM) announced its intention to change its name to Elevance Health, Inc., subject to shareholder approval, to better reflect its expanding business beyond traditional health insurance into areas like pharmacy and behavioral health. This rebranding aims to optimize its portfolio, which serves over 118 million customers, and capitalize on its diversified services and rising virtual care usage. The company's strategic acquisitions and strong financial position are expected to drive long-term growth.

title: Oscar Health Insurance Overview: Features, Pricing, and More
summary: This article provides an overview of Oscar Health Insurance, detailing its features, pricing, and overall ratings. It covers eligibility, plan types (Classic, Simple, Saver), and pricing examples, showcasing Oscar's offerings alongside competitor comparisons and customer service reviews. While Oscar Health receives moderate ratings, it stands out for its virtual care and mobile app.

title: Anthem Inc. stock rises Wednesday, still underperforms market
summary: Anthem Inc. (ANTM) stock increased by 0.67% to $470.82 on Wednesday, outperforming the broader market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. Despite the gain, the stock remains $7.18 below its 52-week high. Competitors such as UnitedHealth Group Inc., Humana Inc., and Centene Corp. also saw increases on the same day.

title: Moderna requests FDA authorization for fourth COVID-19 shot for all adults
summary: Moderna has formally requested the FDA to authorize a fourth dose of its COVID-19 vaccine for all adults, aiming to provide flexibility to the CDC in making recommendations for additional boosters. This follows a similar request by Pfizer for emergency authorization for seniors earlier in the week. The requests are partly based on data from Israel, which has already approved a second booster for those aged 60 and older and healthcare workers.

title: Equifax, Experian, TransUnion to remove majority of medical debts from consumers' credit reports
summary: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion announced they will remove nearly 70% of medical collection debt tradelines from credit reports, starting with paid debts in July 2022 and debts under $500 in the first half of 2023. This change aims to help consumers, extend the grace period before unpaid medical debt appears on reports, and address the impact of medical debt on credit scores, especially for vulnerable populations. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau estimates significant medical debt on credit reports and is reviewing the credit reporting agencies' plans.

title: Vertically integrated payer-provider groups raise antitrust concerns
summary: The article highlights antitrust concerns surrounding vertically integrated payer-provider groups. It notes that this model, where insurers own their own providers, is drawing scrutiny from regulators. A related lawsuit mentioned involves OhioHealth, which is accused by federal and Ohio authorities of anticompetitive tactics against health insurance companies.

title: 3 Dow Stocks That Can Turn $300,000 Into $1 Million by 2030
summary: The article identifies three Dow stocks – Salesforce, UnitedHealth Group, and Visa – that have the potential to turn a $300,000 investment into $1 million by 2030. Each company is highlighted for its strong market position, consistent growth, and specific catalysts that are expected to drive significant shareholder returns. This analysis provides a long-term investment perspective on these established businesses within the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

title: UnitedHealth to buy LHC Group for $5.4 billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group is set to acquire LHC Group for $5.4 billion, signaling a deeper push into home health care. The deal, expected to close later this year, will see UnitedHealth paying $170 in cash per share of LHC's stock and integrating LHC Group into its Optum Health business. This acquisition highlights a growing trend in health care towards home-based services, influenced by the pandemic and cost-efficiency.

title: Pfizer, BioNTech obtain EU authorization for 2nd COVID-19 booster
summary: Pfizer and BioNTech have received emergency use authorization from the FDA for a second COVID-19 booster dose. This booster is approved for adults aged 50 and older, and for immunocompromised individuals aged 12 and older, who have previously received a first booster. The authorization is based on studies showing improved antibody titers against variants and increased protection against severe disease for vulnerable populations.

title: UnitedHealth’s deal with LHC highlights broader interest in home health industry
summary: UnitedHealth Group's proposed $5.4 billion acquisition of LHC Group demonstrates the increasing interest of health insurers in expanding their ownership of health care delivery, particularly in the home health sector. This trend is driven by home care's lower costs and high profitability, especially for Medicare beneficiaries. The article notes that hospitals and financial investors are also significant players in this growing home health market.

title: UnitedHealth to buy home-health firm LHC Group for $5.4B
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. has agreed to acquire LHC Group Inc., a home-health firm, for approximately $5.4 billion in cash, or $170 per share. This deal is part of UnitedHealth's strategy to expand its home-based care services through its Optum health-services arm, aiming to capitalize on the rising demand for care delivered in lower-cost settings compared to nursing homes. The acquisition is expected to close in the second half of 2022 and follows a similar move by Humana Inc., highlighting a growing trend among managed-care companies to invest in home health services.

title: How Optum’s $5.4B LHC Group Acquisition Pushes Behavioral Health Toward Value-Based Care
summary: Optum's $5.4 billion acquisition of home healthcare provider LHC Group, following its Refresh Mental Health purchase, signals UnitedHealth Group's aggressive push into value-based care across various health segments, including behavioral health. This move aims to integrate care services, improve patient outcomes, and potentially reshape the behavioral health industry's approach to reimbursement and care coordination. The acquisitions highlight Optum's strategy to leverage extensive data and algorithms to manage care more effectively and achieve better health outcomes.

title: [UPDATED] UnitedHealth Group to Acquire LHC Group for $5.5 Billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced its acquisition of LHC Group for $5.5 billion, integrating the home health and hospice provider with its Optum Health division. This acquisition, following Humana's purchase of Kindred at Home, signifies a growing interest from payers in the provider space and the expanding role of home-based care. The deal is expected to close in the second half of the year and reflects ongoing trends towards value-based care models and a focus on care in the home.

title: UnitedHealth Group Agrees to Buy LHC Group for Over $5 Billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group has agreed to acquire LHC Group for approximately $5.4 billion, integrating one of the largest home health providers with its Optum Health division. This acquisition highlights a growing trend of payers expanding into care provision, following other significant deals in the home-based care sector. The transaction is expected to close in the latter half of the year, with LHC Group shareholders receiving $170 per share.

title: UnitedHealth to Buy Home-Health Firm LHC Group for $5.4 Billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. has agreed to acquire LHC Group Inc. for approximately $5.4 billion in cash, marking a significant move into the home-health business for the managed-care company. This acquisition will add one of the largest home-health firms to UnitedHealth's Optum health-services portfolio, which already includes various healthcare facilities and services. The deal highlights a growing trend of managed-care companies investing in services that promise lower costs compared to traditional hospitals and nursing homes.

title: UnitedHealth buys in-home care company for $5.4 billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group is acquiring LHC Group, an in-home health company, for $5.4 billion, at $170 per share. LHC Group will be integrated into Optum, UnitedHealth's pharmacy benefit manager and clinic operator, to enhance its reach in the growing home health market. The deal is expected to close in the second half of 2022 and will be financially beneficial for UnitedHealth in the long term.

title: UnitedHealth to buy LHC Group for $5.4 billion in home healthcare push
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced its acquisition of LHC Group for $5.4 billion in cash, expanding its home health services amidst increased demand for home-based care. This deal follows a recent legal challenge by the U.S. Justice Department against UnitedHealth's acquisition of Change Healthcare. The acquisition is expected to be neutral to UnitedHealth's 2022 adjusted profit per share outlook and modestly add in 2023.

title: U.S. Behavioral Health Market Size, Report 2021 to 2030
summary: The U.S. behavioral health market is projected to reach US$132.4 billion by 2027, growing at a CAGR of 5.3% due to increasing prevalence of mental illnesses and substance abuse. Outpatient counseling dominated the market in 2020, along with anxiety and depression as the most prevalent disorders. The market is also experiencing rapid adoption of digital technologies and telehealth services, further boosted by the COVID-19 pandemic and supportive government policies.

title: UnitedHealth to buy home health business LHC for $5.4B
summary: UnitedHealth has agreed to acquire home health and hospice provider LHC Group for $5.4 billion. This acquisition is part of a larger trend of payers entering the home health market due to an aging population and the potential for lower-cost care delivery outside of traditional hospital settings. The deal is expected to contribute to UnitedHealth's integrated care strategy and be modestly accretive to its earnings next year.

title: Optum-Refresh Blockbuster Blazes a Consolidation Trail for the Next Mental Health Platform
summary: Optum's acquisition of Refresh Mental Health highlights the significant investment and consolidation trend in the outpatient mental health sector. This deal, along with others like Lifestance Health's IPO and KKR's Geode Health, demonstrates various strategies for scaling mental health platforms amidst high valuations and increasing interest, largely driven by the pandemic. Industry observers anticipate continued consolidation and the emergence of new national platforms as private equity investment in the space surges.

title: UnitedHealth Tries to Stop Lawsuits From Mom-And-Pop Drugstores
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. is attempting to prevent over 200 small, independent drugstores from pursuing a joint lawsuit, instead forcing them into individual arbitration. These pharmacies accuse UnitedHealth's Optum Rx unit of underpaying them by more than $100 million. UnitedHealth filed litigation in federal court in California to enforce individual arbitration for these disputes.

title: Study shows Kroger Health’s Food as Medicine Platform improves health and diet
summary: A clinical research study funded by Kroger Health found that its "Food as Medicine" platform significantly improves health and diet. The SuperWIN study, conducted by the University of Cincinnati, demonstrated that in-aisle teaching by registered dietitians combined with education on online shopping technologies increased adherence to heart-healthy diets. This research highlights the potential of retailers like Kroger to serve as important healthcare destinations through food and nutrition education.

title: Molina Moves to S&P 500 Index, Capping Huge Share Price Runup
summary: Molina Healthcare Inc. has joined the S&P 500 Index, a recognition that caps a significant share price increase of 47% over the past year. This move is seen as a "stamp of approval" by analysts, bolstering its standing for Medicaid contracts and increasing investor exposure through S&P 500 mirroring funds. Despite soaring premium revenue, Molina faced unexpected medical treatment costs in 2021, particularly from Obamacare exchange patients, and anticipates a more modest 6% revenue growth for the current year as government funding normalizes.

title: Cosm Medical raises $4.7 million CAD for its custom gynecological prosthetics
summary: Cosm Medical has secured $4.7 million CAD in an oversubscribed seed round to develop and launch its digital gynecology platform and custom gynecological prosthetics, known as Gynethotics. The medtech startup aims to change the standard of care for pelvic floor disorders by combining physiological biomarkers, AI-driven software, and 3D printing. The funding will also support further research and development, operations expansion, and team growth.

title: Optum continues buying spree and scoops up Houston-based Kelsey-Seybold Clinic: report
summary: Optum, the UnitedHealth Group arm, has reportedly acquired Kelsey-Seybold Clinic, a large multi-specialty group practice based in Houston, continuing its aggressive acquisition strategy. This deal, if closed, signifies a major investment in value-based care. The acquisition follows other significant purchases by UnitedHealth Group, including Refresh Mental Health and LHC Group, and occurs while the company is fighting to close its acquisition of Change Healthcare.

title: Which Value Stocks Are Leading the Way Over Growth?
summary: Value stocks have significantly outperformed growth stocks, particularly during the first quarter of 2022, solidifying a trend that began in 2021. While surging oil prices and energy stocks contributed significantly to this rally, healthcare companies like AbbVie and consumer defensive stocks such as Costco also played major roles. Despite their strong performance, most value stocks, with the exception of oil and gas drilling companies, are not considered overvalued.

title: Payers Can ‘Feed Their Own Machine’ With Hospice, Home Health Deals
summary: Recent acquisitions of large hospice and home health providers by insurance companies, such as UnitedHealth Group and Humana, indicate a strategy by payers to reduce financial risk and improve cost outcomes within value-based care models. These deals allow insurers to control both the provider and payer sides of healthcare networks, particularly as Medicare Advantage and other value-based payment models grow. The objective is to efficiently manage patient care, manage risk, and promote services like palliative care that reduce hospitalizations and emergency department visits, ultimately feeding the payers' own networks.

title: CEO of upstart PBM: What CVS, Cigna and other PBMs are doing in drug pricing is neither sustainable nor ethical
summary: A.J. Loiacono, CEO of Capital Rx, criticizes major PBMs like CVS, Cigna, and UnitedHealth Group, as well as the federal government, for the unsustainable and unethical state of drug pricing in the U.S. He highlights vast price discrepancies, where a drug can cost $150 with insurance but $6 with a discount card like GoodRx, arguing that the system benefits shareholders of large PBMs rather than patients. Loiacono asserts that his company and other new PBMs aim to create transparency and efficiency by allowing free communication on price between buyers and sellers, using standardized pricing.

title: KT taps Vietnam for digital healthcare and AI-powered diagnosis
summary: South Korean telecom giant KT is entering the Vietnamese healthcare market through a partnership with Hanoi Medical University. They will launch a pilot telemedicine service for chronic disease patients, research AI-powered diagnosis, and train local medical professionals. This move is driven by Vietnam's growing middle class and demand for medical services, with plans to expand to other Southeast Asian countries after establishing their presence in Vietnam.

title: Dexcom announces availability of G6 for Tricare members as formulary pharmacy benefit
summary: Dexcom announced that its G6 continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system is now available to Tricare members as a brand-name formulary pharmacy benefit. This change makes the G6 more accessible and affordable for military members, their families, and retirees with diabetes. Tricare beneficiaries can now obtain the Dexcom G6 through military treatment facility pharmacies, the retail pharmacy network, or mail-order with varying copayments, offering a faster process and more consistent costs compared to previous medical benefit access.

title: UnitedHealth Group ‘Moving at Speed’ in Bringing Together Home-Based Care Capabilities
summary: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) is rapidly expanding its home- and community-based care capabilities to accelerate its value-based care strategy. This expansion includes the anticipated acquisition of LHC Group Inc. for $5.4 billion, which will further integrate home health and other services into UnitedHealth's Optum platform. CEO Andrew Witty highlighted the success of existing programs like HouseCalls and the strategic importance of these efforts in serving populations like D-SNPs and shifting care to appropriate, often lower-cost, settings.

title: UnitedHealth CEO: Refresh Mental Health Acquisition 'Fits Right Into Value-Based Proposition'
summary: UnitedHealth Group's CEO, Sir Andrew Witty, stated that the acquisition of Refresh Mental Health aligns perfectly with the company's value-based care strategy, emphasizing the integration of behavioral health management with medical management. The deal, rumored to be over $1 billion, enhances UnitedHealth's existing behavioral health network and complements its broader strategy to merge different care components into an accessible platform for patients. This reinforces the company's focus on providing quality care across various settings, including virtual and home care, to make healthcare more affordable and convenient.

title: Why it’s a good idea to buy UnitedHealth (UNH) stock and hold it forever
summary: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) is presented as a strong long-term investment opportunity due to its leadership in the healthcare insurance market, consistent growth in customer base, and robust financial performance. Despite recent rallies, the stock is considered to be trading at a reasonable discount, supported by positive first-quarter results and raised earnings guidance for fiscal 2022. The company's strategic initiatives and strong fundamentals, including a steady uptick in payout ratio, make it an attractive option for both growth and income investors.

title: DaVita and its former CEO acquitted of U.S. antitrust charges
summary: A jury in Denver, Colorado, acquitted dialysis provider DaVita and its former CEO Kent Thiry of charges that they conspired with competitors not to hire each other's employees. The Justice Department had alleged "anti-poaching" agreements between DaVita and other companies, which the jury ultimately rejected. This verdict comes as the Biden administration focuses more on antitrust enforcement in labor markets.

title: Addus Hires Former Encompass Health Executive, Gears Up for Major Growth
summary: Addus HomeCare Corporation has appointed Cliff Blessing, former EVP of corporate development for Encompass Health’s home health and hospice business, as its new EVP and chief development officer. This strategic hire signals Addus's intention to aggressively pursue mergers and acquisitions to expand its home health and hospice service lines, moving beyond its traditional Medicaid-based personal care services. The company views acquisitions, combined with a more favorable staffing environment, as crucial for its broader growth strategy and market reach.

title: Five Takeaways from the Big Three PBMs’ 2022 Formulary Exclusions (rerun)
summary: This article analyzes the 2022 formulary exclusion lists of the three largest PBMs—Caremark, Express Scripts, and OptumRx—highlighting trends such as the continued growth of exclusions, particularly for specialty drugs. It notes baffling inconsistencies in how PBMs handle insulin and biosimilars, often favoring higher-priced options. The author also discusses the significant impact these exclusions have on patient access, out-of-pocket costs, and the potential for non-medical switching, advocating for greater transparency and research into these effects.

title: Anthem Profits Hit $1.8 Billion On Medicaid, Medicare Growth
summary: Anthem reported first-quarter profits of $1.8 billion, a significant increase driven by strong enrollment in its Medicaid and Medicare Advantage plans. The company saw an 8.4% rise in profits and a nearly 17.6% increase in revenue, leading to an updated financial outlook for 2021. Anthem plans to rebrand as Elevance Health, aiming to position itself as a holistic health partner.

title: UnitedHealth Inflated Drug Costs, Louisiana Attorney General Alleges in Suit
summary: Louisiana's Attorney General has filed a lawsuit against UnitedHealth Group Inc., alleging that its pharmacy benefits manager, Optum Rx, inflated prescription drug prices within the state's Medicaid program. The suit claims that Optum Rx used undisclosed pricing and the intricate nature of the drug supply chain to overcharge the program by billions of dollars annually. The legal action was initiated on April 13 in state court.

title: 7 Stocks to Buy If You Think Inflation Is Topping Out
summary: This article suggests seven stocks to consider buying if inflation is believed to be topping out. The author highlights that a lower-than-expected core CPI reading has led some analysts to believe the market may have seen peak inflation, shifting investment focus towards growth stocks. The recommended companies include UnitedHealth Group, Abbott Laboratories, Deere & Co., Nucor, Lam Research Corp, Qualcomm, and Nike, with each company's specific growth drivers and financial health discussed.

title: AG Healey signs off on acquisition of state’s largest independent doc group
summary: Massachusetts Attorney General Maura Healey has approved Optum's $236 million acquisition of Atrius Health, the state's largest independent physician organization. This deal will convert Atrius's assets from nonprofit to for-profit and requires review by the state's Supreme Judicial Court. The agreement includes a significant increase in the purchase price to create a foundation for health equity and a $200 million investment from Optum into Atrius.

title: UnitedHealthcare Sees Virtual Care Make Up 66% Of All Behavioral Health Claims
summary: UnitedHealthcare reported that virtual care accounted for 66% of all behavioral health claims in 2021, a significant increase from 1.5% in 2019. Overall virtual visits for UnitedHealthcare members rose by 2,500% compared to pre-pandemic levels, with behavioral health being a major driver. This trend suggests that telehealth, particularly for behavioral health, is becoming a permanent fixture in healthcare.

title: Travel nurses remain pricey, and it’s weighing on hospital profits
summary: The first quarter results from HCA Healthcare indicate that the high cost of travel nurses is having a significant impact on hospital profits, prompting the company to lower its full-year guidance. This trend, exacerbated by the pandemic, suggests that elevated labor costs may persist as nurses increasingly prefer travel roles or alternative healthcare settings. The article, exclusive to STAT+ subscribers, highlights the broader implications for the hospital sector.

title: UnitedHealth Group offers $236M to buy Massachusetts medical group
summary: UnitedHealth Group is offering $236 million to acquire Atrius Health, a large physician-led nonprofit medical group in Massachusetts, to expand its Optum division. The deal, which requires final court approval following clearance by the Attorney General's Office, would integrate Atrius Health into Optum Care, despite financial challenges faced by the nonprofit. This acquisition is part of UnitedHealth's broader strategy to grow its clinic and outpatient medicine businesses, reinforcing its presence in 16 states.

title: UnitedHealth Group's Witty topped $18 million in first year as CEO
summary: Andrew Witty, CEO of UnitedHealth Group, saw his compensation exceed $18 million in his first year in the role in 2021. Other executives at the Minnetonka-based company also received pay increases. This pay bump followed Witty's appointment in February 2021.

title: La. Attorney General Files Lawsuit Against UnitedHealth Over Costs
summary: Louisiana Attorney General Jeff Landry has filed a lawsuit against UnitedHealth Group Inc. and its pharmacy benefit manager, Optum Rx, alleging a scheme to inflate prescription drug costs for the state's Medicaid program by billions of dollars. Landry claims Optum Rx manipulates drug pricing to help UnitedHealth meet its medical-loss ratio requirements while generating additional profits for the parent company. UnitedHealth has denied the allegations, stating the lawsuit is without merit.

title: Anthem Inc. stock rises Monday, outperforms market
summary: Anthem Inc. (ANTM) stock increased by 0.84% on Monday, reaching $506.87. This performance outpaced the broader market, with the S&P 500 rising 0.57% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 0.70%. The rise broke a two-day losing streak for the company, though it remained just short of its 52-week high.

title: Five Ways Employers Can Support Women and Their Health
summary: This article outlines five key ways employers can better support working women, acknowledging the increased needs exacerbated by the pandemic. It emphasizes the importance of offering paid leave for various life events, supporting behavioral health needs with accessible resources, providing comprehensive fertility benefits, and offering robust support for expectant and new mothers. Additionally, the article highlights the significance of career support through fair pay, advancement opportunities, and empowering workplace cultures, ultimately benefiting both employees and employers.

title: UnitedHealth Group founder to retire from the board after more than 40 years
summary: Richard Burke, founder of UnitedHealth Group, is retiring from the health insurer's board of directors after a 45-year tenure. Burke established Charter Med Inc. in 1974, which grew into the nation's largest health insurer and Minnesota's largest company by revenue. His departure, along with fellow director Gail Wilensky, marks the end of an era for the company he helped build into a Fortune 500 giant.

title: 29 Stock Funds That Flip-Flopped in the Rankings
summary: The stock market's volatility in 2022 caused significant shifts in fund rankings, with some previously high-performing funds plummeting and former laggards rising to the top. This analysis by Morningstar identifies 29 U.S. stock funds that experienced major flip-flops, moving from the top 10% to the bottom 10% or vice versa within their categories based on one-year returns. While these short-term swings don't necessarily alter long-term analyst ratings, they highlight strategic biases within funds and offer insights for portfolio construction.

title: |‘Carve-Outs Are a Thing of the Past’, Behavioral Health Must Move to a Total Cost of Care Approach
summary: |Behavioral health carve-outs are becoming obsolete as the industry shifts towards a total cost of care approach, driven by the recognition of the interplay between behavioral and physical health. Executives from UnitedHealth Group, Eleanor Health, and CVS Health advocate for integrated care models, emphasizing value-based care, accessibility, and addressing social determinants of health. This shift aims to improve outcomes and reduce overall healthcare costs by treating individuals holistically rather than separating mental and physical health.

title: Optum's $236 million Atrius Health deal scores final regulatory approval
summary: Optum's acquisition of Atrius Health for $236 million has received final regulatory approval. The article, published on May 2, 2022, provides this key update regarding the merger.

title: Maternal-fetal medicine program keeps moms close to home while improving access to care
summary: HCA Healthcare's maternal-fetal medicine (MFM) telehealth program is expanding access to care for high-risk pregnant women by allowing them to consult with specialists virtually, reducing travel burdens and improving outcomes. Patients like Simms Schnorf, Jordan Griffith, and Haley Shane shared positive experiences, highlighting the convenience and expert care received through these virtual appointments. The program, which started with Dr. Jessica Parrott at Overland Park Regional Medical Center, now operates in 20 sites across five states, demonstrating the accelerated adoption of telehealth post-COVID-19.

title: Rising Admissions, M&A Bolster LHC Group as UnitedHealth Group Deal Proceeds
summary: LHC Group is experiencing resurgent admissions growth and strong revenue from its hospice segment, bolstered by recent acquisitions, even as it faces persistent workforce pressures and increased labor costs. These developments occur as its pending $5.5 billion acquisition by UnitedHealth Group proceeds, with questions remaining about the post-acquisition role of its hospice segment. The company's M&A strategy has focused on co-locating hospice services where it already has home health presence, and future acquisitions are expected later in the year, heavily influenced by the UnitedHealth Group deal.

title: UnitedHealth was this quarter's most profitable payer—again
summary: UnitedHealth Group maintained its position as the most profitable payer in the first quarter, exceeding Wall Street expectations with $5 billion in profit and $80.1 billion in revenue. Other major payers like CVS Health, Elevance Health (Anthem), Cigna, Humana, and Centene also reported strong profits and revenues, with CVS coming in second for both categories. The overall financial performance of these six national payers indicates a robust first quarter for the health insurance industry.

title: Humana Inc. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
summary: Humana Inc. stock slid 1.43% on Monday, closing at $424.51, despite a general market downturn. The stock, however, outperformed some of its competitors like UnitedHealth Group Inc., Anthem Inc., and Centene Corp., which experienced larger drops. Humana Inc. closed $50.93 short of its 52-week high and saw trading volume below its 50-day average.

title: Momentum building despite pandemic headwinds: Pennant Group
summary: Pennant Group reported strong first-quarter earnings, with CEO Daniel Walker noting "momentum building" despite challenges like the Omicron variant and labor pressures. The senior living segment saw increased revenue and occupancy, indicating a successful turnaround. The company also completed strategic transactions to optimize its portfolio and plans further acquisitions in senior living, home health, and hospice.

title: LHC Group shareholder sues company over $5B UnitedHealth deal
summary: A shareholder of LHC Group is suing the home healthcare provider and its board of directors, alleging that the proxy filing for its planned $5.4 billion merger with UnitedHealth Group's Optum is "misleading." The lawsuit claims the filing fails to disclose critical financial information and potential conflicts of interest, violating the Securities and Exchange Act. The shareholder, David Schuppert, seeks an injunction to halt the merger until the information is released.

title: Humana Inc. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: Humana Inc. (HUM) stock declined 4.66% on Wednesday to $420.04, underperforming the broader market. The S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also experienced significant drops. Humana's stock also trailed competitors like UnitedHealth Group Inc., Anthem Inc., and Centene Corp.

title: Empire BlueCross BlueShield opens new headquarters in Midtown
summary: Empire BlueCross BlueShield has opened a new 70,000-square-foot headquarters in Midtown at 1 Pennsylvania Plaza, moving from a temporary space on Wall Street. The move reflects the company's commitment to revitalizing New York City post-pandemic and creating a collaborative, hybrid workspace focused on employee well-being. Additionally, the company, in partnership with its philanthropic arm, will issue a grant to Breaking Ground, New York City's largest provider of aid for the unsheltered homeless.

title: MetLife Inc. stock rises Thursday, outperforms market
summary: MetLife Inc. (MET) saw its stock rise by 3.58% on Thursday, closing at $66.91, outperforming the broader market which also experienced gains. This marked the stock's second consecutive day of increases, though it remained below its 52-week high. The company's trading volume significantly exceeded its 50-day average.

title: How Lyft Healthcare Changed Lanes to Social Determinants of Health Work
summary: Lyft Healthcare, initially sparked by "fraudulent" ride requests for Medicaid's non-emergency medical transportation, has evolved into a dedicated branch of Lyft Inc. focused on addressing social determinants of health. The company streamlines transportation to medical appointments and other vital resources, demonstrating how addressing transport insecurity can significantly improve health outcomes and patient satisfaction. Lyft Healthcare partners with healthcare organizations, payers, and government agencies to integrate ride-sharing solutions and tackle issues like food insecurity and social isolation.

title: Vizient Announces Patty Olsen as Chief People Officer
summary: Vizient, Inc. has announced the appointment of Patty Olsen as its new chief people officer. She will be responsible for leading the design and implementation of the company's talent strategy to support continued growth and enhance performance improvement services for member healthcare organizations. Olsen previously served as chief human resources officer at Huron and brings extensive leadership experience in employee development and talent strategies.

title: Pfizer to exit GSK consumer health joint venture after spinoff
summary: Pfizer plans to sell its 32% stake in the consumer health joint venture with GlaxoSmithKline after it spins off into a new standalone corporation called Haleon. GSK will contribute at least 80% of its 68% holding to Haleon, which is set to begin trading on the London Stock Exchange on July 18. Both companies aim to focus on vaccines and new medicine development, with Pfizer exiting in a "disciplined manner" to maximize shareholder value.

title: Healthcare Dealmakers—Advocate Aurora, Atrium's $27B merger; Centene's $2.8B pharmacy sell-offs and more
summary: The article details various healthcare mergers and acquisitions that were active in May, including Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health's $27 billion merger plan. It also highlights Centene's sale of two pharmacy subsidiaries for $2.8 billion and other significant deals involving providers, payers, and tech companies. The transactions reflect a trend of industry consolidation to expand businesses and gain competitive advantages.

title: State releases names of vendors in the running for Medicaid IT bids
summary: Florida's Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) is moving forward with an estimated $320 million overhaul of its Medicaid information technology system, named Florida Health Care Connections (FX). The agency has released the names of vendors bidding on two of the three modular IT contracts: the provider service module and the unified operations center module. AHCA aims to finalize these contracts before launching a major Medicaid managed care re-procurement later this year.

title: CareBridge Lands $140M from Oak HC/FT, Group of MCOs to Expand Value-Based HCBS Model
summary: CareBridge, a Nashville-based home- and community-based services (HCBS) provider, announced a $140 million funding round led by Oak HC/FT, with participation from four of the largest Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs). The funding, which values the company at over $1 billion, will be used to expand CareBridge's value-based care model for Medicaid and dual-eligible patients with physical or intellectual disabilities nationwide, including building the largest HCBS database and expanding services for I/DD patients. CareBridge utilizes technology, 24/7 clinical support, and data aggregation to deliver better outcomes and reduce hospitalizations for its patients.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s Foundation Commits $100 Million To Health Equity And Diverse Workforce
summary: UnitedHealth Group's philanthropic arm has committed $100 million over the next decade to advance health equity and build a racially and ethnically diverse healthcare workforce. This initiative, the largest philanthropic commitment from the United Health Foundation, will provide scholarships and support to 10,000 underrepresented future clinicians and upskill health professionals. The goal is to address barriers to good health, broaden access to care, and increase primary care providers in underserved communities.

title: FTC to investigate CVS Caremark, Humana, other pharmacy benefit managers
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has launched an investigation into the business practices of six major pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), including CVS Caremark, Cigna's Express Scripts, and Humana. The probe aims to examine how PBMs influence drug pricing, patient access to pharmacies, and reimbursement methods, compelling them to provide records within 90 days. The investigation seeks to address concerns over transparency and potential conflicts of interest within the prescription drug supply chain.

title: Battle of toothpaste brands in Nigerian market
summary: The Nigerian oral care market is a significant battleground for toothpaste brands due to the country's large population. While global oral care markets are growing, local retailers and consumers in Nigeria indicate that economic realities and price points heavily influence consumer choices and brand loyalty, even for widely used brands like Close-Up. This dynamic leads to a diverse market where various brands contend for market share based on formulation, packaging, and marketing strategies.

title: 3 Excellent Dividend-Stock ETFs
summary: This article highlights three excellent dividend-stock ETFs: Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIG), Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD), and Vanguard International High Dividend Yield Index ETF (VYMI). These ETFs are lauded for their low cost, sensible index construction, and backing by investor-friendly firms, catering to different dividend investment strategies. The author provides details on each ETF's methodology, performance, and the types of companies it invests in.

title: P&G taps Microsoft for cloud services to boost production efficiency
summary: Procter & Gamble has partnered with Microsoft to utilize its Azure cloud computing services and predictive analytics to enhance manufacturing efficiency, reduce costs, and improve product delivery. This collaboration aims to leverage digital manufacturing visibility and advanced analytics to optimize production processes for various P&G products globally. The initiative builds on four years of prior cooperation, focusing on better data utilization, automation, digital twins, and sustainability.

title: As Anthem Rebrands To Elevance, Healthcare Services To Be Named ‘Carelon’
summary: Anthem is rebranding to Elevance Health, with its healthcare services adopting the new name "Carelon" and some government-subsidized health insurance products returning to the "Wellpoint" name. This change aims to streamline the company's brand portfolio and reflect its evolution beyond traditional health insurance, focusing on integrated healthcare solutions. The corporate name change and new brand strategy will become official on June 28, with shares trading under the new ticker symbol ELV.

title: 2022年GCFF线上投资会议——医疗保健投资 (北美专场)
summary: The 2022 GCFF Online Investment Conference featured a North American session focused on healthcare investments. This free virtual event, held on June 16, 2022, provided individual investors with insights into the latest trends in small-cap healthcare stocks, emerging opportunities in various healthcare sectors, and direct information from company executives. The conference aimed to capitalize on renewed investor interest in healthcare, driven by recent global events.

title: Probe of PBM Practices
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has launched an inquiry into the practices of pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) to examine potential anti-competitive behavior and their impact on prescription drug access and affordability. This study comes after growing concerns about PBM transparency, their role in the pharmaceutical supply chain, and whether savings are passed on to consumers. The investigation will cover the six largest PBMs and scrutinize practices such as fees charged to pharmacies, spread pricing, and strategies to direct consumers to PBM-owned pharmacies.

title: UnitedHealth Unit to Buy UK Health-Tech Firm EMIS for $1.5 Billion
summary: A unit of UnitedHealth Group Inc. (Optum) has agreed to acquire UK health-technology firm EMIS Group Plc for approximately $1.51 billion in an all-cash deal. The acquisition values EMIS shares at 1,925 pence each, expanding UnitedHealth's presence in the health-tech sector. This move signals continued consolidation and investment in digital health solutions within the global healthcare market.

title: UnitedHealth unit to pick up UK health tech company EMIS for $1.5B
summary: A UnitedHealth Group unit, Optum, plans to acquire UK health technology company EMIS Group for approximately $1.5 billion (1.24 billion pounds sterling) in an all-cash deal. The acquisition, which offers a 49% premium to EMIS's closing price, aims to enhance healthcare technology solutions for the NHS and improve patient care in the UK. This marks one of UnitedHealth's significant European acquisitions under CEO Andrew Witty, continuing Optum's streak of strategic acquisitions across the globe.

title: UnitedHealth's Optum buys U.K.-based software company for $1.5 billion
summary: UnitedHealth's Optum has acquired U.K.-based software company EMIS Group for $1.5 billion. Optum UK has a nearly 20-year history of supporting the NHS through its software, services, and consultancy business. This acquisition strengthens UnitedHealth's presence and capabilities in the UK healthcare technology sector.

title: UnitedHealth Group unit paying $1.5 billion for U.K. technology company
summary: UnitedHealth Group's Optum division is acquiring U.K. health technology firm EMIS Group PLC for $1.5 billion. This acquisition will deepen Optum's existing business with the National Health Service (NHS) in the United Kingdom, where it has been providing software and consulting for nearly 20 years. EMIS, which makes healthcare software and systems, will operate as a standalone unit in Leeds, aiming to enhance technology solutions and improve patient care for the NHS.

title: UnitedHealth Rejected by High Court on Medicare Overpayments
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has rejected an appeal by UnitedHealth Group Inc., upholding a federal rule allowing the government to recoup billions in Medicare Advantage overpayments. UnitedHealth had argued that this rule would negatively impact the program, potentially leading to reduced coverage or increased premiums for seniors.

title: U.S. Supreme Court rebuffs UnitedHealth Group challenge on Medicare overpayments
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has declined to hear UnitedHealth Group Inc.'s challenge to a government rule requiring private insurers administering Medicare plans to return overpayments based on incorrect diagnoses. This decision upholds a lower court ruling that revived the 2014 rule, which mandates insurers return payments within 60 days if an unsupported diagnosis is found. UnitedHealth had argued the rule treated Medicare Advantage differently from traditional Medicare, violating "actuarial equivalence."

title: The Pharmacy Benefit Mafia: The Secret Health Care Monopolies Jacking Up Drug Prices and Abusing Patients and Pharmacists
summary: This article exposes how Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) operate as "health care's ultimate corporate middlemen," contributing to rising drug prices and harming both patients and independent pharmacies. It details issues like vertical integration, consolidation, and conflicts of interest within the PBM industry, highlighting how these practices lead to higher costs, limited patient choice, and the closure of independent pharmacies. The article also criticizes past FTC policies that protected PBMs and underscores the importance of the current FTC investigation to rectify these long-standing problems.

title: General Mills Avoids Anti-BDS Backlash for Pulling Out of Settlements
summary: General Mills successfully avoided anti-BDS backlash after selling its Israeli dough-marketing joint venture by attributing the decision to economic reasons rather than political ones. This contrasts sharply with Ben & Jerry's, which faced severe penalties from several states after explicitly citing human rights concerns for divesting from the West Bank. The case highlights how anti-BDS legislation often targets company speech rather than solely their actions, showing that articulating a political stance can have significant repercussions.

title: LHC Group Shareholders Vote in Favor of UnitedHealth Group Deal
summary: LHC Group shareholders have overwhelmingly approved a $5.5 billion acquisition by UnitedHealth Group's subsidiary Optum, with the deal expected to close in the second half of the year. The acquisition includes new employment contracts for key LHC Group executives, enhancing their roles and compensation within Optum. This transaction highlights the increasing significance of home-based care and value-based reimbursement models in the healthcare industry.

title: Minne Inno - Lifespark taps former UnitedHealth exec to lead national expansion
summary: Lifespark, a St. Louis Park-based senior care company, has appointed Matt Nyquist, formerly a chief product officer at UnitedHealth Group's Optum, as its chief population health officer. Nyquist will lead the company's national market expansion and the development of global risk products. Lifespark CEO Joel Theisen emphasized the critical nature of this role as the company scales beyond Minnesota, aiming to capitalize on the evolving high-volume, low-value market for seniors.

title: Lifespark taps former UnitedHealth Group executive to lead national expansion
summary: Lifespark, a senior care company, has appointed Matt Nyquist, a former UnitedHealth Group executive, as its new chief population health officer. Nyquist's role will focus on leading the company's national expansion efforts. He was drawn to Lifespark by its entrepreneurial spirit and its impactful work in the senior care sector.

title: OptumHealth Names AbleTo Vet Trip Hofer CEO of Behavioral Health Solutions
summary: Trip Hofer, former CEO of AbleTo, has been appointed as the new CEO of OptumHealth's Behavioral Health Solutions. Hofer was previously instrumental in Optum's acquisition of AbleTo and has a long history in healthcare with roles at CVS Health and OptumHealth. His appointment underscores Optum's continuing expansion and investment in the behavioral health sector, following recent acquisitions like Refresh Mental Health and significant growth in behavioral health appointments.

title: Improving human care with ethical Augmented Intelligence
summary: Humana is leveraging Augmented Intelligence (AI) to enhance member health outcomes and decision-making within the company. The article highlights the ethical considerations of AI, particularly concerning bias, and outlines Humana's commitment to fairness through initiatives like signing the Equal AI pledge and establishing AI Ethics Operating and Governance Committees. This proactive approach aims to build trust with members and ensure equitable and inclusive care delivery.

title: How UnitedHealth, Medtronic, Wells Fargo and others are responding to Roe ruling's impact on employees
summary: Following the Roe v. Wade ruling, many Minnesota employers are evaluating their health coverage policies for abortions and considering whether to provide travel assistance for employees seeking care in other states. Companies like UnitedHealth have reportedly indicated their health plans would cover travel and lodging for employees to access legally unavailable care in their home states. This development highlights the significant decisions businesses face regarding employee benefits and reproductive healthcare access.

title: Settled medical debt is now dropping off credit reports — here's how to check your record and make sure it's right
summary: As of July 1, 2022, major credit reporting firms no longer include paid-off medical debt on credit reports, and consumers now have a year before unpaid medical debt appears. Additional changes in 2023 will remove any unpaid debts under $500. These changes are expected to improve credit scores for millions of Americans, and consumers are advised to check their credit reports to ensure accuracy.

title: Enhabit Home Health & Hospice Completes Spinoff from Encompass Health
summary: Enhabit Home Health & Hospice (NYSE: EHAB) has successfully completed its spinoff from Encompass Health Corporation (NYSE: EHC) after more than a year and a half of planning. This move establishes Enhabit as an independent company, providing it with enhanced strategic and operational flexibility to pursue growth, including funding de novo locations and M&A activities. The company has also appointed two new board members, Tina Brown-Stevenson and Susan La Monica, as it embarks on this new chapter.

title: Sanofi’s Discount Program Lowers Cost of Insulin
summary: Sanofi has updated its Valyou Savings Program to offer uninsured individuals a 30-day supply of insulin for $35, down from $99, effective July 1. This initiative aims to make insulin more affordable and aligns with growing support for a $35 monthly price cap on insulin. Additionally, Sanofi is partnering with Direct Relief to donate insulin to underserved communities, bridging the gap between diagnosis and treatment.

title: Healthcare Dealmakers—Oracle closes $28B Cerner acquisition, FTC spoils major hospital transactions and more
summary: This article summarizes significant healthcare mergers and acquisitions in June 2022, highlighting Oracle's $28 billion acquisition of Cerner and several hospital merger cancellations due to FTC pushback. It details various deals across provider, payer, and tech sectors, including ChristianaCare's purchase of Jennersville Hospital and UnitedHealth Group's pending acquisition of LHC Group facing regulatory scrutiny. The report emphasizes ongoing consolidation and the influence of regulatory bodies in the healthcare industry.

title: 더블 딥 우려 확산 금리 인상의 끝
summary: 이 기사는 2022년 7월 첫째 주를 기준으로, 경기 침체 징후가 부각되면서 '더블 딥' 우려가 확산되고 있는 미국 경제 상황을 분석합니다. 금리 인상 사이클의 고점에 접근하며, 인플레이션과 경기 침체 가능성 속에서 투자 전략으로 가치주 중심의 ETF인 VTV를 소개하고, 장기적으로는 성장주 투자가 유리하지만, 단기적으로는 VTV의 가격 방어력이 우수하다고 설명합니다.

title: UnitedHealth accused of underpaying for telehealth
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc is facing a proposed class action lawsuit alleging systematic underpayment for telehealth services since the early part of the COVID-19 pandemic. The lawsuit, filed by a Chicago woman, claims UnitedHealth continued to reimburse at older, lower rates despite increased Medicare rates for telehealth services matching in-person care. This alleged underpayment is argued to be a violation of UnitedHealth's fiduciary duty under ERISA.

title: Optum forms joint venture with healthcare media group
summary: Optum has announced a joint venture with a healthcare media group. The article briefly mentions this development, along with other healthcare news such as CMS finalizing a Medicare pay hike and Dexcom's revenue performance.

title: These Healthcare Companies Made This Year's Fortune 500 List
summary: The 2022 Fortune 500 list includes dozens of healthcare corporations, with four healthcare businesses among the top 10 largest U.S. corporations overall. The article highlights top companies in various healthcare sectors such as insurance, medical facilities, pharmacy services, pharmaceutical companies, and healthcare wholesalers, detailing their 2021 revenues and rankings. Many companies, including COVID-19 vaccine manufacturer Moderna, saw significant revenue increases, reflecting the industry's lucrative nature.

title: Natera Selected for UnitedHealthcare's Preferred Laboratory Network
summary: Natera, Inc. announced its selection to UnitedHealthcare's Preferred Laboratory Network (PLN), effective July 1, 2022. This inclusion signifies Natera's commitment to meeting UnitedHealthcare's high standards for laboratory care, focusing on access, cost, data, quality, and service. As part of the PLN, Natera will continue to provide UnitedHealthcare plan members with personalized genetic testing and diagnostics in oncology, women's health, and organ health.

title: In acquisition, Atrius rejected the biggest names in Massachusetts health care. Here’s what it all means.
summary: Atrius Health, a major independent physician group in Massachusetts, faced significant financial challenges, including a $33.4 million operating loss in fiscal 2021 and projected further losses, prompting it to seek acquisition. Despite bids from prominent local and national healthcare entities like Mass General Brigham and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts, Atrius ultimately chose Optum, the provider arm of UnitedHealth Group. This acquisition, approved by the Attorney General, is seen by experts as a microcosm of market consolidation, raising concerns about potential increases in healthcare spending without clear improvements in quality for Massachusetts.

title: Unitedhealth Group, Inc. Announces Rise In Q2 Income
summary: Unitedhealth Group, Inc. (UNH) announced a rise in its second-quarter income, with earnings increasing to $5.07 billion, or $5.34 per share, compared to $4.27 billion, or $4.46 per share, in the same period last year. Adjusted earnings were $5.29 billion, or $5.57 per share. The company also reported a 12.6% increase in revenue, reaching $80.33 billion for the quarter.

title: UnitedHealth Group raises outlook as quarterly profit again tops $5 billion
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced its second-quarter profit exceeded $5 billion on revenue of $80.33 billion, marking a significant 19% increase over the previous year. The company also raised its financial outlook for the year for the second time, driven by strong growth in its Optum division and lower-than-expected medical costs. This performance echoes its first-quarter results, where profits also topped $5 billion.

title: 경기 방어주로 부각…증시 침체에도 '탄탄'
summary: 글로벌 증시 침체 우려 속에서도 헬스케어 상장지수펀드(ETF)가 경기 방어주로 부각되며 반등하고 있다. 대표적인 미국 헬스케어 ETF인 XLV는 최근 1개월간 주가가 상승했으며, 장기적으로도 안정적인 수익률을 보여주고 있다. 금융투자 업계는 헬스케어 업종의 M&A 모멘텀이 하반기에도 시장 수익률을 넘어설 것으로 전망하고 있다.

title: UnitedHealth Group says Medicare Advantage saves money, but the data say otherwise
summary: UnitedHealth Group executives claim that Medicare Advantage saves the federal government money, but data from the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (MedPAC) contradict this. According to MedPAC, federal payments to Medicare Advantage plans have consistently been higher than traditional Medicare payments since 2018, and even higher in previous years, indicating that the program does not a generate savings as claimed.

title: UnitedHealth Group raked in billions during Q2—but it’s not immune to the effects of inflation
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported a significant profit of $10.1 billion and revenues of $160.5 billion in the first half of 2022, a notable increase from the previous year. Optum, UHG's health services arm, was a major driver of this growth, expanding its care delivery business through several key acquisitions. However, UHG acknowledges that inflation and economic downturns will likely impact future costs for customers and providers, primarily in 2023.

title: HCA Healthcare, Cigna chiefs top the lists of best-paid CEOs among providers, insurers
summary: The article highlights that CEOs of major health insurers and providers continue to receive some of the largest compensation packages in the industry, despite ongoing payment disputes between their companies. In 2021, median CEO pay among 11 insurers and benefits companies reached $30 million, the highest of any sector, driven by rising stock prices.

title: Study: Seniors prefer in-home care, but most are unaware of options available
summary: A new survey by Cross Country Workforce Solutions Group reveals that 70% of individuals aged 50 or older prefer in-home care, yet only 9% are actively investigating their options, and 34% haven't considered their future healthcare needs at all. The study highlights a significant gap between seniors' preference for aging in place and their lack of awareness regarding available in-home care programs and financial planning. This indicates a need for expanding in-home care capabilities and better educating the aging population on their choices.

title: 7 Best Dental Insurance Plans
summary: This article reviews the 7 best dental insurance plans for 2022, highlighting their strengths for specific needs like major work, braces, or affordable coverage. It provides detailed comparison tables including sample premiums, maximum annual benefits, and coverage options for each recommended insurer. The guide also explains how dental insurance works, types of plans, associated costs, and tips for choosing the right provider.

title: Amazon is buying One Medical for $3.49 billion in latest move to dominate healthcare industry
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of primary-care company One Medical for $3.49 billion, marking its latest significant move into the healthcare market. One Medical operates 182 medical offices across 25 U.S. markets, offering subscribers access to physicians and digital health services. This acquisition follows Amazon's previous ventures into healthcare, including an online pharmacy and a primary-care clinic for employees, signaling a continued effort to reinvent healthcare experiences.

title: UnitedHealth, Ping An, China Life top list of world’s largest insurers
summary: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated maintained its position as the world's largest insurance company in 2020 based on net premium written (NPW), followed by Ping An Insurance and China Life Insurance Company. The article also details the top insurers ranked by non-banking assets, with Allianz SE leading this category for the second consecutive year.

title: Shares of HCA Healthcare Rise on Earnings Report
summary: HCA Healthcare Inc. reported second-quarter earnings that surpassed analyst expectations, leading to a significant rise in its stock price. Despite the quarterly earnings beat, the company's shares are down year-to-date and over the last 52 weeks.
