For investors seeking diversified healthcare exposure beyond market-cap weighted ETFs, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Health Care ETF (RYH) offers an alternative with equal weighting for all holdings.

title: Mogul CEO Tiffany Pham Named to SIA’s Prestigious 40 Under 40 List
summary: Tiffany Pham, Founder, CEO, and Chairman of the Board at Mogul, Inc., has been recognized on Staffing Industry Analysts' (SIA) 2022 "40 Under 40 List." Mogul, founded in 2014, has grown to become a leading resource for diverse executives, connecting 494 million individuals globally. The company offers a diversity-focused recruitment system with patent-pending filters to combat biases in traditional talent acquisition and aims to further impact gender and racial inequality, particularly at the board level.

title: White House says more money needed to develop additional COVID-19 vaccines
summary: The White House indicates that additional funding is likely required to develop and launch its fall COVID-19 vaccination campaign, particularly for new variant-adapted vaccines. While HHS stated that a recent 105 million dose order from Pfizer would be funded through reallocated funds, COVID-19 Response Coordinator Ashish Jha suggested more money from Congress would be needed. The Biden administration's request for $22.5 million for coronavirus efforts remains stalled in Congress.

title: CRISPR may not always be safe: Study finds gene editing can damage genome and in extreme cases cause cancer
summary: A study by scientists at Tel Aviv University warns that while the CRISPR gene-editing method is effective, it is not always safe, as rearranging DNA can compromise genomic stability and potentially trigger cancer. The researchers explain that DNA breaks, even those naturally occurring, can lead to chromosomal disruptions seen in cancer cells, suggesting that intentional DNA cleavage in CRISPR therapeutics could, in extreme cases, promote malignancies. They recommend extra caution, alternative methods, and further research into solutions like reducing damaged cells or identifying and removing them before administration.

title: [글로벌ETF64회] 월배당 받는 커버드콜 ETF, JEPI ETF 매력은?
summary: This article discusses the appeal of JEPI ETF, a covered call ETF that offers monthly dividends, especially in a volatile market. It explains that JEPI invests 80-90% in large-cap US stocks and the rest in S&P 500-based ELNs, focusing on undervalued, low-volatility blue-chip stocks. The article highlights JEPI's stability due to consistent monthly dividends, making it an attractive option during periods of stock market volatility.

title: One Stock Superinvestors Are Selling
summary: This article identifies UnitedHealth Group Inc (UNH) as a stock that prominent superinvestors have been selling or reducing positions in, according to their latest 13F filings. Despite the stock being up 26% in the past twelve months, investors such as David Polen, Boykin Curry, and John Armitage significantly reduced their holdings. The report highlights UnitedHealth Group's status as a major private health insurer and healthcare services provider through its Optum franchises.

title: Trudy Busch Valentine Says She'll 'Stand up' to Insurers. She Also Invests in Them.
summary: Trudy Busch Valentine, a Democratic US Senate candidate in Missouri, has pledged to "stand up" to health insurers while simultaneously holding significant investments in major health insurance companies like Humana, UnitedHealth Group, and CVS Health. Her campaign states that her stocks are managed by investment managers with "complete discretion" and that she has committed to placing her investments in a blind trust if elected. Valentine favors a "public option" healthcare plan over "Medicare for All" and has pledged to co-sponsor a ban on stock trading for lawmakers and their immediate families.

title: Optum, Sanofi team to make low-cost insulin available to uninsured
summary: Optum and Sanofi are partnering to provide low-cost insulin to uninsured individuals with diabetes, offering a 30-day supply for $35 through Optum Store. This initiative follows UnitedHealthcare's move to eliminate cost-sharing on certain drugs, including insulin, for its fully insured group plans. The collaboration aims to improve access and affordability of life-saving medication for those in need.

title: 5 Ways Seniors Can Protect Themselves From Health Care Scams
summary: This article highlights five ways seniors can protect themselves from rampant healthcare scams, which cost U.S. seniors over $1.5 billion last year. Tips include verifying caller identities, guarding Medicare ID cards, carefully checking insurance statements, being cautious online, and looking out for fake medication scams. The overarching advice is to remain alert and protect personal information to avoid becoming a victim.

title: Cigna Subsidiary Evernorth’s Behavioral Health Network Doubled in Size Over Past 5 Years
summary: Cigna's health services segment, Evernorth, has significantly expanded its behavioral health network, doubling its size over the past five years in response to increased demand. The company is investing in digital platforms like the Confide Behavioral Health Navigator to improve access to care and is further integrating behavioral and physical health services. Despite higher spending in this sector, Cigna views this investment positively as it addresses critical patient needs.

title: EMIS Group shareholders approve £1.24bn takeover
summary: Shareholders of EMIS Group have approved a £1.24 billion all-cash takeover deal by Optum Health Solutions UK Ltd, a subsidiary of UnitedHealth Group Inc. The Leeds-based NHS software provider will be acquired for 1,925 pence per share, representing a significant premium. EMIS CEO Andy Thorburn believes the combination with UnitedHealth Group's resources will better enable them to support the NHS and clinicians through technology innovations.

title: HCA Healthcare, J&J explore better outcomes, nurse training, early cancer detection in new partnership
summary: HCA Healthcare and Johnson & Johnson have partnered to improve patient outcomes and address workforce issues in healthcare. The collaboration will focus on three key areas: early-stage lung cancer detection among Black patients, incorporating J&J's nursing resources into HCA facilities and building nurse education programs, and conducting cardiovascular health research. This partnership aims to advance health equity and enhance patient care.

title: Employees Credit Comprehensive Insurance Plans With Safeguarding Health, Financial Security
summary: A new AHIP survey reveals that Americans with employer-sponsored health insurance highly value plans that cover both behavioral and physical health needs, with a significant increase in the importance placed on mental health benefits. The study also highlights increasing satisfaction with employer-provided health insurance, driven by affordability, comprehensive coverage, and choice of providers. Additionally, health insurance plays a crucial role in employee recruitment and retention, with a majority of respondents indicating it impacts their job decisions.

title: ScriptDrop and Roadie Work Together to Improve & Scale Medication Access
summary: ScriptDrop, a healthcare technology company, and Roadie, a UPS company, have significantly expanded medication access across all 50 states through their partnership. The collaboration, which began in 2020, has enabled same-day and urgent prescription delivery, helping to address social determinants of health like pharmacy deserts. Their annual report highlights the importance of this partnership in improving long-term health outcomes by ensuring patients receive their medications regularly.

title: UnitedHealthcare expands ownership stake and rebrands Bind Benefits
summary: UnitedHealthcare has increased its majority ownership stake in Bind Benefits and rebranded the company as Surest. Surest offers a unique health plan structure based on copays rather than deductibles and is expanding its "fully insured" option to more states, including Minnesota. This move aims to provide patients with upfront cost information and incentivize access to more efficient care providers.

title: UnitedHealthcare’s Surest Offers a New Approach to Health Insurance
summary: UnitedHealthcare's Surest health plans, formerly Bind, are offering a new approach to health benefits with no deductibles and upfront pricing information. These plans aim to improve member satisfaction and lower healthcare costs for employers by up to 15% while reducing out-of-pocket expenses for members by up to 44%. Surest is expanding its offerings nationwide to employers and to fully insured customers in several states.

title: A CLOSER LOOK: The Mid Year Earnings of 7 Big For-Profit Insurance Companies
summary: This article examines the mid-year earnings of seven major for-profit health insurance companies, revealing significant profits ($43.8 billion) and substantial revenue ($620.6 billion), much of which comes from taxpayers. It highlights the growing control these insurers have over the Medicare Advantage and Medicaid markets, along with the increasing financial power of their Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs). The analysis also details how these companies' profits and enrollment in government programs have surged, while a large percentage of American adults remain underinsured due to high out-of-pocket costs.

title: UnitedHealth Group buys Medicare insurer in Texas
summary: UnitedHealth Group has acquired KS Plan Administrators, a Houston-based Medicare insurer, as disclosed in a recent regulatory filing. This acquisition is part of a larger transaction earlier this year where UnitedHealth Group acquired Kelsey-Seybold, a large medical group in Houston, for an estimated $2 billion. KS Plan Administrators covers approximately 41,000 Medicare beneficiaries and generated about $147 million in premium revenue in Texas during the first quarter.

title: UnitedHealthcare continues investment in local nonprofits
summary: UnitedHealthcare is continuing its investment in San Antonio nonprofits. The company previously announced a $500 million investment, with new grants supporting organizations like the San Antonio Food Bank and Brighter Bites to address social determinants of health through programs like a produce delivery service.

title: Productivity tracking at Allina Health, UnitedHealth Group questioned in New York Times investigation
summary: A New York Times investigation has raised questions about productivity tracking practices at Allina Health and UnitedHealth Group, highlighting the increased adoption of digital employee monitoring tools by white-collar employers, particularly during the pandemic. The article by Kelly Busche briefly touches on this trend and lists related articles concerning employee productivity and employer rankings.

title: Payers have largely shrugged off the industry's financial struggles, but those challenges could catch up to them: Moody's
summary: A Moody's report indicates that while health payers have largely been unaffected by the economic challenges facing providers, inflation and slowing economic growth could eventually impact them. These challenges include potential drops in employer-sponsored coverage enrollment due to job losses and negative impacts on insurer investments. Despite these risks, Moody's suggests that health plans are better positioned now than in 2008 due to increased diversification and a lower reliance on commercial coverage.

title: Amazon’s Signify Health Interest Another Indicator Of At-Home Care Capabilities Buildout
summary: Amazon is reportedly interested in acquiring Signify Health, a value-based care platform with significant home-based care capabilities, just a month after purchasing One Medical. This move signals Amazon's continued expansion into the healthcare sector, particularly strengthening its at-home care offerings. The acquisition could position Amazon to better appeal to payers by leveraging Signify's in-home assessments and integration with the healthcare ecosystem.

title: Rising Regulatory Scrutiny of RAF Scores
summary: The article discusses the increasing regulatory scrutiny surrounding Risk Adjustment Factor (RAF) scores, which are used by CMS to estimate the health status and associated costs of Medicare Advantage (MA) beneficiaries and Accountable Care Organization (ACO) members. It highlights the importance of accurate documentation and processes to ensure correct RAF scores, especially in light of rising MA enrollment and healthcare costs. The piece also details various aspects of RAF score calculation, OIG audit activities, and best practices for compliance, including the role of in-home care delivery.

title: CVS, Amazon, UnitedHealth are among bidders for Signify, Bloomberg reports
summary: CVS Health, Amazon, and UnitedHealth Group are among the companies bidding to acquire home health firm Signify Health, according to Bloomberg News. UnitedHealth has reportedly submitted the highest offer at $30 per share, with Amazon close behind. The potential acquisition aligns with a trend of companies like CVS and Amazon expanding their healthcare services, though antitrust concerns remain a factor in such deals.

title: Signify Health shares jump as Amazon, UnitedHealth reportedly among bidders for takeover deal
summary: Signify Health's shares surged after reports indicated Amazon and UnitedHealth Group are among the bidders for the home health technology and services provider in a deal potentially exceeding $8 billion. This comes as Signify focuses on its home and community services segment and other major players like CVS, Walgreens, and Walmart intensify their efforts in the healthcare market. A potential acquisition by Amazon would mark its second major healthcare deal in 2022, while for UnitedHealth, it aligns with its vertical integration strategy.

title: BCBS of Vermont sues Teva Pharmaceuticals over marketing for its MS drug Copaxone
summary: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Vermont and the Vermont Health Plan have filed a lawsuit against Teva Pharmaceuticals, alleging that the company used deceptive marketing tactics for its multiple sclerosis drug, Copaxone. The suit claims Teva offered coupons to prevent patients from switching to cheaper generic alternatives and pressured doctors to prescribe Copaxone exclusively, leading to inflated costs for payers. Teva reportedly generated $34 billion from Copaxone between 2002 and 2019, while prices significantly increased over the years.

title: UnitedHealth CFO Added to Lawsuit Over 401(k) Offerings
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc.'s CFO, John Rex, has been added to an amended class-action lawsuit. The suit alleges that Rex prioritized business interests over the performance of the company's 401(k) plan, which included low-performing target-date funds managed by Wells Fargo & Co. This alleged action is claimed to have harmed plan participants.

title: More Skilled Nursing Providers Fill Care Gaps with Palliative, Hospice Services
summary: In response to care gaps highlighted by the pandemic, more skilled nursing facility operators are expanding their services to include palliative and hospice care. Companies like National Healthcare Corp. and Marquis Health Consulting Services are either acquiring hospice agencies or building out chronic illness support programs that incorporate these services. This expansion not only aims to improve continuity of care but also offers a potential financial incentive, as hospice care can yield higher Medicare margins compared to traditional skilled nursing services.

title: Amazon mothballing virtual health care service after admitting, ‘It is not a complete enough offering’
summary: Amazon is discontinuing its telehealth service, Amazon Care, by December 31, 2022, citing that it is "not a complete enough offering" for large enterprise customers. This decision comes despite the company's broader expansion into healthcare through acquisitions like PillPack and One Medical, and marks a potential setback for the telehealth industry as demand has reportedly declined. However, Amazon's other healthcare initiatives remain unaffected.

title: UnitedHealth CFO named in amended class action
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc.'s CFO John Rex has been named as an individual defendant in an amended class-action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges Rex and other executive leadership kept a poorly performing Wells Fargo fund as the default investment for employees' retirement plans, potentially compromising their fiduciary duty under ERISA. UnitedHealth denies the claims, stating that investment decisions were made in the best interests of plan participants.

title: UnitedHealth CFO is added to class-action lawsuit over 401(k) plan
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc.'s CFO, John Rex, has been added to a 2021 class-action lawsuit concerning the company's 401(k) plans. This amendment implicates a key financial officer in the ongoing legal challenge against the healthcare giant.

title: Virtual Care Enables Real Connections Between Patients and Providers
summary: This article discusses how virtual care is fostering stronger doctor-patient relationships, moving beyond episodic care to longitudinal, whole-person health. Dr. Vontrelle Roundtree, MDLIVE’s interim chief medical officer, highlights the benefits of virtual primary and preventive care, emphasizing its role in improving access, managing chronic conditions, and enabling comprehensive wellness screenings. The piece illustrates how virtual care can address longstanding barriers to healthcare and will integrate with in-person care for better outcomes.

title: Molina, Elevance, Centene win big with Medicaid contracts in California
summary: California has awarded lucrative five-year Medicaid managed care contracts to Elevance, Molina, and Centene, effective 2024. These contracts are part of California's first competitive procurement for such services within its large Medi-Cal program, aiming to increase accountability for quality care, link payments to outcomes, and require reinvestment of profits in community infrastructure. While the three major health plans secured significant wins, some, like Centene, lost contracts in key counties and are considering appeals, leading to potential member transitions.

title: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) shares fell 2.27% to $529.25 on Friday, underperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average decline significantly. Despite the loss, the stock's performance on the day was better than the overall market decline. The company's stock closed $24.04 below its 52-week high.

title: Scientists question Moderna invention claim in COVID-19 vaccine dispute
summary: Moderna is engaged in a patent dispute with Pfizer and BioNTech over their COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, accusing them of infringing on its patented inventions. However, scientists Drew Weissman and Katalin Karikó claim a key invention cited by Moderna, the 1-methylpseudouridine modification, was patented by them years earlier. This legal battle arises as both companies anticipate new markets for updated vaccine formulations and increased profits.

title: Top 3 Social Determinants of Health Barriers Among Seniors
summary: A study sponsored by Alignment Healthcare identified economic instability, loneliness, and food insecurity as the top three social determinants of health barriers affecting seniors. Economic instability, particularly medical debt, was a widespread issue, with many prioritizing other responsibilities over health. Loneliness impacts a significant number of seniors, and food insecurity, especially the desire for grocery allowances, was a major concern for accessing care.

title: UnitedHealthcare Selects Behavioral Health Startups Mood Health, YourPath to Join Its Health Care Accelerator
summary: UnitedHealthcare has chosen digital mental health company Mood Health and substance use disorder-focused startup YourPath for its four-month health care accelerator program. These two mental health startups are among ten selected to participate, gaining access to mentors, funding, and UnitedHealthcare's clinical expertise. The initiative aims to develop solutions for pressing health care challenges, particularly in the increasingly competitive behavioral health landscape.

title: Connected Pharmacy MedMinder Raises $35M for Polypharmacy & Senior Patients
summary: MedMinder, a connected pharmacy care provider for polypharmacy and senior patients, has secured an additional $35 million in funding through a credit facility with SWK Holdings Corporation and an investment from existing partner Accelmed Partners. This funding will enable MedMinder to expand its services nationally, increase capacity, and develop innovative virtual care and technological capabilities to support patients aging at home. The company's unique pill dispenser and integrated pharmacy services aim to improve medication adherence and reduce healthcare costs for its target demographic.

title: Iowa selects Molina Healthcare to be its third Medicaid managed care organization
summary: Iowa has chosen Molina Healthcare of Iowa to become its third Medicaid managed care organization (MCO), joining Iowa Total Care and Amerigroup Iowa in early 2023. This selection aims to evenly distribute Medicaid members among three insurance companies, focusing on Molina's expertise in government programs and long-term care support. The move comes after the state has operated with only two MCOs since late 2017 when AmeriHealth Caritas departed.

title: Sepsis Awareness Month: HCA Healthcare expert shares his sepsis survival story
summary: Dr. Jeffrey Guy, HCA Healthcare's Vice President of Care Process Design, shares his personal sepsis survival story to highlight the importance of sepsis awareness. The article explains what sepsis is, who is at risk, and how HCA Healthcare uses its Sepsis Prediction and Optimization of Therapy (SPOT) system to detect and treat sepsis early. Dr. Guy emphasizes prevention through vaccinations, managing chronic illnesses, good hygiene, knowing the warning signs, and seeking early medical care.

title: Alderman ‘disappointed’ with developer’s decision to turn down grocer
summary: Alderman Chris Taliaferro (29th Ward) expressed "disappointment" with Novak Construction's decision to reject Jewel-Osco as an anchor tenant for the former Sears site at North and Harlem in Galewood, opting instead for a healthcare company. The community had previously requested a grocery store for the long-vacant site. Taliaferro plans to organize a follow-up community meeting for residents to hear directly from Novak officials regarding their revised development plans.

title: Optum Acquires Houston-Based Physician Group for $2 Billion
summary: Optum, the healthcare services division of UnitedHealth Group, is reportedly acquiring Kelsey-Seybold, a Houston-based physician group, for approximately $2 billion. This acquisition further expands Optum's already vast network of physicians, which made up over 5% of all U.S. physicians as of March 2021 and has since grown to 60,000. The move is central to UnitedHealth's strategy for growth, aiming to increase healthcare services and revenue, with Kelsey-Seybold already planning significant expansions to its facilities and services.

title: CVS takes lead in talks to acquire Signify Health: report
summary: CVS Health Corp. has reportedly taken the lead in talks to acquire home healthcare company Signify Health Inc., with a bid of around $8 billion. This move aligns with CVS's strategy to expand its in-home health services, an area also eyed by competitors like Amazon.com and UnitedHealth Group. A deal could be announced next week, valuing Signify at over $30 per share.

title: CVS to buy Signify Health for nearly $8 billion
summary: CVS Health Corp. has agreed to acquire home-health and technology services provider Signify Health Inc. for approximately $8 billion, priced at $30.50 per share. This acquisition aims to expand CVS's reach beyond its retail origins and strengthen its health-care services strategy, particularly in value-based care. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2023, enhancing CVS's connection to consumers at home and helping providers address patient needs more effectively.

title: CVS Health to acquire Signify Health for $8B
summary: CVS Health announced its plan to acquire home health care company Signify Health for approximately $8 billion. The deal involves CVS acquiring Signify for $30.50 per share in cash, intending to enhance its connection to consumers in their homes and expand product offerings. The acquisition, which faced competition from industry giants like Amazon and UnitedHealth, is expected to be accretive to CVS's earnings and close in the first half of 2023.

title: CVS to buy Dallas-based Signify Health in an $8B deal
summary: CVS Health Corp. has agreed to acquire Dallas-based Signify Health Inc. for $8 billion in a cash deal. Signify Health, a technology-enabled home health services provider, will play a critical role in advancing CVS's health care services strategy and growth in value-based care. The acquisition is expected to enhance CVS's connection to consumers at home and expand new product offerings.

title: Beating Other Bidders, CVS Health Inks Deal To Acquire Dallas’ Signify Health in $8B Deal
summary: CVS Health is acquiring Dallas-based Signify Health for approximately $8 billion, beating out other bidders like Amazon. This acquisition will expand CVS's footprint in the value-based care market and enhance its connection to consumers in their homes through Signify's tech-enabled home health services. Signify Health CEO Kyle Armbrester will continue to lead the company's 600-person team as part of CVS Health.

title: The majority of big insurers' health plan revenues are subsidized by American taxpayers
summary: This article reveals that a significant portion of major health insurers' revenues, particularly from Medicare Advantage plans, comes from American taxpayers rather than private-paying customers. It highlights that the federal government's generosity in subsidies has led insurers like UnitedHealth Group, Humana, and others to increasingly focus on government-funded plans. The author argues that these subsidies contribute to high CEO compensation and notes concerns about potential fraud in Medicare Advantage, as well as the substantial "under-insurance" of ACA beneficiaries despite subsidies.

title: Walmart enlists UnitedHealth Group for 10-year value-based care partnership
summary: Walmart and UnitedHealth Group have entered a 10-year partnership to expand value-based care and launch a new Medicare Advantage plan. The initiative will begin in 2023 in Florida and Georgia, with plans for broader expansion, aiming to reach hundreds of thousands of MA members. UnitedHealth's Optum will provide data analytics and decision support to Walmart Health clinicians, enhancing affordability in healthcare.

title: The Walmart, UnitedHealth Group deal: Another big retail, health care partnership
summary: Walmart and UnitedHealth Group have announced a new partnership, further highlighting the trend of retail giants entering the healthcare sector. This collaboration indicates a continued convergence of retail and health services. The deal aims to expand affordable healthcare options through Walmart's presence and UnitedHealth's expertise.

title: Walmart and UnitedHealth Group Collaborate to Deliver Access to High-Quality, Affordable Health Care
summary: Walmart Inc. and UnitedHealth Group announced a 10-year collaboration to provide high-quality, affordable health care, starting in 2023 with 15 Walmart Health locations in Florida and Georgia. The partnership will leverage Optum's clinical capabilities to advance value-based care for seniors and Medicare beneficiaries, including a co-branded Medicare Advantage plan and virtual care options. The initiative aims to expand access to care for a broader population, including commercial and Medicaid plans, and address social determinants of health.

title: Walmart, UnitedHealth Group Bring Several Behavioral Health Assets to New 10-Year VBC Partnership
summary: Walmart and UnitedHealth Group have announced a 10-year value-based care partnership that will roll out at 15 Walmart Health locations in January 2023, specifically targeting seniors on Medicare Advantage plans. Behavioral health will be a fundamental component, leveraging assets from both companies including Walmart Health's core services and UnitedHealth Group's Optum subsidiary. The collaboration aims to expand access to quality care, improve patient outcomes, and includes a co-branded Medicare Advantage plan and access to virtual care services.

title: Optum office campus near headquarters listed for lease
summary: An Optum office campus in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, near the company's headquarters, has been listed for lease. The campus, formerly occupied by ADC Telecommunications Inc., includes two buildings at 13625 and 13675 Technology Drive. Although it is a significant amount of space, the listing does not involve Optum's headquarters.

title: UnitedHealthcare Vet Ken Burdick Takes the Helm at LifeStance, as Founding CEO Michael Lester Retires
summary: LifeStance Health Group Inc. (Nasdaq: LFST) has appointed Ken Burdick, a UnitedHealthcare veteran, as its new CEO, succeeding founding CEO Michael Lester who retired. Danish Qureshi, the current COO, will also take on the role of president. This leadership change comes as the company continues to focus on expanding access to care and pursuing profitability through strategic initiatives.

title: UnitedHealth Group Announces 10-Year Agreement with Walmart
summary: UnitedHealth Group and Walmart Inc. have announced a decade-long partnership to improve healthcare outcomes at Walmart clinics, leveraging UnitedHealth's Optum subsidiary for analytics and decision-support tools. The collaboration will start in 2023 across 15 Walmart Health locations in Florida and Georgia, with plans for future expansion and the introduction of a co-branded Medicare Advantage plan in Georgia. This initiative aims to provide high-quality, affordable healthcare options and eventually address social determinants of health and other medical services.

title: Morgan Health invests $20M in home diagnostics company LetsGetChecked
summary: Morgan Health, JPMorgan Chase's healthcare business unit, has invested $20 million in the home diagnostics startup LetsGetChecked as part of its Series D-2 funding round. LetsGetChecked provides at-home tests for various conditions, including sexual health, cholesterol, diabetes, and COVID-19, and has recently expanded into genomics and made several acquisitions. This investment aims to improve timely access to clinical testing and support the company's growth in the competitive home diagnostics market.

title: The American Prospect: Another Private Equity–Style Hospital Raid Kills a Busy Urban Hospital
summary: The article discusses the closure of Atlanta Medical Center (AMC), highlighting it as another instance of a hospital closing down despite community need, similar to patterns seen in private equity-style buyouts. It alleges that the nominally nonprofit owner, Wellstar Foundation, intentionally neglected the hospital to make it unprofitable and extract valuable assets, such as residency programs and trauma center designation, for its more affluent facilities. The author argues that this situation is symptomatic of a larger structural issue in healthcare, where state-sanctioned monopolies and a lack of accountability enable financially driven decisions that undermine patient care.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s Ann Williamson: Protecting privacy through security
summary: Ann Williamson, Chief Privacy Officer and Deputy General of UnitedHealth Group, discusses the critical link between privacy and security, stemming from her diverse career path in tech and law. She emphasizes that an effective privacy program is impossible without a robust security program and highlights the importance of collaboration between privacy and security teams. Williamson is also passionate about mentoring women in technology, advocating for training successful women from other fields to address cybersecurity staff shortages.

title: From Meditation Apps to Virtual Care: Are You Covering the Full Continuum of Mental Health Care?
summary: This article emphasizes the critical importance for employers to invest in a full spectrum of mental health care solutions, from meditation apps to crisis intervention, to address "The Great Resignation" and employee burnout. It highlights the positive impact of comprehensive mental wellness programs on employee retention, productivity, and overall business growth. The piece also suggests strategies for destigmatizing mental health in the workplace and tailoring support to diverse employee needs.

title: UnitedHealth Wins Court Approval of Its Change Healthcare Takeover (UNH, CHNG)
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. received court approval for its $7.8 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare Inc., overcoming a Department of Justice lawsuit aimed at blocking the deal. This decision allows UnitedHealth to further diversify its business beyond insurance by merging Change Healthcare's network with its Optum Insight data and consulting operations. Shares of Change Healthcare saw a 7% increase in early trading following the news.

title: Costco's Prescription Program Now Offers Discount Pricing for Glucose Monitoring System
summary: Costco's Member Prescription Program (CMPP) now offers discount pricing for Intuity Medical's POGO Automatic Blood Glucose Monitoring System and POGO Automatic Test Cartridges, aiming to simplify diabetes management for its members. This FDA-cleared system automates blood glucose testing, reducing the financial barrier through CMPP discounts. The program, which is a value-added benefit for Costco members, previously added a migraine treatment device and reflects Costco's broader expansion in health offerings, amidst strong financial performance.

title: UnitedHealthcare and Peloton to Provide Millions of More People With Access to a Leading Interactive Fitness Platform
summary: UnitedHealthcare and Peloton have renewed and expanded their partnership, making a yearlong Peloton App Membership or a three-month waiver toward a Peloton All-Access Membership available to up to 10 million UnitedHealthcare commercial members at no additional cost. This expanded collaboration aims to encourage more people to stay active, with current participants completing over 1 million Peloton classes per month. Additionally, eligible UnitedHealthcare members in most states will receive preferred pricing on select Peloton connected fitness products.

title: How a Top Fidelity Growth Fund Is Navigating This Market
summary: Fidelity Growth Discovery FDSVX, co-managed by Jason Weiner and Asher Anolic, has navigated 2022's challenging market for growth stocks better than many peers by focusing on "growth quality" rather than simply high-growth potential. The fund emphasizes companies with strong gross margins and predictable earnings growth, incorporating names like Microsoft, Coca-Cola, and UnitedHealth Group, which are not typically associated with aggressive growth funds. This strategy has helped the fund outperform its category over various timeframes despite the overall market downturn.

title: Scoop: Novo agrees to acquire Pritzker's KabaFusion
summary: Novo Holdings has reached an agreement to acquire KabaFusion, a home infusion company specializing in intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), from Pritzker Private Capital. This acquisition is significant as the home infusion market is highly fragmented, providing an opportunity for KabaFusion to become a major consolidator akin to OptumRx and Option Care Health. The deal positions KabaFusion as a potential starting point for a larger, diversified platform in the industry.

title: TPG Capital ready to invest in ClaimsXten, name its CEO if deal closes
summary: TPG Capital is reportedly prepared to invest in ClaimsXten and appoint its CEO if the acquisition from UnitedHealth Group goes through. The article indicates this potential investment within the context of healthcare mergers and acquisitions.

title: AGS Health Launches Artificial Intelligence Platform for End-to-End Revenue Cycle Management
summary: AGS Health, a leading revenue cycle management (RCM) solutions provider, has launched its new AI Platform designed to enhance revenue cycle performance for healthcare systems. The platform integrates AI and automation with expert human support to address labor shortages, reduce denial rates, and improve financial stability. It offers solutions such as revenue cycle automation, computer-assisted coding, and clinical documentation improvement, aiming to free up skilled staff for more complex tasks and optimize financial operations for healthcare organizations.

title: New technology used for fall Career Fair
summary: The Fall 2022 Internship & Job Career Fair at Washington University in St. Louis saw record attendance with over 2,200 students and many new employers. The Career Center utilized Handshake, a new technology, to help students prepare and connect with companies, and for companies to personalize their hiring processes. A key takeaway was the emphasis on diversity in skills and backgrounds, with companies encouraging interdisciplinary applicants.

title: DaVita loses bid to dismiss class 'no-poach' claims
summary: A Chicago federal judge denied DaVita Inc's bid to dismiss a class-action antitrust lawsuit alleging the company and others conspired to restrain employee compensation and mobility. While DaVita previously won a criminal antitrust case related to employment practices, this civil case, brought by former employees of a company acquired by UnitedHealth, will now proceed to discovery. The judge dismissed claims against UnitedHealth but allowed plaintiffs to refile amended claims.

title: Amazon.com unveils device that tracks breath while sleeping
summary: Amazon has announced a new contactless sleep-tracking gadget called Halo Rise, priced at $139.99, which monitors room conditions and breathing patterns to provide insights into sleep quality. This device, not FDA-approved, is part of Amazon's broader investment in consumer health technology. The company also unveiled updates to its Kindle e-readers and voice-controlled devices.

title: Report reveals the impact of unintended pregnancies
summary: A new report by Organon, "The Impact of Unintended Pregnancy," reveals that 40% of all pregnancies in Australia are unintended, costing an astounding $7.2 billion in 2020. The report highlights that this issue is disproportionately higher among First Nations women and socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals, often due to geographic isolation and lack of access to contraception and abortion services. Experts emphasize the need for better access to information and effective contraception, particularly long-acting reversible contraception (LARC), to address this significant public health challenge.

title: Brian M. Anderson – Option Care Health
summary: This article profiles Brian M. Anderson, Director of Real Estate, Facility Management & Security at Option Care Health, highlighting his role in overseeing the development of a 50,000-square-foot infusion therapy compounding facility in Itasca, Illinois, during the COVID-19 pandemic. It discusses his extensive career in healthcare facilities management, his focus on efficiency and standardization across Option Care Health's numerous facilities, and his passion for the real estate aspect of the healthcare industry. The piece also touches on his commitment to teamwork, vendor relationships, and community involvement.

title: Evernorth’s Birthday Wish: Better Health for All
summary: Evernorth, a Cigna Corporation organization, celebrates its second anniversary, reflecting on its achievements in making healthcare better through its key capabilities like Pharmacy+, Benefits Management+, Care+, and Intelligence+. Leaders across the organization highlight milestones such as expanding behavioral health networks, improving access and affordability, and developing innovative care solutions. The company reaffirms its commitment to transforming healthcare by focusing on integrated, data-driven approaches and leveraging its talent and expertise.

title: Centene Agrees to Pay Massachusetts $14 Million Over Medicaid Prescription Claims
summary: Centene Corp. has agreed to pay Massachusetts $14.2 million to settle allegations that it overbilled the state's Medicaid program for pharmacy services. This settlement is part of a larger trend, with Centene having settled similar claims with several other states for a total exceeding $489 million. The company, which is the nation's largest Medicaid managed-care insurer, denies wrongdoing but aims to resolve concerns.

title: UnitedHealth closes roughly $8B deal for Change Healthcare
summary: UnitedHealth Group has finalized its approximately $8 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare, two weeks after a federal judge dismissed a challenge from regulators. The technology company will be integrated into UnitedHealth's Optum segment, aiming to streamline administrative and payment processes for healthcare providers. This deal was initially opposed by the U.S. Department of Justice due to concerns about data monopolization, but a judge ultimately ruled in favor of UnitedHealth, noting the company's incentives to protect customer data.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s Optum Closes $13 Billion Change Healthcare Deal
summary: UnitedHealth Group's Optum unit completed its $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare after fending off a U.S. Justice Department challenge. The deal aims to integrate Change Healthcare into OptumInsight, bolstering efforts to improve health outcomes, population health, and streamline healthcare processes. This acquisition is seen as a significant move by UnitedHealth to expand its presence on the medical care provider side of the healthcare system.

title: UnitedHealth closes acquisition of Change Healthcare
summary: UnitedHealth Group has successfully closed its acquisition of Change Healthcare following a federal court win against the Department of Justice's antitrust challenge. The deal aims to simplify and adapt the healthcare system for payers, providers, and patients by connecting core clinical, administrative, and payment processes, promising lower costs and a better experience for all stakeholders. The acquisition moved forward after a judge ruled that the DOJ failed to provide sufficient evidence that the merger would harm competition, provided Change's ClaimsXten business was divested.

title: UnitedHealth Group completes $13 billion deal to acquire Change Healthcare
summary: UnitedHealth Group has successfully completed its $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare after a federal judge ruled against the Justice Department's attempt to block the merger. The court determined the government failed to prove the acquisition would harm competition, citing UnitedHealth's strong incentives to protect sensitive information and preserve its multi-payer business model. Change Healthcare, a health care data firm, will now operate as part of UnitedHealth's Optum division.

title: The Home-Focused Benefits Of 6 Medicare Advantage Organizations for 2023
summary: This article details the home-focused benefits offered by six Medicare Advantage (MA) organizations for 2023, as the annual enrollment period approaches. Companies like Cigna, Humana, UnitedHealth Group, Aetna, and Blue Shield of California are expanding their in-home care services, companionship programs, and other support to address chronic conditions and social determinants of health. These offerings leverage increased flexibility in MA plans to provide primarily health-related and Special Supplemental Benefits for the Chronically Ill (SSBCI) services.

title: Anthem must face U.S. government lawsuit alleging Medicare Advantage fraud
summary: A federal judge has ruled that Anthem Inc. must face a U.S. government lawsuit accusing it of fraudulently collecting tens of millions of dollars in Medicare overpayments. The lawsuit alleges that Anthem submitted inaccurate diagnosis data for its Medicare Advantage plans, with the total alleged overpayment exceeding $100 million. This decision comes as part of ongoing Justice Department efforts against companies involved in Medicare Advantage overbilling.

title: Done deal: UnitedHealth completes $13B Change Healthcare buy
summary: UnitedHealth Group has completed its $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare, after successfully defeating the Department of Justice's attempt to block the deal in federal court. The DOJ has not indicated it will appeal the decision, marking a significant setback for the agency in its antitrust efforts. Change Healthcare's stock trading has been suspended, and UnitedHealth previously agreed to divest ClaimsXten to address antitrust concerns.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s Optum completes $8B merger with Change Healthcare
summary: UnitedHealth Group's Optum has finalized its nearly $8 billion merger with Change Healthcare, bringing an end to a controversial transaction initially announced in 2021. The deal was allowed to proceed after a federal judge ruled against the Department of Justice's antitrust concerns, requiring UnitedHealth Group to divest its ClaimsXen business. This merger is part of a larger trend of acquisitions by UnitedHealth Group amidst increasing scrutiny of consolidation in the healthcare industry.

title: CVS Health selling benefits technology provider bswift to Francisco Partners
summary: CVS Health is selling its benefits technology provider bswift to Francisco Partners, a global investment firm specializing in technology businesses. While financial terms were not disclosed, bswift will continue its partnership with CVS Health and Aetna. This divestiture comes as CVS Health also engages in acquisitions, such as the recent $8 billion deal for Signify Health.

title: TPG Capital closes $2.2B acquisition of claims-editing business ClaimsXten
summary: TPG Capital has finalized its $2.2 billion acquisition of ClaimsXten, the claims-editing business from Change Healthcare, following UnitedHealth Group's acquisition of Change Healthcare. The sale of ClaimsXten was a condition for securing federal approval for the UnitedHealth Group-Change Healthcare merger. TPG Capital plans to significantly increase ClaimsXten's R&D budget to accelerate its growth.

title: ‘The Cash Monster Was Insatiable’: How Insurers Exploited Medicare for Billions (Published 2022)
summary: Major health insurers offering Medicare Advantage plans have been accused of widespread fraud, exploiting the program to inflate profits by billions. They allegedly urged doctors to add additional illnesses to patient records, even offering incentives, leading to diagnoses of serious diseases that might not have existed and allowing insurers to collect more money from the federal government. These practices have prompted numerous lawsuits, inspector general audits, and investigations by watchdogs.

title: Walmart to compete with Walgreens, CVS in recruiting clinical trial subjects
summary: Walmart announced its entry into clinical trial recruitment through its new service, Walmart Healthcare Research Institute, directly competing with Walgreens and CVS Health Group. The initiative aims to leverage Walmart's diverse customer base across its clinics and pharmacies to help drug companies find participants for clinical trials, addressing a common challenge in medical research. This move is part of Walmart's broader strategy to expand into high-margin businesses like healthcare, following similar ventures by its rivals.

title: Johnson & Johnson or UnitedHealth: Which Stock Is More Recession Proof?
summary: This article compares Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) and UnitedHealth Group (UNH) to determine which stock is more recession-proof. It highlights JNJ's historical performance during the Great Recession, its diversified inelastic spending, and its status as a Dividend King. UnitedHealth's increased focus on Medicare customers and managed healthcare is also discussed, though J&J is ultimately deemed the safer choice due to its stability and generous dividend.

title: Getting to Know the Humana Inc. Leaders, Founders, and Executives
summary: This article introduces the key leaders and executives of Humana Inc., a prominent health insurance provider. It details their roles, responsibilities, and significant contributions to the company and the healthcare industry. The article also provides background information on Humana's founding, headquarters, services, and the industries it serves.

title: Press Release: GEHA and the Baltimore Ravens Launch Purple Ticket to Health
summary: GEHA, Novo Nordisk, and the Baltimore Ravens have launched the "Purple Ticket to Health" program to encourage Ravens fans to adopt healthier lifestyles. Participants can complete an online health questionnaire to learn about preventative health practices and enter to win exclusive prizes. The initiative aims to raise awareness about medical conditions like obesity and diabetes and make health resources accessible to the community.

title: UnitedHealth Group's quarterly profit soars to $5.26B
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported a soaring third-quarter profit of $5.26 billion, beating analyst estimates and prompting raised financial guidance for the year. The company is actively expanding in the individual health insurance market and signaled a continued focus on mergers and acquisitions. Operating profit grew significantly in its UnitedHealthcare and Optum divisions, driven by increased membership and strategic management.

title: New initiative to prevent, treat and beat stroke focuses on health equity, heart-brain connection
summary: The American Heart Association, in conjunction with HCA Healthcare and the HCA Healthcare Foundation, launched the "Getting to the Heart of Stroke™" initiative with $15 million in funding. This program aims to prevent, treat, and beat stroke by focusing on health equity, the heart-brain connection, and educating both healthcare professionals and the public. It will target 15 local markets across the U.S. to improve outcomes and address disparities, particularly for populations at higher risk.

title: Follow the Money: Medical Device Firm Orthofix Merges to Form Nearly $700M Revenue Business, Stealthy Men's Health Startup Looks to Raise $2M, Dallas SPAC Targets $200M IPO, and More
summary: This article details various financial activities in North Texas, including Orthofix's merger to create a nearly $700M revenue medical device business and Mavenir's $155M funding round. It also covers a stealthy men's health startup, Mango Rx, seeking to raise $2M, and a Dallas SPAC targeting a $200M IPO, alongside other investments and acquisitions across different sectors. The report highlights significant investments in technology, healthcare, real estate, and sustainability.

title: UnitedHealth Group puts Minnetonka office space up for sublease
summary: UnitedHealth Group is looking to sublease office space at 12700 Whitewater Drive in Minnetonka. This marks the third large office property associated with UnitedHealth Group or its subsidiaries to become available on the leasing market recently. The specific article is a brief update on this development.

title: Benefits Open Enrollment is Nov. 1-15
summary: King County employees have new benefit options available during Open Enrollment from November 1-15. Changes for 2023 include a new Cigna Dental HMO plan, the opportunity to increase supplemental life insurance up to 6x salary, and a fourth network option (Virginia Mason Franciscan Health) for the KingCare Select medical plan. Employees are encouraged to review these changes and attend benefit fairs or online information sessions to learn more.

title: Elevance says it’s now the largest US insurer, beating out UnitedHealthcare. Analysts say it’s not that simple.
summary: Elevance Health claims it has surpassed UnitedHealthcare to become the largest insurer in the U.S. based on medical membership, a position it has held for the past six quarters. However, analysts dispute this claim, arguing that Elevance's method of counting BlueCard members leads to "double counting." While Elevance reports 47.2 million members including BlueCard, and UnitedHealthcare 45.9 million, excluding BlueCard members would place Elevance as the second-largest insurer, highlighting differing interpretations of "largest."

title: Helena Haynes-Carter: Notable Executives in Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 2022
summary: Helena Haynes-Carter, executive vice president and chief diversity, equity and inclusion officer at KeyCorp, is recognized for her extensive experience in fostering diversity and inclusion. She leads enterprise-wide DEI programs at Key, including commitments to increase representation of people of color in senior leadership and significant investments in diverse communities. Haynes-Carter previously orchestrated a $14 million COVID-19 response at UnitedHealth Group and serves on the board of National INROADS.

title: Battle Breast Cancer With Simplify’s PINK
summary: The article highlights Simplify Health Care ETF (PINK) as a fund that supports breast cancer research. Simplify donates 100% of the profits from the PINK ETF to the Susan G. Komen Foundation, with the strategy managed pro-bono by Michael Taylor. The ETF has performed well, outperforming its category average and the S&P 500 over the past month.

title: AccentCare, LHC Group, VITAS Execs: Care Continuum Sprawl Central to Hospice’s Growth
summary: Executives from AccentCare, LHC Group, and VITAS Healthcare emphasize that expanding across the care continuum is crucial for sustainable growth in the hospice industry. The article highlights how these major players are leveraging de novos, mergers, and acquisitions to broaden their service offerings and meet the rising demand from an aging population. It details each company's specific strategies, including LHC Group's focus on co-locating hospice services with home health, AccentCare's integration with serious illness care providers, and VITAS Healthcare's historical emphasis on de novo growth and deeper market penetration.

title: Preferred Pharmacy Networks in 2023’s Medicare Part D Plans: Cigna, CVS Health, Humana, UnitedHealthcare, WellCare, and More
summary: This article analyzes the prevalence of preferred pharmacy networks in 2023 Medicare Part D plans, highlighting their continued dominance with 98% of stand-alone plans and 52% of Medicare Advantage plans utilizing them. It details offerings from major companies like Cigna, CVS Health, Humana, UnitedHealthcare, and WellCare, noting that all major national stand-alone PDPs will feature preferred networks. The article also discusses a trend where Preferred Provider Organization (PPO) MA-PD plans are decreasing their use of preferred networks to offer more flexible pharmacy choices and attract seniors.

title: Popular Dry Shampoos Found to Have Cancer-CausinTg Chemical
summary: An independent study by Valisure found that 70% of 148 batches from 34 brands of spray-on dry shampoo contained high levels of benzene, a known carcinogen. Brands like Not Your Mother's, Batiste, Sun Bum, and John Paul Mitchell Systems were identified, some with significantly higher benzene levels than previously found in other personal-care products. Valisure has filed a petition with the FDA requesting a recall of these products, highlighting concerns about the complexity of the supply chain and the regulation of cosmetics.

title: CVS execs promise a 'seamless' transition for Centene members when PBM contract ends
summary: CVS Health executives addressed Centene's decision to move its pharmacy benefit management contract to Express Scripts, a deal valued at $35 billion covering 20 million members starting in 2024. CVS CEO Karen Lynch stated that Caremark made a competitive bid and will ensure a seamless transition for Centene members. Meanwhile, Centene's CEO Sarah London anticipates significant savings from the new partnership with Express Scripts, which helped Centene exceed third-quarter profit and revenue predictions.

title: CVS looks to 2023 after opioids settlement, Medicare rating decline
summary: CVS Health Corp forecasted a 2023 profit below Wall Street estimates due to a Medicare plan rating decline and announced a $5 billion opioid settlement. The company plans to mitigate the Medicare impact by shifting members to other plans and is considering selling its Omnicare long-term care business. Despite these challenges, CVS is confident in achieving its 2024 earnings target through share repurchases and potential acquisitions.

title: AARP-Branded Medicare Drug Plan Is Too Costly for Many Retirees, Critics Say
summary: The AARP-branded MedicareRx Preferred plan, insured by UnitedHealth Group Inc., is criticized for its high premiums, which are the highest among all national stand-alone Medicare drug plans. Despite covering a higher percentage of drugs and having no deductible, experts suggest that its price has become too high for many retirees, prompting them to consider switching to less expensive alternatives. The plan currently has 1.74 million members, representing a 9% market share in stand-alone Part D coverage.

title: Recent Acquisitions by Humana, UnitedHealth Group and CVS Health/Aetna
summary: This article details recent acquisitions of home health companies by major Medicare Advantage (MA) providers Humana, UnitedHealth Group, and CVS Health/Aetna. These acquisitions, including Kindred at Home, LHC Group, and Signify Health, highlight the growing focus on in-home care delivery as demographics age and chronic disease prevalence increases. The article also discusses how these acquisitions aim to improve patient outcomes, reduce costs, and optimize risk-adjusted factors for the acquiring companies.

title: WellMed Medical Management faces defamation lawsuit from San Antonio company
summary: WellMed Medical Management is being sued for defamation and business disparagement by San Antonio’s CareMore Clinic Solutions. CareMore and its principal, Rolando “Henry” Sanchez, allege that WellMed employees falsely accused Sanchez of "steering" patients, which is a federal crime. The lawsuit seeks damages between $250,000 and $1 million, claiming the accusations harmed Sanchez's professional reputation.

title: Medicare Advantage insurers face high marketing stakes
summary: Medicare Advantage insurers are significantly increasing their marketing efforts. The article highlights the high stakes involved in these intensified marketing activities. It also touches upon related legal actions concerning anti-competitive tactics in healthcare and AI partnerships for prior authorization.

title: Prop. 29: Californians reject measure to alter dialysis clinic rules
summary: For the third time in as many elections, California voters rejected Proposition 29, a ballot measure aimed at mandating significant changes to the operations of dialysis clinics. The proposition, which failed with nearly 70% of voters saying "no," would have required a doctor, nurse practitioner, or physician's assistant to be present during treatments at the state's 600 outpatient dialysis facilities. Opponents argued the financial burden could lead to clinic closures and reduced patient access, while supporters contended it was crucial for patient safety and better care.

title: WPP and SeeHer Release ‘Health On Her Terms’ -- New Research Reveals Significant Gaps and Continued Gender Bias in Marketing, Advertising and Media Portraying Women and their Health
summary: WPP and SeeHer released new research titled 'Health On Her Terms,' revealing significant gaps and continued gender bias in how women's health is portrayed in marketing, advertising, and media. The study highlights that nearly half of women feel media avoids women's health issues, and there's a strong desire for more diverse and authentic representation across reproductive health, weight, and mental health. The research urges brands to break down taboos and adopt a "Marketer’s Hippocratic Oath to Women" to drive real change and better health outcomes.

title: Aveanna’s Home Health, Hospice Business Takes Punches During First Year as Publicly Traded Company
summary: Aveanna Healthcare Holdings, Inc.'s home health and hospice segments experienced disappointing growth in Q3, their first year as a publicly traded company, despite overall revenue increases. The company attributes these struggles to operational headwinds, including new system implementations and labor challenges, but anticipates a rebound in Q4 and 2023 driven by acquisitions and favorable demographics. Executives also expect improved profitability and cash collections as they address these issues and align with new operating systems.

title: Report Finds “Code of Silence” at Mental Health Facility Where Staff Abused and Neglected Patients
summary: A new report from a watchdog office within the Illinois Department of Human Services reveals a "code of silence" among staff at Choate Mental Health and Developmental Center, where employees allegedly covered up a brutal assault on a patient. This report echoes earlier investigative journalism by ProPublica and other news organizations, highlighting a pervasive culture of abuse and neglect. The OIG report recommends stricter consequences for staff who impede investigations, including the use of security cameras, and calls for legislative action to strengthen laws governing conduct standards for direct-care workers.

title: UnitedHealth Group's CCO Jennifer Smoter insists on measurement to hold comms accountable
summary: Jennifer Smoter, CCO of UnitedHealth Group, emphasizes the importance of measurement to hold communications accountable and directly align comms strategy with business goals. She has worked to ensure comms functions are responsible for the success of the business, focusing on demonstrating impact beyond traditional metrics and improving employee engagement through innovative channels like AI-powered intranets. Smoter also highlights UHG's efforts in addressing health equity and promoting value-based care.

title: Grassroots organization holds impromptu protest in lobby of Elevance headquarters
summary: A progressive grassroots organization called People's Action staged an impromptu protest at the headquarters of Elevance Health, formerly BlueCross BlueShield. The protest was triggered by unanswered demands regarding insurance claim denials, with organizers seeking transparency on how denials disproportionately affect certain demographics. One individual reported being physical struck by a security guard during the protest, while another shared a personal experience of a latent claim denial from Anthem.

title: Amazon Starts Virtual Health Referral Service Linking Patients to Doctors
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has launched "Amazon Clinic," a new virtual health referral service designed to connect patients with healthcare providers for various conditions, including acne, hair loss, and allergies. This initiative marks Amazon's continued expansion into the healthcare sector, complementing its existing online pharmacy and its acquisition of One Medical. The service aims to streamline access to virtual medical consultations.

title: At-Home Care Provider DispatchHealth Raises Over $330 Million In Latest Funding Round
summary: DispatchHealth, an in-home medical company, has secured over $330 million in its latest funding round, bringing its total funding to more than $700 million since 2013. The equity raise was led by Optum Ventures with support from existing and new investors, while the debt raise was led by Silicon Valley Bank and K2 HealthVentures. The company plans to use the funds to expand its high-acuity in-home care ecosystem across more than 50 markets and further develop its proprietary Last Mile Health Care Technology Platform.

title: Risky Business: The Build-Versus-Buy Crossroads for Mental Health Companies
summary: As economic conditions shift, mental health companies are evaluating whether to pursue acquisitions or prioritize organic growth through de novo expansion. Some larger providers, like LifeStance Health, are now focusing on organic growth, as smaller "tuck-in" acquisitions can be time-consuming, risky, and may not meet expectations. Industry experts suggest that de novos could be more cost-effective and faster, potentially leading to less demand and multiple compression for smaller behavioral health acquisitions.

title: UnitedHealthcare to Help Millions of AARP Members Save on Hearing Aids
summary: UnitedHealthcare and AARP have partnered to launch AARP® Hearing Solutions™ provided by UnitedHealthcare Hearing, aiming to make hearing aids more affordable and accessible for millions of AARP members. This new program offers prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids at significantly reduced prices, starting as low as $699 per device, along with professional support, no-cost hearing tests, and virtual care options. The initiative addresses historical barriers of high costs and lack of access, offering financial savings and comprehensive support for individuals with hearing loss.

title: A Judge Let UnitedHealth Make a Deal That Gives It Key Data From Insurance Rivals
summary: A federal judge permitted UnitedHealth Group to acquire Change Healthcare, a company that processes a significant portion of U.S. medical insurance claims. This acquisition grants UnitedHealth access to a vast amount of claims data from rival insurers, despite internal company documents suggesting potential antitrust concerns and evidence presented by the Justice Department. The article highlights UnitedHealth's history of questionable practices and the difficulty of blocking vertical mergers in antitrust law.

title: Spotlight on Recent Federal Regulatory Actions Open for Public Comment
summary: This article highlights two key federal regulatory actions by CMS that are open for public comment: a proposed rule to streamline Medicaid and CHIP eligibility processes and a Request for Information (RFI) regarding the creation of a National Directory of Health Providers and Services. The Medicaid rule aims to reduce coverage disruptions and procedural hurdles, impacting states, payers, and providers. The RFI seeks input on standardizing provider directory data to improve accuracy and reduce burdens.

title: Video: Cigna CEO David Cordani Says Now is the Time To Reassess the Blueprint for Employee Well-Being
summary: Cigna CEO David Cordani discusses the importance of employee well-being and the Evernorth Vitality Index with Fortune editor Ruth Umoh. The index provides insights into individual and workforce vitality, helping employers create healthy and engaged workforces, especially in light of increased mental health challenges post-pandemic. Cordani emphasizes the need for companies to reassess their approach to employee well-being to improve overall vitality and quality of life.

title: Hidden audits reveal millions in overcharges by Medicare Advantage plans
summary: Newly released federal audits have uncovered widespread overcharges and errors in payments to Medicare Advantage health plans, revealing some plans overbilled the government by over $1,000 per patient annually. Obtained through a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit, the audits from 2011-2013 identified $12 million in net overpayments, with potential total recoupments estimated at $650 million. Critics argue the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has been slow to hold insurers accountable, while insurers express concerns about the audit process itself.

title: 3 reasons a major health insurer just made a $2.7 billion bet on a Walgreens-backed effort to upend healthcare
summary: Cigna is investing $2.7 billion in the merger between VillageMD and Summit Health-CityMD, a deal that will create a large primary, specialty, and urgent care provider. This investment gives Cigna a minority stake in the growing company, offers an annual dividend of approximately 5.5%, and accelerates its shift towards value-based care models. Cigna CFO Brian Evanko highlighted the financial attractiveness and strategic importance of moving members towards care models that link provider payments to quality and cost.

title: Leader of Walmart health business leaves for JPMorgan Chase
summary: Dr. Cheryl Pegus, head of Walmart's health and wellness business, is departing her role to join Morgan Health, a business unit of JPMorgan Chase. Morgan Health focuses on employer-sponsored health care.

title: Vacant, massive Howard office complex goes up for auction. Starting bid? $2.7 million
summary: A former UnitedHealth Group headquarters in Howard, Wisconsin, valued at $25 million, is going up for auction with a starting bid of $2.7 million. The 382,000-square-foot facility has been vacant for over a year and is attracting interest due to its potential for mixed-use redevelopment given its large size. The auction runs from November 28-30 and the village hopes a new owner will revitalize the property.

title: ETF of the Week: Amplify CWP Enhanced Dividend Income ETF (DIVO)
summary: This article highlights the Amplify CWP Enhanced Dividend Income ETF (DIVO) as the ETF of the Week, discussed by VettaFi's Tom Lydon. DIVO aims to provide monthly dividend income and potential capital appreciation through a strategy of investing in dividend-growing companies and strategically writing covered calls. It offers investors a defensive play with healthy income potential, especially relevant in volatile markets, and targets a gross annual income of 2-3% from dividends and 2-4% from option premiums.

title: Wages Rising for Hospice Workers; Aides See 9.09% Increase
summary: Wages for hospice aides and CNAs increased by 9.09% in 2022, a significant jump from 4.52% in 2021, according to a recent report, as providers combat high turnover rates among these essential staff. The industry faces substantial workforce pressures, leading to higher wages, enhanced benefits, and bonus programs across various roles to attract and retain employees. Companies like VITAS Healthcare are implementing large retention bonuses, using unspent Provider Relief Funds, which has shown positive results in clinician hiring and reduced turnover.

title: UnitedHealth Group projects up to $360B in 2023 revenue, buoyed by Optum growth
summary: UnitedHealth Group projects revenue of up to $360 billion for 2023, primarily driven by the strong growth of its Optum health services arm, which anticipates $212 billion to $214 billion in revenues. This growth is expected despite a recent Department of Justice appeal challenging UnitedHealth's $13 billion acquisition of Change Healthcare. The company also forecasts significant increases in Medicare Advantage and commercial risk-based plan enrollments, along with a profit between $21.7 billion and $22.3 billion in 2023.

title: Challenges Continue for Urban Outfitters Chain
summary: The Urban Outfitters brand is facing significant challenges due to inflation impacting its younger demographic with less discretionary income, leading to a 9% drop in retail comps in Q3. In contrast, its sister brands, Anthropologie and Free People, are performing well as their more affluent customers continue to spend. The company acknowledges issues with price increases and excess inventory at Urban Outfitters North America, contrasting with strong performance in Europe.

title: U.S. Bancorp completes $8 billion acquisition of West Coast's MUFG Union Bank
summary: U.S. Bancorp has finalized its $8 billion acquisition of MUFG Union Bank's core retail banking operations, significantly expanding its presence on the West Coast, particularly in California, Oregon, and Washington. This deal marks U.S. Bancorp's largest transaction since 2001 and is expected to enhance its competitiveness and investment in technology and digital services. The acquisition followed a longer-than-anticipated regulatory approval process, with account conversions and systems integration slated for the first half of 2023.

title: FDA change ushers in cheaper, easier-to-get hearing aids
summary: A recent FDA rule change has made over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids available, significantly reducing costs and increasing accessibility for adults with mild-to-moderate hearing loss. These devices are now sold without a prescription at major retailers, offering a more affordable alternative to traditional prescription hearing aids. The article details who can benefit, where to buy them, what to look for, and outlines the cost differences and insurance considerations.

title: Video: Tips for Improving Your Health, Strength, and Energy in 2023
summary: This article provides eight simple tips for improving health, strength, and energy in 2023, focusing on increasing personal vitality. These tips range from physical activities like walking and healthy eating to social connections, routine check-ups, and fostering a sense of purpose. The advice aims to help individuals achieve a healthier and more fulfilling life as supported by various research studies.

title: The health insurer will see you now: How UnitedHealth is keeping more profits, as your doctor
summary: UnitedHealth Group is projected to increase its profits by directing its insurance members to its own Optum-owned healthcare providers and pharmacies. This strategy allows UnitedHealth to channel insurance premiums to its provider side, as provider profits are not capped in the same way insurer profits are. The company has become a major provider of outpatient care through numerous acquisitions of physician practices, surgery centers, urgent care facilities, and pharmacy benefit managers.

title: Self-funded plans sue Anthem, alleging overcharging and other ERISA violations
summary: Self-funded health plans are suing Anthem, alleging the insurer engaged in overcharging and violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). The lawsuit claims Anthem's practices led to inflated costs for the plans. This legal action highlights concerns about transparency and fair pricing within the health insurance industry for self-funded employers.

title: Optum’s LHC Group Acquisition Expected to Close in Q1 2023
summary: Optum's acquisition of LHC Group, valued at $5.5 billion, is now anticipated to close in the first quarter of 2023, following an initial expectation for a 2022 closure. The delay comes after two requests for more information from the Federal Trade Commission. This deal, along with Humana's purchase of Kindred at Home, signifies a growing trend of payers acquiring healthcare provider companies, particularly those involved in value-based care models.

title: UnitedHealth names Google exec Kirsten Gil to board of directors
summary: UnitedHealth Group has appointed Google executive Kirsten Gil to its Board of Directors. Gil, a long-time leader at Alphabet (Google’s parent company), brings extensive experience in business operations, strategy, and finance across various Google departments, including search, maps, AI, and sustainability. Her appointment is expected to strengthen UnitedHealth's board with diverse tech and business expertise.

title: UnitedHealth buys third building this year near Minnetonka headquarters
summary: United HealthCare Services Inc. recently purchased a third property in Minnetonka this year, located near the headquarters of its parent company, UnitedHealth Group Inc. This acquisition follows other purchases made by the company earlier in the year, indicating a pattern of expanding its real estate holdings in the area. The article also mentions related stories about UnitedHealth Group's real estate activities, including subleasing office space and uncertainty regarding Optum's tech office campus.

title: State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV), including its current stock price, key statistics, holdings, dividend data, and historical performance. As of Q3 2025, XLV has 60 holdings with a total value of $33.97 billion, with top holdings being Eli Lilly and Co, Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie Inc, UnitedHealth Group Inc, and Abbott Laboratories. The article also provides historical data for Price-to-Earnings, Price-to-Book, and Dividend Yield.

title: Centene Gives Big as It Courts Contracts and Settles Accusations of Overbilling
summary: Centene Corp., the largest Medicaid managed-care company, contributed over $26.9 million to state politicians and parties while simultaneously pursuing government contracts and settling accusations of overbilling taxpayers. The company, facing investigations in over 20 states and having paid approximately $613 million in settlements, uses its profits to influence officials overseeing its contracts. Centene maintains its contributions support sound public policy healthcare decisions and comply with all laws.

title: Top 10 Behavioral Health Stories of 2022: How ABA Layoffs, Value-Based Care and Dealmaking Defined the Year
summary: The behavioral health industry in 2022 faced significant challenges and developments, including mass layoffs among autism providers, a push towards value-based care, and robust dealmaking despite setbacks. Key stories highlighted the impact of workforce shortages, payer dynamics, the controversial use of AI in therapy, and major acquisitions like Optum's purchase of Refresh Mental Health. The year also saw scrutiny over patient data privacy and a focus on serious mental illness by leading platforms.

title: 5 Numbers that Shaped Hospice in 2022
summary: In 2022, the hospice industry was shaped by five key numbers: clinical capacity, length of stay, labor costs, utilization, and the rising number of new hospices in certain states. The ubiquitous labor shortage significantly affected capacity, length of stay by delaying admissions, and led to increased labor costs due to higher wages and bonuses. While utilization dipped in 2020 partly due to the pandemic and evolving patient profiles, a new concern emerged with the proliferation of potentially unethical new hospices in states like California, Arizona, Nevada, and Texas, prompting calls for stricter regulation.

title: Zynex: Company Improperly Billing Worker’s Compensation Funds for TENS Devices; Practices Strikingly Similar to Competitor Being Sued by 28 Liberty Mutual Insurers
summary: A Capitol Forum investigation alleges that Zynex (ZYXI) is improperly billing worker's compensation funds for TENS devices and related supplies, using practices strikingly similar to those of competitor Electrostim Medical Services (EMSI), which is being sued by 28 Liberty Mutual insurers for fraudulent billing and unbundling. The issues include using incorrect billing codes, unbundling supply charges, and shipping excessive amounts of supplies to patients. Former employees confirm pressure to increase reimbursement through loopholes, while Zynex disputes the claims.
