title: Addressing Mental Health Parity Enforcement Activities
summary: This article discusses the increasing enforcement of the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act of 2008 (MHPAEA) in the United States, highlighting the critical need for health plans to ensure compliance. It provides an overview of mental health statistics, the regulatory timeline, recent enforcement actions by federal and state agencies, and common areas where organizations fall short in meeting parity requirements. The authors also outline an approach for organizations to improve operations and policies to address MHPAEA compliance effectively.

title: American billionaire Daniel Loeb’s share portfolio revealed
summary: This article details the share portfolio of American billionaire Daniel Loeb, founder and CEO of Third Point. It highlights his investment strategy, recent changes in his firm's holdings, and provides a table of Third Point's top 38 share positions as of September 30, 2022. Key moves include increasing stakes in Colgate-Palmolive and Danaher, and significantly cutting positions in Ovintiv and DuPont de Nemours.

title: UnitedHealth class action alleges company collects fee from phantom savings
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against UnitedHealth Group Inc., alleging the company collects a "savings fee" based on "phantom savings" it claims to have obtained for healthcare plan members. Plaintiffs argue that UnitedHealth deliberately ignores competitive fee data, leading to underpayment for out-of-network services and leaving plan members responsible for the unpaid portions of their bills. The lawsuit seeks to represent a nationwide class of participants in self-funded employer-sponsored health benefit plans and claims UnitedHealth violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA).

title: CVS Has Little Time to Waste as Amazon, Walgreens Ink Doctor Deals
summary: CVS is urged to accelerate its expansion into healthcare services to compete with industry leader UnitedHealth Group and fend off rivals like Amazon and Walgreens, who are also making moves into the medical field. Despite owning a pharmacy-benefits manager and Aetna, CVS needs to continue its aggressive growth strategy, even under pressure to focus on share buybacks. The company, through its MinuteClinics and HealthHub stores, already offers limited healthcare but aims to become a primary medical provider for many Americans.

title: FTC to Investigate CVS Caremark and Other Pharmacy-Benefit Managers - WSJ
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is launching an investigation into six of the largest pharmacy-benefit managers (PBMs), including CVS Caremark and Express Scripts Inc. The inquiry will examine the impact of their business models on the accessibility and affordability of prescription drugs. The FTC will require these PBMs to provide records and information for a study of the industry.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | CVS Is in Advanced Talks to Buy Signify Health for Around $8 Billion
summary: CVS Health Corp. is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire home-healthcare company Signify Health Inc. for approximately $8 billion. This potential acquisition suggests CVS has outbid other interested parties, including Amazon.com Inc. and UnitedHealth Group Inc. The deal for Signify Health could be announced in the near future.

title: America’s largest hospital company is booming. So why is one community trying to run it out of town?
summary: HCA Healthcare, the largest for-profit hospital operator in the U.S., has reported record profits during the pandemic, but its acquisition of Mission Hospital in Asheville, NC, has sparked significant community backlash. Patients and former staff accuse HCA of understaffing, compromising care quality, and prioritizing profits over community health, leading to an antitrust lawsuit and widespread distrust despite the company's financial success and investments.

title: Dashed hopes: Centene’s abrupt shift on its Charlotte expansion
summary: Centene has halted its Charlotte expansion project, initially touted to bring 3,230 jobs and significant investment, after investing $700 million. This abrupt shift is attributed to changed work preferences towards remote roles, the death of former CEO Michael Neidorff, and prior investor dissatisfaction with the company's financial performance and regulatory issues. The unfinished East Coast headquarters building is now up for sale, alongside Centene facing settlements for alleged Medicaid fraud in multiple states.

title: Hospice the Next Generation: How the Benefit Could Change
summary: The Medicare Hospice Benefit, fundamentally unchanged for 40 years, is poised for significant transformation due to catalysts like regulation, technology, and value-based payment models. This shift aims for greater integration with the broader healthcare system, moving away from its historical segregation. While these changes promise to expand access and improve care coordination, they also present challenges such as workforce shortages and the complex negotiation of new payment structures.

title: What You Own in a Growth or Value ETF Just Changed
summary: A significant rebalance of S&P 500 Style Index-based ETFs occurred in late December 2022, altering the composition of growth and value ETFs. This reclassification led to mega-cap energy and healthcare companies historically seen as value, like Chevron and Exxon Mobil, being added to growth ETFs, while some former growth companies moved to value funds. Advisors are urged to re-examine the holdings within these ETFs as their sector exposures and underlying securities have changed considerably, potentially impacting future performance relative to their previous classifications.

title: HR Brew
summary: This HR Brew update highlights strong Q3 and Q4 2022 earnings for payroll companies like Paychex, Paycom, and Paycor, driven by investments in AI and self-service technology. It also features an interview with Joy Fitzgerald, SVP and chief DE&I officer at UnitedHealth Group, about her forthcoming book on advocating for oneself in corporate America. The article concludes with a recap of top HR stories from Q4 2022, covering topics from Web3 talent marketplaces to the importance of soft skills and why investing in employees can help weather a recession.

title: Class-action alleges UnitedHealthcare underpaid out-of-network providers
summary: A new class-action lawsuit accuses UnitedHealthcare of underpaying out-of-network providers using a "self-serving scheme" that leaves plan members liable for unpaid charges and generates "savings fees" for UHC. This lawsuit, filed in December, is not the first of its kind, as UnitedHealth Group has faced similar legal challenges and investigations concerning its reimbursement practices for out-of-network services, including a $15.6 million settlement in 2021 following a Department of Labor investigation. The plaintiffs allege that UnitedHealthcare's actions violate plan terms and the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA), which mandates fiduciaries act solely in the interest of plan participants.

title: Top Home Health Trends For 2023
summary: This article outlines the top trends for the home health industry in 2023, focusing on persistent challenges and emerging opportunities. Key trends include the continued decline in the number of home health agencies due to staffing shortages and Medicare rate cuts, the adaptation required from agencies to a more difficult fee-for-service Medicare environment, and continued M&A activity despite higher interest rates. It also predicts a slowdown in SNF-to-home diversion, a rebound for publicly traded home health companies, and a greater emphasis on value-based care and investment in training and technology for higher-acuity patients.

title: Top Behavioral Health Trends for 2023
summary: The behavioral health industry is expected to undergo significant transitions in 2023, influenced by the end of the COVID-era public health emergency and economic shifts. Key trends include increased M&A activity, a focus on higher-acuity care, government scrutiny of digital health companies, and efforts to address the pediatric behavioral health crisis and workforce shortages. The article also highlights the continued growth of digital MAT providers and REITs' expanding investments in behavioral health facilities.

title: VillageMD Completes $8.9B Acquisition of Summit Health-CityMD
summary: VillageMD has finalized its $8.9 billion acquisition of Summit Health-CityMD, creating one of the largest independent provider groups in the United States. This merger combines VillageMD’s value-based care model with Summit Health-CityMD’s multidisciplinary approach, resulting in a medical group with over 680 provider locations in 26 markets. The acquisition involved investments from Walgreens Boots Alliance, Inc. and Evernorth, Cigna Corporation’s health services business.

title: CVS eyes next-generation health clinics after Amazon’s move for One Medical
summary: CVS Health Corp. is expanding its healthcare services by investing $100 million in Carbon Health Inc., a chain of urgent- and primary-care clinics. Additionally, CVS is reportedly in negotiations to acquire Oak Street Health Inc., a chain specializing in Medicare recipients, for over $10 billion. These moves signal CVS's strategy to evolve from a drugstore chain into a full-service healthcare company in response to trends like Amazon's acquisition of One Medical.

title: Top 10 global insurers – ratings agency announces rundown
summary: AM Best has released its latest rankings of the largest global insurers, with UnitedHealth Group retaining its top position for the eighth consecutive year based on net premiums written (NPW). Allianz SE leads the list for non-banking assets. The rankings highlight the strengthening positions of US-based health insurers and some reshuffling among the top global players.

title: JPM23, Day 2: Progyny projects 56% revenue growth in 2022 as employers eye fertility benefits; Cigna focusing on partnerships in primary care strategy
summary: This article summarizes key announcements from Day 2 of the J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference, highlighting Progyny's projected 56% revenue growth for 2022 due to increasing employer interest in fertility benefits. It also covers Cigna's primary care strategy, which prioritizes partnerships over broad acquisitions, and provides updates on Walgreens, Omada Health, and CVS Health's activities, including rumors of CVS potentially acquiring Oak Street Health.

title: Once again, UnitedHealth is the world’s largest insurer ranked by NPW
summary: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated maintained its position as the world's largest insurance company in 2021 based on net premiums written (NPW), driven by over 12% growth to USD 226.2 billion. Meanwhile, Allianz led the ranking by non-banking assets with USD 1.2 trillion. The report highlights the strong performance of U.S.-based health insurers in terms of NPW, while Japanese firms saw a decline in non-banking asset rankings due to currency depreciation.

title: Omada partners with Intermountain on diabetes management in Utah
summary: Omada Health is partnering with Intermountain Healthcare's value-based care unit, Castell, to offer virtual diabetes care and prevention to Intermountain's primary care patients in Utah. This collaboration marks Omada's first care delivery partnership with a major health system. The program aims to target and enroll thousands of eligible patients, leveraging Omada's virtual care platform, health coaches, and medical devices to manage diabetes and encourage lifestyle changes.

title: UnitedHealth Group's 2022 Earnings are in, PBM Optum outperforms health insurance division
summary: UnitedHealth Group's Optum division, which includes its pharmacy benefit manager (PBM), significantly outperformed its health insurance division in Q4 2022, contributing $4 billion to profits compared to the insurance's $2.9 billion. This trend is also evident in competitors like Cigna and CVS/Aetna, indicating a shift where these companies derive more revenue and profit from their roles as drug supply chain middlemen than from traditional health insurance. The article suggests that government programs like Medicare and Medicaid are increasingly keeping these companies' health plan operations afloat due to rising unaffordable premiums for employers and workers.

title: Enrollment gains boost UnitedHealth in fourth quarter
summary: UnitedHealth Group exceeded fourth-quarter forecasts for 2022 due to increased enrollment in Medicare Advantage and Medicaid, alongside strong performance from its Optum Health and Optum Rx segments. The company reported a 17% profit jump, reaching $4.76 billion, and saw its shares climb during mid-morning trading. UnitedHealth also reaffirmed its adjusted earnings forecast for the current year.

title: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) Earnings: 4Q22 Key Numbers
summary: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) reported strong fourth-quarter 2022 earnings, with revenues reaching $82.7 billion and net earnings of $4.7 billion, or $5.03 per share, surpassing analyst estimates. The company's adjusted EPS was $5.34. For fiscal year 2023, UnitedHealth Group projects revenues between $357 billion and $360 billion, with adjusted EPS expected to be in the range of $24.40 to $24.90.

title: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) Q4 2022 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) reported strong Q4 2022 results, with adjusted EPS growing 19% and full-year revenue increasing by 13% to $324 billion. The company highlighted significant growth across its Optum and UnitedHealthcare segments, particularly in value-based care, Medicare Advantage, and commercial offerings. Executives emphasized the importance of integrated services connecting care, benefits, and pharmacy solutions, and discussed future growth drivers including strategic M&A, biosimilar opportunities in OptumRx, and the impact of the Change Healthcare integration on OptumInsight.

title: From Apple To Amazon And Toyota, Here Are The Top 10 Biggest Companies In The World
summary: This article lists the top 10 biggest companies in the world based on revenue. Walmart, State Grid Corporation Of China, and Amazon lead the list, primarily highlighting a competition between US and Chinese firms. The article also includes companies from Japan and Germany, detailing their revenue, founding year, and number of employees.

title: How to Find Stocks Poised to Outperform
summary: The article explains that combining wide economic moats with low valuations has consistently led to market outperformance over the long term, even during bear markets. It highlights how Morningstar's Wide Moat Focus Index, consisting of undervalued companies with strong competitive advantages, has significantly outperformed broader market and wide moat composite indexes over decades. The success is attributed to the combination of high quality, stable prices, and attractive valuations, leading to long-term gains despite potential underperformance in bull markets.

title: Amedisys CEO Kusserow: Large Home Health Companies Unlikely to Stay Independent
summary: Amedisys CEO Paul Kusserow believes that few, if any, large home health companies will remain independent due to high interest from strategic buyers, like managed-care companies. This trend is driven by the scarcity of quality home health capacity and the desire to reduce care costs for chronic conditions. Despite the growing demand for home-based care, the industry is grappling with a significant labor shortage, which has impacted Amedisys's recent financial performance.

title: Employers Achieve Lower Costs and Improve Health Engagement With Integrated Benefits, Cigna Study Shows
summary: A Cigna study, verified by Aon, shows that employer clients with integrated medical, pharmacy, and behavioral benefits saved $148 per member per year in 2021. Further analysis revealed even greater savings, exceeding $1,400 per member annually for those engaged in health improvement programs, and substantial reductions in care costs for individuals with chronic conditions or those taking specialty drugs. These findings highlight the financial and health benefits of a holistic approach to care, leading to reduced emergency room visits and inpatient procedures.

title: UnitedHealth Group Announces Free Behavioral Health Coaching
summary: UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) has launched a new initiative providing free virtual behavioral health coaching to 5 million members on select commercial health insurance plans. The service, offered through Optum's partnership with AbleTo, targets mild depression, stress, and anxiety with an eight-week program involving one-on-one video or audio sessions with coaches. This move underlines UnitedHealth Group's broadened strategy to integrate behavioral health into its services amidst growing demand.

title: D-Wave Highlights Commercial Customer Engagements, Cross-Platform Product Enhancements
summary: D-Wave announced new commercial customer engagements and product updates for its annealing and gate model quantum computing solutions at its Qubits 2023 user conference. The company highlighted real-world applications with customers like Mastercard and Davidson Technologies, demonstrating the growing commercial adoption of quantum-hybrid solutions. D-Wave also shared significant progress on its next-generation Advantage2™ annealing system and advancements in its gate model platform, emphasizing its commitment to delivering diverse quantum solutions.

title: CVS Expands Mental Health Access with Launch of New Virtual Care Platform
summary: CVS Health Inc. has launched CVS Health Virtual Primary, expanding its mental health services through integrated virtual care teams. This platform, available to select Aetna commercial health plan members aged 18 and older, also allows users to access in-person care providers and in-network providers. The move reflects a growing consumer preference for digital health services, as highlighted by a CVS Health-backed survey, and follows a similar initiative by UnitedHealth Group.

title: Cigna sues CVS, former pharmacy head Bricker over exec’s departure
summary: Cigna is suing CVS and its former pharmacy benefits president, Amy Bricker, to prevent her from taking a new role as chief product officer of CVS's consumer segment. Cigna alleges Bricker's move violates her noncompete agreement and places Cigna's trade secrets at risk, given her previous high-level position at Express Scripts, a major competitor to CVS Caremark. The lawsuit highlights the intense competition between the two largest Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) for market share and contracts, especially after Cigna's Express Scripts won a significant contract from Centene that was previously managed by CVS.

title: Appeals Court Rules Against Plaintiffs in Wit v. United Behavioral Health
summary: The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected an appeal by plaintiffs in Wit v. United Behavioral Health, a decision behavioral health advocates view as a setback for parity in mental health care. The ruling overturns an earlier district court decision that found United Behavioral Health violated ERISA by improperly denying behavioral health claims. Industry leaders expressed distress, stating the decision weakens efforts to ensure insurance coverage for behavioral health is on par with physical health.

title: Focus: AbbVie's Humira gets a U.S. rival, but costs could stay high
summary: Amgen has launched Amjevita, the first biosimilar version of AbbVie's blockbuster drug Humira, offering two pricing tiers. Despite the introduction of competition and expectations of more biosimilars, experts anticipate that significant cost savings for U.S. patients may be limited due to the complex U.S. private insurance system, including pharmacy benefit managers and rebates. Analysts foresee a decrease in Humira's sales in the coming years due to this new competition.

title: STOCK TICKER: Blumenthal’s Wife Invests in Biotech Hedge Fund as He Chairs Panel Overseeing Drug Prices
summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal's wife has made a significant investment, up to $650,000, in Commodore Capital Domestic LP, a hedge fund exclusively focused on biopharmaceutical companies. This investment comes as Senator Blumenthal, chairman of a consumer protection subcommittee, has been actively addressing rising drug prices and the role of pharmaceutical benefit managers (PBMs). The pharmaceutical industry, including organizations supported by companies Commodore Capital invests in, has also been pushing for PBM reform, aligning with Blumenthal's legislative efforts.

title: Cigna restricts coverage of new ALS drug, deepening fears about access
summary: Cigna has restricted coverage for Amylyx Pharmaceuticals' new ALS drug, Relyvrio, classifying it as "experimental, investigational or unproven for any use" due to a "lack of clinical efficacy data." This decision deepens concerns among patients and healthcare providers about access to the expensive rare disease medication, priced at $158,000 per year, despite Amylyx stating that Cigna's policy is an outlier among other insurers. Cigna previously covered the drug under specific criteria and stated it will reevaluate its formulary status as more data from an ongoing larger trial becomes available.

title: 3 Top Buys From a Market-Beating ETF Powered by an AI Stock-Picker
summary: The AI-Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ) is outperforming the S&P 500 in 2023, leveraging IBM's Watson supercomputer to identify promising stocks. This article highlights three top holdings from AIEQ: Celsius Holdings (CELH), UnitedHealth Group (UNH), and Roku (ROKU), detailing their recent performance and growth prospects. It emphasizes how AI-driven stock selection can eliminate bias and contribute to strong investment returns.

title: Centene warns of hit to fast-growing Medicare Advantage business next year
summary: Centene Corp warned that its Medicare Advantage (MA) business will face a profit hit in 2024 due to a sharp cut in its federal rating and anticipated lower government payouts. This outlook overshadowed Centene's Q4 profit beat and follows proposed audit program rules and potential reimbursement rate drops from the U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). The company expects its MA business to likely shrink next year with temporary negative profit margins in 2024.

title: CVS Reaches $10.6 Billion Deal to Buy Clinic Owner Oak Street Health - WSJ
summary: CVS Health Corp. has agreed to acquire Oak Street Health Inc. for approximately $10.6 billion, including debt, in an all-cash deal for $39 a share. This acquisition is part of a broader trend of health insurers integrating with primary care providers and will expand CVS's healthcare offerings by adding Oak Street Health's network of 169 senior-focused clinics and 600 healthcare professionals. The deal is expected to close in 2023 and follows CVS's previous acquisition of Signify Health Inc.

title: CVS digs into primary care with $9.5 bln Oak Street Health deal
summary: CVS Health is acquiring Oak Street Health Inc for approximately $9.5 billion in cash to expand its primary care services, a strategic move following similar actions by rivals. Despite Oak Street Health currently losing money, analysts view the deal as strategically sound, aiming to integrate primary care centers with CVS's existing pharmacy and health insurance businesses. This acquisition, along with a pending deal for Signify Health, will position CVS to enhance its care offerings, especially for Medicare Advantage members, though it may face antitrust scrutiny.

title: CVS buys primary care provider Oak Street for $10.6 billion
summary: CVS Health is acquiring primary care provider Oak Street Health for approximately $10.6 billion, paying $39 per share in cash. This acquisition deepens CVS's presence in primary care, particularly in value-based care arrangements for Medicare Advantage patients, aligning with federal efforts to cut costs and improve health outcomes. The deal follows other major investments by CVS and rivals like UnitedHealth Group and Walgreens into primary care services.

title: Navigate 2023 With Recession-Resistant ETF ZECP
summary: The Zacks Earnings Consistent Portfolio ETF (ZECP) is presented as a recession-resistant strategy for investors concerned about a potential economic downturn in 2023. ZECP, Zacks Investment Management's first ETF, identifies companies with strong balance sheets and consistent earnings, having demonstrated resilience through past recessions. The fund seeks to offer an active approach to navigate market volatility, focusing on quality companies with stable historic and forecasted earnings per share.

title: Humana Inc. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Humana Inc. (HUM) stock rose 1.36% on Friday, outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also increase. The company's shares closed at $498.62, still below its 52-week high reached in November. Humana's performance was mixed compared to competitors like UnitedHealth Group Inc., Elevance Health Inc., and Chubb Ltd.

title: The Inadequacy of Revenue Cycle Diligence
summary: Private equity firms acquiring healthcare organizations often overlook revenue cycle due diligence, leading to financial issues post-acquisition. Comprehensive revenue cycle management (RCM) diligence, conducted either pre- or post-close, is crucial for identifying potential risks, ensuring successful integration, and accurately valuing targets. This diligence should cover operating models, staff organization, technology, reporting, and policies to prevent negative impacts like integration delays and revenue leakage.

title: Boston Scientific, MDMA call for more transparency and oversight of Medicare Advantage plans
summary: Boston Scientific and the Medical Device Manufacturers Association (MDMA) are urging federal regulators to increase transparency and oversight for Medicare Advantage plans. They argue that these plans often lack clear reasons for coverage denials and consistent coverage criteria, unlike traditional Medicare. Both organizations support CMS efforts to improve prior authorization rules and call for better enforcement and data analysis to ensure equitable access to care.

title: Cigna Rebrands Holding Company, Subsidiaries
summary: Cigna is rebranding its holding company to "The Cigna Group" to reflect its expanded portfolio, with Cigna Healthcare handling health benefits and Evernorth Health Services managing pharmacy and care solutions. This strategic move follows similar rebranding efforts by other major payers like Anthem (now Elevance Health) and Humana, aiming to better align their brands with evolving business structures and market presence. The company has also been expanding its reach in the Affordable Care Act marketplace and Medicare Advantage.

title: Quest Diagnostics Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Quest Diagnostics Inc. (DGX) stock rose 0.03% on Thursday, closing at $146.66, despite a general market downturn with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both falling. This marks the stock's second consecutive day of gains, bringing it to within $11.68 of its 52-week high. The company's performance also surpassed that of several competitors, whose stocks declined.

title: UnitedHealth Group closes $5.4B acquisition of LHC Group
summary: UnitedHealth Group has finalized its $5.4 billion acquisition of home health care provider LHC Group through its subsidiary Optum. This deal aims to integrate value-based care into patients' homes and follows other significant acquisitions by UnitedHealth Group, including Change Healthcare and EMIS Group. The collaboration is expected to enhance high-quality, comprehensive in-home care as demand for such services increases.

title: Ben & Jerry's, Magnum Ice Cream May Reformulate To Cut Energy Costs
summary: Unilever, the maker of Ben & Jerry's and Magnum ice cream, is exploring reformulating its products to be stored at higher temperatures. This initiative aims to cut energy consumption by 20-30% in retail freezers, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions and operational costs. The company plans to share its findings with competitors to encourage broader industry adoption of these energy-saving efforts.

title: Uncommon perks: How one healthcare company developed a menopausal leave policy for its employees
summary: Organon, a multinational pharmaceutical company focusing on women's health, has implemented a menopausal leave policy for its employees. The policy, driven by CHRO Aaron Falcione, aims to destigmatize menopause in the workplace and provide employees with a minimum of 10 days of self-care leave to manage symptoms. This initiative is part of Organon's broader effort to create a globally consistent care-leave framework and support gender parity.

title: Humana to Exit Employer Group Commercial Medical Products Business
summary: Humana Inc. announced its decision to exit the Employer Group Commercial Medical Products business over the next 18 to 24 months, including fully insured, self-funded, and Federal Employee Health Benefit medical plans. This strategic move allows Humana to focus on its core insurance lines, primarily government-funded programs like Medicare and Medicaid, and its CenterWell healthcare services. The exit is not expected to materially impact the company's full-year 2023 Adjusted earnings per share guidance, though it will affect the first-quarter earnings and Insurance segment benefit ratio for non-GAAP purposes.

title: Humana exits $4B commercial market, goes ‘all in’ on Medicare
summary: Humana is exiting the commercial employer insurance market, a segment worth $4 billion, to focus entirely on its Medicare business. This strategic shift indicates the company's commitment to strengthening its position in the government-funded healthcare sector. The decision highlights a trend among major insurers to streamline operations and prioritize core, profitable markets.

title: Referring patients to infusion centers reduces costs while maintaining quality of care
summary: Referring patients to infusion centers for specialty drug administration rather than hospitals can significantly reduce costs for patients and healthcare providers while maintaining high-quality care. Marcus Garcia of Rocky Mountain Cancer Centers highlights that infusion centers offer specialized staff, follow strict regulatory guidelines, and collaborate closely with referring physicians. These centers also offer improved access, flexible scheduling, and lower out-of-pocket expenses compared to hospital settings.

title: Headquarters of Optum subsidiary Solutran on the market in Plymouth
summary: The headquarters building of Solutran, an Optum subsidiary, located at 13305 12th Ave. N. in Plymouth, is currently for sale. This marks the fourth office property linked to UnitedHealth Group Inc. or its subsidiaries that has been listed. The sale comes amidst other news regarding UnitedHealth's real estate activities, including recent office building acquisitions and uncertainty surrounding Optum’s tech office campus in Eden Prairie.

title: Is Exiting the Employer Insurance Market a Smart Move for Humana?
summary: Humana announced its exit from the Employer Group Commercial Medical Products business over the next 18-24 months, including fully insured, self-funded, and Federal Employee Health Benefit plans. This strategic move aims to refocus resources on its Medicare Advantage business, where it holds the second-highest enrollment. Industry experts view this as a smart specialization given increasing market differentiation, though it will impact employers and employees with concerns about network continuity and benefit transitions.

title: Inside the Earnings Call: Xponential Fitness Confirms Boutique Fitness is a ‘Must-Have;’ Shares Climb
summary: Xponential Fitness reported strong financial results for Q4 and FY 2022, leading to a 14% climb in shares. The company highlighted significant growth in memberships, system-wide sales exceeding $1 billion, and a successful expansion strategy, affirming boutique fitness as a "must-have" for consumers. Xponential also detailed plans for continued global expansion, B2B partnerships including LG, and further development of its omnichannel fitness offerings with a new app and gamification platform.

title: The largest insurance companies in the US - based on market cap
summary: This article ranks the 10 largest publicly traded insurance companies in the US based on their market capitalization, providing details on their headquarters, market cap, and underwriting expertise. It highlights that US insurance companies constitute the largest portion of the world's market cap and explains why market cap is an important metric for investors.

title: New cancer center opens in Denver
summary: Presbyterian/St. Luke’s Medical Center in Denver has opened a new cancer center. The facility aims to bring cancer research and treatment under one roof on the campus. This development is part of broader activity in the Colorado healthcare landscape, with other institutions also expanding or planning new facilities.

title: Evolution of Primary Care Delivery
summary: The article discusses the evolving landscape of primary care delivery, driven by an aging population, the growth of Medicare Advantage and other value-based payment models, and digital transformation. It highlights the increasing role of insurers and retail providers in primary care, physician consolidation and shortages, and the innovations in care models focusing on improved patient outcomes and cost reduction. The author emphasizes that the future of primary care will be supported by technology and incentivized by value-based payments, requiring strategic adaptation from healthcare providers.

title: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock rises Tuesday, still underperforms market
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) stock increased by 0.19% on Tuesday, closing at $464.58. This rise occurred during a positive trading session for the broader market, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also seeing gains. Despite the daily increase, UNH still closed $93.52 short of its 52-week high and underperformed the market overall, though it outperformed some competitors like CVS Health Corp., Elevance Health Inc., and Cigna Group.

title: 7 Kinds of Telehealth Care You Can Get Through Alexa
summary: Amazon's Alexa has evolved beyond simple requests to offer a range of telehealth services, partnering with organizations like Teladoc and One Medical for virtual doctor visits and primary care. Users can manage prescriptions via Amazon Pharmacy, utilize Alexa Together for remote caregiving, and access medical information and reminders through Mayo Clinic First Aid and WebMD skills. The integration of telemedicine with voice assistants aims to make healthcare more accessible and convenient for minor illnesses and ongoing health management.

title: Video: 4 ways employers can support women’s health and well-being
summary: This article highlights four key ways employers can support women's health and well-being to retain talent and foster a healthier workforce. It emphasizes offering paid leave, supporting behavioral health, providing fertility benefits, and promoting career development. The article underscores that addressing these needs is crucial for both employees and employer success.

title: Hospital gets big check from bank
summary: Ameris Bank presented Liberty Regional Medical Center (LRMC) with a $400,000 check, part of the bank's larger $2 million donation to 15 rural hospitals in Georgia through the Georgia HEART Hospital Program. The funds will support LRMC's new wound care program, addressing a critical need identified in the community health assessment, particularly for diabetes patients. This donation highlights the importance of such programs in sustaining vital services, like oncology and delivery rooms, in rural hospitals, which often face funding challenges.

title: CVS Health Corp. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: CVS Health Corp. (CVS) stock decreased by 2.74% on Thursday, closing at $72.37, despite an overall positive trading day for the stock market. This marks the second consecutive day of losses for CVS, and its stock is now significantly below its 52-week high. The company's performance was mixed compared to competitors, with Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) rising, while UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) and Elevance Health Inc. (ELV) also experienced declines.

title: CVS to close on $8B Signify Health acquisition this week
summary: CVS is set to finalize its $8 billion acquisition of Signify Health this week. This acquisition is a strategic move for CVS to expand its primary care footprint, particularly by gaining a 50-state value-based provider network and a technology platform for home-based patient care. The deal aligns with CVS's broader strategy to enhance its presence in the healthcare sector.

title: 'It's Extremely Difficult': Payvider Models Demonstrate How Far Behavioral Health Integration Challenges Go
summary: Integrating behavioral health services into "payvider" models, where organizations own both payer and provider assets, presents significant challenges, as highlighted by leaders from Optum and CVS Health. Despite major acquisitions and a commitment to whole-person care, difficulties arise from reconciling disparate IT systems, establishing data sharing, and quantifying the value of behavioral health interventions. The article emphasizes that while these efforts are crucial for improving overall health, the process is labor-intensive and requires overcoming deep-seated legacy issues within the healthcare system.

title: Lawsuit slams PBMs Cigna, Humana as price-fixing ‘modern gangsters’
summary: Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost has filed a lawsuit against pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) including Express Scripts and Cigna, alleging they illegally inflated drug prices. The suit claims PBMs use a complex rebate system and a Switzerland-based company, Ascent Health Services, to drive up costs for life-saving drugs like insulin, rather than lowering them for consumers. Yost describes PBMs as "modern gangsters" who have destroyed transparency in drug pricing.

title: Major insurers to ease prior authorizations ahead of federal crackdown
summary: Major insurers Cigna and UnitedHealth Group are modifying their prior authorization processes. This move comes as federal pressure mounts to address issues surrounding these approvals. This development could streamline healthcare access for patients.

title: CVS Health Finalizes $8B Acquisition of Signify Health
summary: CVS Health has completed its $8 billion acquisition of home healthcare company Signify Health, accelerating its value-based care strategy. The merger aims to improve care delivery, lower costs, and enhance member engagement, particularly for Medicare Advantage beneficiaries. Signify Health's CEO, Kyle Armbrester, will continue to lead the company, which also includes Caravan Health.

title: 'You forget to eat': How Ozempic went from diabetes medicine to blockbuster diet drug
summary: Ozempic, originally a diabetes medication, has become a highly sought-after weight loss drug, leading to supply issues for diabetic patients. The drug's popularity, fueled by celebrity endorsements and social media, has driven up prices and spurred new businesses. Doctors express concern over its prescription for non-life-threatening weight loss and potential unknown long-term side effects.

title: iShares Global Healthcare ETF (IXJ) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of the iShares Global Healthcare ETF (IXJ), detailing its stock price, holdings, dividend yield, and key statistics. As of September 30, 2025, IXJ holds 114 stocks with a total portfolio value of $3.85 billion, featuring top holdings like Eli Lilly and Co, Johnson & Johnson, and AbbVie Inc. The ETF's current PE Ratio is 26.75 and its dividend yield is 1.43%.

title: Richardson Office Complex Sees $39M CMBS Loan Transferred To Special Servicing
summary: A $38.7M CMBS loan for the Granite 190 Center in Richardson, Texas, has been transferred to a special servicer due to a significant downsizing by its largest tenant, United Healthcare. This move, combined with expiring leases for five other major tenants and a drop in occupancy, puts the property at risk of default. Experts suggest that a resolution might involve a note of sale or foreclosure rather than a modification or extension, highlighting ongoing distress in office-backed CMBS loans.

title: Burnout Brings Hospice Nurses to an ‘Urgent Crossroad’
summary: A new analysis from the National Council of State Boards of Nursing indicates that nearly 900,000 registered nurses, including many younger and less experienced ones, are expected to leave the healthcare workforce by 2027 due to burnout and stress exacerbated by the pandemic. This impending exodus, particularly affecting hospice nurses who report increased workloads and emotional drain, highlights an urgent need for changes in recruitment and retention strategies, including flexible scheduling and improved educational pathways. Organizations like VITAS Healthcare are taking steps such as establishing scholarship grants to address the nursing shortage and promote diversity in the profession.

title: UnitedHealth CEO Andrew Witty pay rose 13% in 2022
summary: UnitedHealth Group's CEO, Andrew Witty, received a compensation of over $20 million in 2022, marking a 13% increase from the previous year. This article briefly highlights his pay rise and includes related news about UnitedHealth's performance and operational changes.

title: Humana Details CenterWell Home Health Growth, MA Success
summary: Humana (NYSE: HUM) discussed its strategy for continued success in Medicare Advantage (MA) and future growth in home health care following an unfavorable final rule for MA plans. The company anticipates strong MA growth and is expanding its CenterWell home health business, including recent acquisitions. Humana reported first-quarter revenues of $26.7 billion, a 12.3% increase year-over-year.

title: MDLIVE for Cigna cuts wait times by 50 percent by predicting changing healthcare demands with Azure Machine Learning
summary: MDLIVE for Cigna partnered with AIDAN Health to implement Azure Machine Learning for predicting patient demand, leading to a 50 percent reduction in patient wait times. This initiative helps balance medical professional workloads and optimize staffing, particularly critical after the surge in telehealth usage during the COVID-19 pandemic. The advanced forecasting models, developed on Azure, have also saved the company approximately $1 million each busy season in provider incentives.

title: One-third of US nurses plan to quit profession - report
summary: A survey indicates that nearly one-third of US nurses are considering leaving their profession due to overwhelming fatigue from the COVID-19 pandemic. This figure is up 7 percentage points from 2021, with 36% also considering changing workplaces, highlighting ongoing mental health and well-being challenges in the nursing workforce. Key demands from nurses include increased salaries and safer working environments to reduce stress.

title: CVS' Karen Lynch was the highest paid payer CEO last year. Here's what her competitors earned
summary: The article highlights that CVS CEO Karen Lynch was the highest-paid CEO among major national payers last year. It implies a comparison will be made with the earnings of her competitors in the payer industry. The content provided is minimal and serves mostly as an introduction to the topic.

title: Option Care Health to pick up home health and hospice firm Amedisys in $3.6B deal
summary: Option Care Health is set to acquire Amedisys, a home health and hospice firm, for $3.6 billion, creating a large post-acute care provider with projected annual revenues of $6.2 billion. This merger aims to expand capabilities and meet the increasing demand for in-home and alternative site care. The deal is expected to close in the second half of 2023 and will enable Option Care Health to move deeper into value-based care and offer a broader range of services to patients.

title: Alignment Health's CEO predicts that the insurtech will break even next year, turn a profit in 2025
summary: Alignment Health's CEO, John Kao, anticipates that the insurtech company will achieve a break-even point next year and become profitable by 2025. Despite a net loss in the first quarter, the company saw significant revenue and membership growth, outperforming competitors in a volatile market. Kao attributes this success to a highly personalized approach to care for members with chronic conditions, often involving direct engagement and in-home services to control healthcare spend.

title: Chile private health insurers owe US$1.4 billion
summary: Chile's government has confirmed that private health insurance companies (Isapres) must pay approximately US$1.4 billion in overcharges, following a 2022 Supreme Court ruling. This decision, impacting some 725,000 contracts, presents a significant challenge for the industry and President Gabriel Boric's administration, as the public health system is already strained. The Isapres argue the repayments will cripple the sector.

title: Humana partners with 2 durable medical equipment companies for home care
summary: Humana has partnered with AdaptHealth Corp. and Rotech Healthcare to provide value-based durable medical equipment (DME) services to its Medicare Advantage HMO members starting July 1. These agreements are part of Humana's broader strategy to expand value-based care into the home, aiming to serve 40% of its Medicare Advantage members by 2025 and streamline DME sourcing. The partnerships are expected to enhance access to home care services and help reduce unnecessary hospitalizations.

title: Record number of Americans are high on marijuana at work
summary: A new analysis by Quest Diagnostics reveals a record number of U.S. workers testing positive for cannabis, reaching the highest rate in 25 years. This increase is linked to the growing legalization of marijuana and is particularly prevalent in the food service and hospitality industries. The report also suggests a concerning correlation between rising marijuana use and workplace accidents, prompting questions about safety in an era of increasing cannabis acceptance.

title: Humana Avoids ‘Zero-Sum Game’ In Home Health Care Via Payvider Structure
summary: Humana is cementing its position as a home-based care powerhouse by expanding its CenterWell brand, which includes home health, primary care, and pharmacy services. Dr. Andrew Agwunobi, president of Humana's home solutions business, emphasizes the importance of integrating care delivery in the home to reduce costs and improve patient outcomes. Humana leverages its "payvider" structure (being both a payer and a provider) to align incentives and innovate in value-based care, with a focus on growth, integration, and meeting customer needs, particularly in the growing Medicare Advantage market.

title: Five (or Maybe Six?) Reasons that the Largest PBMs Operate Group Purchasing Organizations
summary: This article explores the reasons behind the largest Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) establishing Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs). It discusses five plausible explanations, including aggregating purchasing volume, creating new revenue streams, and exploiting tax efficiencies. The author also highlights a sixth alleged reason related to sharing pricing information, which is currently under litigation.

title: Omada Health Launches GLP-1-Specific Program for Patients Battling Chronic Obesity
summary: Omada Health has introduced a specialized program for individuals using GLP-1 medications for weight management, recognizing the increasing demand and addressing concerns about long-term efficacy and cost. The program incorporates behavior and lifestyle changes alongside medication through specialized training for coaches, free educational resources, community support, and services to assist employers and PBMs with reimbursement policies. This initiative aims to align with FDA guidelines emphasizing GLP-1 use as an adjunct to diet and exercise to ensure sustained weight loss and avoid reliance solely on medication.

title: Omada Launches Program To Support Patients on GLP-1s
summary: Omada Health has launched a new program offering lifestyle and behavior support for patients with chronic obesity who are taking GLP-1 medications. While Omada will not prescribe the drugs, its program provides coaching, peer support, and educational materials on proper drug use, side effects, and preventing weight regain. This initiative aims to ensure lasting behavior change alongside medication to address the high costs and potential for weight regain associated with GLP-1s.

title: With Option Care Deal Pending, Optum Makes Bid for Amedisys
summary: Optum, a subsidiary of UnitedHealth Group, has made an unsolicited all-cash bid of $100 per share to acquire home health and hospice provider Amedisys. This proposal comes while Amedisys has a pending $3.6 billion merger agreement with Option Care Health, which Amedisys's board is now assessing as a potentially "superior proposal." If Amedisys accepts Optum's offer and terminates the current merger, it may owe Option Care Health a $106 million fee.

title: UnitedHealth offers $3.2B to lure Amedisys away from Option Care merger
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. has made an unsolicited bid of $3.2 billion for Amedisys Inc., a home health care provider. This offer comes after Amedisys had previously agreed to a merger with a different company, Option Care. The bid by UnitedHealth aims to attract Amedisys away from its prior merger agreement.

title: Fortune 500's top 10 healthcare companies
summary: In 2022, despite economic uncertainty, healthcare companies remained prominent on Fortune 500's list of top revenue-generating corporations. The 69th annual list, released on June 5, shows UnitedHealth Group leading the healthcare sector with $324.16 billion in revenue, followed by other major players like CVS Health, McKesson, and AmerisourceBergen. A total of 80 healthcare companies made the Fortune 500 list, highlighting the sector's significant economic impact.

title: Is Cigna Stock A Better Pick Over UNH?
summary: This article analyzes whether Cigna (CI) is a better investment than UnitedHealth (UNH). While UnitedHealth has shown better historical revenue growth and profitability, Cigna is currently trading at a lower valuation and is projected to have stronger top-line growth in the coming years. Based on Trefis Machine Learning analysis, Cigna is predicted to offer a significantly higher return over the next three years compared to UnitedHealth.

title: Minnesota has 15 companies on the Fortune 500 list, one fewer than last year
summary: Minnesota now has 15 companies on the Fortune 500 list, a decrease of one from the previous year, primarily due to Securian dropping out of the Top 500. UnitedHealth Group remains Minnesota's highest-ranking company at 5th nationally, while Target and other major corporations also feature on the list. The article also details other Minnesota-based companies just outside the Fortune 500, noting that private companies like Cargill are not included.

title: 2 Alabama companies among Fortune 500
summary: Regions Financial and Vulcan Materials, both Birmingham-based companies, have been included in the annual Fortune 500 ranking. Regions secured the 483rd spot with $7.5 billion in revenue, while Vulcan Materials ranked 494th with $7.3 billion. The article also touches on overall trends in the Fortune 500 list, such as an increase in women CEOs.

title: 3 exercise options for older adults trying to stay in shape
summary: Staying physically active is crucial for older adults, even though it can become more challenging with age. Regular exercise can improve mobility and balance, and reduce the risk of various health conditions. This article highlights three beneficial exercise options for older adults: walking, swimming, and group classes, each offering unique advantages like cardiovascular health, joint benefits, and social interaction.

title: T. Rowe Price’s New ETF, TCAF, Is Worthy of Appreciation
summary: T. Rowe Price has launched a new active ETF, TCAF, managed by veteran David Giroux, which focuses solely on equities and aims for broader diversification than his existing mutual fund, PRWCX. TCAF offers a more tax-efficient and accessible alternative to the capacity-constrained PRWCX, catering to advisors who favor active management. The ETF is designed to identify high-quality companies with strong risk-adjusted return potential and attractive valuations.

title: 26 MN Companies Make Fortune 500 List For 2023
summary: Twenty-six Minnesota-based companies have been named to the 2023 Fortune 500 list, which ranks the biggest American companies by revenue. This year's list sets a new record with 52 female CEOs, including four from Minnesota companies: Best Buy, Land O'Lakes, Thrivent Financial for Lutherans, and H.B. Fuller. UnitedHealth Group is the highest-ranked Minnesota company at #5, and globally, Walmart retains its top position for the eleventh consecutive year.

title: ProShares Ultra Dow30 Review and Aggregate Rating (DDM)
summary: This article provides an aggregate rating and price target for the ProShares Ultra Dow30 ETF (DDM). MarketBeat calculates these by weighing analyst ratings and price targets of the ETF's constituent stocks. DDM currently holds a "Moderate Buy" aggregate rating with an aggregate price target of $58.54, based on recent analyst coverage of its top holdings.

title: What If You Can’t Afford Long-Term Care?
summary: Many older Americans cannot afford long-term care, and traditional Medicare does not cover these expenses. This article explores several options for those who cannot afford long-term care, including reverse mortgages, long-term care insurance (including hybrid policies), facilities with benevolent funds, and life settlements. These alternatives offer different ways to finance necessary care for individuals who fall into the "monetary middle" and do not qualify for substantial government assistance.

title: Opinion | Why Do We Tolerate Our Health Insurance Problem?
summary: This article criticizes the U.S. health insurance industry, arguing that it prioritizes profit over patient well-being, leading to inefficiencies, high costs, and compromised care. It highlights issues such as exorbitant profits of major insurers, questionable practices like prior authorizations and payment denials, and the detrimental effects of vertical integration and the medical loss ratio loophole. The author calls for policymakers, physicians, and regulatory bodies to push for reforms that prioritize patients, promote competition, and ensure accountability.

title: 3 Health Insurance Stocks Getting Killed by Rising Costs
summary: This article highlights three health insurance-related stocks – iShares U.S. Healthcare Providers ETF (IHF), Centene (CNC), and Manulife Financial Corp (MFC) – that are struggling due to rapidly rising medical costs. It details how increasing healthcare expenses and other market challenges are negatively impacting their profitability and growth prospects, making them potentially risky investments.

title: Is UnitedHealth Stock a Buy, Sell, or Fairly Valued After Earnings?
summary: UnitedHealth Group's stock is considered fairly valued by Morningstar with a 3-star rating, despite surging demand for healthcare services potentially straining near-term margins. While the company's 2023 guidance remains unchanged, Morningstar has raised its fair value estimate to $462 per share. Other managed care stocks, however, are seen as significantly undervalued following UnitedHealth's update.

title: United States et al. v. UnitedHealth Group Incorporated et al.
summary: Professors Gautam Gowrisankaran and Ben Handel testified at trial regarding the proposed $13.8 billion merger between UnitedHealth Group’s Optum unit and Change Healthcare. The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) retained Cornerstone Research to support the experts, alleging the merger would give UnitedHealth Group access to competitors' sensitive information and control innovations. The professors analyzed the potential for anticompetitive harm, both horizontally and vertically, particularly concerning data access and control over claims clearinghouse innovations.

title: New Humira rivals likely to hit US market with small discounts in July
summary: Multiple biosimilar versions of AbbVie's top-selling drug Humira are expected to launch in the U.S. in July, adding to the competition started by Amgen in January. Despite increased generic competition, industry experts anticipate only small price discounts for these new versions due to pharmacy benefit managers' negotiation strategies. This pricing dynamic means that while health plans might secure some savings, patients paying co-insurance based on list prices may not see significant relief.

title: Value-Based Care: Operational Context Matters
summary: The article discusses the growing importance and implementation of value-based care (VBC) in the healthcare industry, primarily driven by Medicare's efforts to shift from volume to value. It highlights the FTI Consulting Value-based Care Operating Model, which comprises Clinical & Service Integration, Operations, and Financial Performance, emphasizing the need for organizational maturity to optimize VBC performance. The piece underlines that VBC is a permanent fixture in healthcare, requiring adaptable operational structures to succeed with varied patient populations.

title: Markets Brief: There’s Good News for Investors in Rates Staying Higher for Longer
summary: Despite the Federal Reserve's anticipated interest rate hikes, rising bond yields are creating attractive opportunities for investors, particularly in fixed-income assets. The strong June jobs report reinforces the likelihood of continued rate increases, but strategists believe this "higher-for-longer" environment allows investors to lock in significant yields, with even real returns exceeding inflation expectations. This shift signals a favorable period for revisiting fixed-income portfolios before the Fed concludes its hiking cycle.

title: Janus Henderson’s Singapore CEO Surveys How Global Life Sciences Offer Potential Amidst Uncertainty
summary: Andrew Hendry, Singapore CEO of Janus Henderson Investors, presented on the enduring investment merits of healthcare and biotech, highlighting their resilience and upside potential amid global uncertainty. He noted that demographic trends, particularly the aging population in the US, continue to drive healthcare demand. Hendry also pointed out that major pharmaceutical companies are acquiring smaller firms due to expiring patents and high R&D costs, creating significant M&A opportunities and growth in the life sciences sector.

title: Federal judge advances class action lawsuit against DaVita for alleged wage violations
summary: A federal judge has allowed a class action lawsuit against DaVita, Inc. to proceed, alleging the company failed to compensate nurses and technicians for interrupted meal breaks as required by law. While the judge narrowed the class to employees in nine specific states, she found sufficient evidence to suggest that DaVita nurses and technicians were deprived of paid meal breaks. DaVita denies a company-wide policy of violating labor laws, claiming interruptions are rare and compensated.

title: Home-Based Care M&A Rebounds Significantly In Q2, Highlighted By Addus’ $106M Tennessee Quality Care Deal
summary: Home-based care mergers and acquisitions significantly rebounded in Q2 2023 with 29 transactions across home health, home care, and hospice sectors, surpassing Q1 2023 and Q2 2022 volumes. Notable deals include Addus HomeCare's $106 million acquisition of Tennessee Quality Care and Humana's CenterWell Home Health acquiring Trilogy Home Health. The activity signals a strong rebound, with demand for cashflow-positive companies driven by private equity interest and a potential active second half of 2023 despite proposed payment rule uncertainties for home health.

title: HCA's raised forecast fails to impress amid spike in surgeries
summary: HCA Healthcare Inc. raised its annual profit forecast after beating quarterly earnings estimates, but its shares fell due to investor expectations for a stronger outlook reflecting a rebound in non-urgent medical procedures. Major insurers like UnitedHealth Group and Humana have already reported higher costs due to a surge in such surgeries. HCA, the largest for-profit hospital operator in the U.S., now expects adjusted core earnings between $12.3 billion and $12.8 billion, up from $12.1 billion and $12.7 billion previously.

title: AbbVie trims forecast for Humira sales drop on favorable coverage
summary: AbbVie has revised its 2023 forecast for Humira sales, now expecting a 35% decline instead of 37%, due to favorable insurance coverage for the drug despite new biosimilar competition. The company raised its annual profit forecast and announced that its newer immunology drugs, Skyrizi and Rinvoq, are performing strongly, helping to offset Humira's anticipated sales decline. This positive outlook led to a significant surge in AbbVie's shares.

title: P&G Beats Profit and Sales Estimates on Higher Prices
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) surpassed profit and sales estimates for its fiscal 2023 fourth quarter, driven by higher prices for its products, even while facing increased costs. Shares rose over 3% following the announcement. However, the company's outlook for fiscal 2024 fell below forecasts due to anticipated macroeconomic challenges.

title: Teva CEO says not too late to launch Humira biosimilar in 2024
summary: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries plans to launch its biosimilar version of AbbVie's Humira in 2024, despite a competitive market that saw eight companies launch similar products in 2023. CEO Richard Francis believes the market still offers opportunities, emphasizing Teva's autoinjector as a competitive advantage and the high quality of their biosimilar. He also noted that while the Humira biosimilar might not achieve initial forecasts, Teva's broader biosimilar pipeline, including a Stelara biosimilar in 2025, remains strong.

title: CVS Health begins cost saving plan ahead of uncertain 2024
summary: CVS Health has initiated a cost-saving plan, including job cuts and the closure of its clinical trials services, in anticipation of a challenging 2024 for its health insurance business. The company also lowered its 2024 profit forecast and withdrew its 2025 earnings forecast, citing high integration costs from recent acquisitions and increasing medical costs. Despite these adjustments, CVS shares saw a modest increase.

title: Labor Department files suit alleging Wausau-based UMR Inc. wrongly denied medical claims
summary: The U.S. Department of Labor has filed a lawsuit against UMR Inc., a subsidiary of UnitedHealth Group Inc., alleging that the Wisconsin-based company routinely denied healthcare claims. The lawsuit, filed in federal court, claims UMR Inc. wrongly denied emergency room services and urinary drug screenings since 2015.

title: GSK will close its factory in Nigeria and move to third party direct distribution
summary: GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) Consumer Nigeria is shutting down its manufacturing operations and moving to a third-party distribution model, impacting 290 employees. While Nigerian media link this to foreign exchange shortages, the article suggests GSK's decision is more influenced by its corporate demerger with Haleon and a strategic review of African operations, exemplified by similar moves in Kenya. This transition follows a trend of multinational companies restructuring their presence in Nigeria due to economic challenges and strategic shifts.

title: Enhabit Announces Intent to Launch Strategic Alternatives Process
summary: Enhabit Inc. announced its intent to launch a strategic review process to explore various options for the company's future, including a potential sale or merger. This decision is driven by the need to satisfy conditions of its Tax Matters Agreement with Encompass Health Corp. and comes amidst significant M&A activity within the home health industry. The company's Q2 results showed a net loss and a decline in home health revenue, leading some analysts to express disappointment despite progress in MA contracts.

title: DOJ taking a closer look at UnitedHealth's $3.3B bid for Amedisys
summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) is requesting more information from Amedisys regarding its proposed $3.3 billion acquisition by UnitedHealth Group. This "second request" for information extends the waiting period for the deal to close, allowing regulators to further scrutinize potential antitrust concerns. While previous large healthcare deals have faced similar delays and ultimately closed, the DOJ and FTC have indicated increased oversight of mergers in the healthcare sector.

title: Progressive had a great quarter, but it's not Jim Cramer's top insurance stock
summary: Progressive reported strong quarterly results, leading to an 8.43% rise in its shares. Despite this, CNBC's Jim Cramer prefers Chubb as his top insurance pick, citing its benefits from higher interest rates, which aligns with recent Federal Reserve hikes and contributed to Chubb's earnings beat.

title: GSK Announces AREXVY, Its Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Vaccine, Is Now Available at All Major US Retail Pharmacies
summary: GSK announced that its Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) vaccine, AREXVY, is now available at all major US retail pharmacies. This makes the vaccine widely accessible to adults aged 60 and older ahead of the fall and winter RSV season, with most Medicare and commercial insurance plans expected to cover it. The vaccine is indicated for the prevention of RSV-lower respiratory tract disease in older adults and was approved by the FDA on May 3rd, 2023, as the world's first RSV vaccine for this demographic.

title: Tammi Morton takes on Chief Security Officer role at UnitedHealth Group
summary: Tammi Morton has been appointed as the new Chief Security Officer at UnitedHealth Group, bringing nearly 30 years of security experience to the role. She will lead the Enterprise Workplace Security Program, focusing on protecting the company's global workforce and physical assets. Morton's extensive background includes leadership positions at Raytheon Technologies, United Technologies Corporation, Hewlett Packard Inc., and Merck.

title: Is CVS Stock a Buy After Blue Shield of California Dropped the Company?
summary: CVS Health was recently dropped by Blue Shield of California as a pharmacy benefit manager in favor of new entrants like Amazon Pharmacy, leading Morningstar to maintain a "buy" rating on CVS stock despite reducing its fair value estimate to $103 per share from $113. While this client loss highlights potential industry disruption and policy risks, Morningstar believes CVS remains significantly undervalued and possesses a narrow economic moat due to its scale and diverse operations in medical insurance, PBM, and pharmacy retail. The company is expected to face growth hurdles in its PBM and Medicare Advantage businesses, but new healthcare service acquisitions offer higher-margin opportunities.

title: 4 New Insights On The Amedisys, Optum, Option Care Health Saga
summary: This article provides four new insights into the acquisition saga involving Amedisys, Optum, and Option Care Health, drawing from an SEC filing. It reveals that UnitedHealth Group's interest in Amedisys dates back to 2020, Option Care Health faced multiple competitors, and other payers were involved in potential bids. A significant factor influencing Amedisys' decision to consider acquisition was the unexpected negative changes in Medicare reimbursement rates by CMS.

title: UnitedHealthcare announces data breach involving South Carolina residents
summary: UnitedHealthcare announced a data breach affecting some South Carolina residents, where an unauthorized third party accessed a broker portal between December 2022 and January 2023. The breach involved personal health information such as names, member IDs, plan types, and residency details, but did not expose Social Security numbers, driver's licenses, or financial accounts. UHC has notified law enforcement, implemented additional safeguards, and will inform affected individuals directly.

title: UnitedHealthcare data breach: Officials warning Texas residents about incident
summary: UnitedHealthcare (UHC) has reported a data security incident affecting certain Texas residents, involving personal health information such as names, member IDs, plan types, and residency details. The breach, which occurred between December 1, 2022, and January 25, 2023, involved an unauthorized third party accessing a UHC broker portal. UHC states that social security numbers, driver's license numbers, or financial account information were not compromised, and affected individuals are being notified, with a dedicated hotline available for questions.

title: Humana sues HHS over Medicare Advantage audits
summary: Humana has filed a lawsuit against the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) challenging the federal regulators' new rule for auditing Medicare Advantage (MA) payments. The company, a major MA plan provider, argues that the rule is "arbitrary and capricious," particularly disagreeing with the elimination of a "fee-for-service adjuster" used to ensure payment parity. This legal action comes as concerns rise over potential MA overpayments, with some watchdogs estimating billions in excess payments.

title: How Contessa’s Palliative Care Business Factored Into the Amedisys-Optum Transaction
summary: The acquisition of Amedisys by Optum was significantly influenced by negotiations surrounding Amedisys' Contessa subsidiary, particularly its palliative care business. Accounting changes related to Contessa's risk-based palliative care contracts initially complicated Amedisys' merger talks with Option Care Health, leading to revised ownership terms. Ultimately, Optum's superior, all-cash offer led Amedisys to terminate the Option Care deal and accept Optum's proposition, reflecting UnitedHealth Group's strategic interest in home-based care and palliative services.

title: Polyclinic, Everett Clinic parent company lays off WA employees
summary: Optum Washington, the parent company of The Polyclinic and Everett Clinic, has laid off an undisclosed number of employees in Washington. This decision follows similar job cuts at several Seattle-area hospitals over the past year, as the healthcare industry grapples with stagnant revenues and increasing operational costs. The layoffs reflect a broader trend of financial challenges affecting the region's healthcare providers.

title: Are super-personalized solutions the future of healthcare?
summary: Johnson & Johnson is pioneering precision medicine, aiming to develop individualized treatments based on a patient’s genetic profile to move beyond the traditional one-size-fits-all approach. The company is actively working on targeted therapies for various diseases, partnering with diagnostic companies, and focusing on educating patients and physicians to overcome barriers to access. This approach promises more effective treatments and better outcomes by ensuring patients receive the right test and the right therapy at the right time.

title: Home-Based Care Provider BrightSpring Health Services Again Eyeing IPO
summary: BrightSpring Health Services, backed by KKR, is once again planning an IPO, aiming to raise $1 billion after shelving an $800 million IPO bid in late 2022. The company, which provides home- and community-based services to 350,000 patients daily, expects the listing to occur in the fourth quarter. This move comes despite challenges in the public market for home health and hospice providers, with BrightSpring's diversified services potentially offering some insulation.

title: Paine Schwartz' $1.7bn agrifood fund: The Week in AgriFoodTech
summary: Paine Schwartz closed its latest $1.7 billion food and agribusiness-focused fund, with 40% already deployed to sustainable investments. This week in AgriFoodTech also saw Tikehau Capital investing in a biologicals startup, Infarm declared bankrupt, and ongoing layoffs in the sector. The article summarizes significant funding rounds, M&A activities, and other news across foodtech and agtech.

title: An Inside Look Into UnitedHealthcare Group’s Commitment to Diversity Equity And Inclusion
summary: UnitedHealth Group (UHG) is actively working to foster a diverse, equitable, and inclusive environment through strategic programs. The company's efforts include recruitment initiatives, building cultural competencies, and focusing on representation across demographics, with women holding 40% of top leadership roles. Additionally, UHG is investing $100 million philanthropically to advance a more diverse healthcare workforce and address health equity across six key areas by 2033.

title: Alignment Health, Instacart roll out co-branded Medicare Advantage plans
summary: Alignment Health and Instacart are launching co-branded Medicare Advantage (MA) plans in 2024 across 13 California and Nevada counties. These plans will offer enhanced food benefits, including quarterly allowances for groceries and complimentary Instacart+ memberships, aiming to address food insecurity and transportation barriers for chronically ill dual-eligible seniors. This partnership highlights the competitive nature of the MA market, with Alignment Health focusing on comprehensive benefits and strong market penetration.

title: Cigna will pay $172 million for allegedly overcharging Medicare Advantage
summary: Cigna has agreed to pay $172 million to settle allegations that it overcharged Medicare Advantage by submitting false diagnostic codes. The lawsuit, brought under the False Claims Act, claims Cigna used vendor-conducted in-home assessments to generate inaccurate codes that led to increased payments. This settlement follows another recent lawsuit against Cigna regarding its alleged use of algorithms to improperly deny claims.

title: Humana CEO stepping down after more than 10 years; successor named
summary: Humana Inc. CEO Bruce Broussard will step down in 2024 after more than 10 years at the helm. Kentucky-native Jim Rechtin, President and CEO of Envision Healthcare, will take over as Humana's chief operating officer in the latter half of 2024. Broussard will remain with the company as a strategic advisor into 2025.

title: Higher Prices Drive Procter & Gamble's Better-Than-Expected Earnings
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported stronger-than-expected Q1 FY 2024 earnings, with sales up 6% and profit up 17% year-over-year, primarily driven by higher product prices. While some segments saw declining sales volume due to these price increases, the overall financial performance remained robust. The company's successful management of prices and margins has been crucial in navigating inflation, leading to a significant increase in gross margin for the quarter.

title: Barclays appoints Jed Brody as Head of Americas Healthcare Banking
summary: Barclays has appointed Jed Brody as a Managing Director and Head of Americas Healthcare Banking, based in New York. Brody rejoins Barclays from Leerink Partners and has over 20 years of experience in the industry, including significant transaction work. This appointment is part of Barclays' continued investment in its Healthcare coverage, following other recent key hires in the sector.

title: A heart for people: The common thread in medical assistants
summary: HCA Healthcare recognizes its 4,000+ medical assistants annually during the third week of October for their vital role in patient care. This article highlights five HCA Healthcare medical assistants – Tracy Shortt, Hunter Lawson, Ella Floyd, Casey May, and Bonnie Greene – showcasing their dedication and compassion. Each individual shares their motivation for working in healthcare, emphasizing a common commitment to helping others and making a positive impact on patients' lives.

title: 6 Top Geriatric Psychiatry Services in San Diego
summary: This article highlights six top geriatric psychiatry services in San Diego, emphasizing the specialized care available for older adults facing mental health challenges such as depression, anxiety, and dementia. Each listed provider offers unique expertise, compassionate approaches, and comprehensive treatment plans tailored to the needs of seniors, aiming to enhance their quality of life. The piece also includes a FAQ section defining geriatric psychiatry and addressing common concerns about mental health in older adults.

title: Centene Expects ‘Really Nice Tailwinds’ For Medicaid Behavioral Health Division
summary: Centene Corp. anticipates significant growth in its Medicaid behavioral health division due to state governors prioritizing behavioral health. The company, which acquired Magellan Health in 2022, sees opportunities to expand its services and integrate physical and mental health care. While behavioral health costs are not currently a major driver of overall medical expenses, Centene continues to monitor utilization, especially for substance use and opioid use disorder.

title: Option Care Health resets M&A strategy after failed Amedisys bid
summary: Option Care Health is re-evaluating its merger and acquisition strategy following the unsuccessful bid for Amedisys. The company's President and CEO, John Rademacher, is leading this pivot. This strategic shift comes after the Amedisys deal did not materialize.

title: How Quality, Utilization Will Shape Hospice M&A in 2024
summary: The hospice industry's M&A landscape in 2024 will be significantly influenced by quality and utilization metrics, as a more diverse group of buyers, including private equity and health systems, engage in transactions. Payers, specifically, are showing increased interest due to hospice's value proposition in cost savings and quality outcomes. Providers like Stillwater Hospice and VITAS Healthcare emphasize the importance of demonstrating quality data and forming strategic partnerships to maintain competitiveness amidst ongoing consolidation and financial pressures.

title: Lawsuit Over UnitedHealth Group’s AI Strategy Corroborates Home Health Providers’ Convener Claims
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against UnitedHealth Group (UNH) over its naviHealth subsidiary's alleged use of AI algorithms to deny care for Medicare Advantage beneficiaries. This lawsuit echoes long-standing complaints from home health providers regarding conveners' role in dictating care and potentially suppressing utilization. While Optum refutes the allegations, the case highlights growing concerns about AI's influence in healthcare and the practices of post-acute care conveners.

title: Legendary value investor's firm launches new fund targeting ‘quality' stocks
