summary: Legendary value investor Jeremy Grantham's firm, GMO, has launched its first active ETF, the GMO U.S. Quality ETF, focusing on "quality" stocks. Managed by Tom Hancock, the fund targets companies that can sustainably deploy capital at high rates of return, primarily in technology, healthcare, and consumer staples, offering potential tax advantages and ease of trading for clients. The ETF aims to identify "battleship companies" with strong balance sheets and competitive moats.

title: At Hologic, women come first. And that help extends to employees in many stages of familyhood.
summary: Hologic, a medical devices company focused on women's health, offers extensive benefits to support female employees through various stages of familyhood. These benefits include fertility services through Progyny, $10,000 child adoption reimbursements, free nurse lactation consultations, and breastmilk storage and delivery services via Milk Stork. The company aims to attract and retain female talent by providing comprehensive support, ultimately enabling new mothers to return to the workforce sooner.

title: Cash-strapped Crozer Health turns to Temple and Jefferson for help maintaining services
summary: Crozer Health, facing severe financial difficulties under Prospect Medical Holdings, is seeking partnerships with Temple and Jefferson Health to maintain vital services and avoid further closures. The health system's troubles, including vendor payment issues and a state citation for closing a transplant program, mirror problems at other Prospect hospitals in Connecticut and Rhode Island. Amidst litigation and an ongoing agreement to sell, Crozer's future remains uncertain.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s ‘Flawed’ AI Model Wrongfully Denies Elderly Patients Post-Acute Care Coverage, Class Action Alleges
summary: A class-action lawsuit has been filed against UnitedHealth Group, UnitedHealthcare, and naviHealth, alleging that they use a "flawed" AI model called "nH Predict" to wrongfully deny post-acute care coverage to elderly patients with Medicare Advantage Plans. The lawsuit claims that this AI algorithm leads to premature denial of necessary medical care, forcing patients to leave facilities or pay out-of-pocket, contradicting Medicare Advantage plan coverage rules. The plaintiffs assert that the companies discipline employees who deviate from the AI's recommendations, prioritizing cost savings over personalized patient care, and that the high reversal rate of denied claims via appeals proves the model's inaccuracy.

title: UnitedHealth forecasts 2024 revenues that top expectations
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. released its 2024 outlook, forecasting revenues of $400 billion to $403 billion, exceeding the FactSet consensus of $394 billion. The company expects adjusted earnings per share between $27.50 and $28.00, aligning with analyst estimates. UnitedHealth also reaffirmed its long-term EPS growth target of 13% to 16%.

title: Why Fidelity Low-Priced Stock Still Gets a High Rating
summary: Fidelity Low-Priced Stock (FLPSX) maintains its "Silver" Morningstar Medalist Rating due to the strength of its new co-lead managers, Morgen Peck and Sam Chamovitz, and its disciplined investment approach. The fund is completing a management transition from legendary manager Joel Tillinghast and continues to show strong performance, boasting diversified holdings with above-market profitability and below-average debt, along with significant international exposure. Peck and Chamovitz have made recent portfolio adjustments, including paring large-cap stocks and increasing small- and mid-cap holdings, while upholding the fund's unique risk/return profile.

title: Eli Lilly obesity drug now available in US pharmacies
summary: Eli Lilly's newly approved obesity treatment, Zepbound, is now available in U.S. pharmacies, with a potential cost of $550 per month for those without insurance coverage, which is half its list price. The drug enters a rapidly growing market, with Wall Street analysts projecting Zepbound sales to reach approximately $2 billion in 2024. Zepbound has already been added to the preferred medicines list by at least one major pharmacy benefit manager, Cigna's Express Scripts.

title: Applied Research Works, Inc. Announces Cozeva's Achievement in NCQA's Data Aggregator Validation Program
summary: Applied Research Works, Inc. (ARW) announced that its product, Cozeva, has successfully passed NCQA's Data Aggregator Validation (DAV) program, including the addition of Cozeva User Interface Entered + Enhanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and FHIR output. This achievement is expected to significantly improve HEDIS reporting for healthcare providers and payers by extending data collection timelines and reducing chart chase burden, ultimately enhancing data quality and provider participation. The DAV certification from NCQA allows ARW customers to bypass costly Primary Source Verification and efficiently gather clinical information, transforming healthcare data management.

title: Cigna abandons pursuit of Humana, plans $10 billion share buyback, sources say
summary: Cigna has reportedly ended its attempt to acquire Humana after the two companies failed to agree on a price. Following this decision, Cigna announced plans for an additional $10 billion in share repurchases, bringing the total to $11.3 billion, citing significant undervaluation of its shares. Cigna is also exploring the sale of its Medicare Advantage business, a move that could potentially aid future consolidation efforts and address antitrust concerns.

title: Cigna’s ‘Bolt-On’ Deals Could Target Smaller Health Insurers Or Providers
summary: Cigna's CEO David Cordani announced that the company will pursue "bolt-on acquisitions" after reportedly abandoning a larger deal with Humana. These acquisitions could focus on smaller health insurers to bolster Cigna's presence in areas like Medicare Advantage or expand its commercial and employer coverage. Additionally, Cigna's Evernorth health services business might target doctor practices or other healthcare providers, following a trend seen with rivals like CVS Health and UnitedHealth Group.

title: Survey: Majority of Healthcare Executives Foresee Better Organizational Health in 2024
summary: A new survey by AMN Healthcare reveals that 52% of healthcare executives anticipate better organizational health in 2024, an increase from 37% in the previous year, despite ongoing financial challenges and high leadership turnover. The survey also indicates that 66% of executives plan to seek new opportunities, and facilities are increasingly using interim leaders to fill vacancies. Expanding existing service lines and implementing cost reduction measures are identified as top revenue enhancement strategies for the coming year.

title: National Vision Holdings, Inc. Accepts the Resignation of Heather Cianfrocco as Director
summary: National Vision Holdings, Inc. (EYE) announced that its Board of Directors accepted the resignation of Heather Cianfrocco as a director, effective December 7, 2023. Ms. Cianfrocco's resignation was due to a change in her role at UnitedHealth Group, and there were no disagreements with the Company. Following her departure, the Board reduced its size from nine to eight members.

title: Humana uses AI to deny elderly patients Medicare care, class action claims
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Humana Inc., alleging that the company uses an AI model, nH Predict, to unlawfully deny medically necessary care to elderly patients with Medicare Advantage plans. The plaintiffs claim Humana continues to use this flawed AI despite knowing its inaccuracies, leading to patients being denied care or prematurely removed from care facilities. The lawsuit seeks to represent a nationwide class and alleges unjust enrichment, breach of contract, and breach of good faith and fair dealing.

title: Humana sued for allegedly using AI for Medicare Advantage denials
summary: Humana is being sued in a class action lawsuit for allegedly using its nH Predict AI model to deny care to Medicare Advantage members. The lawsuit claims the AI model makes "highly inaccurate" recovery predictions, leading to premature termination of payments for rehabilitative care and forcing patients to end care early or use personal savings. This follows similar lawsuits against UnitedHealth Group, which developed nH Predict, and Cigna regarding their use of algorithms for claim denials.

title: UnitedHealth Could Be A Combination Of Dividend Growth And Capital Appreciation (NYSE:UNH)
summary: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) is presented as a strong investment opportunity for 2024, combining dividend growth and capital appreciation potential. The company's robust financial health, featuring a strong balance sheet, low debt, and consistent growth in revenue, net income, and free cash flow over the last decade, underpins this outlook. UNH operates as a defensive stock within the healthcare sector through its UnitedHealthcare and Optum divisions, serving millions.

title: Our history
summary: This article chronicles the history of CVS Health, detailing key milestones from its founding in 1963 as a Consumer Value Store to its evolution into a major healthcare company. It highlights significant acquisitions, strategic shifts, and commitments to public health and community initiatives, including its response to the COVID-19 pandemic and recent acquisitions in 2023. The narrative emphasizes CVS Health's continuous growth and unwavering commitment to consumers, now serving over 100 million people daily.

title: Here are Seacoast 10 to Watch young professionals winners for 2023
summary: The 2023 10 To Watch contest recognized young professionals under 40 in the Seacoast region at an awards ceremony on October 11 in Portsmouth. This year marked the 10th anniversary of the contest, presented by Catapult Seacoast and Local iQ, and sponsored by Bank of America, Heritage Home Services, and Eversource. The article details the achievements and community contributions of ten winners, including bankers, healers, marketing coordinators, housing advocates, and entrepreneurs.

title: Digital Mental Health Startup Tava Health Lands $16M
summary: Tava Health, a virtual mental health company, has secured $16 million in fundraising and is seeking an additional $4 million to close the round. The company partners with employers to provide accessible, evidence-based mental health care, distinguishing itself from traditional EAPs by offering quicker access and ongoing support. This funding comes amidst a generally sluggish quarter for digital health investments, though digital behavioral health has shown relative strength with other notable deals.

title: UnitedHealth’s rehab restrictions, Texas medical school drama, and health care’s biggest profits
summary: This article covers several key issues in the healthcare industry, including UnitedHealth Group's alleged use of specific rules and an algorithm to deny rehab care for Medicare Advantage members. It also explores an analysis of the most profitable sectors in healthcare, the watch-worthy health policies in various states, and a critical look at how a medical school in Austin, Texas, prioritized its own development over providing care for indigent patients. Additionally, the article discusses a new appeals process for Medicare beneficiaries mislabeled as outpatients, and recent financial news from Devoted Health, UnitedHealth, Bright Health Group, and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals.

title: One Year Later: Recapping Quality Growth in 2023
summary: The article reviews the performance of the WisdomTree U.S. Quality Growth Fund (QGRW) in 2023, one year after its launch. It highlights QGRW's outperformance against the Russell 1000 Growth Index, attributing much of this to its focus on high-quality growth stocks with strong profitability. The semi-annual rebalance and key characteristics of the index are also discussed, alongside potential portfolio construction strategies combining QGRW with the WisdomTree U.S. Quality Dividend Growth Fund (DGRW).

title: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) stock rose 0.34% to $538.37 on Tuesday, outperforming the broader market which saw declines in the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This increase broke a two-day losing streak for the company's shares. The market faced a rough trading session overall.

title: Marcus & Millichap sells 217-unit apartment community in St. Louis Park
summary: Marcus & Millichap successfully brokered the sale of Via Sol, a 217-unit multifamily property in St. Louis Park, Minnesota. The transaction involved both the representation of the seller, Place E-Generation One LLC, and the procurement of the buyer, Bigos-Via Sol LLC, by Abe Roberts, Will Balthrope, and Drew Garza. Completed in 2022, the property boasts sustainable infrastructure and a range of amenities, and is conveniently located near major corporate headquarters.

title: The UnitedHealth Group Inc (UNH) DCF Valuation: Is The Stock Undervalued?
summary: This article analyzes UnitedHealth Group Inc (UNH) using a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation model to determine if the stock is undervalued. Based on the DCF analysis, which included a 6% discount rate and 2% terminal growth rate, UNH appears to be undervalued with a margin of safety of 34.72%, suggesting an intrinsic value of $826.48 per share compared to a current market price of $539.54. The authors emphasize that this is a preliminary analysis and investors should conduct their own thorough research.

title: UnitedHealth Group Looks Buyable After AI-Fueled Double Beat
summary: UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) reported a double beat on fourth-quarter earnings, exceeding analyst expectations for both EPS and revenue. Despite this, the stock initially dropped due to investor concerns over a sharp rise in medical expenses, particularly from its Medicare Advantage business. However, the company's Optum division, leveraging AI for revenue accuracy and efficiency, showed significant growth, and technical analysis suggests UNH stock could be a buy as it approaches its 100-day simple moving average.

title: Key highlights from UnitedHealth Group’s (UNH) Q4 2023 earnings results
summary: UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) released its Q4 2023 earnings report, showing a significant increase in total revenues to $94.4 billion from $82.8 billion year-over-year. Net earnings attributable to common shareholders rose to $5.4 billion, or $5.83 per share, with adjusted EPS reaching $6.16. The company also returned $14.8 billion to shareholders during 2023 through dividends and share repurchases.

title: UnitedHealth Earnings: Diversification Benefits On Display as Medical Utilization Rises
summary: UnitedHealth Group reported stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter results, driven by its diversified business model despite rising medical utilization. While medical insurance operating profit growth was constrained, the Optum franchises, particularly Optum Health and Optum Rx, benefited from these trends, offsetting weakness. Morningstar maintains its 2024 earnings forecast for UnitedHealth slightly above management's outlook, anticipating the company to outperform initial projections.

title: Global Medicine Spending to Reach $2.3 Trillion by 2028 as More Patients Get Access to Better Therapies, Says IQVIA Institute Report
summary: A new IQVIA Institute report projects global medicine spending to hit $2.3 trillion by 2028, driven by increased patient access to novel therapies, especially in immunology, endocrinology, and oncology. This updated outlook raises the growth forecast despite lower expectations for COVID-19 vaccines and therapeutics, indicating that global use and spending are surpassing pre-pandemic rates. The report highlights significant growth drivers including innovative oncology drugs and GLP-1 agonists for obesity, while noting the impact of biosimilars on immunology spending.

title: Which companies are ‘Most Admired for HR’? Here are the leaders
summary: The 19th annual "Most Admired for HR" list, compiled by Korn Ferry and HRE, shows significant shifts, with DHL Group rising to No. 1. Megabanks and semiconductor companies also saw substantial climbing in rankings, while perennial leaders like Apple maintained high positions. The report highlights trends like emphasizing learning and development, strategic workforce planning, and a focus on culture alignment with business objectives for HR excellence.

title: Humana patients are using their insurance more than expected
summary: Humana announced a surprise increase in medical costs due to higher-than-anticipated insurance utilization, particularly in Medicare Advantage. This led to a significant drop in Humana's stock and a lowered profit outlook for 2024. The trend, believed to be industry-wide, could result in higher premiums in 2025.

title: Humana Tumbles After Cutting 2023 Outlook On High Medical Costs
summary: Humana Inc. shares plummeted after the company cut its 2023 earnings outlook due to higher-than-expected medical costs and forecast sluggish enrollment growth for the current year. This news led to a decline in shares across the health insurance sector, although some losses were pared later in the day. Humana closed down 8% following the announcement.

title: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock falls Friday, underperforms market
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) stock fell 2.48% on Friday, closing at $503.56. This decline occurred despite a strong day for the broader market, with the S&P 500 Index rising 1.23% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average increasing by 1.05%. This marks the second consecutive day of losses for UnitedHealth Group's stock.

title: Medicaid Innovation Collaborative Announces 5 Pilot Programs To Improve Outcomes for Medicaid Patients
summary: The Medicaid Innovation Collaborative (MIC) unveiled five new pilot programs in Kentucky, New York, and Iowa, aiming to enhance the health outcomes of Medicaid beneficiaries with chronic conditions, especially diabetes. These programs, funded by grants from the Helmsley Charitable Trust and Acumen America partners, focus on addressing health-related social needs such as food insecurity, housing, and transportation. The MIC emphasizes collaborating with tech-enabled solutions experienced in working with the Medicaid population to ensure effective and sustainable interventions.

title: A New Chapter in FreeStyle Libre Technology
summary: Abbott's new FreeStyle Libre 2 Plus sensor now integrates with Tandem Diabetes Care's t:slim X2 insulin pump, offering U.S. insulin pump users the benefits of an automated insulin delivery (AID) system. This integration allows for continuous glucose monitoring and automatic insulin adjustments, reinforcing Abbott's leadership in diabetes care. The sensor is notable for its 15-day wear time and marks the latest in a series of partnerships to streamline diabetes management.

title: Humana’s stock falls to four-year low and drags rivals down with it
summary: Humana's stock dropped 13% after the company reported a widened quarterly loss and significantly cut its 2024 profit guidance due to surging medical costs for Medicare Advantage patients. This decline marks its lowest level in over four years and also pulled down shares of rival managed care companies like UnitedHealth Group, Cigna Group, and Elevance Health.

title: Humana's stock tanks as it cuts 2024 guidance amid soaring medical costs
summary: Humana's stock dropped sharply after the company cut its 2024 profit guidance by almost half due to soaring medical costs from Medicare Advantage patients. The healthcare provider's stock fell to a four-year low and impacted rivals like UnitedHealth Group, Cigna Group, and Elevance Health. This highlights a broader issue of rising medical expenses affecting managed care companies.

title: Humana stock plunges on dismal 2024 forecast, as insurers face soaring medical costs
summary: Humana's stock plunged after the health insurer issued a grim 2024 earnings forecast, significantly below Wall Street's expectations. The company cited surging medical costs, particularly from older adults returning for delayed procedures, which is impacting the broader insurance industry. This forecast also negatively affected shares of other major health insurance companies.

title: Health insurer Humana warns of hit to 2025 profit, shares sink
summary: Health insurer Humana's shares plunged 13% after the company warned that unprecedented increases in medical costs will negatively impact its 2024 earnings and push its 2025 profit target out of reach. Humana, which focuses on Medicare Advantage plans, reported a higher-than-expected benefit ratio and forecast significantly lower adjusted profits for both 2024 and 2025, while rivals have not yet indicated similar issues.

title: Exclusive | Cigna Sells Medicare Business to Health Care Service Corp. for $3.3 Billion
summary: Cigna Group is selling its Medicare business to Health Care Service Corp. for $3.3 billion in cash. This deal includes Cigna's Medicare Advantage, Medicare supplement, Medicare drug plans, and its CareAllies unit, marking Cigna's exit from a significant growth sector in the health-insurance industry. The transaction is expected to close in 2025, pending regulatory approvals.

title: Aetna scored big Medicare Advantage gains in Southeastern Pa. for 2024
summary: Aetna achieved the largest net gain in Medicare Advantage customers in Southeastern Pennsylvania in 2024, adding over 13,000 new enrollees. The article highlights strong growth for major national providers like Humana and UnitedHealthcare in the region, while Independence Blue Cross maintains the largest market share. The Medicare Advantage market is experiencing pressure due to increased healthcare usage and federal rate cuts, impacting profitability for some companies.

title: Tenet announces sale of seven hospitals in South Carolina and California
summary: Tenet Healthcare Corporation has completed the sale of three South Carolina hospitals to Novant Health for approximately $2.4 billion and entered into an agreement to sell four California hospitals to UCI Health for $975 million. These transactions will help Tenet reduce leverage and are expected to positively impact the company's income tax expense in 2024. Tenet also anticipates exceeding its FY23 Adjusted EBITDA Outlook.

title: Complications and Mortality Risk of CVC-Related Bloodstream Infections
summary: A retrospective analysis investigated the clinical burden of catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSIs) in hemodialysis patients with central venous catheters (CVCs). The study found that nearly 33% of CVC hemodialysis patients developed a CRBSI, which was associated with high rates of cardiovascular events and a 1-year mortality rate of 36%. The researchers highlight the critical need for early intervention to prevent CRBSIs due to their significant morbidity and mortality burden.

title: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) stock rose 1.53% to $510.67 on Tuesday, performing positively in a generally up market where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also saw gains. Despite the daily increase, the stock underperformed compared to some competitors. UnitedHealth Group Inc. closed $44.03 below its 52-week high of $554.70.

title: UnitedHealth's chief operating officer Dirk McMahon to retire
summary: Dirk McMahon, the president and chief operating officer of UnitedHealth, is set to retire on April 1, 2024, after more than 20 years with the company. McMahon, 64, previously served as CEO of various units before assuming his current role in February 2021. This announcement follows Andrew Witty's appointment as CEO, succeeding David Wichmann.

title: Ipsen drug approved by FDA for early pancreatic cancer
summary: The FDA has approved Ipsen's Onivyde for use with chemotherapy in treating recently diagnosed metastatic pancreatic cancer, allowing for earlier intervention than its previous second-line use. This decision was based on Phase 3 trial results demonstrating improved survival and delayed tumor progression when Onivyde was combined with FOLFOX. The approval comes with a financial impact for Ipsen, triggering a $225 million milestone payment to Merrimack.

title: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) stock saw a slight gain of 0.13% on Friday, closing at $521.55, despite a generally down day for the broader market. This marked the third consecutive day of gains for the stock. However, it still underperformed compared to its competitors, even as the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced declines.

title: Making Well-Being Programs Work for Millennials & Gen Z
summary: The article emphasizes the growing importance for employers to tailor well-being programs to meet the specific needs of Millennials and Gen Z, who together form a significant portion of the modern workforce. It highlights that these generations prioritize work-life balance and well-being, impacted by economic and societal challenges, and provides recommendations for benefits such as financial well-being, family support, mental health, and physical fitness programs to attract and retain them.

title: Travelers Insurance applies for AI software trademark
summary: Travelers Insurance has filed a trademark application for "TRAVAI," an AI software intended for insurance claims processing, administration, and loss control management, among other tasks. This development comes as the insurance industry faces increasing scrutiny and regulatory guidance regarding the responsible use of AI, with some companies already facing lawsuits over alleged discriminatory or arbitrary AI-driven claim denials. The application highlights the growing integration of AI in insurance operations amidst regulatory efforts to ensure fairness and prevent bias.

title: Change Healthcare hit by cyberattack
summary: Change Healthcare, a UnitedHealth-owned healthcare technology company, experienced a cyberattack, leading to system disconnections and potential network disruptions. The company took its systems offline after detecting an "outside threat," which it believes is isolated. This incident highlights the growing challenge of cyberattacks in the healthcare sector, following other recent high-profile breaches and concerns from regulators about cybersecurity standards.

title: FDA approves Alvotech and Teva’s Simlandi as interchangeable Humira biosimilar
summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Alvotech and Teva’s Simlandi (adalimumab-ryvk) injection as an interchangeable biosimilar to AbbVie’s Humira (adalimumab). Simlandi is the first high-concentration, citrate-free biosimilar to Humira to receive interchangeability status, which is significant as almost 88% of US prescriptions for adalimumab are for the high-concentration presentation. The approval was based on extensive evidence, including clinical data demonstrating similar efficacy and safety to Humira for conditions like moderate-to-severe chronic plaque psoriasis.

title: Change Healthcare clicked the wrong link
summary: The Change Healthcare cyberattack, attributed to a nation-state, has significantly disrupted the healthcare sector, prompting organizations like the AHA to advise disconnecting from its services. This incident highlights the substantial financial and operational risks cybersecurity breaches pose to healthcare organizations, some of which have incurred losses exceeding $100 million from similar attacks. Additionally, the article covers other major healthcare news, including R1 RCM's take-private offer, VillageMD's exit from Florida, and quarterly earnings reports from various healthcare companies.

title: US launches antitrust investigation into UnitedHealth, WSJ reports
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has launched an antitrust investigation into UnitedHealth Group, according to a Wall Street Journal report. Investigators are interviewing healthcare industry representatives about the relationship between UnitedHealthcare's insurance unit and its Optum health services arm, and examining potential impacts of the company's doctor-group acquisitions and Medicare billing practices. This comes amid broader Biden administration efforts to lower healthcare costs and scrutinize pharmacy benefit managers.

title: Pharmaceutical giant Cencora discloses a data breach
summary: Pharmaceutical giant Cencora disclosed a data breach after suffering a cyberattack that resulted in data exfiltration from its systems. The company, which had $238.6 billion in revenue for fiscal year 2022, discovered the breach on February 21, 2024, and initiated an investigation. While Cencora stated the incident has not materially impacted operations or financial condition yet, the specific nature of the attack is currently unknown.

title: Healthcare Showing That Big Tech Isn't the Only Bull in Town
summary: The healthcare sector is outperforming the S&P 500 and is proving to be a resilient investment, even compared to big tech. The sector's long-term trend, supported by an aging population, makes it an appealing option for investors. For those looking to leverage its growth, the Direxion Daily Healthcare Bull 3X ETF (CURE) offers a triple-leveraged exposure to the Health Care Select Sector Index.

title: Johnson & Johnson drug benefits suit ‘absolutely’ a wake-up call for employers, exec says
summary: A recent lawsuit against Johnson & Johnson, alleging the company overpaid for prescription drugs through its employee health plans, serves as a critical warning for all employers. The suit highlights the lack of transparency in pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) dealings, making it difficult for employers to understand the true cost of drugs and negotiate favorable terms. Experts suggest that employers need to demand more data from PBMs and seek greater transparency in their contracts to ensure they are providing cost-effective benefits to their employees.

title: Hackers behind UnitedHealth Group cyberattack reportedly identified
summary: The Blackcat ransomware group, also known as ALPHV or Noberus, has reportedly claimed responsibility for the cyberattack on UnitedHealth Group's Change Healthcare, stating they stole several terabytes of personal data from "millions" of patients. This data, which includes medical insurance and health records, was allegedly taken from UnitedHealth and its partners, such as Medicare, Tricare, and CVS Health. The attack caused significant disruptions in pharmacies across the U.S., with experts warning of potential identity theft and credit score downgrades for affected individuals.

title: Change Healthcare cyberattack outage could persist for weeks, UnitedHealth Group executive suggests
summary: A UnitedHealth Group executive indicated that the outage caused by the Change Healthcare cyberattack could last for weeks. The company is establishing a loan program to assist healthcare providers who are unable to submit insurance claims due to the system being offline. This timeline offers more clarity than UnitedHealth had previously provided about the duration of the disruption.

title: Molina loses Medicaid contract in Virginia
summary: Molina Healthcare of Virginia was not re-awarded a Medicaid contract in Virginia, which it has held for eight years. This loss is a setback for Molina's membership growth plans in the safety-net insurance program, as it will impact the 140,000 individuals it currently covers in the state. Despite recent contract wins in other states, this marks Molina's second Medicaid state loss, following Indiana in October.

title: Insurers report significant reduction in claims data following Change Healthcare hack
summary: Humana and Elevance Health reported a 15% to 20% reduction in claims data from providers following the Change Healthcare cyberattack, which has disrupted healthcare operations nationwide. While Humana is still assessing the full impact, with up to 20% of claims dependent on Change, Elevance Health noted a shift in provider submissions to other clearinghouses like Availity, with their data reduction now at 10%. Both insurers plan to adjust their reserving approach in the first quarter due to the ongoing situation.

title: Hacker forum post claims UnitedHealth paid $22 mln ransom in bid to recover data
summary: A post on a hacker forum claims that UnitedHealth Group paid $22 million in ransom to the "Blackcat" ransomware gang to recover their data and systems. While UnitedHealth has not confirmed the payment, a cryptocurrency tracing firm partially corroborated the claim. The cyberattack on UnitedHealth's Change Healthcare unit has caused significant disruption across the U.S. medical system.

title: UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Aetna Continue To Outgain Peers In Medicare Advantage
summary: UnitedHealthcare, Humana, and Aetna (CVS Health) continue to significantly outgain their peers in the Medicare Advantage market, attracting over 80% of new beneficiaries to for-profit plans. These major players also show strong ambitions in the home-based care sector through direct ownership or strategic investments. However, the industry is seeing a slowdown or decline in supplemental benefit offerings as plans adjust to rate cuts and new regulations.

title: Evernorth expands GLP-1 program, unveils new Behavioral Health Care Group
summary: Cigna's Evernorth arm announced an expansion to its GLP-1 management solution, EncircleRx, which now includes a financial guarantee for plan sponsors and clients, addressing the high cost of these therapies. Additionally, Evernorth launched a new Behavioral Health Care Group, an outpatient practice offering virtual and in-person services with guaranteed appointments within 72 hours, aiming to improve access and focus on value-based care in behavioral health. The initiative seeks to empower clinicians by reducing administrative burdens and enhance patient outcomes across various mental health needs.

title: UnitedHealth to restore hacked medical claims and payment services mid-March
summary: UnitedHealth expects to restore its medical claims and payments platforms by mid-March following a cyberattack on its Change Healthcare unit. The pharmacy operations went back online on Thursday, with the payment platform scheduled for March 15 and the medical claims network for March 18. The attack by the "Blackcat" ransomware group in late February severely impacted U.S. healthcare providers, leading to calls for financial assistance from the government.

title: Ensign CEO: Nursing Homes Have Decent Legal and Legislative Means To Challenge Staffing Proposal
summary: Ensign CEO Barry Port believes the nursing home industry has strong legal and legislative grounds to challenge the proposed federal staffing mandate due to a perceived disconnect between White House and union objectives and practical implementation. He anticipates significant industry churn if the rule is enforced, potentially creating acquisition opportunities for Ensign. Port also notes improvements in staffing metrics, moderated wage inflation, and strong reimbursement rates for Ensign.

title: 5 Things To Know About Pharmacy Benefit Managers
summary: Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) are key middlemen in the prescription drug supply chain, often contributing to inflated drug costs for consumers and insurers through practices like retaining negotiated rebates and spread pricing. A lack of transparency in PBM operations, coupled with market consolidation, exacerbates these issues by allowing PBMs to prioritize profits over cost savings. Although PBMs are not the sole cause of high drug prices, bipartisan legislative efforts are underway to introduce greater transparency and reform, complementing broader drug pricing initiatives like those in the Inflation Reduction Act.

title: GE HealthCare establishes foundation to advance access to care
summary: GE HealthCare has established the GE HealthCare Foundation, a philanthropic entity dedicated to improving equitable access to healthcare globally. The Foundation will initially focus on enhancing maternal health outcomes and plans to provide grants to non-profit organizations. Inaugural grantees include the Urban Institute, Lwala Community Alliance, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, and Project ECHO, with initiatives ranging from data analysis to training and community support.

title: US health department opens probe into UnitedHealth hack
summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has launched an investigation into the cyberattack on UnitedHealth Group's Change Healthcare, focusing on potential breaches of protected health data and compliance with HIPAA. This probe comes amid an "unprecedented magnitude" cyberattack that has significantly disrupted healthcare services across the country. UnitedHealth, which processes about 50% of U.S. medical claims, has committed to cooperating with the investigation and is working to restore systems and protect data.

title: MGV: Large Value Makes More Sense Now
summary: The article suggests a potential sector rotation as momentum favors large caps, but growth large caps show signs of fatigue. It highlights the Vanguard Mega Cap Value ETF (MGV) as a suitable investment for those bullish on large-cap value, noting its diversified portfolio including companies like Berkshire Hathaway and Exxon Mobil. The author, Michael A. Gayed, CFA, discusses his investment philosophy focused on risk-on/risk-off signals.

title: UnitedHealth says advanced over $2 bln in payments to providers
summary: UnitedHealth Group has advanced over $2 billion in payments to healthcare providers to assist them following a cybersecurity attack on its Change Healthcare unit. The company is restoring its medical claims software and other services, which were disrupted by the cyberattack on February 21. Change Healthcare processes about 50% of U.S. medical claims, affecting numerous healthcare entities.

title: UnitedHealth Group Inc. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH) shares advanced 1.29% to $493.32 on Tuesday, outperforming competitors and the broader market. The S&P 500 Index rose 0.56% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.83% on the same trading day. UnitedHealth Group Inc. closed $61.38 below its 52-week high of $554.70, reached on December 1st.

title: Food as Medicine | Employers, It’s Time to EAT
summary: The "Food as Medicine" concept emphasizes using food to promote health and fight disease, a critical strategy given the prevalence of chronic conditions linked to the Western diet and food insecurity. This article urges employers to adopt an "EAT" approach to incorporate healthy eating into their wellness strategies. This involves establishing programs for access to nutritious food, adjusting the work environment to support healthy habits, and tailoring plan designs to cover medically necessary dietary interventions.

title: UnitedHealth says unit Change has restored and rebuilt functions handled by Amazon
summary: UnitedHealth announced that its Change Healthcare unit has fully restored and rebuilt its cloud-based medical claims services, which were crippled by a cyberattack in February. The restoration, assisted by cybersecurity firms like Palo Alto Networks and Mandiant, includes services previously handled by Amazon and involves rigorous security protocols. The attack severely impacted the U.S. healthcare system, prompting UnitedHealth to advance over $2 billion to affected providers and drawing government investigation.

title: How the Sleep Therapy Sector Is Responding to Philips Respironics’ Exit
summary: Philips Respironics' decision to discontinue several products and pause CPAP device sales for several years has significantly impacted the sleep therapy sector. Other medical device companies are scaling up operations and manufacturing capacity to meet the increased demand and fill the void left by Philips, while healthcare providers face challenges in finding replacements and navigating insurance coverage for patients. The situation is leading to a potential shift towards alternative sleep apnea therapies like oral appliances and positional therapies.

title: Palo Alto Networks CEO explains why he's partnering with companies like Nvidia
summary: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora is partnering with AI companies like Nvidia, Google, AWS, and OpenAI to protect customers from hackers who are increasingly using AI to conduct cyberattacks. Arora emphasized the transformative nature of AI and the necessity of embedding it into Palo Alto's products. The company is also working with Change Healthcare to establish a gold standard for healthcare cybersecurity following a recent cyberattack on the UnitedHealth subsidiary.

title: Private payers initially deny nearly 15% of medical claims
summary: A new Premier Inc. survey revealed that nearly 15% of medical claims submitted to private payers are initially denied, including some pre-approved through prior authorizations. While over half of these initially denied claims are eventually paid, providers face significant costs and delays in pursuing reimbursement, with an estimated $10.6 billion wasted annually on claims that should have been paid at submission. The lengthy appeals process impacts providers' resources, patient satisfaction, and quality scores, with specific concerns raised about Medicare Advantage plans having high denial rates and costs to dispute.

title: Indiana AG Sues Drugmakers, PBMs Over High Insulin Prices
summary: Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita has filed a lawsuit against major drugmakers Sanofi-Aventis and Novo Nordisk, and PBMs CaremarkPCS Health, Express Scripts, CVS Health Corp., and Optum RX, alleging a conspiracy to inflate insulin prices by over 1000% despite decreasing manufacturing costs. The suit highlights that diabetes costs Indiana residents $5 billion annually and affects over 12% of the state's population. Rokita aims to set a precedent against pharmaceutical companies prioritizing profits over patient health.

title: UnitedHealth, Hilton Grand Vacations elevate CFOs to dual president roles
summary: UnitedHealth Group and Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. have elevated their CFOs to dual president roles, a move reflecting the increasing operational responsibilities finance chiefs are taking on. This trend offers critical learning opportunities for CFOs aspiring to CEO positions, especially in sales and marketing, areas where they have traditionally lacked experience. The article highlights compensation changes for HGV's CFO, Daniel Mathewes, following his promotion.

title: 3 Strong Buy Healthcare Stocks to Add to Your Q2 Must-Watch List
summary: This article highlights three strong buy healthcare stocks – UnitedHealth Group (UNH), Abbott Laboratories (ABT), and Merck & Co. (MRK) – to consider for Q2, given the global aging population and projected growth in healthcare spending. Each company demonstrates resilience, innovation, and a strong dividend history. UNH is nearing Dividend Aristocrat status, ABT is a Dividend Aristocrat focused on diversification and new technologies, and MRK is leveraging AI and strategic acquisitions to grow its pipeline.

title: Why the CMS’ Medicare Advantage rate is hurting stocks of Humana, UnitedHealth
summary: Shares of health insurers like Humana and UnitedHealth were negatively impacted after the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) announced a lower-than-expected payment rate for Medicare Advantage plans. The CMS stated that government payments to MA plans are projected to increase by 3.7% in 2025, an amount that disappointed investors hoping for a larger boost. This news led to Humana's stock falling to a four-year low and UnitedHealth's stock declining towards a nine-month low.

title: Costco launches weight-loss program for members
summary: Costco is expanding its partnership with healthcare marketplace Sesame to offer a weight-loss program for its members. The program, which costs $179 for an initial three-month subscription, includes clinical consultation, a nutritional guide, and an individualized treatment program, with clinicians able to pair interventions with medications when appropriate (medication costs are separate). This initiative follows a previous partnership where Costco offered members discounted access to other healthcare services through Sesame.

title: Protenus Awarded Drug Diversion Software Solutions Agreement With Premier, Inc.
summary: Protenus has secured a national group purchasing agreement with Premier, Inc. for its Drug Diversion Software Solutions, effective March 1, 2024. This agreement allows Premier's extensive network of hospitals and healthcare providers to access Protenus's award-winning technology at pre-negotiated terms. The solution aims to help organizations efficiently detect and prevent drug diversion through automated surveillance of medical use transactions.

title: Ardent Health Opts for New Employee Benefits and Employee Experience with Quantum Health and Imagine360
summary: Ardent Health Services has partnered with Quantum Health and Imagine360 to offer new health benefits to its 23,000 employees and their dependents. This collaboration combines Quantum Health's navigation and care coordination with Imagine360's high-performance network and price protection to address rising healthcare costs and employee retention challenges within health systems. Both companies anticipate this model will be replicated by other self-insured employers seeking alternative managed care solutions and better employee healthcare experiences.

title: CMS final rule on broker comp, health equity could shake up Medicare Advantage
summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has finalized a new rule for Contract Year 2025 Medicare Advantage and Part D, introducing significant changes to broker compensation, health equity requirements, mental health provisions, supplemental benefits, and biosimilars. Experts anticipate these changes will profoundly impact MA plans, requiring them to redesign their star ratings and quality approaches. A key aspect is the restriction on "excessive compensation" for brokers, aiming to eliminate financial incentives that swayed plan choices, alongside new protections against the sale of seniors' personal information.

title: BME: Trading At A Historical Discount To NAV (NYSE:BME)
summary: The BlackRock Health Sciences Trust (BME), a diversified closed-end fund focusing on healthcare, offers a 6.35% dividend yield and is currently trading at a significant historical discount to its Net Asset Value (NAV) of nearly -8%. This presents an attractive investment opportunity given the projected growth in the healthcare industry and increased medical spending. However, a potential concern highlighted is the fund's continued reliance on return of capital to fund its distributions.

title: Molina Hits Medicaid Renewal Snags
summary: Molina Healthcare is experiencing setbacks in its Medicaid contract renewal streak, losing bids in Indiana and Virginia after years of successful contract wins. This comes as a significant portion of Molina's Medicaid program revenue is up for re-procurement in the coming years, creating uncertainty despite the company's strong past performance. The company also faces pressure on its Medicare business due to anticipated lower payment rates from the Biden administration for 2025 Medicare Advantage plans.

title: VOOV: A Decent Passively Managed Value ETF, But Not The Best (NYSEARCA:VOOV)
summary: This article evaluates the Vanguard S&P 500 Value Index Fund ETF Shares (VOOV), highlighting its strategy of weighting S&P 500 stocks based on value and growth metrics. It notes VOOV's significant allocation to financials and its diversified portfolio compared to the broader S&P 500. The author observes VOOV's good performance relative to peers over the past decade, despite some rivals performing better.

title: ‘There’s Not a Business Case’: Lack of Parity Hinders Transition to Value-Based Care
summary: The behavioral health industry's transition to value-based care is significantly hampered by a lack of financial parity and insufficient incentives, placing a disproportionate burden on providers and patients. Experts argue that without substantial investments from payers and governments, the necessary infrastructure for value-based care cannot be built, as current fee-for-service models fail to compensate for innovations or measurement-based care. This situation creates a challenging environment for providers, especially startups, who struggle to make a business case for adopting new, uncompensated technologies and services aimed at improving outcomes.

title: Japan Offers Lessons in Longevity
summary: Japan, with the world's fastest-aging population, offers critical insights for other nations grappling with increased longevity. The country faces challenges such as rising social costs, the need to boost productivity, and a shrinking labor force. Morgan Stanley Research highlights Japan's strategies, including managing healthcare and pension costs, leveraging technology for efficiency, and reskilling older workers, as potential models for global adaptation.

title: UnitedHealth Chair, Executives Sold $102 Million in Stock Before US Probe Became Public
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. Chairman Stephen Hemsley and three senior executives sold stock worth $101.5 million in the four months before news of a federal antitrust investigation became public. The sales happened between October 16, 2023, and February 26, 2024. The company's stock dropped after the investigation was reported.

title: Mark Cuban praises Eli Lilly, explains one thing it’s doing right
summary: Mark Cuban, co-founder of Cost Plus Drugs and owner of the Dallas Mavericks, has praised Eli Lilly’s new LillyDirect platform, suggesting it could be a template for other pharmaceutical manufacturers. LillyDirect offers direct-to-patient services for those with obesity, migraine, and diabetes, providing easier access to medicines, affordability solutions, and connections to telehealth providers. Cuban's own company is also exploring selling GLP-1 agonists.

title: NationsBenefits, Instacart Team Up To Provide Online Grocery Services
summary: NationsBenefits and Instacart have partnered to offer online grocery delivery services as a supplemental benefit for members of Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and commercial health plans. This collaboration aims to improve access to healthy food, especially for vulnerable populations and those in food deserts, by allowing members to use their plan-sponsored funds for same-day delivery from a wide network of grocery stores. The move addresses transportation barriers and expands budget options for beneficiaries, aligning with the growing trend of healthcare organizations integrating "food as medicine" programs.

title: Elevance Health And Private Equity Firm To Invest In Primary Care
summary: Elevance Health has partnered with private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice to invest in and advance primary care delivery across multiple U.S. regions. This strategic partnership will combine assets from Elevance Health’s Carelon Health, apree health, and Millennium Physician Group to serve nearly one million consumers. The investment aims to expand access to advanced primary care for various health plans and improve healthcare quality.

title: UnitedHealth hack looms over first-quarter earnings report
summary: UnitedHealth is expected to report higher medical costs in its first-quarter earnings due to a significant cyberattack that disrupted its systems. Analysts predict a "messy" quarter with an anticipated adjusted profit of $6.61 per share, down from earlier estimates, as the company incurs additional medical and legal costs. The hack, which affected prescription and medical claims processing, has led to billions in advanced reimbursements and suspended prior authorizations, impacting the company's financials despite efforts to restore services.

title: UnitedHealth, CVS, Molina the big losers in Florida Medicaid contract awards
summary: Humana, Centene, and Elevance Health won statewide Medicaid contracts in Florida, impacting approximately 4.8 million people. UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Molina Healthcare, and AmeriHealth Caritas Florida, which previously held contracts, were not selected this time. Centene's success in Florida follows a recent protest over Medicaid scoring in Texas and contributed to a boost in its stock price.

title: Elevance partners with private equity firm on primary care
summary: Elevance is partnering with Clayton, Dubilier and Rice (CD&R) to expand its primary care offerings by integrating its Carelon health services business with two of CD&R's primary care portfolio companies. This deal aims to create a new care delivery model accessible to various insurers, positioning Elevance to compete with other major players like UnitedHealth and CVS in the care delivery sector. The partnership will serve nearly one million consumers and seeks to enhance advanced primary care with care coordination, referral management, and health coaching, though financial terms were not disclosed.

title: Change Healthcare breach could cost UnitedHealth $1.6B this year
summary: The Change Healthcare cyberattack is projected to cost UnitedHealth $1.6 billion this year. This financial impact will affect UnitedHealth's income. The article highlights the significant repercussions of the breach on the healthcare giant.

title: UnitedHealth Group Reports First Quarter 2024 Results
summary: UnitedHealth Group announced its first-quarter 2024 results, showcasing broad-based growth from its Optum and UnitedHealthcare segments despite the impact of the Change Healthcare cyberattack. The company's revenues reached $99.8 billion, with specific financial impacts from the cyberattack detailed as $0.74 per share. UnitedHealth Group has also advanced over $6 billion in funding to support affected healthcare providers.

title: UnitedHealth CEO Defends Change Healthcare Deal After Hack
summary: UnitedHealth CEO Andrew Witty defended the company's acquisition of Change Healthcare following a major cyberattack, arguing that recovery would have been more difficult had Change Healthcare remained an independent entity. The attack caused widespread disruptions in the US healthcare system, leading to scrutiny from lawmakers and healthcare providers. UnitedHealth faces ongoing criticism and antitrust concerns regarding its expanding presence in the industry.

title: Why are US pharmacy benefit managers under fire?
summary: Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) are facing intense scrutiny from US lawmakers, drugmakers, and government officials for their role in high prescription drug costs. These companies, which negotiate drug benefits for health insurers, are being investigated by the Federal Trade Commission for practices like charging fees, reimbursing pharmacies, and possibly favoring more expensive drugs. Lawmakers are introducing bills to address issues such as "spread pricing" and to increase transparency in PBM negotiations, while the Department of Justice is also investigating some PBMs.

title: UnitedHealth unit Change faces issue processing some medical claims
summary: UnitedHealth Group's technology unit, Change Healthcare, experienced and resolved an issue processing batches of medical claims for some customers. While a fix has been implemented and is being monitored, it is unclear if this incident is related to a wider February cyberattack that is expected to cost UnitedHealth up to $1.6 billion this year. Optum, Change's operator, stated that a "small subset" of customers may have been affected.

title: Elevance's higher premiums keep costs under control, boost quarterly profit
summary: Elevance Health reported first-quarter profits above Wall Street estimates and slightly raised its annual earnings forecast, driven by higher premiums from commercial insurance plans. The company's smaller presence in the government-backed Medicare Advantage (MA) market helped keep medical costs under control, contributing to its strong financial performance. Elevance's shares rose over 5%, positively impacting rivals UnitedHealth, Centene Corp, and Humana.

title: Digital Behavioral Health Providers Poised to Deliver Coveted Outcomes Data, but Contracts Remain Customized
summary: Digital behavioral health providers are uniquely positioned to offer valuable outcomes data to payers and employers, who are increasingly shifting away from fee-for-service models. Their ability to track data over time allows for more nuanced and tailored outcome measures, addressing the diverse needs of patients with different behavioral health conditions. While no national standard for outcome measures exists, digital providers emphasize collaboration and flexibility to meet specific partnership goals, focusing on engagement, clinical outcomes, and reducing emergency room utilization.

title: Cardinal Health Loses Contracts With UnitedHealth's OptumRX, Stock Slips
summary: Cardinal Health (CAH) shares fell after the company announced that its contracts with UnitedHealth Group's (UNH) OptumRX, which accounted for 16% of its 2023 revenue, would not be renewed. Despite the loss, Cardinal Health affirmed its 2024 adjusted EPS guidance and long-term targets, expecting to offset the impact through new customer wins and growth initiatives. The stock was down 5% following the news.

title: Cardinal Health Reaffirms Fiscal 2024 non-GAAP EPS Guidance and Long-term Targets Amidst Nonrenewal of OptumRx Customer Contracts
summary: Cardinal Health (NYSE: CAH) announced the nonrenewal of its pharmaceutical distribution contracts with OptumRx, effective June 2024. Despite this, the company reaffirmed its fiscal 2024 non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance of $7.20 to $7.35 and its long-term segment profit and consolidated non-GAAP EPS CAGR targets. Cardinal Health expects to offset the impact through new customer wins, specialty growth, and other actions, anticipating growth in fiscal 2025.

title: Another hospital sues MultiPlan, alleging scheme to ‘suppress’ payments
summary: MultiPlan is facing a new class action lawsuit filed by Allegiance Health Management, alleging that MultiPlan and major health insurers conspired to "fix, suppress, and stabilize" out-of-network medical claim payments. This lawsuit underscores the ongoing tension between hospitals and MultiPlan, a data technology vendor that helps insurers determine out-of-network care payments. The legal action follows a New York Times investigation into MultiPlan's alleged practice of low-balling payments, highlighting the skewed incentives within the healthcare system where inflated out-of-network billing meets insurer efforts to minimize payments, leaving patients with high costs.

title: Centene offers look at its Medicaid strategy in 2024
summary: Centene discussed its 2024 Medicaid strategy during its Q1 earnings call, highlighting progress in the redeterminations process and key contract wins. The company exceeded Q1 profit and revenue expectations and raised its full-year guidance, attributing success to strong performance across diversified platforms and strategic execution.

title: Cardinal Health lifts 2024 profit view on demand for costly specialty drugs
summary: Cardinal Health has raised its annual profit forecast for 2024, citing strong demand in its pharmaceutical unit for expensive specialty drugs used to treat complex conditions. The company now anticipates adjusted earnings between $7.30 and $7.40 per share, an increase from previous estimates. This growth comes despite reporting total sales that missed analysts' expectations and the upcoming expiration of significant contracts with UnitedHealth Group's OptumRx.

title: WeightWatchers Struggles to Adapt Amid GLP-1 Drug Boom
summary: WeightWatchers (WW International) is struggling to convince investors that GLP-1 weight-loss drugs like Ozempic are a positive development for its business model. Despite its efforts to adapt and integrate prescription services, investor skepticism remains. The article highlights the financial pressures on WeightWatchers as it navigates the impact of these new pharmaceutical treatments on the weight management industry.

title: Talkspace Achieves Profitability, Reveals Medicare Push
summary: Talkspace Inc. (Nasdaq: TALK) achieved its first profitable quarter since its 2021 IPO on an adjusted basis, driven by a strategic shift towards payer- and government-focused business lines. The company is significantly expanding its reach into traditional Medicare, planning to cover all 50 states by year-end, alongside discussions with Medicare Advantage plans. Despite its financial improvements and expansion efforts, Talkspace's stock price experienced a slight dip, though it remains up significantly over the past year.

title: Change Healthcare lacked safeguards even as it gave security advice
summary: UnitedHealth Group CEO Andrew Witty testified that Change Healthcare, which his company acquired in 2022, lacked basic cybersecurity safeguards like multi-factor authentication despite experts at Change publishing articles on the need for such measures. This lapse allowed a cyber attack in February by the BlackCat/ALPHV group, crippling healthcare payments and leading to a $22 million ransom payment and potential exposure of millions of patient records. Critics, including Senator Ron Wyden, argue the attack could have been prevented with fundamental cybersecurity practices.

title: DocGo says hackers stole patient data in a recent cyberattack
summary: Mobile medical services provider DocGo has disclosed a cyberattack that compromised a limited number of healthcare records from its US-based ambulance transportation business. The company states that the incident has not had a material impact on its operations or financial condition and that it has contained the unauthorized activity. This incident highlights the heightened adversary activities targeting the healthcare sector, as seen in recent attacks on Change Healthcare and NextGen Healthcare.

title: [UPDATED] Enhabit Will Remain a Standalone Business
summary: Enhabit, Inc. (NYSE: EHAB) has concluded its strategic review, opting to remain a standalone company instead of pursuing a sale or merger. The decision was influenced by macro headwinds, regulatory uncertainties, and a difficult healthcare operating environment, which prevented transaction proposals that would enhance shareholder value. Enhabit's management plans to focus on core business operations, leveraging momentum from late 2023 and early 2024 to drive future growth.

title: Report: Amedisys May Sell 100 Locations to Advance UnitedHealth Group Deal
summary: Amedisys Inc. is reportedly considering selling over 100 home health and hospice locations to a private equity buyer to address antitrust concerns raised by regulators regarding its pending acquisition by UnitedHealth Group's Optum. This move, reported by The Capitol Forum, aims to facilitate the $3.3 billion deal, which the U.S. Department of Justice is currently scrutinizing for potential antitrust issues. UnitedHealth Group is also trying to sell 87 of Optum's locations, as both companies work to resolve regulatory hurdles that have caused investor concern and a dip in Amedisys stock values.

title: Denied by AI: STAT series honored as 2024 Pulitzer Prize finalist
summary: The STAT series "Denied by AI" by Casey Ross and Bob Herman was recognized as a 2024 Pulitzer Prize finalist for investigative reporting. The series exposed how UnitedHealth Group utilized an unregulated algorithm to override clinical judgments, leading to denied care for severely ill older and disabled patients. This impactful reporting has prompted significant attention from Congress, federal agencies, and courts, leading to follow-up investigations and policy discussions regarding AI use in Medicare Advantage plans.

title: Medicaid, Medicare integration rule to shake up market
summary: A new rule regarding Medicare and Medicaid integration is expected to significantly impact the D-SNP market. This regulatory change could lead to substantial shifts for companies operating in the dual-eligible special needs plans sector. The article highlights the potential for market disruption due to CMS's actions.

title: Syra Health reports 47% revenue growth YOY and more digital health earnings
summary: Syra Health, a healthcare technology company, reported a 47% increase in revenue year-over-year for Q1 2024, reaching $1.7 million, driven by growth in its Population Health and Healthcare Workforce solutions. Concurrently, Clover Health, a Medicare Advantage insurtech company, achieved profitability on an adjusted EBITDA basis for the first time in Q1 2024, with revenues of $346.9 million and an improved net loss. Both companies expressed confidence in their future guidance, with Syra Health anticipating $9 million to $11 million in 2024 revenue and Clover Health raising its 2024 adjusted EBITDA guidance.

title: abrdn Life Sciences Investors (HQL) and abrdn Healthcare Investors (HQH) Announce an Additional 20% Increase in Distribution Rates Representing a 50% Increase Since January 2024
summary: abrdn Life Sciences Investors (HQL) and abrdn Healthcare Investors (HQH) have announced an additional 20% increase in their annualized distribution rates, bringing the total increase to 50% since January 2024. This raise, from 10% to 12% of rolling NAV, will take effect with distributions payable on June 28, 2024. The Funds' Boards considered long-term positive total returns and an optimistic outlook on the healthcare sector driven by an aging US population and ongoing innovation.

title: Rick Scott tries to rewrite history on $1.7 billion Medicare fraud controversy
summary: Senator Rick Scott is attempting to reframe his past $1.7 billion Medicare fraud controversy as "political persecution," drawing parallels to Donald Trump's current legal challenges. Critics, including a whistleblower from his former company Columbia/HCA, dispute this, pointing to Scott's previous admissions of corporate mistakes and the company's systemic defrauding of federal healthcare programs. Despite the controversy, Scott has successfully won multiple elections, often acknowledging responsibility while denying personal wrongdoing.

title: Humana CEO Bruce Broussard to depart July 1
summary: Humana has announced that CEO Bruce Broussard will officially step down on July 1, after a decade leading the company. He will be succeeded by current Chief Operating Officer Jim Rechtin, who joined Humana in January. Broussard will remain as an advisor until early 2025, assisting with the transition and various company matters, while Humana continues to navigate challenges in the Medicare Advantage market.

title: Jim Rechtin to become Humana CEO on July 1
summary: Jim Rechtin will take over as President and CEO of Humana on July 1, succeeding Bruce Broussard, who will transition to a strategic advisor role. Rechtin brings extensive healthcare experience, including previous leadership positions at Envision Healthcare and OptumCare. This leadership change comes as Humana adjusts its Medicare Advantage growth projections and reported a decrease in first-quarter net profit.

title: Acadia Healthcare Eyes PHP, IOP Growth
summary: Acadia Healthcare is focusing on expanding its partial hospitalization programs (PHPs) and intensive outpatient programs (IOPs) as a new growth avenue. The company sees these outpatient services as a way to provide a broader continuum of care, improve patient outcomes, and achieve significant financial upside due to lower capital requirements and cost-effectiveness compared to inpatient care. This move aligns with a broader industry trend of increasing investment and interest in the PHP and IOP space.

title: Weight Loss Drugs: GLP-1 Agonists
summary: GLP-1 agonists are a new class of drugs that help with weight loss and were initially approved for type 2 diabetes. While effective for obesity, these medications are expensive and have significantly increased costs for employers. Employers are advised to use data to understand cost impact, implement prior authorization programs based on FDA guidelines and BMI, and consider additional management programs to control spending.

title: Hims Debuts $199 Weight-Loss Shots at 85% Discount to Wegovy
summary: Hims & Hers Health Inc. is entering the weight-loss drug market by offering compounded versions of GLP-1s, the active ingredients found in popular drugs like Wegovy, for a significantly reduced price of $199 a month. This strategy allows customers to access these medications despite shortages and high costs of branded versions, leveraging FDA rules that permit compounding for drugs in short supply. The company's stock saw a substantial increase following the announcement, as Hims plans to further expand its offerings and integrate name-brand drugs when supply becomes adequate.

title: Express Scripts enhances strategies to support access to care at independent pharmacies
summary: Express Scripts, through its IndependentRx initiative and collaboration with CPESN® USA, is expanding access to care via independent pharmacies, especially for Medicare beneficiaries with hypertension and diabetes. This effort, guided by its Independent Pharmacy Advisory Committee, aims to bridge care gaps and improve medication management at the community level. The collaboration is seen as a key step in strengthening the role of independent pharmacists and supporting small businesses.

title: Optum buys fast-growing mental health provider Care Counseling
summary: UnitedHealth Group's Optum has acquired Care Counseling, a rapidly expanding outpatient mental health provider based in St. Louis Park. Care Counseling, co-founded in 2014 by Dr. Andrea Hutchinson and John Hutchinson, has grown to 300 employees and operates 10 locations in Minnesota. This acquisition integrates Care Counseling into Optum's Refresh Mental Health network.

title: Building partnerships to enhance the health and vitality of health care workers
summary: This article discusses the critical health and vitality challenges faced by healthcare workers, including high rates of overweight/obesity, back pain, and significant mental health issues such as burnout and substance use. Cigna Healthcare addresses these issues by forming specialized partnerships with hospitals and health systems, offering tailored solutions like customized benefit plans, 24/7 client support, on-site service coordinators, and shared medical management models. The initiatives aim to improve the overall well-being of healthcare professionals, enhance patient care, and address critical staffing shortages exacerbated by the pandemic.

title: DEADLINE ALERT: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Investigates Claims on Behalf of Investors of Humana
summary: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP is investigating potential securities fraud claims against Humana Inc. (NYSE: HUM) on behalf of investors who suffered losses exceeding $100,000. The firm alleges that Humana downplayed increased medical costs from pent-up demand for healthcare procedures, leading to increased utilization rates and reduced profitability. Investors have until August 2, 2024, to seek the role of lead plaintiff in the federal securities class action lawsuit.

title: HeartFlow AI Plaque Analysis Achieves Major Milestone Towards Medicare Coverage
summary: HeartFlow announced a significant step towards Medicare coverage for its AI Plaque Analysis product, with five Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs) releasing draft Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs). These draft LCDs recognize the importance of quantifying coronary artery plaque and highlight HeartFlow's technology in diagnosing and managing cardiovascular care. The company anticipates similar widespread coverage and adoption for Plaque Analysis as it achieved with its HeartFlow FFRCT product.

title: The Spoon: Securian Financial, Fastenal rejoin Fortune 500
summary: Minnesota now has 17 Fortune 500 companies again, as Securian Financial and Fastenal rejoined the list due to strong 2023 sales. The article also touches on local news including an investigation request into the Minnesota State Patrol, a proposed pay raise for Minneapolis police officers, and St. Paul road closures due to Mississippi River flooding.

title: 17 Minnesota Companies Land on 2024 Fortune 500 List
summary: Seventeen Minnesota-based companies made the 2024 Fortune 500 list, with two businesses, Securian Financial Group and Fastenal, returning to the ranking. While UnitedHealth Group held a top spot at fourth place, several financial firms saw significant jumps in their rankings. Minnesota continues to have a notable number of Fortune 500 companies on a per capita basis.

title: Lawsuits over Change Healthcare data breach centralized in Minnesota
summary: A federal panel has centralized 49 lawsuits against UnitedHealth Group's Change Healthcare in Minnesota. These lawsuits accuse the payment processing unit of failing to protect personal data during a February cyber attack. The cases, involving both individual consumers and healthcare providers, will be overseen by U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank.

title: Addus HomeCare expands personal care services to 2 new states with $350M deal
summary: Addus HomeCare is set to acquire Gentiva's personal care business for $350 million, expanding its personal care services into two new states: Texas and Missouri. This acquisition is expected to boost Addus' annualized revenues by approximately $280 million and is part of its strategic growth plan through accretive acquisitions. Meanwhile, Gentiva will sharpen its focus on its core hospice and palliative care businesses.

title: The J&J lawsuit should be a wakeup call to the PBM industry — and to companies everywhere
summary: A lawsuit filed against Johnson & Johnson by an employee, Ann Lewandowski, alleges overpayment for prescription drugs through its PBM, Express Scripts, leading to higher insurance premiums and out-of-pocket costs. This case highlights transparency issues and flawed evaluation models within the PBM industry, particularly concerning the dominance of the "Big 3" PBMs (CVS Caremark, Express Scripts, and OptumRx). The author argues it should prompt employers to seek more transparent, cost-effective pharmacy benefit solutions.

title: US health dept says UnitedHealth can notify patients of data breach
summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has allowed healthcare providers to ask UnitedHealth Group to notify patients affected by the February data breach at its Change Healthcare unit. This decision brings relief to hospitals and providers who had urged the HHS to transfer the notification responsibility. UnitedHealth Group appreciates the clarification, which aligns with its goal to ease reporting obligations for its customers.

title: Top 10: Healthcare Insurance Companies
summary: This article lists and describes the top 10 healthcare insurance companies in the United States by revenue, highlighting their headquarters, market share, and revenue. It also provides an overview of the global health insurance market, noting its projected growth and the US's dominance. The companies are presented in reverse order, culminating with the largest player.

title: CMS is recalculating 2024 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings
summary: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) is recalculating the 2024 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings, specifically for quality bonus payments, following two recent court rulings in favor of insurers SCAN Health Plan and Elevance Health. This recalculation will use the actual cut points from the 2023 Star Ratings as guardrails and will not decrease any contract's quality bonus payment rating. Affected plans have a limited window to resubmit their 2025 bids, though CMS has not yet decided whether to appeal the court judgments.

title: Evoke Pharma Reports Commercial Strategy Progress & Positive Momentum for GIMOTI
summary: Evoke Pharma announced significant progress in its commercial strategy for GIMOTI, including expanded Medicaid access and record-high prescription fills in April and May 2024. The company has also promoted Mark Kowieski to Chief Financial Officer to streamline operations and drive growth. These initiatives aim to enhance market penetration and accelerate revenue for GIMOTI.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s lawsuit against former executives over alleged trade secrets theft dismissed
summary: UnitedHealth Group's lawsuit against former executives Ken Ehlert and Mark Pollman, alleging they stole confidential information to create rival companies like Lore Health, has been dismissed. The parties settled all claims on mutually agreeable terms following arbitration, with neither side acknowledging fault. Lore Health, which recently launched an AI-driven social network, has raised $100 million from private investors and continues its operations unaffected by the litigation.

title: Rate of US uninsured to rise to 8.9% in the next decade, Congressional Budget Office says
summary: The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) projects that the U.S. uninsured rate will increase to 8.9% over the next decade from 7.7% in 2024. This rise is attributed to increased immigration and reduced eligibility for 19-to-24 year-olds due to federal policy changes and the expiration of COVID-19 pandemic-era policies and Obamacare subsidies. While employer-sponsored plans are expected to grow, the CBO anticipates 32 million uninsured people by 2034, still lower than pre-pandemic levels due to an older U.S. population covered by Medicare.

title: FDA lifts hold on PTC Huntington’s disease trial
summary: The FDA has lifted a partial clinical hold on PTC Therapeutics' Phase 2 trial for its Huntington's disease drug, PTC518, following new data. The data showed that the drug significantly suppressed levels of the mutant huntingtin protein in patients, meeting expectations and potentially allowing advancement to Phase 3 trials. This development positions PTC to compete with UniQure in the race for a Huntington's disease treatment.

title: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation Market Report
summary: The global Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT) market is projected to grow significantly, from $8.86 billion in 2023 to $13.31 billion by 2028, driven by an aging population, chronic diseases, and healthcare access initiatives. Key trends include technology integration, patient-centric solutions, and collaborations with ride-sharing platforms. North America currently leads the market, with major players including Transdev, FirstGroup, Lyft, ModivCare, and Falck.

title: Meet the Four Executives Headlining the Drug Channels Leadership Forum
summary: The inaugural Drug Channels Leadership Forum in March 2025 will feature fireside chats with four prominent executives from leading drug channel companies: Cencora, Optum Rx, Eli Lilly and Company, and Walgreens Boots Alliance. Moderated by Adam J. Fein, Ph.D., the event aims to discuss crucial issues and strategic concerns affecting the prescription drug market and U.S. healthcare system through one-on-one conversations and panel discussions.
