Attendance and sponsorship opportunities are limited to maximize networking and learning value for stakeholders across the drug channel ecosystem.

title: Steward Health Care's physician group sale to Optum is off, regulator says
summary: UnitedHealth Group’s Optum has reportedly backed out of its deal to acquire Steward Health Care’s physician group, a key part of Steward's bankruptcy liquidation plans. The Massachusetts Health Policy Commission (HPC) confirmed that Optum is no longer pursuing the acquisition. This development comes after significant scrutiny from lawmakers and critics regarding the potential anticompetitive implications of the deal, and amid concerns over Steward's financial troubles.

title: Amedisys Divests Locations in Advance of Optum Deal
summary: Amedisys has divested several home health locations to VitalCaring, which also acquired some UnitedHealth Group care centers, with financial terms undisclosed. This transaction comes as Optum, a subsidiary of UnitedHealth Group, prepares to complete its acquisition of Amedisys. The divestiture and Optum's larger acquisition strategy are under scrutiny for potential antitrust concerns by the U.S. Department of Justice.

title: The Best Way to Prevent Falls in Older Adults? Not Vitamin D or Calcium Supplements
summary: New guidelines from the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) emphasize structured exercise, particularly activities that improve balance, gait, and mobility, as the primary method for preventing falls in adults aged 65 and older. The guidelines also recommend doctors assess patients for other fall risk factors like vision and hearing problems. Notably, the USPSTF found no evidence that low-dose vitamin D and calcium supplements are effective in preventing falls and thus did not recommend them for this purpose.

title: Wave Life Sciences' Antisense Oligonucleotide WVE-003 Demonstrates Ability to Lower Mutant Huntingtin in Phase 1b/2a Trial
summary: Wave Life Sciences' WVE-003, an allele-selective antisense oligonucleotide, has demonstrated its ability to significantly reduce mutant huntingtin (mHTT) protein levels in the cerebrospinal fluid of Huntington disease patients, while preserving wild-type huntingtin (wtHTT) protein levels. Data from the SELECT-HD trial showed a mean reduction of mHTT by 46% at 8 weeks and 44% at 12 weeks after the last dose, favoring a quarterly or less frequent dosing approach. The drug was characterized as generally safe and well-tolerated, marking the first clinical demonstration of allele-selective silencing for a disease target.

title: Amedisys Expects to Close UnitedHealth Group Deal By Q4
summary: Amedisys has divested some of its home health locations to VitalCaring, a move expected to facilitate the closure of its acquisition by UnitedHealth Group's Optum. This divestiture addresses antitrust concerns previously raised by regulatory bodies like the U.S. Department of Justice, increasing the likelihood of the deal closing in the second half of 2024. The acquisition, valued at $3.3 billion, comes after earlier scrutiny over Optum's previous large-scale healthcare acquisitions.

title: New Medicare Advantage star ratings give extra bonuses to multiple insurers
summary: More than two dozen Medicare Advantage insurers received higher quality ratings for 2024, as revealed by new federal data. This recalculation, spurred by federal court rulings against the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services' previous methodology, will grant ten major health insurance companies, including UnitedHealthcare and Aetna, significant taxpayer-funded bonuses. These "star ratings" indicate a plan's quality, and the upgrades mean hundreds of millions of dollars in extra revenue for the insurers.

title: After A 15% Fall This Year Is Monster Beverage A Better Pick Over Intuitive Surgical Stock?
summary: This article compares Monster Beverage (MNST) and Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) stocks, suggesting MNST is a better investment despite ISRG's historical revenue growth. The analysis highlights MNST's stronger profitability and recent outperformance in stock returns over the last three years. Given the current market conditions, the authors predict MNST will outperform ISRG in the next three years, attributing this to MNST's pricing actions, cost-cutting, and robust demand for energy drinks.

title: BME: Quality Healthcare Fund With 6% Income And An Attractive Discount (NYSE:BME)
summary: BlackRock Health Sciences Trust (BME), a healthcare sector-specific closed-end fund, offers a 6.3% yield and trades at an attractive discount of nearly -8% below NAV. Despite a strong long-term record that has matched or exceeded the S&P 500, its recent performance has been suboptimal. The fund invests in a diversified portfolio of common stocks within the healthcare sector.

title: 3 Stocks to Buy From the ‘Ultimate’ Buy-and-Hold Portfolio
summary: This article identifies three dividend-paying stocks—UnitedHealth Group (UNH), Walmart (WMT), and Brookfield Corporation (BN)—from Gordon Pape's "Internet Wealth Builder Buy and Hold Portfolio." These companies are chosen for their strong long-term growth profiles, industry leadership, and sound financial health. Despite recent challenges like cyberattacks for UNH or valuation concerns for WMT, the article highlights their resilience, analyst support, and strategic strengths, positioning them as ideal buy-and-hold investments.

title: Middlemen have outsized influence on U.S. drug prices due to market consolidation, FTC says
summary: The FTC states that market consolidation among pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) has given them excessive influence over prescription drug prices in the U.S. These PBMs, acting as middlemen, negotiate drug prices and set medication coverage lists, often benefiting themselves at the expense of smaller pharmacies and consumers. The report highlights that the three largest PBMs—UnitedHealth Group's Optum, CVS Caremark, and Cigna's Express Scripts—manage 79% of U.S. prescription drug claims and are vertically integrated with insurance companies and pharmacy chains, creating conflicts of interest.

title: HarmonyCares pockets $200M to expand in-home value-based primary care service
summary: HarmonyCares, a provider of in-home primary care, has secured $200 million in new funding to expand its services to additional states. The company, founded in 1993, operates in 15 states, offering a physician-driven model that includes ancillary services like home health, hospice, and radiology to senior Medicare patients. The investment, led by General Catalyst, McKesson Ventures, and a national payer, will also be used to develop new technology to improve clinical outcomes.

title: Final Trades: Edwards Lifesciences, First Citizens, UnitedHealth and iShares US Real Estate ETF
summary: The Investment Committee has shared their top stock picks for the second half of the year, featuring Edwards Lifesciences, First Citizens, UnitedHealth, and iShares US Real Estate ETF. This article focuses on video content discussing these final trades. The primary content is a video clip of the Investment Committee announcing their stock selections.

title: Top 4 Must-Have Healthcare Stocks for Long-Term Growth
summary: The healthcare industry offers significant long-term growth opportunities driven by an aging global population, technological advancements, and rising healthcare costs. This article highlights four companies poised to benefit from these trends: UnitedHealth Group (UNH), DexCom (DXCM), CVS Health (CVS), and HCA Healthcare (HCA). Each company leverages different aspects of the evolving healthcare landscape, from managing health insurance for the elderly to developing cutting-edge medical devices and focusing on cost-effective care.

title: Cardiovascular startup raises $260 million led by ex-Moderna execs’ new VC fund
summary: Cardurion Pharmaceuticals, a startup focusing on shelved cardiovascular drug candidates from Takeda Pharmaceuticals, has successfully raised $260 million in a Series B funding round. The funding was led by Ascenta Capital, a new venture capital firm founded by Lorence Kim and Evan Rachlin, both former executives from Moderna. Ascenta Capital emphasizes a patient- and operator-centric investment approach, including meeting with patients before making investment decisions.

title: Elevance tumbles as health insurer warns Medicaid members are using more care
summary: Elevance Health's stock fell almost 6% after the insurer reported that its Medicaid members are using more care than states are compensating them for, despite beating Wall Street's earnings estimates. This follows a similar market reaction earlier in the year when another insurer warned about the "disturbance" in Medicaid, driven by states redetermining eligibility post-Covid-19 pandemic. The article indicates that Medicaid redeterminations are causing financial pressures on health insurers as patient utilization patterns shift.

title: Top 10: MedTech Companies
summary: This article lists the top 10 MedTech companies by market capitalization, highlighting their origins, global operations, key products, and employee numbers. The companies featured include industry giants like Johnson & Johnson, UnitedHealth Group, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Abbott Laboratories, and Danaher, all contributing significantly to medical technology advancements worldwide. The MedTech industry encompasses diverse products and solutions from prevention to treatment, improving global healthcare.

title: ARDT Stock Price and Chart — NYSE:ARDT
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of Ardent Health, Inc. (ARDT) stock performance on the NYSE, including its current price, historical chart data, key financial statistics, and analyst ratings. It covers market capitalization, revenue, earnings, and future forecasts, offering insights into the company's operational performance and investment potential.

title: Private Nursing Services Market Hits USD 1179 Billion by 2032
summary: The global private nursing services market is projected to grow from USD 609.7 billion in 2022 to USD 1179 billion by 2032, expanding at a 7% CAGR, driven by an aging population and rising chronic diseases. Despite challenges like rural accessibility and a shortage of skilled professionals, the market is adapting through technological advancements like remote monitoring and telehealth. Key players include The Ensign Group, Knight Health Holdings, and Genesis Healthcare, all contributing to the sector's evolution and continued expansion.

title: Health insurer Elevance cautious on Medicaid business this year
summary: Elevance Health's shares fell after the insurer indicated that medical costs would remain high this year due to increased claims from its government-backed Medicaid plans. The company anticipates higher care utilization by Medicaid members in the second half of 2024, leading to a revised full-year medical loss ratio forecast at the upper end of its initial range. Rival insurers also saw their shares drop amid similar concerns over Medicaid-related costs.

title: Vermont latest state to sue PBMs for allegedly driving up drug prices
summary: Vermont has become the latest state to sue major pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), accusing CVS Health's Caremark and Cigna Group's Express Scripts of artificially inflating prescription drug prices. The lawsuit alleges these PBMs steer patients towards more expensive medications, even when cheaper alternatives are available, and profit from the opaque fee system. This action aligns with similar lawsuits from other states and increased scrutiny from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission regarding PBM practices.

title: Global IT outage a 'huge wake-up call' for cyber insurance industry
summary: A global IT outage on July 19, caused by a faulty update from cybersecurity vendor CrowdStrike, is expected to lead to significant claims for the cyber insurance industry and trigger a reevaluation of policy coverage. The disruption, which impacted critical sectors like banking and aviation, highlights the systemic risk posed by single service providers and human error, rather than just malicious cyberattacks. Insurers anticipate a wave of business interruption claims, prompting a potential shift in how such non-malicious errors are underwritten and priced in future policies.

title: Inspire Medical appoints chief people officer
summary: Inspire Medical Systems has appointed Melissa Mann as its new Chief People Officer. Mann brings over 25 years of experience in human capital management, previously serving at UnitedHealth Group and Target Corporation. She will be responsible for shaping the company's human capital strategy and supporting its continued growth.

title: CVS Caremark® defines future of pharmacy benefit management
summary: CVS Caremark announced a renewed pledge to accelerate transparency, drive to the lowest net cost prescription drugs, strengthen pharmacy relations, and deliver the best clinical care in pharmacy. This initiative builds on their commitment to greater affordability for prescription drugs, promoting low-list price drugs, and innovating to increase transparency through solutions like TrueCost™. The company aims to make it easier for pharmacies to do business with them and to continue challenging pharmaceutical company price hikes.

title: ConnectiCare sold to California-based Molina Healthcare for $350 million, affecting 140,000 members
summary: Molina Healthcare has acquired ConnectiCare from EmblemHealth for $350 million, adding 140,000 members to its national base. This acquisition allows Molina Healthcare to expand its presence in the health insurance market, with ConnectiCare expecting $1.4 billion in premiums this year. The change in ownership signals potential operational shifts as Molina Healthcare implements its business strategies in Connecticut.

title: To get a fair deal on Wegovy, buying Novo Nordisk might not be Medicare’s worst option
summary: Medicare and Medicaid are grappling with the high cost of new weight loss drugs like Wegovy, with current spending on GLP-1s already in the billions. The article suggests that if broader coverage for obesity is enacted, the costs could be astronomical, potentially bankrupting parts of the federal health care budget. This financial challenge raises the question of whether unusual strategies, such as Medicare buying Novo Nordisk, might be considered to manage drug pricing effectively.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s Optum Cuts 100+ Jobs, Including Behavioral Health Roles
summary: Optum, the services arm of UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH), has laid off over 100 employees, including behavioral health managers, as part of a restructuring. This marks the second round of significant layoffs for Optum in recent months, following hundreds of eliminations and the discontinuation of its virtual care business in May. Despite publicly prioritizing behavioral health, UnitedHealth Group has faced challenges, including losing an appeal regarding federal behavioral health parity laws and significant impacts from the Change Healthcare cyberattack.

title: UnitedHealth is tapping the bond market as it moves to get ahead of election-related volatility
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc. has launched a $12 billion, eight-part bond offering to refinance debt and prepare for potential market volatility related to the upcoming U.S. presidential election. The healthcare giant plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including refinancing short-term borrowings and repurchasing more expensive outstanding debt. This move follows the company's recent report of better-than-expected quarterly earnings.

title: Molina’s Medicaid growth offsets worst of redeterminations pressures in Q2
summary: Molina Healthcare exceeded Wall Street's second-quarter earnings and revenue expectations despite concerns about its Medicaid business, reporting $9.9 billion in revenue thanks to new contracts and existing business growth. While net income was slightly down due to increased spending on Medicaid beneficiaries, company executives anticipate an improvement in Medicaid pressures in the second half of the year. Molina also remains open to further mergers and acquisitions, following two recent large purchases, and plans to launch a new subsidiary to manage its growth strategy in dual-eligible Medicare and Medicaid plans.

title: The future of women's health: Key takeaways for brands
summary: WPP's Health@WPP and the World Woman Foundation hosted panels at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity to discuss the future of women's health. The sessions highlighted the need for greater equity, innovation, and empowerment, urging brands and advertisers to champion inclusive research, invest in women-led innovation, and amplify women's voices across different life stages. Key discussions covered the cultural impact of "girlhood," the importance of community in reproductive health, addressing maternal healthcare inequities, destigmatizing menopause, and challenging ageism in media and the workplace for women over 40.

title: ‘They must leave’: Coalition begins push for HCA to relinquish Mission
summary: A broad coalition in Western North Carolina, including doctors, patient advocates, and a state senator, is demanding that HCA Healthcare relinquish ownership of the Mission Health network. They assert that HCA has provided a suboptimal level of care since its $1.5 billion acquisition in 2019, leading to a "marked divestment in staff, resources, and services." The coalition, Reclaim Healthcare WNC, aims to replace HCA with a non-profit owner committed to regional healthcare needs.

title: SouthCoast Health Data Breach Lawsuit Investigation
summary: Attorneys are investigating a potential class action lawsuit against SouthCoast Health following a data breach that occurred between June 15 and June 18, 2023. The breach exposed various types of personal information, including names, Social Security numbers, medical information, and financial data. Individuals affected by the breach may be able to recover compensation for privacy loss and related costs.

title: Cigna CEO promises ‘aggressive’ defense of pharmacy benefit managers
summary: Cigna's CEO, David Cordani, announced an "aggressive" defense strategy for its pharmacy benefit manager (PBM), Express Scripts, amidst increasing public and regulatory scrutiny over drug costs. The strategy includes enhanced lobbying efforts, sponsoring more PBM value research, and collaboration with independent pharmacists. This comes as Express Scripts continues to be a major revenue driver, contributing substantially to Cigna's impressive second-quarter financial results of $60.5 billion in revenue and $1.5 billion in net income, exceeding Wall Street expectations.

title: Cigna CEO David Cordani defends PBMs as scrutiny of the industry ramps up
summary: Cigna CEO David Cordani defended pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) during the company's earnings call, despite increasing regulatory scrutiny. He argued that PBMs like Cigna's Express Scripts play a crucial role in making expensive new pharmacological innovations more affordable by keeping cost-sharing relatively flat. Cigna reported strong second-quarter results, with revenue growing 25% year-over-year, largely driven by its Evernorth division and significant client wins for Express Scripts.

title: National Vision Appoints Caitlin Zulla to Board of Directors
summary: National Vision Holdings, Inc. has appointed Caitlin Zulla to its Board of Directors, a move effective immediately. Zulla, who brings extensive healthcare and financial expertise, currently serves as CEO of Optum Health East and will join the Board’s Compensation Committee. Her appointment is expected to support National Vision's long-term goals and strategic initiatives.

title: National Vision Appoints Caitlin Zulla To Board Of Directors
summary: National Vision Holdings, Inc. announced the appointment of Caitlin Zulla to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. Zulla, CEO of Optum Health East, brings extensive healthcare and finance expertise to the Compensation Committee. Her appointment is part of the Board's strategy to refresh and support the company's long-term goals and value creation.

title: UnitedHealth and HCA clash over hospital chain’s rates in ‘battle of the giants’
summary: A significant contract dispute has emerged between UnitedHealthcare, the largest private health insurer, and HCA Healthcare, the biggest hospital chain. If an agreement on rates isn't reached by September 1, 38 HCA hospitals and affiliated groups across four states (Texas, Colorado, South Carolina, and New Hampshire) will become out-of-network for UnitedHealthcare members, marking a major "battle of the giants" in the health care industry.

title: Enhabit Walks Away From UnitedHealthcare After ‘9 Months Of Unsuccessful Negotiations’
summary: Enhabit Inc. has decided to terminate its contract with UnitedHealthcare after nine months of unsuccessful negotiations, citing a focus on payer innovation strategy and better-reimbursing contracts. This decision was announced during the company's second-quarter earnings call, alongside discussions supporting the Preserving Access to Home Health Care Act to prevent payment cuts. Enhabit aims to reallocate clinical resources to fee-for-service Medicare patients and its 68 favorable contracts, confident in its ability to replace the census from UnitedHealthcare.

title: NHC completes acquisition of White Oak Senior Living’s 15-property portfolio
summary: National HealthCare Corp. (NHC) has finalized its $221.4 million acquisition of White Oak Senior Living’s 15-property portfolio, expanding its presence in North and South Carolina. The deal includes continuing care retirement communities and nursing homes, adding 1,928 skilled nursing beds, 48 assisted living units, and 302 independent living units to NHC's operations. Both companies emphasized cultural alignment centered on excellent patient care.

title: Meet Karen Peck, 2024 Hall of Honor inductee
summary: Karen Peck, a registered nurse with 35 years of experience in senior living, has been named a 2024 Hall of Honor inductee by McKnight's Women of Distinction. Starting at Brookdale Senior Living in 2011, she is known for her leadership, integrity, and significant contributions, including developing a nurse retention program that reduced turnover by 38%. Her responsibilities include overseeing healthcare services and quality for 90 assisted living communities and she has also received several awards for her advocacy and service in the long-term care field.

title: Insurers’ big profits stem from care delivery, not core business
summary: Major health insurers like UnitedHealth Group and Cigna are increasingly deriving their profits from care delivery, pharmacy services, and other non-core businesses rather than traditional health insurance. This strategic shift, aimed at boosting profits and controlling costs by integrating various parts of the healthcare ecosystem, is drawing scrutiny from regulators and Congress due to concerns about potential conflicts of interest and monopolies. While proponents argue this approach can lead to better patient outcomes, critics worry about increased power concentrated in a few hands and the impact on healthcare consumers.

title: For-profit health systems see Medicaid supplemental payment bump in Q2
summary: Most leading for-profit health systems like Tenet Healthcare, HCA Healthcare, and Universal Health Services saw increased profits in Q2, partly due to an uptick in state Medicaid supplemental payments. These payments, which help cover the gap between Medicaid reimbursement rates and actual care costs, boosted revenues between $30 million and $125 million for these systems. While executives still argue that these funds don't fully cover costs, a new CMS rule allowing higher payment rate ceilings is expected to increase supplemental payments significantly in the coming years.

title: What directors can learn from cyber incident disclosures
summary: A Zscaler analysis of SEC filings reveals that cyber incidents, particularly ransomware attacks, significantly impact public companies, with consumer cyclical and healthcare sectors being the most frequent targets. The article highlights that over half of affected companies saw their stock prices remain below pre-incident levels a month after disclosure, emphasizing the importance of robust cybersecurity, zero-trust architectures, and critical third-party risk management for directors. It also notes that assessing materiality within the mandated four-day reporting window is challenging but crucial for accurate disclosures.

title: When Payers Become Producers: Inside the PBM Private-Labeling Trend
summary: This article examines the increasing trend of Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) vertically integrating into biosimilar production, with major players like CVS Health, Cigna, and UnitedHealth Group launching their own biosimilar subsidiaries. A survey by MMIT reveals that most payers anticipate a positive impact on biosimilar competition, but also express concerns about increased contracting complexity and potential market saturation. The piece also discusses regulatory changes regarding biosimilar interchangeability and potential governmental pushback against the growing vertical integration in the PBM sector.

title: 1,500 volunteers to pack thousands of meals for 9/11
summary: Nearly 1,500 volunteers will pack 420,000 meals at the Curtis Culwell Center in observance of the 23rd anniversary of 9/11 and Hunger Action Month. This initiative, part of the 9/11 Day nonprofit's National Day of Service and Remembrance, aims to turn the somber anniversary into "a day of doing good." All meals packed in North Texas will be donated to the North Texas Food Bank to help food-insecure individuals and families.

title: Judge finds 'serious flaws' in AZ Medicaid program's contract awards
summary: An administrative law judge has identified "serious flaws" in how Arizona's Medicaid program awarded contracts, leading to a halt in planned coverage changes for thousands of residents. The judge recommended upholding appeals challenging the state's decision to grant long-term managed care contracts to affiliates of national for-profit companies, rather than local non-profits. This ruling impacts the contracts announced on December 1.

title: Top US oilfield firm Halliburton hit by cyberattack, source says
summary: U.S. oilfield services firm Halliburton was hit by a cyberattack on Wednesday, affecting certain company systems and global connectivity networks. Halliburton is working with external experts to address the issue, which has prompted some staff to disconnect from internal networks. The incident follows a series of cyberattacks on major U.S. companies and highlights the ongoing threat of ransomware, particularly for the energy industry.

title: Humana to pay $90M to settle fraudulent Medicare bid lawsuit
summary: Humana has agreed to pay a $90 million settlement to the federal government to resolve allegations of submitting fraudulent bids for Medicare Part D prescription drug contracts between 2011 and 2017. The lawsuit, filed by a former Humana actuary, alleged the company overcharged the government by committing to provide a required level of coverage while planning to provide less, effectively keeping two sets of books. This settlement is significant as it marks the first resolution of its kind involving fraud in the Part D contracting process.

title: Teladoc Health: Transforming telehealth operations with Copilot
summary: Teladoc Health has revolutionized its telehealth operations by implementing Microsoft Copilot for Microsoft 365, leading to significant time savings, increased efficiency, and improved employee satisfaction. Copilot automates routine tasks, streamlines processes, and enhances client service response times, setting a new standard in the telehealth industry. The integration of Copilot with other Microsoft tools like Power Automate and Power BI has further optimized client interactions and project management.

title: Halliburton alerts oil clients after cybersecurity breach, activates response plan
summary: Halliburton Co. has alerted customers and activated its cybersecurity response plan after an unauthorized third party gained access to some of its systems. The company is investigating the incident and has notified law enforcement, taking some systems offline for protection. This event highlights the increasing cybersecurity risks faced by the energy sector, following other attacks on critical infrastructure.

title: US Physical Therapy Industry on the Rise: Market Projected to Reach $87.83 Billion by 2031
summary: The U.S. physical therapy market is projected to reach $87.83 billion by 2031, growing from $46.75 billion in 2023 with an 8.2% Compound Annual Growth Rate. This growth is driven by increased patient autonomy and the vital role of physical therapists, despite challenges like practitioner burnout. Rehabilitation centers are leading market advancements, providing specialized care for recuperation.

title: Executive Changes at Interim HealthCare, Amedisys, Traditions Health
summary: This article details recent executive changes across three healthcare companies. Interim HealthCare appointed Rexanne Domico as its new President and COO. Michael North, CIO of Amedisys, is departing the company with a significant separation payout, amid its pending acquisition by Optum. Traditions Health also announced Jessica Hellwege as its new VP of Hospice Operations.

title: Halliburton Warning Oil Clients After Cybersecurity Attack
summary: Halliburton Co., a major provider of fracking services, is alerting customers and law enforcement after an unauthorized third party accessed some of its systems, leading the company to take certain systems offline. This incident highlights the increasing vulnerability of the energy sector to cyberattacks, following similar incidents affecting other critical U.S. services. Halliburton is currently investigating the materiality of the breach and working on system restoration.

title: Feds Killed Plan To Curb Medicare Advantage Overbilling After Industry Opposition
summary: A 2014 plan by federal officials to prevent Medicare Advantage insurers from overbilling the government was abandoned after significant industry opposition, newly released court documents reveal. This decision is central to a multibillion-dollar Justice Department civil fraud case against UnitedHealth Group, which alleges the insurer cheated Medicare by identifying additional diagnoses for higher payments while ignoring overcharges. Critics argue this points to a pattern of inadequate CMS oversight of Medicare Advantage plans, leading to billions in inflated government costs.

title: UnitedHealth pledged a hands-off approach after buying a Connecticut medical group. Then it upended how doctors practice
summary: UnitedHealth Group promised a hands-off approach when acquiring ProHealth Physicians in Connecticut, assuring doctors they would lead primary care and better serve patients while the company handled business. However, nearly a decade later, the primary care network is significantly diminished, with doctors leaving and patients struggling to get appointments or complaining of questionable diagnoses. This has led to widespread disillusionment among patients who are now seeking care elsewhere.

title: Protesters Outside UnitedHealthcare Headquarters Allege Company Systemically Denies Care
summary: A protest outside UnitedHealth Group's headquarters led to 11 arrests, with demonstrators alleging the company systemically denies care. Organized by People's Action as part of its Care Over Cost campaign, the protest highlighted concerns about denied claims, prior authorizations, and and the use of AI in claims processing. This event coincided with UnitedHealth Group reporting $7.9 billion in quarterly profits, leading critics to accuse the company of prioritizing profits over patient care.

title: UnitedHealthcare to launch prior authorization gold card program
summary: UnitedHealthcare announced its plan to introduce a prior authorization gold card program. This initiative, detailed by Hayley DeSilva on September 3, 2024, aims to streamline the prior authorization process for certain healthcare providers.

title: Mississippi awards Medicaid contracts to Centene, Molina, TrueCare
summary: Mississippi has awarded new four-year, $3.8 billion Medicaid managed care contracts to Centene subsidiary Magnolia Health, Molina, and newcomer TrueCare. These contracts resolve a two-year delay caused by challenges from UnitedHealth and Elevance regarding the bidding process. Molina and Magnolia Health are incumbents, while TrueCare, a nonprofit formed by the Mississippi Hospital Association, replaces UnitedHealthcare.

title: With 90% institutional ownership, UnitedHealth Group Incorporated (NYSE:UNH) is a favorite amongst the big guns
summary: UnitedHealth Group (NYSE:UNH) is favored by institutional investors, who collectively own 90% of the company, indicating significant influence over its share price. The Vanguard Group is the largest shareholder with 9.1%, and the top 18 shareholders together own 50%. Insiders hold less than 1% of the stock, while the general public owns about 10%.

title: Mississippi Medicaid awarding contracts to Centene, Molina, TrueCare after 2-year delay
summary: After a two-year delay caused by protests from UnitedHealthcare and Elevance Health, Mississippi Medicaid is finally awarding four-year contracts worth $3.8 billion to Centene subsidiary Magnolia Health Plan, Molina Healthcare, and TrueCare. The new contracts are expected to begin operations on July 1, 2025, with enrollment starting May 1, 2025. The protests over the blind bidding process are still being litigated, highlighting scrutiny faced by several states regarding their Medicaid contract award processes.

title: CMS says data breach at contractor could affect more than 946,000 Medicare beneficiaries
summary: A data breach at Wisconsin Physicians Service Insurance Corporation, a CMS contractor, may have exposed the personal and health information of over 946,000 Medicare beneficiaries. The breach stemmed from a vulnerability in the MOVEit file transfer software, which allowed an unauthorized party to copy files in late May 2023. While the vulnerability was later patched, a recent investigation revealed that data was compromised before the fix, though there are no reports of identity fraud or improper data use at this time.

title: Essentia Health to drop from Medicare Advantage networks at UnitedHealthcare, Humana
summary: Essentia Health announced it will drop from Medicare Advantage networks at UnitedHealthcare and Humana starting next year, impacting about 14,000 seniors in Minnesota. The health system cited high rates of claim denials, delayed payments, and excessive prior authorization requirements as reasons for the decision. Both insurers expressed a desire to continue negotiations to keep Essentia Health in their networks.

title: PACS Group more than doubles senior living footprint with recent acquisition
summary: PACS Group, a major nursing home operator, has significantly expanded its senior living portfolio by acquiring 53 new communities from Prestige Care and Prestige Senior Living. This acquisition, which includes independent living, assisted living, and skilled nursing facilities across eight states, more than doubles PACS Group's senior living footprint and establishes a dedicated senior living vertical within the company. The move expands PACS Group's network to the Pacific Northwest and increases its senior living communities from 16 to 37, driven by a recognized market need for more senior living options.

title: Economic, cyber worries among top CFO concerns: Travelers
summary: A recent Travelers study reveals that CFOs are increasingly focused on mitigating business risks, with economic uncertainty, market competition, and inflation being their top concerns. Cybersecurity threats, interest rates, and regulatory compliance also rank high, prompting finance chiefs to prioritize proactive risk management strategies like employee education and cyber insurance. Despite these challenges, CFOs express optimism regarding their companies' financial stability and customer satisfaction.

title: In times of uncertainty, health-care ETFs offer a defensive investment choice
summary: Health-care ETFs are presented as a defensive investment choice, offering growth potential driven by demographics and technological advancements despite market uncertainties. The article highlights several Canadian health-care ETFs, including Hamilton Healthcare Yield Maximizer ETF (TSX: LMAX), Harvest Healthcare Leaders Income ETF (TSX: HHL), and Brompton Global Healthcare Income & Growth ETF (TSX: HIG), detailing their strategies, holdings, and fees. Experts suggest that the sector's lower volatility, combined with the rising global demand for healthcare, makes these ETFs attractive for diversification and risk management, especially with covered-call strategies to enhance yields.

title: Cyberattacks plague health care. Critics call the federal response 'inadequate'
summary: The U.S. healthcare system continues to be a prime target for cyberattacks, with critics labeling the federal government's response as insufficient and underfunded. The recent Change Healthcare hack highlighted widespread vulnerabilities beyond just hospitals, yet current federal strategies are seen as too narrow, focusing primarily on hospitals while neglecting other critical entities in the healthcare supply chain. Experts advocate for stronger mandates and incentives to improve cybersecurity across the entire sector.

title: Leidos Names Tina Jonas to Board; Tom Bell Quoted
summary: Leidos has appointed Tina Jonas, an aerospace and defense industry veteran, to its board of directors, effective September 25. Jonas will also serve on the board’s audit and finance committee. Leidos CEO Tom Bell highlighted Jonas's extensive leadership experience in government and industry, stating that her insights will be invaluable in supporting critical customer missions and driving innovation and growth for the organization.

title: 3 Healthcare ETFs to Buy for Defensive Growth in 2024
summary: This article recommends three healthcare ETFs—iShares U.S. Healthcare Providers ETF (IHF), Vanguard Health Care Index Fund ETF Shares (VHT), and Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV)—for defensive growth in 2024. It highlights the stability of the healthcare sector and its growth driven by digital transformation and increasing medical needs. The article details the holdings, performance, and financial metrics of each ETF, emphasizing their potential for robust returns.

title: 'Stop ripping us off': Senate grills Novo Nordisk CEO on weight loss drug pricing
summary: Novo Nordisk's CEO, Lars Fruergaard Jørgensen, was grilled by the Senate over the high prices of the company's weight loss drug Wegovy and diabetes treatment Ozempic in the U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders accused the company of charging Americans significantly more than patients in other countries, demanding they "stop ripping us off." While Jørgensen did not explicitly promise price cuts, he committed to working with lawmakers on policy solutions and engaging with pharmacy benefit managers to address drug affordability, attributing high costs partly to the complex U.S. healthcare system and PBM negotiations.

title: Health Information Exchange Market Set to Experience Robust Growth with a CAGR of 8.5%
summary: The Health Information Exchange (HIE) market is projected to grow at an 8.5% CAGR from 2024 to 2032, driven by the increasing need for secure patient information sharing among healthcare providers and systems. The market's expansion is attributed to the rising adoption of EHR systems, government initiatives for interoperability, and a focus on value-based care, despite challenges like data privacy concerns and high implementation costs. Key players include major healthcare technology companies such as Allscripts, Cerner, Epic Systems, and UnitedHealth Group.

title: US Senator Sanders says middlemen won't punish Novo if it cuts weight-loss drug prices
summary: U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders stated that major pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) have committed to expanding coverage for Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy if the company reduces their list prices. This preempts the pharmaceutical industry's argument that price cuts lead to narrower coverage due to PBM rebate incentives. Despite criticism from Sanders regarding the high U.S. prices compared to other countries, Novo Nordisk CEO Lars Jorgensen did not commit to price reductions, expressing skepticism about PBMs' willingness to make the drugs more affordable.

title: 3 Healthcare Investing Trends to Watch
summary: The Morgan Stanley Global Healthcare Conference highlighted three key investing trends: a rebounding M&A environment driven by potential interest rate reductions and capital deployment, the increasing investment in AI for productivity, cost reduction, and drug discovery, and innovations in digital health and biotechnology coupled with positive utilization trends for healthcare services and products. These trends suggest an evolving landscape for healthcare investing, with a focus on efficiency, technological advancement, and strategic mergers to unlock capital and drive growth.

title: Acadia Healthcare to Pay $16.6 Million to Settle False Claims Allegations for Improper Billing of Behavioral Health Services
summary: Acadia Healthcare Company Inc. has agreed to pay $16.6 million to settle False Claims Act allegations for improperly billing Medicare, Medicaid, and TRICARE for medically unnecessary or prolonged behavioral health services. The settlement also includes $3.18 million to resolve state claims in Florida, Georgia, Michigan, and Nevada. Whistleblowers, former Acadia employees Franka Tirado, Brian Snyder, and Jamie Thompson, will receive $3.16 million from the federal settlement.

title: Evolving the Healthcare Consumer Experience
summary: Elevance Health's chief experience officer, Saurabh Tandon, discusses the evolution of healthcare consumer experience towards greater personalization and loyalty. He emphasizes moving beyond administrative functions to become a trusted health partner, using technology like AI to offer smooth, proactive, and individualized care. The goal is to build long-lasting relationships and provide support even before problems arise, akin to a 'My Health Advocate' model.

title: CVS is working with advisors on strategic review, sources say
summary: CVS Health's board has engaged advisors to conduct a strategic review of its business amid potential activist pressure and a depressed stock price. One option being considered is a break up of the insurance and retail businesses. The company is facing challenges such as heightened medical costs in its insurance unit and declining sales in its retail segment due to inflation, softer consumer spending, and competition.

title: PBM Private-Label Units Are Drawing Pharma Contracting, Scrutiny
summary: The "Big Three" PBMs are increasingly rolling out private-label subsidiaries, particularly for biosimilars and generics, which offer both benefits and risks to pharmaceutical companies. These units are drawing significant scrutiny from government bodies like the FTC and Senate, who are investigating potential anti-competitive practices and impacts on consumer access to affordable drugs. Experts weigh in on the advantages of market reach and shared resources versus disadvantages such as brand dilution and increased regulatory issues stemming from these co-branding efforts.

title: Humana faces financial challenges after lower-than-expected star ratings
summary: Humana's stock plummeted after reporting a significant drop in its Medicare Advantage (MA) star ratings for 2025. This reduction in star ratings will impact the company's financial incentives and comes despite Humana believing there may be errors in CMS's calculations. Other major health insurers like CVS Health's Aetna and Elevance Health have also faced financial challenges due to lower star ratings.

title: CVS Health Lays Off 3,000 Employees Amid Industry Challenges and Restructuring
summary: CVS Health announced it will lay off nearly 3,000 corporate employees in 2024, representing about 1% of its workforce, as part of a $2 billion cost-saving initiative. This decision addresses industry challenges like shrinking reimbursement rates and regulatory pressures, following previous job cuts in 2023. The company is exploring a potential split of its retail and insurance divisions and is providing severance packages to affected employees.

title: Nine health plans to provide MI Coordinated Health starting Jan. 1, 2026.
summary: The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) has awarded contracts to nine health plans to launch MI Coordinated Health starting Jan. 1, 2026. This new benefit plan will serve individuals enrolled in both Medicare and Medicaid, initially in select counties before expanding statewide in 2027. It replaces the MI Health Link program and aims to improve healthcare for low-income seniors and people with disabilities through comprehensive care coordination.

title: Alignment Healthcare Continues to Deliver High-Quality Medicare Advantage Plans, 4 Stars or Greater for 98% of Members in 2025
summary: Alignment Healthcare has announced that 98% of its Medicare Advantage members will be enrolled in plans rated 4 stars or greater by CMS for 2025. This includes retaining a 5-star rating in North Carolina and Nevada for the third consecutive year, and a 4.5-star rating for its California PPO. The company attributes its consistent high ratings to its commitment to member health and delivering quality care.

title: Medicare Advantage star ratings 2025—Who are the winners and losers?
summary: The 2025 Medicare Advantage star ratings show significant shifts, with insurtechs like Alignment Healthcare and Clover Health performing well, while traditional major players such as UnitedHealth and Humana experienced notable declines. Despite these drops for leading insurers, investor reactions have been mixed, with some stock prices remaining stable or even increasing. The new ratings are expected to lead to considerable plan switching during open enrollment, as plans with higher star ratings gain strategic advantages.

title: UnitedHealth Q3 Earnings Beat on Domestic Commercial Business
summary: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) reported a strong third quarter in 2024, with adjusted earnings per share and revenues surpassing analyst estimates due to growth in its domestic commercial business and Optum segments. Despite higher medical costs and a cyberattack impact, the company's operating earnings increased. However, membership declined in global commercial and Medicaid businesses, and operating cash flows decreased year-over-year.

title: UnitedHealth lowers adjusted profit outlook as cyberattack costs rise
summary: UnitedHealth Group has lowered the top end of its adjusted profit guidance for 2024, citing increased costs from a cyberattack on its subsidiary Change Healthcare. The insurer has recorded $2.5 billion in total impacts from the attack through the first nine months of the year, including $1.7 billion in direct response costs. Despite this, UnitedHealth exceeded investor expectations for revenue and earnings per share in the third quarter, driven by growth in its UnitedHealthcare and Optum divisions, though its Change Healthcare unit has not fully recovered.

title: UnitedHealth Group CEO Witty bullish on Medicare Advantage
summary: Andrew Witty, CEO of UnitedHealth Group, expressed a positive outlook on Medicare Advantage. This article, published by Modern Healthcare, highlights Witty's bullish stance on the program.

title: CVS and Walgreens are ailing. Here's why
summary: Walgreens is closing 1,200 stores and CVS recently laid off 2,900 corporate staff as both pharmacy chains face significant financial challenges. The issues stem from overexpansion, changing shopper habits, fierce competition from online retailers and big-box stores, and an ailing relationship with health insurers that has driven down prescription profits. Both companies are now re-evaluating their business models and seeking new payment frameworks for prescriptions to turn fortunes around.

title: Elevance lowers guidance on ‘unprecedented’ Medicaid challenges
summary: Elevance Health lowered its 2024 profit guidance due to "unprecedented challenges" in its Medicaid business, stemming from increased costs and a mismatch between payment rates and member acuity following redeterminations. CEO Gail Boudreaux expects conditions to improve as states update payment rates, despite current rates being inadequate to cover rising medical costs. The insurer reported $1 billion in profit on $45.1 billion in revenue, missing analyst expectations on EPS but beating on revenue.

title: Elevance Health Latest Insurer Battered By Higher Medical Costs
summary: Elevance Health recently reported higher-than-expected medical care costs, leading to a more than 20% tumble in third-quarter profits. This trend mirrors that of other insurers and is attributed partly to pent-up demand for medical care post-pandemic and an influx of sick Medicaid patients. Consequently, Elevance Health has lowered its financial forecast for the remainder of 2024.

title: Elevance Health Will Add To Carelon Portfolio With Carebridge Acquisition
summary: Elevance Health announced its acquisition of Carebridge, a manager of home care and community-based services, to expand its Carelon healthcare services portfolio. The acquisition aims to strengthen Carelon's home health business and its capabilities in managing healthcare spending, despite Elevance Health's recent drop in third-quarter earnings. The financial terms of the deal have not yet been disclosed.

title: CVS replaces CEO Karen Lynch with exec David Joyner as profits, share price suffer
summary: CVS has replaced CEO Karen Lynch with executive David Joyner, citing struggles with profitability and stock performance. The change comes amidst pressure from major shareholder Glenview Capital and ongoing challenges including higher medical costs. Joyner, previously president of pharmacy services, will now lead the company as it faces increased scrutiny over its PBM business and aims to improve its Medicare Advantage segment.

title: Cigna-Humana merger talks are back on: report
summary: Cigna and Humana have reportedly restarted informal merger discussions, though they are in early stages, with Cigna aiming to divest its Medicare Advantage business first. The potential merger could create a rival to industry giants like UnitedHealth Group, but faces scrutiny from federal regulators who have recently increased pre-merger notification requirements and have a history of blocking large healthcare mergers. Following the news, Humana's stock rose, while Cigna's shares dropped.

title: CVS Health CEO Karen Lynch steps down, replaced by David Joyner, after 19% stock plunge
summary: CVS Health CEO Karen Lynch has stepped down following a 19% stock plunge and repeated warnings about earnings falling short of Wall Street forecasts. She is replaced by David Joyner, the former CVS Caremark president, who will attempt to navigate the company through rising medical costs and financial pressures. The company also announced a preliminary third-quarter earnings forecast below analyst expectations, citing higher-than-expected medical cost trends.

title: BME: Defensive Healthcare Exposure With A Tender Offer Opportunity (NYSE:BME)
summary: The BlackRock Health Sciences Trust (BME) offers investors exposure to healthcare companies with a covered call strategy to support its distribution. The fund recently qualified for BlackRock's discount management program, although it was a close call. With a 6.15% distribution yield, BME is highlighted as a consistent and steady option in the closed-end fund (CEF) space.

title: Humana sues to reverse cut to Medicare Advantage ratings
summary: Humana has filed a lawsuit to challenge a reduction in its Medicare Advantage star ratings. The company is seeking to reverse this cut, which impacts its Medicare Advantage plans. The article mentions other related news in the healthcare sector, including CMS's finalization of a Medicare pay hike for doctors.

title: Health insurance giants restart merger talks
summary: Health insurance giants Cigna and Humana have rekindled merger talks that were abandoned last year, a move that would create a new major player in the health-care industry, rivaling UnitedHealth. The timing of these renewed discussions is influenced by potential changes in antitrust oversight following the upcoming presidential election and challenges faced by competitors like CVS. However, Cigna still needs to complete the sale of its Medicare Advantage business, which could complicate regulatory approval for a Humana merger.

title: State of Health Tech 2024
summary: Bessemer Venture Partners' 2024 State of Health Tech report highlights the sector's resilience and recovery, driven significantly by the rise of AI. The report details public and private market performance, introduces new benchmarks for "AI Services-as-Software" business models, and offers predictions for future trends including payer administration insourcing, transparency in pharmacy, AI-assisted clinical services, and value-based care systems.

summary: This article provides details for trading Invesco Optimum Yield Diversified Commodity Strategy No K-1 ETF (PDBC) as a CFD, highlighting current stock price data, historical performance, and key trading conditions. title: Not to be left out, Centene sues CMS over 2025 star ratings
summary: Centene Corporation is suing CMS over its 2025 star ratings, claiming that a secret shopper call was miscategorized and unfairly penalized the insurer. The company estimates this single call could cost them $73 million in gross revenue and significantly impacted its overall star rating, leading to potential ineligibility for certain benefits. Centene joins other major insurers like UnitedHealth and Humana in challenging CMS star ratings, highlighting the critical financial implications of these evaluations.

summary: This article provides the current stock price quote and chart for the AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ), detailing its performance and investment strategy. title: Health insurer Centene eases investor fears with better-than-expected profit
summary: Centene (CNC.N) reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings, driven by strong performance in its commercial health insurance plans, and maintained its annual profit forecast. This helped to alleviate investor concerns following cautious outlooks from rival insurers the previous week. The company's shares jumped nearly 12%, despite higher medical costs, as Centene anticipates these costs to ease next year.

title: Tradr 1X Short Innovation Daily ETF (SARK) Stock Price Quote Today & Current Price Chart
summary: This article provides the current stock price quote and chart for the Tradr 1X Short Innovation Daily ETF (SARK), highlighting its performance data including current price, high, low, and 1-year change. title: Pfizer tops earnings estimates, hikes full-year guidance as Covid products help sales
summary: Pfizer reported third-quarter revenue and adjusted profit that significantly exceeded expectations, driven by strong sales of its Covid vaccine and antiviral pill, Paxlovid. The company subsequently raised its full-year guidance, despite facing activist pressure from Starboard Value regarding its capital deployment and investment strategies. Pfizer's non-Covid products, including those from its Seagen acquisition and Vyndaqel, also contributed to growth, though future sales of its blood thinner Eliquis may be affected by Medicare price negotiations.

title: 2025 Healthcare Cost Outlook | Drivers & Trend Insights
summary: Large employers face significant financial hurdles in managing 2025 healthcare budgets, with costs expected to rise by an average of 6.7% after plan changes. Key drivers include broader economic inflation, rising prescription drug costs (especially GLP-1s), increased utilization of behavioral health services, and a growing volume of large claimants. The article advises employers to proactively manage costs by reviewing existing strategies, optimizing GLP-1 management, setting realistic budgets, and closely monitoring large claimant activity.

title: Vail Resorts doubles mental health benefits access
summary: Vail Resorts has expanded its mental health benefits, now offering 12 free therapy sessions per year to employees, their dependents, and roommates, doubling the previous offering of six sessions. This coverage extends to all year-round workers and seasonal employees working both winter and summer seasons, while single-season employees receive six sessions. The initiative comes amid a growing focus on worker well-being and is available regardless of enrollment in the company's healthcare plan.

title: Alignment Healthcare Still Losing Money Even As Medicare Enrollment Rises
summary: Alignment Healthcare reported a net loss of $26.4 million in its third quarter, despite a nearly 58% increase in Medicare Advantage health plan members and a 62% rise in total revenue to $692.4 million. The company's medical expenses jumped significantly, impacting profitability, similar to larger rivals in the Medicare Advantage sector. Alignment, which went public in 2021, aims for profitability in 2025 as it navigates increased healthcare utilization post-pandemic.

title: Humana increases revenue to $29.4 billion in Q3
summary: Humana reported a significant increase in revenue to $29.4 billion in Q3, up from $25.4 billion in Q3 2023, and raised its 2024 adjusted EPS outlook. Despite growth in Medicare Advantage membership and positive performance from CenterWell Primary Care, the insurer faces risks to its MA margin target due to unfavorable 2025 MA Star Ratings, prompting a lawsuit against CMS. The company plans additional long-term investments focusing on profitable membership growth and strengthening its Stars program.

title: Humana updates guidance as it beats on revenue, profit in Q3
summary: Humana updated its full-year guidance after exceeding revenue and profit expectations in Q3, despite ongoing challenges in its Medicare Advantage star ratings performance. The insurer anticipates "at least $16" earnings per share for the year and reported substantial revenue growth, even as it faces a decline in star ratings for 2025 and plans to exit some MA markets. The company is actively investing to improve star ratings and expects membership growth for 2024 but foresees declines in 2025 due to market exits.

title: FDA Says All Doses of Novo’s Ozempic, Wegovy Now Available
summary: The FDA has announced that all doses of Novo Nordisk's GLP-1 drugs, Ozempic and Wegovy, are now available, though semaglutide still appears on the regulator's drug shortage list. This update follows a year of significant manufacturing investments by Novo Nordisk to meet demand. The article also highlights ongoing controversy surrounding Novo Holdings' acquisition of Catalent, with concerns raised by competitors and lawmakers about potential anti-competitive effects.

title: People Moves: Marlene Creighton, Kraft Heinz Company
summary: Marlene Creighton has been appointed as the new Chief Sales Officer for US retail operations at Kraft Heinz Company. With two decades of sales expertise from companies like Unilever, PepsiCo, and Mars, Creighton will lead global sales strategies and drive revenue growth. Her focus at Kraft Heinz is on transforming sales capabilities, enhancing customer relationships, and fostering growth through innovation and digital transformation.

title: Elevance Is Latest to Invest in Home Health with CareBridge Acquisition
summary: Elevance Health's subsidiary Carelon plans to acquire value-based home health company CareBridge for an estimated $2.7 billion. This acquisition positions Elevance to expand its home-based care services, following a trend among other insurers like UnitedHealth Group and Humana, amidst a shift towards value-based care in the healthcare industry. Carelon reported a 15% increase year over year in total operating revenue to $13.8 billion for Elevance's third quarter.

title: Addus Taking ‘Conservative’ Approach to Hospice, Home Health M&A
summary: Addus HomeCare Corporation is adopting a conservative approach to mergers and acquisitions in the near term as it integrates Gentiva’s personal care business, a deal expected to close in Q4. Despite this, the company is seeing more acquisition opportunities that could strengthen all three of its segments—personal care, home health, and hospice—and remains committed to strategic growth while maintaining financial discipline. The company reported strong Q3 2024 results, including a 7% year-over-year increase in total revenue and a 3.5% rise in hospice service line revenue, exceeding market forecasts in some areas.

title: UnitedHealth Emails Reveal Tension Over Cuts to Doctor Pay
summary: Newly unsealed court documents reveal internal tension within UnitedHealth Group over systematic cuts to payments for out-of-network emergency room visits and mental health care. The records, stemming from litigation with a private equity-backed physician group, expose a dispute between financial giants in the US medical system concerning the insurer's practices of reducing doctor compensation. This issue highlights long-standing accusations from doctors that UnitedHealth underpays for services provided by clinicians outside its network.

title: Are Wall Street Analysts Bullish on PPL Corporation Stock?
summary: PPL Corporation (PPL) stock has underperformed the broader S&P 500 Index and the Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU) over the past year. Despite this, the company reported stronger-than-expected Q3 earnings, with increased operating revenue and adjusted EPS, leading to a "Moderate Buy" consensus rating from analysts, with a significant shift towards "Strong Buy" recommendations. Analysts anticipate continued EPS growth and a potential upside from current price levels.

title: CVS Earnings: Full Extent of Weakness Seen in Aetna Operations
summary: CVS Health released its full third-quarter earnings, highlighting significant weaknesses in its Aetna medical insurance operations due to an ongoing mismatch in rates and elevated medical utilization, particularly in Medicare Advantage. Despite a substantial decline in adjusted operating profit for the Aetna segment, the retail pharmacy stores and healthcare services segments performed admirably. Morningstar maintains its fair value estimate of $93 per share, considering CVS stock undervalued, with potential relief for Medicare Advantage from Republican election wins.

title: CVS CEO: ‘Lots of Headwinds in This Market’
summary: CVS Health's Q3 earnings reflect ongoing struggles in its Health Services division despite overall revenue growth, due to market headwinds and strategic overhauls. CEO David Joyner acknowledged underperformance in the Health Care Benefits segment and discussed restructuring efforts, including significant charges for pharmacy closures and workforce optimization. The company is focusing on integrated health services and digital innovation, such as SimplePay Health, to reposition for future profitability.

title: New CVS Health CEO Shakes Up Management, Commits To Integrated Model
summary: New CVS Health CEO David Joyner has restructured his management team by promoting Prem Shah to group president and hiring former UnitedHealth Group executive Steve Nelson to lead Aetna. This comes as CVS reported a significant drop in third-quarter net income. Joyner is committed to the company's integrated model, aiming to leverage its diverse businesses, including drugstores, PBM services, and Aetna, to improve financial and operational performance.

title: CVS posts mixed results, holds off on guidance in Joyner's first earnings report as CEO
summary: CVS Health reported mixed third-quarter results as higher medical costs squeezed its bottom line, leading to a decision to withhold forward-looking guidance. This marks CEO David Joyner's first earnings report at the helm, and the company also announced a new president for Aetna, Steve Nelson, formerly of UnitedHealthcare. Shares of CVS rose more than 10% on Wednesday despite the mixed results and ongoing challenges with medical costs.

title: Insurers prep for Trump admin friendly to Medicare Advantage and mergers, hostile to Medicaid and ACA
summary: Following Donald Trump's victory, health insurers' stocks rose due to expectations of a more relaxed regulatory environment, particularly favoring Medicare Advantage plans and mergers. While some insurers like CVS Health, Humana, and UnitedHealth Group saw gains, others like Centene, Molina Healthcare, and Oscar Health experienced dips due to anticipated cuts to Medicaid funding and the potential expiration of ACA subsidies. The article also discusses the potential for increased mergers and acquisitions in healthcare, with regulatory bodies likely to be more lenient under a Trump administration.

title: Analysts Say ‘We Would Be Aggressive Buyers on Any Pullbacks’ in Microsoft Stock. Should You Be Too?
summary: Despite a slight dip after its latest earnings report due to increased capital expenditures, Microsoft (MSFT) is viewed by analysts, including Morgan Stanley's Keith Weiss, as a strong buy on any pullbacks. The company exceeded Q1 earnings expectations across all segments, particularly in Intelligent Cloud (Azure), and analysts project continued strong growth for its stock. With 41 out of 48 analysts recommending a "Strong Buy" and an average price target implying a 27% upside, the sentiment suggests that Microsoft's AI advancements and robust financial performance make it an attractive investment despite market fluctuations.

title: CVS names former UnitedHealth exec to run Aetna, shares jump
summary: CVS Health appointed Steve Nelson, a former UnitedHealth executive, to lead its Aetna insurance business following a period of rising medical costs and an earnings miss. Shares of CVS jumped nearly 13% on the news, which also coincided with other health insurers seeing boosts after the U.S. election. The company is undergoing restructuring, including layoffs and store closures, and did not provide a 2024 forecast.

title: Cigna confirms it is not pursuing Humana acquisition
summary: Cigna has officially stated it is not pursuing an acquisition of Humana, putting an end to yearlong rumors of a potential merger. This confirmation follows earlier attempts by Cigna's CEO to downplay speculation and a failure to agree on price during prior discussions. Cigna plans to focus on share repurchases with excess cash rather than large-scale M&A.

title: Enhabit, Inc. (NYSE:EHAB) Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Enhabit, Inc. (NYSE: EHAB) discussed its Q3 2024 earnings, highlighting sequential volume growth in its Hospice segment and improved efficiencies in Home Health. The company is actively managing challenges such as declining home health recertifications and United Healthcare negotiations, while also planning to consolidate or close underperforming branches and pursue de novo expansion. Enhabit provided revised 2024 guidance and outlined strategies for revenue growth and cost streamlining in 2025, including hospice reimbursement increases and payor innovation.

title: Justice Department sues to block UnitedHealth Group’s $3.3 billion purchase of Amedisys
summary: The Justice Department is suing to prevent UnitedHealth Group's $3.3 billion acquisition of Amedisys, a move it fears would reduce competition in the home health and hospice care markets. The antitrust complaint, joined by attorneys general from four states, argues that UnitedHealth's aggressive acquisition strategy stifles patient choice and limits employment options for healthcare professionals. This lawsuit follows UnitedHealth's previous acquisition of LHC Group Inc. and comes amidst the Biden administration's push for tougher antitrust enforcement.

title: Focusing on value to deliver better care to Aetna® Medicare Advantage members
summary: CVS Health, through Aetna, is addressing cost and quality pressures in the U.S. health care system by enabling value-based care (VBC) models, particularly for Medicare Advantage members. VBC prioritizes patient health outcomes by incentivizing providers for high-quality, coordinated care, leading to improved health and lower costs. Aetna's VBC arrangements have resulted in better health outcomes for members, including fewer hospitalizations and significant cost savings, by fostering strong partnerships with over 1,200 value-based health care provider groups.

title: Glenview, Sachem Head, Third Point buy CVS shares during Q3-filings
summary: Three prominent investment firms—Glenview Capital Management, Sachem Head Capital Management, and Third Point—increased or established new positions in CVS Health during the third quarter. These moves were made ahead of CVS tapping David Joyner to replace Karen Lynch as CEO, following a significant drop in the company's stock price and worsening financial forecasts. The investments signal a belief in impending changes at the ailing healthcare giant, with some investors already pushing for strategic shifts.

title: RFK Jr. may start a food and drug ‘culture war.’ Investors are running for cover.
summary: Donald Trump's nomination of Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to lead the Department of Health and Human Services has raised concerns among investors due to his vows to reform the food and drug industries. This move is seen as one of several unorthodox appointments by President-elect Trump. The HHS secretary position oversees a massive budget of over $1.7 trillion for healthcare products and services, causing investors to scramble to understand the potential market impact.

title: Medicaid members, providers continue to face challenges with FSSA’s Pathways implementation
summary: Medicaid members and providers in Indiana are still encountering significant problems with the state's new Pathways for Aging program. Issues include a support line that cannot provide basic information about insurers and timely processing of provider claims by managed care companies, leading to payment delays and interest charges. The Family and Social Services Administration acknowledges these challenges and is working with insurers to rectify them, with a temporary waiver for timely filing requirements remaining in place.

title: Lexaria: GLP-1 Drugs Expand Beyond Weight Loss Into Major Disease Treatments
summary: Lexaria Bioscience highlights the expanding therapeutic applications of GLP-1 drugs, moving beyond their initial use in diabetes and weight loss to treat a range of major diseases. The GLP-1 market is projected to grow significantly, with new research focusing on conditions such as heart disease, Alzheimer's, liver disease, sleep apnea, knee pain, and chronic kidney disease. Lexaria intends to continue its research and development using its DehydraTECH drug delivery platform to enhance the effectiveness of GLP-1 drugs for these emerging applications.

title: [UPDATED] Court Orders VitalCaring to Share 43% of Profits With Encompass Health, Enhabit
summary: A federal judge in Delaware has ordered home health and hospice provider VitalCaring and its private equity backers, Vistria Group and Nautic Partners, to share 43% of their future profits with Encompass Health (NYSE: EHC) and Enhabit Inc. (NYSE: EHAB). This ruling stems from a lawsuit initiated by Encompass Health and Enhabit, alleging that VitalCaring's CEO, April Anthony, engaged in unethical practices and breached employment agreements following the 2022 spinoff of Enhabit from Encompass. The court appointed a trustee to manage the profit-sharing trust, a decision that could also impact UnitedHealth Group's acquisition of Amedisys, as Amedisys plans to divest some locations to VitalCaring.

title: P&G Taps into AI and Automation for Faster, Smarter Operations
summary: Procter & Gamble is leveraging AI and automation to enhance various business operations, including media, marketing, and production. The company uses generative AI for concept generation and content testing, and automation for media scheduling and quality control in manufacturing plants. These innovations have resulted in significant efficiencies, cost reductions, and the ability to run some factory shifts without human supervision, contributing to a projected $2 billion in productivity gains.

title: Staffing solutions company Aya Healthcare to buy Cross Country Healthcare in $615M deal
summary: Aya Healthcare plans to acquire Cross Country Healthcare for approximately $615 million in an all-cash transaction, representing a 67% premium to Cross Country’s closing price on Dec. 3. This acquisition aims to diversify Aya’s coverage with Cross Country’s clinical services in nonclinical settings and combine their tech-enabled workforce solutions. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2025 following stockholder and regulatory approvals, after which Cross Country will become a private company.

title: Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield reverses course on controversial anesthesia policy after widespread backlash
summary: Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield has withdrawn a controversial policy change regarding anesthesia claims after significant public backlash, particularly heightened following the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. Critics, including the American Society of Anesthesiologists, had argued the policy would deny claims for anesthesia care exceeding arbitrary time limits, regardless of medical necessity. Anthem cited "widespread misinformation" for its decision, asserting it would never deny medically necessary services.

title: Pharma execs share their projections for the industry in 2025
summary: Healthcare executives offer their predictions for the pharmaceutical industry in 2025, focusing on the continued impact of GLP-1 medications, the evolving role of compounding pharmacies, and the increasing integration of AI agents. They discuss how these elements will shape personalized care, chronic disease management, and operational efficiencies within the sector.

title: What Nashville public companies are paying to protect their CEOs
summary: Following the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, companies are reassessing executive security. An analysis of filings from Greater Nashville's public companies reveals that security disclosures for top executives are uncommon. Dollar General Corp., for example, reported $51,692 in security and travel expenditures for its CEO, Todd Vasos.

title: Masimo update: SEC announces investigation of RTW Investments and role in proxy war voting
summary: The SEC has launched an investigation into RTW Investments' role in Masimo's recent proxy war, specifically regarding an "empty voting" scheme. Masimo alleges that former CEO Joe Kiani and RTW conspired to manipulate shareholder votes, rigging 19% in Kiani's favor through practices like put options or selling shares after record dates. While empty voting is not inherently illegal, Masimo claims evidence of an insider group, which is a red flag for the SEC and potentially the Department of Justice.

title: Health insurers remove executive bios, images from websites after UnitedHealthcare CEO killing
summary: Following the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, major health insurers have begun removing images and biographies of their top executives from corporate websites. This move comes amid a wave of negative social media reactions to Thompson's killing, which highlighted widespread public anger and frustration with the health insurance industry over claims denials and coverage policies. While some companies removed entire leadership pages, others, like Centene and CVS, only scrubbed executive headshots, and Centene also moved its investor day to a virtual-only event.

title: Centene cancels in-person investor day in NYC, will be held virtually
summary: Centene Corp. (NYSE: CNC) has canceled its in-person Investor Day event in New York City and will instead hold it virtually. This change comes in response to the shooting death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson outside the New York Hilton Midtown, where Thompson's company was hosting an event. Centene's CEO, Sarah London, expressed sadness over Thompson's death and offered support to those affected.

title: Centene cancels in-person investor day after UnitedHealthcare CEO killing, will hold event virtually
summary: Centene has canceled its in-person investor day and will hold the event virtually following the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. This decision comes as other healthcare companies, like CVS and Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield, are also increasing security measures and removing executive photos from their websites. The industry is responding to the "premeditated, targeted attack" on Thompson, with a manhunt for the suspect underway.

title: First Trust Global Tactical Commodity Strategy Fund (FTGC) Stock Price Quote Today & Current Price Chart
summary: This article provides current and historical stock price data for the First Trust Global Tactical Commodity Strategy Fund (FTGC). It highlights the current trading price, daily performance metrics, and key statistics, along with details on CFD trading conditions. The page also features recent articles related to shares and client reviews of the Capital.com platform.

title: Who is Luigi Mangione, suspect in the UnitedHealth CEO shooting?
summary: Luigi Mangione, a 26-year-old former data engineer with an Ivy League background, has been arrested in connection with the fatal shooting of a UnitedHealth Group executive. He was found with a homemade gun and an anti-capitalist manifesto. Mangione's online activity suggests an admiration for the Unabomber and potential struggles with chronic back pain, raising questions about his motive and the broader public sentiment against the insurance industry.

title: US CEO murder suspect was Ivy League graduate who praised Unabomber
summary: Luigi Mangione, a 26-year-old Ivy League graduate and data engineer, has been arrested for the murder of healthcare CEO Brian Thompson in New York. Mangione, found with a homemade gun and an anti-capitalist manifesto, is seen by some as a folk hero protesting the insurance industry, while others view him as a symptom of societal breakdown.

title: Schwab Fundamental U.S. Large Company ETF (FNDX) Stock Price Quote Today & Current Price Chart
summary: This article provides the current stock price quote and chart for the Schwab Fundamental U.S. Large Company ETF (FNDX), highlighting its current trading data, key statistics, and CFD trading conditions. It details aspects like spread, overnight funding adjustments, margin requirements, and commission. The page also features a section with related market articles and customer reviews for the trading platform.
